# SwiftUI Motion Library: full reference

> Every effect with its API, usage, an implementation description and the complete source. Generated from the catalog; 145 effects.

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library", from: "0.5.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "MotionLibrary", package: "SwiftUI-Motion-Library")
```

Then `import MotionLibrary`. Requires iOS 17, macOS 14 or visionOS 1; effects marked iOS 18+ are `@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)`.

In an Xcode app project, add the package with **File → Add Package Dependencies…** rather than editing `project.pbxproj` by hand. To use one effect without the package, copy its source file plus any files listed under "Files" for it (shared helpers such as `Support/Haptics.swift`); every effect compiles from just those files.

---

## Typewriter (`typewriter`)

Characters appear one by one with a blinking cursor.

- API: `TypewriterText("…")`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/TypewriterText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/TypewriterText.swift

### Usage

```swift
TypewriterText("Hello, SwiftUI!", interval: .milliseconds(60))
    .font(.title.bold())
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI "typewriter" text view (iOS 17+). It reveals a string one character at a time at a fixed interval (default 60 ms), followed by a cursor character "|" in the accent color that blinks every 0.5 s. Implementation: keep a @State visibleCount, render Text(String(text.prefix(visibleCount))) concatenated with the cursor Text, and drive it from .task(id: text) with Task.sleep so it restarts when the text changes and cancels when the view disappears. Use the full text as the accessibility label.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Reveals a string one character at a time with an optional blinking cursor.
///
/// ```swift
/// TypewriterText("Hello, SwiftUI!")
///     .font(.title.bold())
/// ```
///
/// The animation restarts whenever `text` changes.
public struct TypewriterText: View {
    private let text: String
    private let interval: Duration
    private let showsCursor: Bool
    private let cursor: String

    @State private var visibleCount = 0
    @State private var cursorVisible = true

    public init(
        _ text: String,
        interval: Duration = .milliseconds(60),
        showsCursor: Bool = true,
        cursor: String = "|"
    ) {
        self.text = text
        self.interval = interval
        self.showsCursor = showsCursor
        self.cursor = cursor
    }

    public var body: some View {
        (
            Text(String(text.prefix(visibleCount)))
            + Text(showsCursor ? cursor : "")
                .foregroundStyle(cursorVisible ? Color.accentColor : Color.clear)
        )
        .accessibilityLabel(text)
        .task(id: text) {
            visibleCount = 0
            guard !text.isEmpty else { return }
            for index in 1...text.count {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: interval)
                if Task.isCancelled { return }
                visibleCount = index
            }
        }
        .task {
            guard showsCursor else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(500))
                cursorVisible.toggle()
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    TypewriterText("Turning complex data into meaningful visuals.")
        .font(.title2.weight(.semibold))
        .padding()
}
```

## Scramble / Decode (`scramble`)

Random glyphs resolve into the real text from left to right.

- API: `ScrambleText("…")`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/ScrambleText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/ScrambleText.swift

### Usage

```swift
ScrambleText("ACCESS GRANTED", duration: 1.0)
    .font(.title.bold())
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI "decode" text effect (iOS 17+). On appear, every character of the string is shown as a random glyph from a charset (A–Z, 0–9, #%&*), re-randomised every 30 ms. Over the given duration, characters lock into their real values from left to right until the full string is shown. Spaces never scramble. Use a monospaced font design so the width doesn't jitter, drive frames from .task(id: text) with Task.sleep, and set the real string as the accessibility label.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// "Decoding" text effect: random glyphs settle into the real string from
/// left to right.
///
/// ```swift
/// ScrambleText("ACCESS GRANTED")
///     .font(.title.bold())
/// ```
public struct ScrambleText: View {
    private let text: String
    private let duration: Double
    private let charset: [Character]

    @State private var display: String
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    public init(
        _ text: String,
        duration: Double = 1.0,
        charset: String = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789#%&*"
    ) {
        self.text = text
        self.duration = duration
        self.charset = Array(charset)
        _display = State(initialValue: text)
    }

    public var body: some View {
        Text(display)
            .fontDesign(.monospaced)
            .accessibilityLabel(text)
            .task(id: text) {
                await run()
            }
    }

    private func run() async {
        // Reduce Motion: show the text without the flicker of random glyphs.
        guard !reduceMotion else {
            display = text
            return
        }
        let target = Array(text)
        let frameInterval = 0.03
        let steps = max(1, Int(duration / frameInterval))

        for step in 0...steps {
            let revealed = Int(Double(target.count) * Double(step) / Double(steps))
            var output: [Character] = []
            output.reserveCapacity(target.count)
            for (index, character) in target.enumerated() {
                if index < revealed || character == " " || charset.isEmpty {
                    output.append(character)
                } else {
                    output.append(charset.randomElement() ?? character)
                }
            }
            display = String(output)

            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(frameInterval))
            if Task.isCancelled { return }
        }
        display = text
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrambleText("ACCESS GRANTED", duration: 1.2)
        .font(.title.bold())
        .padding()
}
```

## Shimmer (`shimmer`)

A band of light sweeps across text or skeleton placeholders.

- API: `.shimmer()`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/Shimmer.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/Shimmer.swift

### Usage

```swift
Text("Loading…")
    .font(.title)
    .shimmer()

RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8)
    .fill(.gray.opacity(0.3))
    .frame(height: 44)
    .shimmer(duration: 1.2)
```

### How it works

Create a reusable SwiftUI .shimmer() view modifier (iOS 17+). A soft white highlight band (a horizontal LinearGradient clear → white 80% → clear, about 35% of the view width) moves from just off the left edge to just off the right edge, repeating forever with linear timing (~1.6 s). The band is placed in an overlay with a GeometryReader and masked by the original content so it only lights up the view's own pixels (text glyphs or skeleton shapes). It must not intercept touches and should accept isActive, duration, bandWidth and highlight color parameters.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A band of light that sweeps across the view, clipped to the view's own
/// shape. Works on text, images, and skeleton placeholders.
struct ShimmerModifier: ViewModifier {
    var isActive: Bool
    var duration: Double
    var bandWidth: CGFloat
    var highlight: Color

    @State private var animating = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                if isActive {
                    GeometryReader { geometry in
                        let width = geometry.size.width
                        let band = max(1, width * bandWidth)
                        LinearGradient(
                            colors: [.clear, highlight, .clear],
                            startPoint: .leading,
                            endPoint: .trailing
                        )
                        .frame(width: band, height: geometry.size.height)
                        .offset(x: animating ? width : -band)
                    }
                    .mask { content }
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
                    .onAppear {
                        animating = false
                        // Reduce Motion: no sweep; the band stays parked off-screen.
                        guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                        withAnimation(.linear(duration: duration).repeatForever(autoreverses: false)) {
                            animating = true
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Sweeps a highlight across the view.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text("Loading…").font(.title).shimmer()
    /// RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8).fill(.gray.opacity(0.3)).shimmer()
    /// ```
    func shimmer(
        isActive: Bool = true,
        duration: Double = 1.6,
        bandWidth: CGFloat = 0.35,
        highlight: Color = .white.opacity(0.8)
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ShimmerModifier(
            isActive: isActive,
            duration: duration,
            bandWidth: bandWidth,
            highlight: highlight
        ))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 16) {
        Text("Shimmering title")
            .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            .foregroundStyle(.gray)
            .shimmer()
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
            .fill(.gray.opacity(0.25))
            .frame(height: 60)
            .shimmer()
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Gradient Sweep (`gradient-sweep`)

A multi-colour gradient flows through the letters forever.

- API: `.gradientSweep()`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/GradientSweep.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/GradientSweep.swift

### Usage

```swift
Text("Motion Library")
    .font(.largeTitle.weight(.heavy))
    .gradientSweep()

Image(systemName: "sparkles")
    .font(.system(size: 60))
    .gradientSweep(colors: [.yellow, .orange, .pink], duration: 2)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .gradientSweep(colors:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+) that paints a view's own pixels with a flowing multi-colour gradient. In an overlay, use a GeometryReader to draw a horizontal LinearGradient twice as wide as the view whose colours are the palette repeated twice plus the first colour again (so the right half matches the left half). Offset it from 0 to −width with a linear animation that repeats forever without autoreversing, so the loop is seamless. Mask the overlay with the original content so only glyphs or shapes are coloured, and disable hit testing. Default palette pink, orange, yellow, mint, cyan, purple over 3 s. With Reduce Motion on, show the gradient without moving it.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Fills the view's own pixels with a multi-colour gradient that keeps
/// flowing sideways. Made for headlines, but works on symbols and shapes too.
struct GradientSweepModifier: ViewModifier {
    var colors: [Color]
    var duration: Double

    @State private var flowing = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                GeometryReader { geometry in
                    let width = max(1, geometry.size.width)
                    // Two copies of the palette side by side, twice as wide as
                    // the view. Sliding left by one view width shows the second
                    // copy, which looks exactly like the first, so it loops.
                    let palette = colors.isEmpty ? [Color.primary] : colors
                    LinearGradient(
                        colors: palette + palette + [palette[0]],
                        startPoint: .leading,
                        endPoint: .trailing
                    )
                    .frame(width: width * 2, height: geometry.size.height)
                    .offset(x: flowing ? -width : 0)
                }
                .mask { content }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
            .onAppear {
                guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                flowing = false
                withAnimation(.linear(duration: duration).repeatForever(autoreverses: false)) {
                    flowing = true
                }
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Paints the view with a gradient that flows sideways forever.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text("Motion Library")
    ///     .font(.largeTitle.bold())
    ///     .gradientSweep()
    /// ```
    func gradientSweep(
        colors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .mint, .cyan, .purple],
        duration: Double = 3
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(GradientSweepModifier(colors: colors, duration: duration))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Text("Motion Library")
        .font(.largeTitle.weight(.heavy))
        .gradientSweep()
        .padding()
}
```

## Blur-in Words (`blur-in`)

Words come into focus one after another: fade, rise and un-blur.

- API: `BlurInText("…")`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/BlurInText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/BlurInText.swift

### Usage

```swift
BlurInText("Design is how it works.")
    .font(.title.weight(.semibold))

BlurInText("Letter by letter", by: .character, stagger: 0.03)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI BlurInText view (iOS 17+) that reveals a string piece by piece, split by word (default) or by character. Lay the pieces out with a custom Layout that flows left to right, wraps to new lines and centres each line; the gap between words is about 0.28 × the line height. Each piece starts at opacity 0, blur radius 8 and 8 pt lower, and animates to opacity 1, no blur and no offset with easeOut(0.6 s), delayed by index × stagger (0.08 s default). Replay when the text changes by resetting a revealed flag and setting it again on the next run loop. Expose the whole string as one accessibility label. With Reduce Motion on, only fade.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Text that comes into focus one word (or one letter) at a time: each piece
/// fades in, rises a few points and un-blurs, staggered from first to last.
/// Replays whenever the string changes.
public struct BlurInText: View {
    /// How the string is split into animated pieces.
    public enum Unit: Sendable {
        case word
        case character
    }

    private let text: String
    private let unit: Unit
    private let stagger: Double
    private let duration: Double

    @State private var revealed = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - text: The string to show.
    ///   - unit: Animate word by word or character by character.
    ///   - stagger: Delay between consecutive pieces, in seconds.
    ///   - duration: How long each piece takes to come into focus.
    public init(_ text: String, by unit: Unit = .word, stagger: Double = 0.08, duration: Double = 0.6) {
        self.text = text
        self.unit = unit
        self.stagger = stagger
        self.duration = duration
    }

    public var body: some View {
        FlowLayout(spacing: unit == .word ? 0.28 : 0) {
            ForEach(Array(pieces.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, piece in
                Text(piece)
                    .opacity(revealed ? 1 : 0)
                    .blur(radius: revealed || reduceMotion ? 0 : 8)
                    .offset(y: revealed || reduceMotion ? 0 : 8)
                    .animation(
                        .easeOut(duration: duration).delay(Double(index) * stagger),
                        value: revealed
                    )
            }
        }
        .id(text)
        .onAppear(perform: reveal)
        .onChange(of: text) { reveal() }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(text)
    }

    private var pieces: [String] {
        switch unit {
        case .word:
            text.split(separator: " ", omittingEmptySubsequences: true).map(String.init)
        case .character:
            text.map(String.init)
        }
    }

    private func reveal() {
        revealed = false
        DispatchQueue.main.async { revealed = true }
    }
}

/// Lays children out left to right, wrapping onto new lines. `spacing` is a
/// fraction of the line height, so word gaps scale with the font.
struct FlowLayout: Layout {
    var spacing: CGFloat

    func sizeThatFits(proposal: ProposedViewSize, subviews: Subviews, cache: inout ()) -> CGSize {
        let rows = arrange(subviews: subviews, maxWidth: proposal.width ?? .infinity)
        let width = rows.map(\.width).max() ?? 0
        let height = rows.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.height }
        return CGSize(width: width, height: height)
    }

    func placeSubviews(in bounds: CGRect, proposal: ProposedViewSize, subviews: Subviews, cache: inout ()) {
        let rows = arrange(subviews: subviews, maxWidth: bounds.width)
        var y = bounds.minY
        for row in rows {
            // Centre each row, like multi-line centred text.
            var x = bounds.minX + (bounds.width - row.width) / 2
            for item in row.items {
                subviews[item.index].place(at: CGPoint(x: x, y: y), proposal: ProposedViewSize(item.size))
                x += item.size.width + item.gap
            }
            y += row.height
        }
    }

    private struct Row {
        var items: [(index: Int, size: CGSize, gap: CGFloat)] = []
        var width: CGFloat = 0
        var height: CGFloat = 0
    }

    private func arrange(subviews: Subviews, maxWidth: CGFloat) -> [Row] {
        var rows: [Row] = []
        var row = Row()
        for index in subviews.indices {
            let size = subviews[index].sizeThatFits(.unspecified)
            let gapBefore = row.items.last?.gap ?? 0
            let width = row.items.isEmpty ? size.width : row.width + gapBefore + size.width
            if width > maxWidth, !row.items.isEmpty {
                rows.append(row)
                row = Row()
                row.width = size.width
            } else {
                row.width = width
            }
            row.items.append((index, size, size.height * spacing))
            row.height = max(row.height, size.height)
        }
        rows.append(row)
        return rows
    }
}

#Preview {
    BlurInText("Design is not just what it looks like. Design is how it works.")
        .font(.title2.weight(.semibold))
        .padding()
}
```

## Marquee (`marquee`)

Text too long for its line scrolls sideways forever, with faded edges.

- API: `MarqueeText("…")`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/MarqueeText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/MarqueeText.swift

### Usage

```swift
MarqueeText("Now playing: Midnight Drive — Neon Coast")
    .font(.headline)
    .frame(width: 200)

MarqueeText(longTitle, speed: 60, gap: 24)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI MarqueeText view (iOS 17+) for a single line of text. Measure the text's natural width (fixedSize text with a GeometryReader background) and the container width. If the text fits, show it still. If not, show two copies in an HStack separated by a gap (40 pt) and offset them left by (time × speed) modulo (textWidth + gap) using TimelineView(.animation), so the second copy takes the first copy's place and the loop is seamless. Speed defaults to 40 pt/s. Clip to the container and mask the edges with 16 pt linear fades. Reserve one line of height with a hidden copy of the text. Expose the full text to accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, don't scroll.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A single line of text that scrolls sideways forever when it's too long to
/// fit, with faded edges. Short text just sits still.
public struct MarqueeText: View {
    private let text: String
    private let speed: Double
    private let gap: CGFloat
    private let fadeWidth: CGFloat

    @State private var textWidth: CGFloat = 0
    @State private var containerWidth: CGFloat = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - text: The string to show.
    ///   - speed: Scroll speed in points per second.
    ///   - gap: Space between the end of the text and its next repetition.
    ///   - fadeWidth: Width of the faded edges.
    public init(_ text: String, speed: Double = 40, gap: CGFloat = 40, fadeWidth: CGFloat = 16) {
        self.text = text
        self.speed = speed
        self.gap = gap
        self.fadeWidth = fadeWidth
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let scrolls = textWidth > containerWidth && !reduceMotion
        // Reserve one line of height; the measured text lives in the overlay.
        Text(text)
            .lineLimit(1)
            .hidden()
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .overlay(alignment: .leading) {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: !scrolls)) { timeline in
                    let cycle = textWidth + gap
                    let offset = scrolls
                        ? -CGFloat((timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed)
                            .truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: Double(max(cycle, 1))))
                        : 0
                    HStack(spacing: gap) {
                        label
                        if scrolls { label }
                    }
                    .offset(x: offset)
                }
            }
            .background {
                GeometryReader { proxy in
                    Color.clear
                        .onAppear { containerWidth = proxy.size.width }
                        .onChange(of: proxy.size.width) { _, width in containerWidth = width }
                }
            }
            .clipped()
            .mask {
                if scrolls {
                    HStack(spacing: 0) {
                        LinearGradient(colors: [.clear, .black], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
                            .frame(width: fadeWidth)
                        Color.black
                        LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .clear], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
                            .frame(width: fadeWidth)
                    }
                } else {
                    Color.black
                }
            }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
            .accessibilityLabel(text)
    }

    private var label: some View {
        Text(text)
            .lineLimit(1)
            .fixedSize()
            .background {
                GeometryReader { proxy in
                    Color.clear
                        .onAppear { textWidth = proxy.size.width }
                        .onChange(of: proxy.size.width) { _, width in textWidth = width }
                }
            }
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 20) {
        MarqueeText("Now playing: Midnight City — M83 · Hurry Up, We're Dreaming")
            .font(.headline)
        MarqueeText("Short text stays put")
    }
    .frame(width: 240)
    .padding()
}
```

## Wave Text (`wave-text`)

Letters bob in a travelling wave, drawn with a TextRenderer.

- API: `WaveText("…")`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 18+ · macOS 15+ · visionOS 2+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/WaveText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/WaveText.swift

### Usage

```swift
if #available(iOS 18, *) {
    WaveText("Making waves")
        .font(.largeTitle.bold())
        .foregroundStyle(.blue)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI WaveText view for iOS 18+ (mark it @available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)) that makes each letter bob up and down in a travelling wave while keeping normal text layout. Implement a TextRenderer whose draw(layout:in:) walks every line, run and glyph, keeps a running glyph index, copies the GraphicsContext, translates it vertically by sin((index / wavelength − time × speed) × 2π) × amplitude, and draws the glyph. Set displayPadding to the amplitude above and below so nothing clips. Drive time from TimelineView(.animation) and apply the renderer with .textRenderer. Defaults: amplitude 5 pt, wavelength 8 letters, 1 wave per second. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline and use zero amplitude.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Letters bob up and down in a travelling wave, drawn with a `TextRenderer`
/// so the text keeps its normal layout, wrapping and accessibility.
@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)
public struct WaveText: View {
    private let text: Text
    private let amplitude: CGFloat
    private let wavelength: Double
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - text: The string to show.
    ///   - amplitude: How far letters move up and down, in points.
    ///   - wavelength: Number of letters in one full wave.
    ///   - speed: Waves per second.
    public init(_ text: String, amplitude: CGFloat = 5, wavelength: Double = 8, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.init(Text(text), amplitude: amplitude, wavelength: wavelength, speed: speed)
    }

    /// Wraps an existing `Text`, keeping its styling.
    public init(_ text: Text, amplitude: CGFloat = 5, wavelength: Double = 8, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.text = text
        self.amplitude = amplitude
        self.wavelength = wavelength
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            text.textRenderer(WaveRenderer(
                time: reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate,
                amplitude: reduceMotion ? 0 : amplitude,
                wavelength: wavelength,
                speed: speed
            ))
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)
struct WaveRenderer: TextRenderer {
    var time: Double
    var amplitude: CGFloat
    var wavelength: Double
    var speed: Double

    var displayPadding: EdgeInsets {
        EdgeInsets(top: amplitude, leading: 0, bottom: amplitude, trailing: 0)
    }

    func draw(layout: Text.Layout, in context: inout GraphicsContext) {
        var index = 0
        for line in layout {
            for run in line {
                for glyph in run {
                    let angle = (Double(index) / max(wavelength, 1) - time * speed) * 2 * .pi
                    var copy = context
                    copy.translateBy(x: 0, y: CGFloat(sin(angle)) * amplitude)
                    copy.draw(glyph)
                    index += 1
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    if #available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *) {
        WaveText("Making waves in SwiftUI")
            .font(.title.bold())
            .foregroundStyle(.blue)
            .padding()
    }
}
```

## Count Up (`count-up`)

A number counts up from zero, and from old to new value on change.

- API: `CountUpText(value: …)`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/CountUpText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/CountUpText.swift

### Usage

```swift
CountUpText(value: revenue, prefix: "$")
    .font(.largeTitle.bold())

CountUpText(value: 98.6, fractionDigits: 1, suffix: "%", duration: 2)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI CountUpText view (iOS 17+) with value, duration (1.4 s), fractionDigits (0), prefix and suffix. Keep a @State shown value starting at 0; on appear and whenever value changes, set shown = value inside withAnimation(.easeOut(duration:)). Render through a private view that conforms to both View and Animatable (animatableData = the number) so SwiftUI calls body on every frame with the interpolated value, and format it with value.formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(fractionDigits))) between prefix and suffix. Use .monospacedDigit() so the width doesn't jitter, and give it the final formatted value as its accessibility label. With Reduce Motion on, jump straight to the value.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A number that counts up from zero on appear, and counts from the old value
/// to the new one whenever `value` changes.
public struct CountUpText: View {
    private let value: Double
    private let duration: Double
    private let fractionDigits: Int
    private let prefix: String
    private let suffix: String

    @State private var shown: Double = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - value: The number to count to.
    ///   - duration: Length of the count, in seconds.
    ///   - fractionDigits: Digits after the decimal point.
    ///   - prefix: Text before the number, e.g. "$".
    ///   - suffix: Text after the number, e.g. "%".
    public init(
        value: Double,
        duration: Double = 1.4,
        fractionDigits: Int = 0,
        prefix: String = "",
        suffix: String = ""
    ) {
        self.value = value
        self.duration = duration
        self.fractionDigits = fractionDigits
        self.prefix = prefix
        self.suffix = suffix
    }

    public var body: some View {
        CountingLabel(value: shown, fractionDigits: fractionDigits, prefix: prefix, suffix: suffix)
            .monospacedDigit()
            .onAppear { count(to: value) }
            .onChange(of: value) { _, newValue in count(to: newValue) }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
            .accessibilityLabel(CountingLabel.format(value, fractionDigits: fractionDigits, prefix: prefix, suffix: suffix))
    }

    private func count(to target: Double) {
        // Reduce Motion: jump straight to the value.
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeOut(duration: duration)) {
            shown = target
        }
    }
}

/// Re-renders the formatted number for every animation frame.
private struct CountingLabel: View, Animatable {
    var value: Double
    let fractionDigits: Int
    let prefix: String
    let suffix: String

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { value }
        set { value = newValue }
    }

    var body: some View {
        Text(Self.format(value, fractionDigits: fractionDigits, prefix: prefix, suffix: suffix))
    }

    static func format(_ value: Double, fractionDigits: Int, prefix: String, suffix: String) -> String {
        prefix + value.formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(max(0, fractionDigits)))) + suffix
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 12) {
        CountUpText(value: 12_480)
            .font(.largeTitle.bold())
        CountUpText(value: 98.6, fractionDigits: 1, suffix: "%")
            .font(.title)
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Split Text (`split-text`)

Letters rise into place one after another with a small overshoot.

- API: `SplitText("…")`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 18+ · macOS 15+ · visionOS 2+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/SplitText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/SplitText.swift

### Usage

```swift
if #available(iOS 18, *) {
    SplitText("Letters take the stage")
        .font(.largeTitle.bold())
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI SplitText view for iOS 18+ (mark it @available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)) with duration per letter (0.5 s), stagger (0.035 s) and distance (18 pt). Apply a TextRenderer that is also Animatable, with a progress value 0…1 as animatableData. In draw(layout:in:), count all glyphs, then for glyph i compute start = spread × i / (count − 1), where spread is the share of the total time taken by the delays, and local = clamp((progress − start) / (1 − spread), 0, 1). Copy the GraphicsContext, set opacity to min(1, local × 2), translate it down by (1 − backOut(local)) × distance (backOut: ease-out with ~1.7 overshoot) and draw the glyph. Set displayPadding at the bottom to distance. In .task(id: string), reset progress to 0 without animation, then animate it to 1 with linear timing over duration + stagger × (count − 1). With Reduce Motion on, use zero distance (a fade).

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Letters rise into place one after another with a small overshoot, drawn
/// with a `TextRenderer` so the text keeps its normal layout and wrapping.
/// Plays on appear and again when the string changes.
@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)
public struct SplitText: View {
    private let string: String
    private let duration: Double
    private let stagger: Double
    private let distance: CGFloat

    @State private var progress: Double = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - string: The text to show.
    ///   - duration: How long each letter takes to land, in seconds.
    ///   - stagger: Delay between consecutive letters, in seconds.
    ///   - distance: How far below its place each letter starts, in points.
    public init(_ string: String, duration: Double = 0.5, stagger: Double = 0.035, distance: CGFloat = 18) {
        self.string = string
        self.duration = duration
        self.stagger = stagger
        self.distance = distance
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let glyphs = max(1, string.count)
        let total = duration + stagger * Double(glyphs - 1)
        Text(string)
            .textRenderer(SplitRenderer(
                progress: progress,
                spread: total > 0 ? stagger * Double(glyphs - 1) / total : 0,
                distance: reduceMotion ? 0 : distance
            ))
            .task(id: string) {
                var reset = Transaction()
                reset.disablesAnimations = true
                withTransaction(reset) { progress = 0 }
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(16))
                withAnimation(.linear(duration: reduceMotion ? 0.3 : total)) { progress = 1 }
            }
    }
}

@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)
struct SplitRenderer: TextRenderer, Animatable {
    /// 0 = nothing shown, 1 = every letter in place.
    var progress: Double
    /// Fraction of the timeline taken up by the delays between letters.
    var spread: Double
    var distance: CGFloat

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    var displayPadding: EdgeInsets {
        EdgeInsets(top: 0, leading: 0, bottom: distance, trailing: 0)
    }

    func draw(layout: Text.Layout, in context: inout GraphicsContext) {
        let count = layout.flatMap { $0 }.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.count }
        var index = 0
        for line in layout {
            for run in line {
                for glyph in run {
                    let start = count > 1 ? spread * Double(index) / Double(count - 1) : 0
                    let local = min(1, max(0, (progress - start) / max(0.0001, 1 - spread)))
                    var copy = context
                    copy.opacity = min(1, local * 2)
                    copy.translateBy(x: 0, y: (1 - Self.backOut(local)) * distance)
                    copy.draw(glyph)
                    index += 1
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Ease-out with a small overshoot.
    static func backOut(_ t: Double) -> Double {
        let c1 = 1.70158, c3 = c1 + 1
        return 1 + c3 * pow(t - 1, 3) + c1 * pow(t - 1, 2)
    }
}

#Preview {
    if #available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *) {
        SplitText("Letters take the stage")
            .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            .padding()
    }
}
```

## Rotating Text (`rotating-text`)

Words take turns: the current one slides up and out as the next rises in.

- API: `RotatingText([…])`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/RotatingText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/RotatingText.swift

### Usage

```swift
HStack {
    Text("We")
    RotatingText(["design", "build", "ship"])
        .foregroundStyle(.blue)
}
.font(.largeTitle.bold())
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI RotatingText view (iOS 17+) that cycles through an array of words every interval (2 s). Keep a @State index and show Text(words[index]).id(index) inside a ZStack with .fixedSize() and .clipped(). Give the text an asymmetric transition: insertion .move(edge: .bottom) combined with .opacity, removal .move(edge: .top) combined with .opacity. Drive it from .task with a loop of Task.sleep followed by withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.8)) { index += 1 }, so the width also springs to fit each word. Expose all words joined by commas as the accessibility label. With Reduce Motion on, use a plain opacity transition.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Cycles through a list of words: the current word slides up and out while
/// the next one rises in, and the width springs to fit.
public struct RotatingText: View {
    private let words: [String]
    private let interval: Double

    @State private var index = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - words: The words to cycle through.
    ///   - interval: Seconds each word stays on screen.
    public init(_ words: [String], interval: Double = 2) {
        self.words = words
        self.interval = interval
    }

    public var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            if !words.isEmpty {
                Text(words[index % words.count])
                    .id(index)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .asymmetric(
                        insertion: .move(edge: .bottom).combined(with: .opacity),
                        removal: .move(edge: .top).combined(with: .opacity)
                    ))
            }
        }
        .fixedSize()
        .clipped()
        .task {
            guard words.count > 1 else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(interval))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.8)) {
                    index = (index + 1) % words.count
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(words.joined(separator: ", "))
    }
}

#Preview {
    HStack(spacing: 6) {
        Text("We")
        RotatingText(["design", "build", "ship"])
            .foregroundStyle(.blue)
        Text("apps.")
    }
    .font(.title.bold())
    .padding()
}
```

## Glitch (`glitch`)

Every few seconds the view tears: an RGB split, sliced rows and jitter.

- API: `.glitch()`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/Glitch.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/Glitch.swift

### Usage

```swift
Text("SYSTEM FAILURE")
    .font(.title.monospaced().bold())
    .glitch()

Image("logo")
    .glitch(intensity: 2, interval: 4)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .glitch(isActive:intensity:interval:) view modifier (iOS 17+) that works on any view. Use TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1/24)) and derive everything from the clock: glitch during the first 0.35 s of every interval (2 s); within that window pick new pseudo-random values 24 times a second from a cheap integer hash of (frame, salt). While glitching: (1) behind the content, draw two silhouettes of it, content.brightness(1).colorMultiply(.cyan) offset left and content.brightness(1).colorMultiply(.red) offset right by 2–6 pt × intensity, at 85 % opacity; (2) in an overlay, draw a copy of the content offset sideways by up to ±12 pt, masked to a horizontal strip at a random height (10–35 % of the view tall); (3) jitter the whole view by up to ±1.5 pt. Outside the window, show the content untouched. With Reduce Motion on, don't glitch at all.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Digital glitch: every couple of seconds the view splits into red and cyan
/// copies, and horizontal slices jump sideways for a fraction of a second.
/// Works on any view (text, images, logos).
struct GlitchModifier: ViewModifier {
    var isActive: Bool
    var intensity: CGFloat
    var interval: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: no glitching at all.
        let running = isActive && !reduceMotion
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 24, paused: !running)) { timeline in
            let state = running
                ? GlitchState(time: timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate, interval: interval)
                : .calm
            content
                // Colour fringes: solid cyan and red silhouettes (brightness 1
                // turns any colour white first) to the left and right.
                .background {
                    ZStack {
                        content.brightness(1).colorMultiply(.cyan).offset(x: -state.split * intensity)
                        content.brightness(1).colorMultiply(.red).offset(x: state.split * intensity)
                    }
                    .opacity(state.split == 0 ? 0 : 0.85)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
                // A slice of the view displaced sideways.
                .overlay {
                    GeometryReader { geometry in
                        let height = geometry.size.height
                        content
                            .offset(x: state.sliceOffset * intensity)
                            .mask {
                                Rectangle()
                                    .frame(height: height * state.sliceHeight)
                                    .offset(y: height * (state.sliceY - 0.5))
                            }
                            .frame(width: geometry.size.width, height: height)
                    }
                    .opacity(state.sliceOffset == 0 ? 0 : 1)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
                .offset(x: state.jitter * intensity)
        }
    }
}

/// The glitch values for one moment, derived from the clock so the effect
/// needs no state.
private struct GlitchState {
    var split: CGFloat = 0
    var sliceOffset: CGFloat = 0
    var sliceY: CGFloat = 0.5
    var sliceHeight: CGFloat = 0.2
    var jitter: CGFloat = 0

    static let calm = GlitchState()

    init() {}

    init(time: Double, interval: Double) {
        let cycle = max(0.4, interval)
        let phase = time.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: cycle)
        // Glitch for the first 0.35 s of every cycle.
        guard phase < 0.35 else { return }
        // Change the random values 24 times a second.
        let step = Int(time * 24)
        split = 2 + 4 * Self.noise(step, 1)
        if Self.noise(step, 2) > 0.35 {
            sliceOffset = (Self.noise(step, 3) - 0.5) * 24
            sliceY = 0.15 + 0.7 * Self.noise(step, 4)
            sliceHeight = 0.1 + 0.25 * Self.noise(step, 5)
        }
        jitter = (Self.noise(step, 6) - 0.5) * 3
    }

    /// Cheap hash to 0..<1.
    static func noise(_ step: Int, _ salt: Int) -> CGFloat {
        var x = UInt64(bitPattern: Int64(step &* 7919 &+ salt &* 104_729))
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xc4ce_b9fe_1a85_ec53
        x ^= x >> 33
        return CGFloat(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Makes the view glitch every `interval` seconds: an RGB split, displaced
    /// slices and a little jitter.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text("SYSTEM FAILURE")
    ///     .font(.title.monospaced().bold())
    ///     .glitch()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isActive: Turns the effect on and off.
    ///   - intensity: Multiplies every offset (1 = default strength).
    ///   - interval: Seconds between glitch bursts.
    func glitch(isActive: Bool = true, intensity: CGFloat = 1, interval: Double = 2) -> some View {
        modifier(GlitchModifier(isActive: isActive, intensity: intensity, interval: interval))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Text("SYSTEM FAILURE")
        .font(.largeTitle.monospaced().bold())
        .glitch()
        .padding()
}
```

## Circular Text (`circular-text`)

Text wrapped around a circle that slowly turns, like a rotating badge.

- API: `CircularText("…")`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/CircularText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/CircularText.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    CircularText("SWIFTUI • MOTION • LIBRARY • ", radius: 60)
        .font(.caption.monospaced().bold())
    Image(systemName: "sparkles").font(.largeTitle)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI CircularText view (iOS 17+) with text, radius (60 pt) and speed (20° per second). Split the string into characters and place each one in a ZStack as Text(character).offset(y: −radius).rotationEffect(.degrees(index / count × 360)), so letters stand evenly spaced around the circle. Wrap the ZStack in TimelineView(.animation) and rotate it by time × speed degrees (modulo 360). Frame it to 2 × radius plus 12 pt padding. Use the full text as a single accessibility label. With Reduce Motion on (or speed 0), pause the timeline.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Text laid out around a circle that slowly turns, like a rotating badge or
/// stamp. Put an icon in the middle with a `ZStack`.
public struct CircularText: View {
    private let characters: [String]
    private let text: String
    private let radius: CGFloat
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - text: The text to wrap around the circle. Add a separator such as
    ///     " • " at the end so the start and end don't touch.
    ///   - radius: Radius of the circle the letters stand on, in points.
    ///   - speed: Rotation speed in degrees per second (negative turns
    ///     counter-clockwise, 0 stops it).
    public init(_ text: String, radius: CGFloat = 60, speed: Double = 20) {
        self.text = text
        self.characters = text.map(String.init)
        self.radius = radius
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion || speed == 0)) { timeline in
            let angle = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            ZStack {
                ForEach(characters.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                    Text(characters[index])
                        .offset(y: -radius)
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(Double(index) / Double(max(1, characters.count)) * 360))
                }
            }
            .rotationEffect(.degrees(angle.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 360)))
        }
        .frame(width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
        .padding(12)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(text)
    }
}

#Preview {
    ZStack {
        CircularText("SWIFTUI • MOTION • LIBRARY • ")
            .font(.system(size: 13, weight: .bold, design: .monospaced))
        Image(systemName: "sparkles")
            .font(.largeTitle)
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Focus Text (`focus-text`)

Focus hops from word to word: sharp and bracketed, the rest blurred.

- API: `FocusText("…")`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/FocusText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/FocusText.swift

### Usage

```swift
FocusText("Motion made simple")
    .font(.title.bold())

FocusText("Plan Build Ship", interval: 0.8, bracketColor: .pink)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI FocusText view (iOS 17+) that splits a sentence into words in an HStack (10 pt spacing). A @State focus index advances every interval (1.2 s) in a .task loop with withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.8)). Unfocused words get blur radius 3 and opacity 0.55; the focused word is sharp. Behind the focused word only, draw four L-shaped corner brackets (Canvas, 2.5 pt round strokes, arms 8 pt, 2 pt outside the word's padded frame) and give them .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "focus", in: namespace) so the brackets glide and resize from word to word. Use the sentence as the accessibility label. With Reduce Motion on, use a short ease instead of the spring.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Focus moves from word to word: the current word is sharp and framed by
/// corner brackets that glide to it, while the others are blurred.
public struct FocusText: View {
    private let words: [String]
    private let text: String
    private let interval: Double
    private let blur: CGFloat
    private let bracketColor: Color

    @State private var focus = 0
    @Namespace private var namespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - text: The sentence; it is split into words at spaces.
    ///   - interval: Seconds the focus stays on each word.
    ///   - blur: Blur radius of the unfocused words.
    ///   - bracketColor: Colour of the corner brackets.
    public init(_ text: String, interval: Double = 1.2, blur: CGFloat = 3, bracketColor: Color = .accentColor) {
        self.text = text
        self.words = text.split(separator: " ").map(String.init)
        self.interval = interval
        self.blur = blur
        self.bracketColor = bracketColor
    }

    public var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 10) {
            ForEach(words.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                let focused = index == focus
                Text(words[index])
                    .padding(.horizontal, 6)
                    .padding(.vertical, 2)
                    .blur(radius: focused ? 0 : blur)
                    .opacity(focused ? 1 : 0.55)
                    .background {
                        if focused {
                            FocusBrackets(color: bracketColor)
                                .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "focus", in: namespace)
                        }
                    }
            }
        }
        .task {
            guard words.count > 1 else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(interval))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.8)) {
                    focus = (focus + 1) % words.count
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(text)
    }
}

/// Four L-shaped corners.
private struct FocusBrackets: View {
    let color: Color

    var body: some View {
        Canvas { context, size in
            let arm: CGFloat = min(8, size.width / 3, size.height / 3)
            var path = Path()
            for (x, y, dx, dy) in [(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0), (size.width, 0, -1, 1), (0, size.height, 1, -1), (size.width, size.height, -1, -1)] {
                path.move(to: CGPoint(x: x + dx * arm, y: y))
                path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: y))
                path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: y + dy * arm))
            }
            context.stroke(path, with: .color(color), style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 2.5, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
        }
        .padding(-2)
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
    }
}

#Preview {
    FocusText("Motion made simple")
        .font(.title.bold())
        .padding()
}
```

## Highlighter (`highlighter`)

A marker pen swipes across the text, or underlines it, left to right.

- API: `.highlighter()`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/Highlighter.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/Highlighter.swift

### Usage

```swift
Text("the important part")
    .highlighter()

Text("Pricing")
    .highlighter(isActive: isSelected, color: .pink, style: .underline)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .highlighter(isActive:color:style:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+) with two styles. In a background GeometryReader, draw a rounded rectangle 6 pt wider than the text: for .marker, 55 % of the text height, yellow at 45 % opacity, rotated −1.2° and sitting over the lower half; for .underline, a full-opacity capsule about 10 % of the height (at least 3 pt) at the baseline. Scale it horizontally from 0 to 1 with anchor .leading, animated with easeOut(0.6 s) on appear and whenever isActive changes, so it swipes on from the left and back off. Disable hit testing and hide it from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, switch it without animation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The look of a `.highlighter()` stroke.
public enum HighlighterStyle: Sendable {
    /// A translucent marker band behind the lower part of the text.
    case marker
    /// A thick line under the text.
    case underline
}

/// A highlighter pen swipes across the text from left to right, and back off
/// again when deactivated.
struct HighlighterModifier: ViewModifier {
    var isActive: Bool
    var color: Color
    var style: HighlighterStyle
    var duration: Double

    @State private var drawn = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .background(alignment: .bottomLeading) {
                GeometryReader { geometry in
                    let size = geometry.size
                    let band: CGFloat = style == .marker ? size.height * 0.55 : max(3, size.height * 0.1)
                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: style == .marker ? 3 : band / 2)
                        .fill(color.opacity(style == .marker ? 0.45 : 1))
                        .frame(width: size.width + 6, height: band)
                        // Slightly tilted, like a hand-drawn stroke.
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(style == .marker ? -1.2 : 0))
                        .scaleEffect(x: drawn ? 1 : 0, anchor: .leading)
                        .offset(x: -3, y: size.height - band * (style == .marker ? 0.9 : 0.6))
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .onAppear { update(isActive) }
            .onChange(of: isActive) { _, newValue in update(newValue) }
    }

    private func update(_ active: Bool) {
        // Reduce Motion: fade in place of the swipe.
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeOut(duration: duration)) {
            drawn = active
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Draws a highlighter stroke across the view while `isActive` is true.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text("the important part")
    ///     .highlighter()
    ///
    /// Text("Pricing")
    ///     .highlighter(isActive: isSelected, color: .pink, style: .underline)
    /// ```
    func highlighter(
        isActive: Bool = true,
        color: Color = .yellow,
        style: HighlighterStyle = .marker,
        duration: Double = 0.6
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(HighlighterModifier(isActive: isActive, color: color, style: style, duration: duration))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 20) {
        Text("Read the important part")
            .font(.title2.bold())
            .highlighter()
        Text("Underlined")
            .font(.title2.bold())
            .highlighter(color: .pink, style: .underline)
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Morphing Text (`morphing-text`)

Words melt into each other with a gooey, liquid morph.

- API: `MorphingText([…])`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/MorphingText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/MorphingText.swift

### Usage

```swift
MorphingText(["Design", "Build", "Ship"])
    .font(.system(size: 44, weight: .black, design: .rounded))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI MorphingText(_ words:interval:morphDuration:color:) view (iOS 17+) that cycles through words with a gooey morph. Size it with hidden copies of every word in a ZStack and draw in an overlay Canvas padded out by 12 pt. In TimelineView(.animation), word index = Int(time / interval) % count; the morph runs over the last morphDuration (0.9 s) of each interval (2.2 s) with smoothstep progress p. In the Canvas, add .alphaThreshold(min: 0.3, color: color) then .blur(radius: 1.5), and inside drawLayer draw the outgoing word (resolved symbol, tagged by index) with its own .blur(radius: 6 × p) and opacity min(1, 2(1 − p)), and the incoming word with blur 6 × (1 − p) and opacity min(1, 2p), both centred; keeping both opaque through the middle stops the blob thinning out below the threshold. The threshold turns the overlapping blurry glyphs into one liquid shape. With Reduce Motion on, cross-fade plain Text views on a TimelineView(.periodic). Set the accessibility label to the words.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Cycles through words with a gooey morph: the outgoing word melts into the
/// incoming one. Both are blurred inside a `Canvas` and cut back to sharp
/// edges with an alpha threshold, so overlapping strokes fuse like liquid.
public struct MorphingText: View {
    private let words: [String]
    private let interval: Double
    private let morphDuration: Double
    private let color: Color

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - words: The words to cycle through, in order.
    ///   - interval: Seconds each word stays, including the morph.
    ///   - morphDuration: Seconds the morph takes.
    ///   - color: Fill colour. The alpha threshold needs a solid colour.
    public init(_ words: [String], interval: Double = 2.2, morphDuration: Double = 0.9, color: Color = .primary) {
        self.words = words.isEmpty ? [""] : words
        self.interval = max(interval, morphDuration + 0.1)
        self.morphDuration = morphDuration
        self.color = color
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Hidden copies of every word size the view to the widest one.
        ZStack {
            ForEach(words.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                Text(words[index]).hidden()
            }
        }
        .overlay {
            if reduceMotion {
                // Reduce Motion: a plain cross-fade.
                TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: interval)) { timeline in
                    let index = wordIndex(at: timeline.date)
                    Text(words[index])
                        .foregroundStyle(color)
                        .id(index)
                        .transition(.opacity)
                        .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.4), value: index)
                }
            } else {
                TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
                    morph(at: timeline.date)
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(words.joined(separator: ", "))
    }

    private func wordIndex(at date: Date) -> Int {
        Int(date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate / interval) % words.count
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private func morph(at date: Date) -> some View {
        let time = date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
        let current = wordIndex(at: date)
        let next = (current + 1) % words.count
        let local = time.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: interval)
        // 0 while the word rests, then 0 → 1 over the last `morphDuration`.
        let raw = (local - (interval - morphDuration)) / morphDuration
        let progress = min(1, max(0, raw))
        let eased = progress * progress * (3 - 2 * progress)

        if progress <= 0 {
            // At rest: crisp, plain text.
            Text(words[current]).foregroundStyle(color)
        } else {
            morphCanvas(current: current, next: next, eased: eased)
        }
    }

    private func morphCanvas(current: Int, next: Int, eased: Double) -> some View {
        Canvas { context, size in
            context.addFilter(.alphaThreshold(min: 0.3, color: color))
            context.addFilter(.blur(radius: 1.5))
            context.drawLayer { layer in
                let centre = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                // Each word is blurred more the further it is from fully shown,
                // so mid-morph they overlap as soft blobs that the threshold fuses.
                // Both stay fully opaque through the middle so the blob never
                // thins out below the threshold and vanishes.
                if eased < 1, let outgoing = layer.resolveSymbol(id: current) {
                    var copy = layer
                    copy.addFilter(.blur(radius: 6 * eased))
                    copy.opacity = min(1, (1 - eased) * 2)
                    copy.draw(outgoing, at: centre)
                }
                if eased > 0, let incoming = layer.resolveSymbol(id: next) {
                    var copy = layer
                    copy.addFilter(.blur(radius: 6 * (1 - eased)))
                    copy.opacity = min(1, eased * 2)
                    copy.draw(incoming, at: centre)
                }
            }
        } symbols: {
            ForEach(words.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                Text(words[index]).tag(index)
            }
        }
        .padding(-12)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

#Preview {
    MorphingText(["Design", "Build", "Ship"])
        .font(.system(size: 44, weight: .black, design: .rounded))
        .padding()
}
```

## Neon Flicker (`neon`)

A glowing neon tube that stutters on and glitches now and then.

- API: `.neon(color:flicker:)`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/NeonFlicker.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/NeonFlicker.swift

### Usage

```swift
Text("OPEN")
    .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
    .neon(color: .pink)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .neon(color:flicker:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for text or symbols on a dark background. Draw the content white when lit (or the colour at 55 % opacity when it drops out) and stack three shadows in the colour: radius 2 (opacity = level), 8 (0.9 × level) and 18 (0.7 × level), with overall opacity 0.35 + 0.65 × level. With flicker on, drive level from TimelineView(.animation) over a 6 s cycle: a stuttering switch-on with dips to 0.1 (0–0.08 s), 0.2 (0.14–0.18 s), 0.15 (0.26–0.30 s) and 0.5 (0.38–0.40 s), a glitch at 4.20–4.45 s (0.3, 0.15, 0.6), otherwise a faint hum of 0.94 + 0.06 × sin(time × 40). With Reduce Motion on, keep a steady glow with no flicker.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A neon tube: a white-hot core with layered coloured glow. With `flicker`
/// on, it stutters on like a tube warming up, then glitches now and again.
struct NeonModifier: ViewModifier {
    var color: Color
    var flicker: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: a steady glow (flashing can also be uncomfortable).
        if flicker && !reduceMotion {
            TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
                let level = Self.brightness(at: timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate)
                glow(content, level: level)
            }
        } else {
            glow(content, level: 1)
        }
    }

    private func glow(_ content: Content, level: Double) -> some View {
        content
            // A white-hot core when lit; the bare coloured glass when it drops out.
            .foregroundStyle(level > 0.55 ? Color.white : color.opacity(0.55))
            .shadow(color: color.opacity(level), radius: 2)
            .shadow(color: color.opacity(0.9 * level), radius: 8)
            .shadow(color: color.opacity(0.7 * level), radius: 18)
            .opacity(0.35 + 0.65 * level)
    }

    /// 1 = fully lit, lower = dimmed. A 6 s cycle: a stuttering switch-on,
    /// a steady stretch, then a short double glitch.
    static func brightness(at time: Double) -> Double {
        let t = time.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 6)
        let dips: [(start: Double, end: Double, level: Double)] = [
            (0.00, 0.08, 0.1), (0.14, 0.18, 0.2), (0.26, 0.30, 0.15), (0.38, 0.40, 0.5),
            (4.20, 4.24, 0.3), (4.30, 4.36, 0.15), (4.42, 4.45, 0.6),
        ]
        for dip in dips where t >= dip.start && t < dip.end {
            return dip.level
        }
        // A barely visible hum keeps the steady part alive.
        return 0.94 + 0.06 * sin(time * 40)
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Turns text or symbols into a glowing neon sign.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text("OPEN")
    ///     .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
    ///     .neon(color: .pink)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - color: The colour of the glow.
    ///   - flicker: Stutter on and glitch now and again, like a real tube.
    func neon(color: Color = .pink, flicker: Bool = true) -> some View {
        modifier(NeonModifier(color: color, flicker: flicker))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 24) {
        Text("OPEN").font(.system(size: 52, weight: .bold, design: .rounded)).neon()
        Image(systemName: "bolt.fill").font(.system(size: 40)).neon(color: .cyan, flicker: false)
    }
    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
    .background(Color(white: 0.08))
}
```

## Karaoke Text (`karaoke-text`)

A line fills with colour left to right as progress goes from 0 to 1.

- API: `KaraokeText(_:progress:)`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Value change / Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/KaraokeText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/KaraokeText.swift

### Usage

```swift
KaraokeText("Never gonna stop the music", progress: playback, highlight: .pink)
    .font(.title2.bold())
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI KaraokeText(_:progress:highlight:base:feather:) view (iOS 17+): a single-line Text in the base colour (secondary at 50 %) with an overlay of the same Text in the highlight colour, masked (alignment .leading) by an HStack in a GeometryReader: a Rectangle of width max(0, (width + feather) × progress − feather) followed by a LinearGradient black → clear of width feather (14 pt), so progress 0 shows nothing, 1 shows everything and the leading edge is soft. progress is clamped to 0…1 and changes to it animate because the frame width animates. Hide the overlay from accessibility.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A line of text that fills with colour from left to right as `progress`
/// goes from 0 to 1, with a soft leading edge, like karaoke lyrics or a
/// reading progress highlight. Drive `progress` from playback time, a scroll
/// position or an animation.
public struct KaraokeText: View {
    private let string: String
    private let progress: Double
    private let highlight: Color
    private let base: Color
    private let feather: CGFloat

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - string: The text. It's laid out on one line.
    ///   - progress: 0 = nothing filled, 1 = all filled. Animatable.
    ///   - highlight: The fill colour.
    ///   - base: The colour of the unfilled text.
    ///   - feather: Width of the soft edge, in points.
    public init(_ string: String, progress: Double, highlight: Color = .accentColor, base: Color = .secondary.opacity(0.5), feather: CGFloat = 14) {
        self.string = string
        self.progress = progress
        self.highlight = highlight
        self.base = base
        self.feather = feather
    }

    public var body: some View {
        Text(string)
            .lineLimit(1)
            .foregroundStyle(base)
            .overlay {
                Text(string)
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .foregroundStyle(highlight)
                    .mask(alignment: .leading) {
                        GeometryReader { geometry in
                            let p = min(1, max(0, progress))
                            // The solid part grows from -feather so 0 shows nothing
                            // and 1 shows everything, edge included.
                            HStack(spacing: 0) {
                                Rectangle()
                                    .frame(width: max(0, (geometry.size.width + feather) * p - feather))
                                LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .clear], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
                                    .frame(width: feather)
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var progress = 0.0
        var body: some View {
            KaraokeText("Never gonna stop the music", progress: progress, highlight: .pink)
                .font(.title2.bold())
                .onAppear {
                    withAnimation(.linear(duration: 3).repeatForever(autoreverses: false)) { progress = 1 }
                }
                .padding()
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Weight Wave (`weight-wave`)

Letters swell from thin to black and back in a travelling wave.

- API: `WeightWaveText(_:)`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/WeightWaveText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/WeightWaveText.swift

### Usage

```swift
WeightWaveText("Variable weight")
    .font(.system(size: 36, design: .rounded))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI WeightWaveText(_:speed:wavelength:) view (iOS 17+) that lays the characters out in an HStack(spacing: 0) inside TimelineView(.animation). Each character gets .fontWeight from the nine weights ultraLight…black, indexed by level = (sin(2π × (index / wavelength − time × speed)) + 1) / 2 (wavelength 8 letters, speed 0.6 waves/s), so a swell of bold travels through the word. The font comes from the environment. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline and use .regular. Combine into one accessibility element labelled with the string.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Letters swell from thin to black and back in a travelling wave, like a
/// variable font being played. Uses the font from the environment.
public struct WeightWaveText: View {
    private let string: String
    private let speed: Double
    private let wavelength: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private static let weights: [Font.Weight] = [
        .ultraLight, .thin, .light, .regular, .medium, .semibold, .bold, .heavy, .black,
    ]

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - string: The text to show.
    ///   - speed: Waves per second.
    ///   - wavelength: Letters per wave.
    public init(_ string: String, speed: Double = 0.6, wavelength: Double = 8) {
        self.string = string
        self.speed = speed
        self.wavelength = max(1, wavelength)
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let characters = Array(string)
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            HStack(spacing: 0) {
                ForEach(characters.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                    Text(String(characters[index]))
                        .fontWeight(reduceMotion ? .regular : weight(index: index, time: time))
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(string)
    }

    private func weight(index: Int, time: Double) -> Font.Weight {
        let phase = (Double(index) / wavelength - time * speed) * 2 * .pi
        let level = (sin(phase) + 1) / 2
        let weights = Self.weights
        return weights[min(weights.count - 1, Int(level * Double(weights.count)))]
    }
}

#Preview {
    WeightWaveText("Variable weight")
        .font(.system(size: 36, design: .rounded))
        .padding()
}
```
