## Exploding Text (`exploding-text`)

Letters blast apart spinning and spring back into place.

- API: `ExplodingText(_:isExploded:)`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Value change / Tap
- Requires: iOS 18+ · macOS 15+ · visionOS 2+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/ExplodingText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/ExplodingText.swift

### Usage

```swift
ExplodingText("Kaboom!", isExploded: exploded)
    .font(.system(size: 44, weight: .heavy, design: .rounded))
    .onTapGesture { exploded.toggle() }
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ExplodingText(_:isExploded:distance:) view (iOS 18+) using a TextRenderer that is Animatable over progress (0 = assembled, 1 = scattered). Its displayPadding is distance on every side (60 pt). In draw(layout:in:), for each glyph (counted across lines and runs) take three stable pseudo-random values r0, r1, r2 from a hash of its index; translate by (cos, sin)(r0 × 2π) × distance × (0.5 + 0.5 × r1) × progress, rotate around the glyph's typographic-bounds centre by (r2 − 0.5) × 540° × progress, and set opacity 1 − 0.7 × progress. Animate with .easeOut(0.45 s) when exploding and .spring(duration: 0.8, bounce: 0.35) when reassembling. With Reduce Motion on, use distance 0 (just a fade) and a 0.3 s ease. Keep the string as the accessibility label.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Letters blast apart in random directions, spinning, and spring back into
/// place, drawn with a `TextRenderer` so the text keeps its normal layout.
@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)
public struct ExplodingText: View {
    private let string: String
    private let isExploded: Bool
    private let distance: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - string: The text to show.
    ///   - isExploded: `true` scatters the letters, `false` reassembles them.
    ///   - distance: How far letters fly, in points.
    public init(_ string: String, isExploded: Bool, distance: CGFloat = 60) {
        self.string = string
        self.isExploded = isExploded
        self.distance = distance
    }

    public var body: some View {
        Text(string)
            .textRenderer(ExplodeRenderer(
                progress: isExploded ? 1 : 0,
                distance: reduceMotion ? 0 : distance
            ))
            // Out fast, back on a bouncy spring. Reduce Motion: a fade only.
            .animation(
                reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.3)
                    : isExploded ? .easeOut(duration: 0.45) : .spring(duration: 0.8, bounce: 0.35),
                value: isExploded
            )
            .accessibilityLabel(string)
    }
}

@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)
struct ExplodeRenderer: TextRenderer, Animatable {
    /// 0 = assembled, 1 = fully scattered.
    var progress: Double
    var distance: CGFloat

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    var displayPadding: EdgeInsets {
        EdgeInsets(top: distance, leading: distance, bottom: distance, trailing: distance)
    }

    func draw(layout: Text.Layout, in context: inout GraphicsContext) {
        var index = 0
        for line in layout {
            for run in line {
                for glyph in run {
                    let random = Self.random(index)
                    let angle = random.0 * 2 * .pi
                    let reach = distance * (0.5 + 0.5 * random.1)
                    let bounds = glyph.typographicBounds.rect
                    var copy = context
                    copy.opacity = 1 - 0.7 * min(1, max(0, progress))
                    copy.translateBy(x: cos(angle) * reach * progress, y: sin(angle) * reach * progress)
                    // Spin around the glyph's own centre.
                    copy.translateBy(x: bounds.midX, y: bounds.midY)
                    copy.rotate(by: .degrees((random.2 - 0.5) * 540 * progress))
                    copy.translateBy(x: -bounds.midX, y: -bounds.midY)
                    copy.draw(glyph)
                    index += 1
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Three stable pseudo-random values in 0..<1 for a glyph index.
    static func random(_ index: Int) -> (Double, Double, Double) {
        func hash(_ n: Int) -> Double {
            var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: n &* 2_654_435_761)
            x = (x ^ (x >> 31)) &* 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15
            x ^= x >> 29
            return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
        }
        return (hash(index * 3 + 1), hash(index * 3 + 2), hash(index * 3 + 3))
    }
}

@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)
private struct ExplodingTextPreview: View {
    @State private var exploded = false

    var body: some View {
        ExplodingText("Kaboom!", isExploded: exploded)
            .font(.system(size: 44, weight: .heavy, design: .rounded))
            .onTapGesture { exploded.toggle() }
            .padding(60)
    }
}

#Preview {
    if #available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *) {
        ExplodingTextPreview()
    }
}
```

---

## Liquid Fill Text (`liquid-fill-text`)

A wavy water line rises inside the letters as progress grows.

- API: `LiquidFillText(_:progress:)`
- Component: Text
- Trigger: Value change / Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/LiquidFillText.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/LiquidFillText.swift

### Usage

```swift
LiquidFillText("\(Int(level * 100))%", progress: level, color: .cyan)
    .font(.system(size: 64, weight: .black, design: .rounded))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI LiquidFillText(_:progress:color:waveHeight:) view (iOS 17+). Draw the Text in the colour at 15 % opacity as an empty glass, then overlay a TimelineView(.animation) with a ZStack of two wave shapes, masked by the same Text: a back wave in the colour at 45 % (phase = time × 2.2 + 1.3, amplitude 0.8 × waveHeight) and a front wave in the full colour (phase = time × 3, amplitude waveHeight, default 6 pt). The wave Shape has level, phase and amplitude, animates level, and fills everything below y = baseline + amplitude × sin(x / width × 3π + phase). A line of text has descender room below the glyphs and space above the caps, so fill between bottom = maxY − 0.2 × height + 2 × amplitude and top = minY + 0.12 × height − 2 × amplitude: baseline = bottom − (bottom − top) × level, so 0 is empty and 1 full. Clamp progress to 0…1 and animate level changes with .spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.25). With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline (the level still animates). Hide the overlay from accessibility; the label is the text.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Text that fills with liquid: a wavy water line rises inside the glyphs as
/// `progress` goes from 0 to 1, with a second, lighter wave behind it.
///
/// ```swift
/// LiquidFillText("72%", progress: 0.72, color: .cyan)
///     .font(.system(size: 64, weight: .black, design: .rounded))
/// ```
public struct LiquidFillText: View {
    private let text: String
    private let progress: Double
    private let color: Color
    private let waveHeight: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - text: The string to fill.
    ///   - progress: Fill level, 0 (empty) to 1 (full). Changes animate.
    ///   - color: Colour of the liquid.
    ///   - waveHeight: Height of the waves, in points.
    public init(_ text: String, progress: Double, color: Color = .blue, waveHeight: CGFloat = 6) {
        self.text = text
        self.progress = min(1, max(0, progress))
        self.color = color
        self.waveHeight = waveHeight
    }

    public var body: some View {
        Text(text)
            .foregroundStyle(color.opacity(0.15))
            .overlay {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
                    let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
                    ZStack {
                        LiquidWave(level: progress, phase: time * 2.2 + 1.3, amplitude: waveHeight * 0.8)
                            .fill(color.opacity(0.45))
                        LiquidWave(level: progress, phase: time * 3, amplitude: waveHeight)
                            .fill(color)
                    }
                    .animation(.spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.25), value: progress)
                }
                .mask { Text(text) }
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .accessibilityLabel(text)
    }
}

/// A sine-wave water line at `level` (0 = bottom, 1 = top), filled below.
struct LiquidWave: Shape {
    var level: Double
    var phase: Double
    var amplitude: CGFloat

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { level }
        set { level = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        // A line of text has room for descenders below the glyphs and accents
        // above them; fill between roughly the baseline and the cap height,
        // going a wave's height past both so 0 is empty and 1 full.
        let bottom = rect.maxY - rect.height * 0.2 + amplitude * 2
        let top = rect.minY + rect.height * 0.12 - amplitude * 2
        let baseline = bottom - (bottom - top) * level
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.maxY))
        let steps = max(8, Int(rect.width / 4))
        for step in 0...steps {
            let x = rect.minX + rect.width * CGFloat(step) / CGFloat(steps)
            let angle = Double(x / max(rect.width, 1)) * 2 * .pi * 1.5 + phase
            path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: baseline + amplitude * sin(angle)))
        }
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.maxY))
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var progress = 0.3
        var body: some View {
            LiquidFillText("72%", progress: progress, color: .cyan)
                .font(.system(size: 80, weight: .black, design: .rounded))
                .onTapGesture { progress = progress > 0.8 ? 0.1 : progress + 0.3 }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Pressable (`pressable`)

Button squashes and darkens on press, then springs back with a light haptic.

- API: `.buttonStyle(.pressable)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Press
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/PressableButtonStyle.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/PressableButtonStyle.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/Haptics.swift

### Usage

```swift
Button("Continue") { }
    .buttonStyle(.pressable)

Button("Big squish") { }
    .buttonStyle(.pressable(scale: 0.85))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ButtonStyle called PressableButtonStyle (iOS 17+). While pressed, the label scales to 0.94 and its brightness drops slightly (-0.06); on release it springs back using .spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.6). Fire a light impact haptic with .sensoryFeedback only when the press begins. Expose it as .buttonStyle(.pressable) and .buttonStyle(.pressable(scale:haptics:)) via a static extension on ButtonStyle.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A button style that squashes slightly and darkens while pressed, then
/// springs back. Adds a light haptic on press (iOS).
///
/// ```swift
/// Button("Continue") { }
///     .buttonStyle(.pressable)
///
/// Button("Big squish") { }
///     .buttonStyle(.pressable(scale: 0.85))
/// ```
public struct PressableButtonStyle: ButtonStyle {
    public var scale: CGFloat
    public var haptics: Bool

    public init(scale: CGFloat = 0.94, haptics: Bool = true) {
        self.scale = scale
        self.haptics = haptics
    }

    public func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
        configuration.label
            .scaleEffect(configuration.isPressed ? scale : 1)
            .brightness(configuration.isPressed ? -0.06 : 0)
            .animation(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.6), value: configuration.isPressed)
            .haptic(.lightImpact, trigger: configuration.isPressed) { _, isPressed in
                haptics && isPressed
            }
    }
}

public extension ButtonStyle where Self == PressableButtonStyle {
    static var pressable: PressableButtonStyle { PressableButtonStyle() }

    static func pressable(scale: CGFloat = 0.94, haptics: Bool = true) -> PressableButtonStyle {
        PressableButtonStyle(scale: scale, haptics: haptics)
    }
}

#Preview {
    Button {
    } label: {
        Text("Press me")
            .font(.headline)
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(.horizontal, 28)
            .padding(.vertical, 14)
            .background(Capsule().fill(Color.accentColor))
    }
    .buttonStyle(.pressable)
    .padding()
}

// MARK: - Haptics.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

import SwiftUI

/// The haptics the package plays. `SensoryFeedback` and `sensoryFeedback`
/// need visionOS 26, but the package supports visionOS 1, so call sites use
/// this enum and `.haptic(…)`, which does nothing on visionOS (it has no
/// haptics anyway).
enum Haptic: Equatable {
    case success
    case error
    case lightImpact

    #if !os(visionOS)
    var feedback: SensoryFeedback {
        switch self {
        case .success: .success
        case .error: .error
        case .lightImpact: .impact(weight: .light)
        }
    }
    #endif
}

extension View {
    /// Plays `haptic` every time `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays `haptic` when `trigger` changes and `condition` returns true.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (T, T) -> Bool) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger, condition: condition)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays the haptic returned by `haptic` (if any) when `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(trigger: T, _ haptic: @escaping (T, T) -> Haptic?) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(trigger: trigger) { old, new in haptic(old, new)?.feedback }
        #endif
    }
}
```

## Tap Ripple (`ripple`)

A circular ripple expands from the exact tap location.

- API: `.ripple()`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Ripple.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Ripple.swift

### Usage

```swift
Text("Tap")
    .frame(width: 200, height: 60)
    .background(.indigo, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12))
    .ripple(color: .white, cornerRadius: 12)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .ripple() view modifier (iOS 17+) that shows a Material-style ripple. Use a simultaneous SpatialTapGesture so it doesn't block the view's own button action. Each tap appends a ripple at the tap location; each ripple is a translucent circle (white, 35% opacity) sized to 2× the view's diagonal that scales from ~0 to 1 while fading to 0 with easeOut over 0.7 s, then is removed. Ripples are drawn in an overlay clipped to a rounded rectangle with a configurable corner radius and never intercept touches. Multiple quick taps should produce overlapping ripples.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Material-style ripple that expands from the exact point the user tapped.
struct RippleModifier: ViewModifier {
    var color: Color
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat
    var duration: Double

    @State private var ripples: [Ripple] = []

    private struct Ripple: Identifiable {
        let id = UUID()
        let location: CGPoint
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                GeometryReader { geometry in
                    let size = geometry.size
                    // Large enough to cover the view from any tap point.
                    let diameter = 2 * hypot(size.width, size.height)
                    ZStack {
                        ForEach(ripples) { ripple in
                            RippleCircle(color: color, diameter: diameter, duration: duration)
                                .position(ripple.location)
                        }
                    }
                    .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)
                }
                .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                SpatialTapGesture().onEnded { value in
                    let ripple = Ripple(location: value.location)
                    ripples.append(ripple)
                    DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + duration + 0.1) {
                        ripples.removeAll { $0.id == ripple.id }
                    }
                }
            )
    }
}

private struct RippleCircle: View {
    let color: Color
    let diameter: CGFloat
    let duration: Double

    @State private var expanded = false

    var body: some View {
        Circle()
            .fill(color)
            .frame(width: diameter, height: diameter)
            .scaleEffect(expanded ? 1 : 0.01)
            .opacity(expanded ? 0 : 0.35)
            .onAppear {
                withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: duration)) {
                    expanded = true
                }
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Adds a ripple that starts at the tap location.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Tap") { }
    ///     .padding()
    ///     .background(.blue, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12))
    ///     .ripple(cornerRadius: 12)
    /// ```
    func ripple(
        color: Color = .white,
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 12,
        duration: Double = 0.7
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(RippleModifier(color: color, cornerRadius: cornerRadius, duration: duration))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Text("Tap anywhere")
        .font(.headline)
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .frame(width: 240, height: 80)
        .background(Color.indigo, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16, style: .continuous))
        .ripple(cornerRadius: 16)
        .padding()
}
```

## Error Shake (`shake`)

Horizontal "no" shake for wrong input, triggered by a value change.

- API: `.shake(trigger:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Shake.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Shake.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var attempts = 0

SecureField("Password", text: $password)
    .shake(trigger: attempts)
    .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: attempts)

// On a failed login:
attempts += 1
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .shake(trigger:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for error feedback. Every time the Equatable trigger changes, the view shakes horizontally using keyframeAnimator on an x offset: -10, +10, -7, +7, -3 points (≈0.07 s each, cubic keyframes) and then settles back to 0 with a bouncy SpringKeyframe. Amplitude should be configurable. Pair it with .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger:) for haptics.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Horizontal "no" shake, e.g. for a wrong password. Plays every time
/// `trigger` changes.
struct ShakeModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var amplitude: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: no shake (pair it with a colour or message change).
        let scale: CGFloat = reduceMotion ? 0 : 1
        return content.keyframeAnimator(initialValue: CGFloat(0), trigger: trigger) { view, offset in
            view.offset(x: offset * scale)
        } keyframes: { _ in
            KeyframeTrack {
                CubicKeyframe(-amplitude, duration: 0.07)
                CubicKeyframe(amplitude, duration: 0.07)
                CubicKeyframe(-amplitude * 0.7, duration: 0.07)
                CubicKeyframe(amplitude * 0.7, duration: 0.07)
                CubicKeyframe(-amplitude * 0.3, duration: 0.06)
                SpringKeyframe(0, duration: 0.2, spring: .bouncy)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shakes the view horizontally whenever `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// @State private var attempts = 0
    ///
    /// SecureField("Password", text: $password)
    ///     .shake(trigger: attempts)
    /// // on failure: attempts += 1
    /// ```
    func shake<Trigger: Equatable>(trigger: Trigger, amplitude: CGFloat = 10) -> some View {
        modifier(ShakeModifier(trigger: trigger, amplitude: amplitude))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var attempts = 0
        var body: some View {
            Button("Wrong password") { attempts += 1 }
                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                .tint(.red)
                .shake(trigger: attempts)
                .haptic(.error, trigger: attempts)
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Magnetic Button (`magnetic`)

The button drifts toward a nearby pointer or dragging finger, then springs home.

- API: `.magnetic()`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Hover / Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Magnetic.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Magnetic.swift

### Usage

```swift
Button("Get started") { }
    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    .magnetic()

Image(systemName: "plus.circle.fill")
    .font(.system(size: 44))
    .magnetic(strength: 0.5, radius: 40)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .magnetic(strength:radius:) view modifier (iOS 17+) that pulls a view toward the pointer. Pad the view by `radius` (60 pt) to enlarge its tracking area, give it a rectangular contentShape, measure the padded size with a GeometryReader background, then remove the padding again with .padding(-radius). In onContinuousHover (pointer on iPad, Mac and visionOS) and in a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) (touch), offset the original content by (location − centre) × strength (0.3) using an interactiveSpring(response 0.25, damping 0.7). When hover ends or the drag ends, spring back to zero with spring(response 0.45, damping 0.45) for a little overshoot. With Reduce Motion on, don't move.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Pulls the view toward the pointer while it hovers nearby (iPad pointer,
/// Mac, visionOS), or toward the finger while it drags on touch screens, then
/// springs back to rest.
struct MagneticModifier: ViewModifier {
    var strength: CGFloat
    var radius: CGFloat

    @State private var offset: CGSize = .zero
    /// Size of the padded tracking area.
    @State private var areaSize: CGSize = .zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .offset(reduceMotion ? .zero : offset)
            // Grow the tracking area by `radius` so the pull starts before the
            // pointer reaches the view.
            .padding(radius)
            .contentShape(Rectangle())
            .background {
                GeometryReader { proxy in
                    Color.clear
                        .onAppear { areaSize = proxy.size }
                        .onChange(of: proxy.size) { _, newSize in areaSize = newSize }
                }
            }
            .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) { phase in
                switch phase {
                case let .active(location):
                    attract(to: location)
                case .ended:
                    release()
                }
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0, coordinateSpace: .local)
                    .onChanged { attract(to: $0.location) }
                    .onEnded { _ in release() }
            )
            .padding(-radius)
    }

    private func attract(to location: CGPoint) {
        // `location` is in the padded tracking area, whose centre is the view's centre.
        let centre = CGPoint(x: areaSize.width / 2, y: areaSize.height / 2)
        withAnimation(.interactiveSpring(response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.7)) {
            offset = CGSize(
                width: (location.x - centre.x) * strength,
                height: (location.y - centre.y) * strength
            )
        }
    }

    private func release() {
        withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.45)) {
            offset = .zero
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Makes the view drift toward a nearby pointer (or a dragging finger) and
    /// spring back when it leaves.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Get started") { }
    ///     .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    ///     .magnetic()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - strength: Fraction of the pointer's distance from the centre that
    ///     the view moves (0…1).
    ///   - radius: How far outside the view, in points, the pull starts.
    func magnetic(strength: CGFloat = 0.3, radius: CGFloat = 60) -> some View {
        modifier(MagneticModifier(strength: strength, radius: radius))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Button("Get started") { }
        .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
        .controlSize(.large)
        .magnetic()
        .padding(80)
}
```

## Hold to Confirm (`hold-to-confirm`)

Liquid fills the button while you hold; the action runs only when it's full.

- API: `HoldToConfirmButton("…") { }`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Press
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/HoldToConfirmButton.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/HoldToConfirmButton.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/Haptics.swift

### Usage

```swift
HoldToConfirmButton("Hold to delete") {
    deleteAccount()
}

HoldToConfirmButton(duration: 2, fillColor: .orange) {
    launch()
} label: {
    Label("Hold to launch", systemImage: "flame")
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI HoldToConfirmButton (iOS 17+) for destructive actions. A capsule with a 15% tint of fillColor (red) shows the label in fillColor. While pressed (onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration:perform:onPressingChanged:)), animate a progress value linearly from its current value to 1 over the remaining duration (1.2 s); releasing early animates it back to 0 with easeOut(0.35). Draw the liquid as a Shape filled from the bottom up to progress, with a sine-wave top edge (4 pt amplitude, phase driven by TimelineView) that flattens when empty or full. Mask a stack of the liquid plus a white copy of the label with the same shape, so the submerged part of the text turns white. On completion, run the action, swap the label for a checkmark with a spring, play a success haptic and reset after 1.2 s. Scale to 0.97 while pressing.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A capsule button that fills with liquid while it is held and runs its
/// action only when the fill reaches the top. Letting go early drains it.
/// Good for destructive or irreversible actions.
public struct HoldToConfirmButton<Label: View>: View {
    private let duration: Double
    private let fillColor: Color
    private let action: () -> Void
    private let label: Label

    @State private var progress: CGFloat = 0
    @State private var isPressing = false
    @State private var isConfirmed = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - duration: Seconds the user must hold.
    ///   - fillColor: Colour of the liquid. The resting background is a tint
    ///     of it and the label is drawn in it, turning white where submerged.
    ///   - action: Runs once the hold completes.
    ///   - label: The button's content.
    public init(
        duration: Double = 1.2,
        fillColor: Color = .red,
        action: @escaping () -> Void,
        @ViewBuilder label: () -> Label
    ) {
        self.duration = duration
        self.fillColor = fillColor
        self.action = action
        self.label = label()
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion || (!isPressing && progress == 0))) { timeline in
            let liquid = LiquidFill(
                progress: progress,
                phase: reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * 6,
                waveHeight: progress > 0 && progress < 1 ? 4 : 0
            )
            // The label sizes the button; the capsule and liquid only decorate it.
            content
                .foregroundStyle(fillColor)
                .background(Capsule().fill(fillColor.opacity(0.15)))
                .overlay {
                    // The liquid, with the label redrawn in white where it's submerged.
                    ZStack {
                        liquid.fill(fillColor)
                        content.foregroundStyle(.white)
                    }
                    .mask(liquid)
                }
                .clipShape(Capsule())
        }
        .scaleEffect(isPressing ? 0.97 : 1)
        .animation(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.6), value: isPressing)
        .contentShape(Capsule())
        .onLongPressGesture(minimumDuration: duration) {
            confirm()
        } onPressingChanged: { pressing in
            guard !isConfirmed else { return }
            isPressing = pressing
            if pressing {
                withAnimation(.linear(duration: duration * (1 - progress))) { progress = 1 }
            } else if progress < 1 {
                withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.35)) { progress = 0 }
            }
        }
        .haptic(.success, trigger: isConfirmed) { _, confirmed in confirmed }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
        .accessibilityHint("Press and hold to confirm")
        .accessibilityAction { action() }
    }

    /// The label (swapped for a checkmark once confirmed), padded to button size.
    private var content: some View {
        label
            .opacity(isConfirmed ? 0 : 1)
            .overlay {
                Image(systemName: "checkmark")
                    .fontWeight(.bold)
                    .scaleEffect(isConfirmed ? 1 : 0.3)
                    .opacity(isConfirmed ? 1 : 0)
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 24)
            .padding(.vertical, 14)
    }

    private func confirm() {
        isPressing = false
        withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.6)) { isConfirmed = true }
        action()
        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 1.2) {
            withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.4)) {
                isConfirmed = false
                progress = 0
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension HoldToConfirmButton where Label == Text {
    /// A hold-to-confirm button with a text label.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// HoldToConfirmButton("Hold to delete") { deleteAccount() }
    /// ```
    init(
        _ title: LocalizedStringKey,
        duration: Double = 1.2,
        fillColor: Color = .red,
        action: @escaping () -> Void
    ) {
        self.init(duration: duration, fillColor: fillColor, action: action) {
            Text(title).font(.headline)
        }
    }
}

/// A rectangle filled from the bottom up to `progress`, with a sine wave on top.
private struct LiquidFill: Shape {
    var progress: CGFloat
    var phase: Double
    var waveHeight: CGFloat

    var animatableData: AnimatablePair<CGFloat, CGFloat> {
        get { AnimatablePair(progress, waveHeight) }
        set { progress = newValue.first; waveHeight = newValue.second }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        // Overfill slightly so the wave crests are hidden when full.
        let level = rect.maxY - (rect.height + waveHeight * 2) * progress
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.maxY))
        let steps = 24
        for step in 0...steps {
            let x = rect.minX + rect.width * CGFloat(step) / CGFloat(steps)
            let angle = Double(step) / Double(steps) * .pi * 3 + phase
            path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: level + CGFloat(sin(angle)) * waveHeight))
        }
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.maxY))
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

#Preview {
    HoldToConfirmButton("Hold to delete") { }
        .padding()
}

// MARK: - Haptics.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

import SwiftUI

/// The haptics the package plays. `SensoryFeedback` and `sensoryFeedback`
/// need visionOS 26, but the package supports visionOS 1, so call sites use
/// this enum and `.haptic(…)`, which does nothing on visionOS (it has no
/// haptics anyway).
enum Haptic: Equatable {
    case success
    case error
    case lightImpact

    #if !os(visionOS)
    var feedback: SensoryFeedback {
        switch self {
        case .success: .success
        case .error: .error
        case .lightImpact: .impact(weight: .light)
        }
    }
    #endif
}

extension View {
    /// Plays `haptic` every time `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays `haptic` when `trigger` changes and `condition` returns true.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (T, T) -> Bool) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger, condition: condition)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays the haptic returned by `haptic` (if any) when `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(trigger: T, _ haptic: @escaping (T, T) -> Haptic?) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(trigger: trigger) { old, new in haptic(old, new)?.feedback }
        #endif
    }
}
```

---

## Loading → Success (`status-button`)

The button morphs into a spinner, then a green checkmark or a red shake.

- API: `StatusButton("…", status:) { }`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/StatusButton.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/StatusButton.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/CheckmarkShape.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/Haptics.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var status = MotionButtonStatus.idle

StatusButton("Pay now", status: status) {
    status = .loading
    Task {
        status = await pay() ? .success : .failure
        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.5))
        status = .idle
    }
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI StatusButton (iOS 17+) driven by a status enum: idle, loading, success, failure. It is a 50 pt tall capsule Button. Idle shows the title at its natural width. For any other status the frame width animates to 50 pt, turning the capsule into a circle (spring response 0.45, damping 0.75), and the title shrinks and fades. Loading shows a white 70% arc spinning forever. Success turns the fill green and draws a white checkmark path with trim from 0 to 1 (easeOut 0.35 s, 0.15 s delay). Failure turns the fill red, scales in an xmark and shakes horizontally with a GeometryEffect (8 pt, three swings). Play success and error haptics with sensoryFeedback, disable the button when not idle, and expose the status as the accessibility value.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The phases a `StatusButton` moves through.
public enum MotionButtonStatus: Equatable, Sendable {
    case idle
    case loading
    case success
    case failure
}

/// A capsule button that morphs to show the result of its action: it shrinks
/// into a spinning circle while loading, then turns green with a drawn
/// checkmark on success, or red with a shake on failure.
///
/// You own the status, so it works with any async work:
///
/// ```swift
/// @State private var status = MotionButtonStatus.idle
///
/// StatusButton("Pay now", status: status) {
///     status = .loading
///     Task {
///         status = await pay() ? .success : .failure
///         try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.5))
///         status = .idle
///     }
/// }
/// ```
public struct StatusButton: View {
    private let title: LocalizedStringKey
    private let status: MotionButtonStatus
    private let tint: Color
    private let action: () -> Void

    @State private var spin = false
    @State private var shakes = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let height: CGFloat = 50

    public init(
        _ title: LocalizedStringKey,
        status: MotionButtonStatus,
        tint: Color = .accentColor,
        action: @escaping () -> Void
    ) {
        self.title = title
        self.status = status
        self.tint = tint
        self.action = action
    }

    public var body: some View {
        Button(action: action) {
            ZStack {
                Text(title)
                    .font(.headline)
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .fixedSize()
                    .padding(.horizontal, 28)
                    .opacity(status == .idle ? 1 : 0)
                    .scaleEffect(status == .idle ? 1 : 0.6)

                if status == .loading {
                    Circle()
                        .trim(from: 0, to: 0.7)
                        .stroke(.white, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 3, lineCap: .round))
                        .frame(width: 22, height: 22)
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(spin ? 360 : 0))
                        .onAppear {
                            spin = false
                            withAnimation(.linear(duration: 0.8).repeatForever(autoreverses: false)) {
                                spin = true
                            }
                        }
                        .transition(.scale(scale: 0.4).combined(with: .opacity))
                }

                CheckmarkShape()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: status == .success ? 1 : 0)
                    .stroke(.white, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 3.5, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
                    .frame(width: 20, height: 16)
                    .animation(status == .success ? .easeOut(duration: 0.35).delay(0.15) : nil, value: status)

                Image(systemName: "xmark")
                    .font(.system(size: 18, weight: .bold))
                    .scaleEffect(status == .failure ? 1 : 0.3)
                    .opacity(status == .failure ? 1 : 0)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .frame(width: status == .idle ? nil : height, height: height)
            .background(Capsule().fill(background))
            .contentShape(Capsule())
        }
        .buttonStyle(StatusPressStyle())
        .disabled(status != .idle)
        .modifier(StatusShake(shakes: CGFloat(shakes)))
        .animation(.spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.75), value: status)
        .onChange(of: status) { _, newValue in
            if newValue == .failure, !reduceMotion {
                withAnimation(.linear(duration: 0.4)) { shakes += 1 }
            }
        }
        .haptic(trigger: status) { _, newValue in
            switch newValue {
            case .success: .success
            case .failure: .error
            default: nil
            }
        }
        .accessibilityLabel(Text(title))
        .accessibilityValue(accessibilityStatus)
    }

    private var background: Color {
        switch status {
        case .idle, .loading: tint
        case .success: .green
        case .failure: .red
        }
    }

    private var accessibilityStatus: Text {
        switch status {
        case .idle: Text("")
        case .loading: Text("Loading")
        case .success: Text("Done")
        case .failure: Text("Failed")
        }
    }
}

private struct StatusPressStyle: ButtonStyle {
    func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
        configuration.label
            .scaleEffect(configuration.isPressed ? 0.95 : 1)
            .animation(.spring(response: 0.25, dampingFraction: 0.6), value: configuration.isPressed)
    }
}

/// Horizontal shake, one full shake per unit of `shakes`.
private struct StatusShake: GeometryEffect {
    var shakes: CGFloat

    var animatableData: CGFloat {
        get { shakes }
        set { shakes = newValue }
    }

    func effectValue(size: CGSize) -> ProjectionTransform {
        ProjectionTransform(CGAffineTransform(translationX: 8 * sin(shakes * .pi * 6), y: 0))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var status = MotionButtonStatus.idle

        var body: some View {
            StatusButton("Pay now", status: status) {
                status = .loading
                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 1.2) { status = .success }
                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 2.8) { status = .idle }
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - CheckmarkShape.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

// Shared by StatusButton and AnimatedCheckmark.

import SwiftUI

/// A checkmark drawn left to right, sized to its frame.
struct CheckmarkShape: Shape {
    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.midY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX + rect.width * 0.38, y: rect.maxY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.minY))
        return path
    }
}

// MARK: - Haptics.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

import SwiftUI

/// The haptics the package plays. `SensoryFeedback` and `sensoryFeedback`
/// need visionOS 26, but the package supports visionOS 1, so call sites use
/// this enum and `.haptic(…)`, which does nothing on visionOS (it has no
/// haptics anyway).
enum Haptic: Equatable {
    case success
    case error
    case lightImpact

    #if !os(visionOS)
    var feedback: SensoryFeedback {
        switch self {
        case .success: .success
        case .error: .error
        case .lightImpact: .impact(weight: .light)
        }
    }
    #endif
}

extension View {
    /// Plays `haptic` every time `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays `haptic` when `trigger` changes and `condition` returns true.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (T, T) -> Bool) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger, condition: condition)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays the haptic returned by `haptic` (if any) when `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(trigger: T, _ haptic: @escaping (T, T) -> Haptic?) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(trigger: trigger) { old, new in haptic(old, new)?.feedback }
        #endif
    }
}
```

## Glow Border (`glow-border`)

A rainbow border runs around the view with a soft glow behind it.

- API: `.glowBorder()`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/GlowBorder.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/GlowBorder.swift

### Usage

```swift
Text("Upgrade to Pro")
    .padding()
    .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14))
    .glowBorder(cornerRadius: 14)

CardView()
    .glowBorder(colors: [.orange, .yellow], cornerRadius: 24, lineWidth: 3)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .glowBorder(colors:cornerRadius:lineWidth:glowRadius:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+). In a non-interactive overlay, use TimelineView(.animation) to compute a rotation angle of (time / duration) turns (3 s per turn). Build an AngularGradient from the palette plus its first colour again (pink, purple, blue, cyan, mint by default) starting at that angle. Stroke a continuous RoundedRectangle with it twice: once at 2× line width, blurred by glowRadius (8) at 80% opacity for the glow, and once crisp at lineWidth (2). With Reduce Motion on, pause the rotation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A gradient border that keeps rotating around the view, with a soft glow
/// behind it. Draws attention to a primary action or a highlighted card.
struct GlowBorderModifier: ViewModifier {
    var colors: [Color]
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat
    var lineWidth: CGFloat
    var glowRadius: CGFloat
    var duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
                    let turns = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate / duration
                    let gradient = AngularGradient(
                        colors: colors + [colors.first ?? .clear],
                        center: .center,
                        angle: .degrees(turns.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1) * 360)
                    )
                    let shape = RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous)
                    ZStack {
                        shape.stroke(gradient, lineWidth: lineWidth * 2)
                            .blur(radius: glowRadius)
                            .opacity(0.8)
                        shape.stroke(gradient, lineWidth: lineWidth)
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Adds a rotating gradient border with a glow.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text("Upgrade to Pro")
    ///     .padding()
    ///     .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14))
    ///     .glowBorder(cornerRadius: 14)
    /// ```
    func glowBorder(
        colors: [Color] = [.pink, .purple, .blue, .cyan, .mint],
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 14,
        lineWidth: CGFloat = 2,
        glowRadius: CGFloat = 8,
        duration: Double = 3
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(GlowBorderModifier(
            colors: colors,
            cornerRadius: cornerRadius,
            lineWidth: lineWidth,
            glowRadius: glowRadius,
            duration: duration
        ))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Text("Upgrade to Pro")
        .font(.headline)
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(.horizontal, 28)
        .padding(.vertical, 16)
        .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14, style: .continuous))
        .glowBorder()
        .padding(40)
}
```

## Shine (`shine`)

A slanted glint of light sweeps across the button, on cue or on a beat.

- API: `.shine(every:) / .shine(trigger:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Value change / Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Shine.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Shine.swift

### Usage

```swift
PremiumBadge()
    .shine(every: 3)

Button("Upgrade") { purchases += 1 }
    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    .shine(trigger: purchases)
```

### How it works

Create two SwiftUI modifiers (iOS 17+): .shine(trigger:color:duration:) and .shine(every:color:duration:). Both overlay a "band": a horizontal LinearGradient clear → white 70 % → clear, 30 % of the view's width (at least 24 pt), twice the view's height, rotated 20°, whose x offset goes from −1.5 × band (fully off the left) at progress 0 to width + 1.5 × band (off the right) at progress 1. Mask the band with the content so only the view's own pixels shine, and disable hit testing. The trigger version runs progress 0 → 1 with keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0, trigger:) and one CubicKeyframe over duration (0.75 s), so the band is hidden at rest. The looping version uses TimelineView(.animation) with progress = (time mod interval) / duration, clamped to 1. With Reduce Motion on, skip the band.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A slanted glint of light that sweeps across the view once, either every
/// time `trigger` changes or on a fixed interval.
struct ShineModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var color: Color
    var duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: no sweep.
        let enabled = !reduceMotion
        let color = color
        return content
            .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0.0, trigger: trigger) { view, progress in
                view.overlay {
                    if enabled {
                        ShineBand(progress: progress, color: color).mask { view }
                    }
                }
            } keyframes: { _ in
                // 0 and 1 are both off the view, so the band is hidden at rest.
                CubicKeyframe(1, duration: duration)
            }
    }
}

/// Repeats the glint every `interval` seconds.
struct LoopingShineModifier: ViewModifier {
    var interval: Double
    var color: Color
    var duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            if !reduceMotion {
                TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
                    let time = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
                    let phase = time.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: max(interval, duration))
                    ShineBand(progress: min(1, phase / duration), color: color)
                }
                .mask { content }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The band itself: a skewed white gradient that travels left to right as
/// `progress` goes from 0 to 1.
private struct ShineBand: View {
    var progress: Double
    var color: Color

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let width = geometry.size.width
            let band = max(24, width * 0.3)
            LinearGradient(colors: [.clear, color, .clear], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
                .frame(width: band, height: geometry.size.height * 2)
                .rotationEffect(.degrees(20))
                .offset(x: -band * 1.5 + (width + band * 3) * progress, y: -geometry.size.height / 2)
        }
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Sweeps a glint of light across the view every time `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Upgrade") { purchases += 1 }
    ///     .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    ///     .shine(trigger: purchases)
    /// ```
    func shine<Trigger: Equatable>(
        trigger: Trigger,
        color: Color = .white.opacity(0.7),
        duration: Double = 0.75
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ShineModifier(trigger: trigger, color: color, duration: duration))
    }

    /// Sweeps a glint of light across the view every `interval` seconds.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// PremiumBadge()
    ///     .shine(every: 3)
    /// ```
    func shine(
        every interval: Double,
        color: Color = .white.opacity(0.7),
        duration: Double = 0.75
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(LoopingShineModifier(interval: interval, color: color, duration: duration))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Text("Go Premium")
        .font(.headline)
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(.horizontal, 24)
        .padding(.vertical, 12)
        .background(Capsule().fill(Color.orange.gradient))
        .shine(every: 2)
        .padding()
}
```

## Jelly (`jelly`)

A rubbery squash-and-stretch wobble on every tap.

- API: `.jelly(trigger:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Jelly.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/Jelly.swift

### Usage

```swift
Button("Boing") { taps += 1 }
    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    .jelly(trigger: taps)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .jelly(trigger:amount:) view modifier (iOS 17+) using keyframeAnimator(initialValue:trigger:) on a struct with x and y scale (both 1), applied with scaleEffect(x:y:). With a = amount (0.25): the x track goes 1 + a (0.1 s), 1 − 0.8a (0.12 s), 1 + 0.5a (0.12 s) with cubic keyframes, then a SpringKeyframe(.bouncy) back to 1 over 0.4 s; the y track does the opposite (1 − a, 1 + 0.8a, 1 − 0.5a, spring to 1), so the view squashes wide and flat, then stretches tall and thin, then settles. With Reduce Motion on, use a = 0.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

private struct JellyScale {
    var x: CGFloat = 1
    var y: CGFloat = 1
}

/// A rubbery squash-and-stretch wobble that plays every time `trigger`
/// changes: wide and flat, then tall and thin, settling back with a spring.
struct JellyModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var amount: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: stay still.
        let a = reduceMotion ? 0 : amount
        return content.keyframeAnimator(initialValue: JellyScale(), trigger: trigger) { view, scale in
            view.scaleEffect(x: scale.x, y: scale.y)
        } keyframes: { _ in
            KeyframeTrack(\.x) {
                CubicKeyframe(1 + a, duration: 0.1)
                CubicKeyframe(1 - a * 0.8, duration: 0.12)
                CubicKeyframe(1 + a * 0.5, duration: 0.12)
                SpringKeyframe(1, duration: 0.4, spring: .bouncy)
            }
            KeyframeTrack(\.y) {
                CubicKeyframe(1 - a, duration: 0.1)
                CubicKeyframe(1 + a * 0.8, duration: 0.12)
                CubicKeyframe(1 - a * 0.5, duration: 0.12)
                SpringKeyframe(1, duration: 0.4, spring: .bouncy)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Wobbles the view like jelly every time `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Boing") { taps += 1 }
    ///     .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    ///     .jelly(trigger: taps)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameter amount: How far it squashes (0.25 = 25 %).
    func jelly<Trigger: Equatable>(trigger: Trigger, amount: CGFloat = 0.25) -> some View {
        modifier(JellyModifier(trigger: trigger, amount: amount))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var taps = 0
        var body: some View {
            Button("Boing") { taps += 1 }
                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                .controlSize(.large)
                .jelly(trigger: taps)
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding(40)
}
```

## Click Spark (`click-spark`)

Short spark lines shoot out from the exact point you tapped.

- API: `.clickSpark()`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/ClickSpark.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/ClickSpark.swift

### Usage

```swift
Button("Launch") { }
    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    .clickSpark(color: .orange)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .clickSpark(color:count:radius:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Detect taps with .simultaneousGesture(SpatialTapGesture()) and append a spark (UUID + location) to a @State array, removing it 0.6 s later. In a hit-testing-disabled overlay, place each spark at its location: count (8) capsules 2.5 pt wide and 0.45 × radius tall, each rotated by index / count × 360°. On appear, animate with easeOut(0.45 s) from offset −0.3 × radius to −radius (outward), scaleEffect(y:) from 1 to 0.1 anchored at the top (so each line shrinks toward its outer tip) and opacity from 1 to 0. With Reduce Motion on, don't add sparks.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Short spark lines shoot out from the exact point the user tapped.
struct ClickSparkModifier: ViewModifier {
    var color: Color
    var count: Int
    var radius: CGFloat

    @State private var sparks: [Spark] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private struct Spark: Identifiable {
        let id = UUID()
        let location: CGPoint
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                ZStack {
                    ForEach(sparks) { spark in
                        SparkLines(color: color, count: count, radius: radius)
                            .position(spark.location)
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                SpatialTapGesture().onEnded { value in
                    // Reduce Motion: no sparks.
                    guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                    let spark = Spark(location: value.location)
                    sparks.append(spark)
                    DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.6) {
                        sparks.removeAll { $0.id == spark.id }
                    }
                }
            )
    }
}

private struct SparkLines: View {
    let color: Color
    let count: Int
    let radius: CGFloat

    @State private var fired = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(0..<max(1, count), id: \.self) { index in
                Capsule()
                    .fill(color)
                    .frame(width: 2.5, height: radius * 0.45)
                    // Shrinks toward its outer end as it flies.
                    .scaleEffect(y: fired ? 0.1 : 1, anchor: .top)
                    .offset(y: -(fired ? radius : radius * 0.3))
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(Double(index) / Double(max(1, count)) * 360))
            }
        }
        .opacity(fired ? 0 : 1)
        .onAppear {
            withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.45)) { fired = true }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shoots spark lines out of every tap point.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Launch") { }
    ///     .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
    ///     .clickSpark(color: .orange)
    /// ```
    func clickSpark(color: Color = .orange, count: Int = 8, radius: CGFloat = 28) -> some View {
        modifier(ClickSparkModifier(color: color, count: count, radius: radius))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16)
        .fill(.black)
        .frame(width: 260, height: 160)
        .overlay(Text("Click anywhere").foregroundStyle(.white))
        .clickSpark()
}
```

## Like Button (`like-button`)

The heart pops in as a ring bursts open and coloured dots fly out.

- API: `LikeButton(isLiked:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/LikeButton.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/LikeButton.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/Haptics.swift

### Usage

```swift
LikeButton(isLiked: $post.isLiked)

LikeButton(isLiked: $liked, size: 40, color: .red)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI LikeButton (iOS 17+) bound to isLiked, with size (28 pt), color (pink) and dotColors. It's a plain Button showing Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart"); tapping toggles and, on like, increments a counter used as a keyframeAnimator trigger over a struct {heart, ring, dots}. Tracks: heart drops to 0.2 instantly, holds 0.15 s, then springs to 1 with a bouncy overshoot; ring goes 0 → 1 over 0.3 s then back to 0; dots wait 0.15 s then go 0 → 1 over 0.55 s. Behind the heart draw (a) a circle strokeBorder in color whose diameter is 1.5 × size × ring and whose line width is 0.5 × size × (1 − ring), so it bursts open and thins out; (b) 7 pairs of small dots (0.16 × size) at angles i/7 × 360° ± 10°, at distance size × (0.6 + 0.55 × dots), scaling down to 10 % as they fly. Unliking only springs the heart back. Add a light haptic on like, and hide the burst for Reduce Motion.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

private struct LikePop {
    var heart: CGFloat = 1
    var ring: CGFloat = 0
    var dots: CGFloat = 0
}

/// A Twitter-style like button: on like, a ring bursts open, the heart pops
/// in with an overshoot and a circle of coloured dots flies out. Unliking
/// just shrinks the heart back.
public struct LikeButton: View {
    @Binding private var isLiked: Bool
    private let size: CGFloat
    private let color: Color
    private let dotColors: [Color]

    @State private var likes = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isLiked: Whether the item is liked; tapping toggles it.
    ///   - size: Point size of the heart.
    ///   - color: Colour of the filled heart and the ring.
    ///   - dotColors: Colours cycled through by the burst dots.
    public init(
        isLiked: Binding<Bool>,
        size: CGFloat = 28,
        color: Color = .pink,
        dotColors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .mint, .cyan, .purple]
    ) {
        _isLiked = isLiked
        self.size = size
        self.color = color
        self.dotColors = dotColors
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let showBurst = !reduceMotion
        let size = size, color = color, dotColors = dotColors
        return Button {
            isLiked.toggle()
            if isLiked { likes += 1 }
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
                .font(.system(size: size))
                .foregroundStyle(isLiked ? color : Color.secondary)
                .frame(width: size * 1.6, height: size * 1.6)
                .contentShape(Rectangle())
                .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: LikePop(), trigger: likes) { heart, pop in
                    heart
                        .scaleEffect(pop.heart)
                        .background {
                            if showBurst { LikeBurst(pop: pop, size: size, color: color, dotColors: dotColors) }
                        }
                } keyframes: { _ in
                    KeyframeTrack(\.heart) {
                        CubicKeyframe(0.2, duration: 0.05)
                        CubicKeyframe(0.2, duration: 0.15)
                        SpringKeyframe(1, duration: 0.5, spring: .bouncy(duration: 0.4, extraBounce: 0.25))
                    }
                    KeyframeTrack(\.ring) {
                        LinearKeyframe(0.01, duration: 0.01)
                        CubicKeyframe(1, duration: 0.3)
                        LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.01)
                    }
                    KeyframeTrack(\.dots) {
                        LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.15)
                        CubicKeyframe(1, duration: 0.55)
                        LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.01)
                    }
                }
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .animation(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.6), value: isLiked)
        .haptic(.lightImpact, trigger: likes)
        .accessibilityLabel(isLiked ? "Unlike" : "Like")
    }
}

/// The ring and the dots behind the heart.
private struct LikeBurst: View {
    let pop: LikePop
    let size: CGFloat
    let color: Color
    let dotColors: [Color]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            // The ring grows and its stroke thins out to nothing.
            if pop.ring > 0 {
                Circle()
                    .strokeBorder(color, lineWidth: max(0.1, size * 0.5 * (1 - pop.ring)))
                    .frame(width: size * 1.5 * pop.ring, height: size * 1.5 * pop.ring)
            }
            // Seven pairs of dots fly outward and shrink.
            if pop.dots > 0 {
                ForEach(0..<14, id: \.self) { index in
                    dot(index)
                }
            }
        }
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func dot(_ index: Int) -> some View {
        let pair = index % 2
        let base = Double(index / 2) / 7 * 2 * .pi - .pi / 2
        let angle = base + (pair == 0 ? -0.18 : 0.18)
        let reach: CGFloat = 0.6 + 0.55 * pop.dots
        let distance: CGFloat = size * reach * (pair == 0 ? 1 : 0.85)
        let fill: Color = dotColors.isEmpty ? color : dotColors[index % dotColors.count]
        return Circle()
            .fill(fill)
            .frame(width: size * 0.16, height: size * 0.16)
            .scaleEffect(1 - pop.dots * 0.9)
            .offset(x: CGFloat(cos(angle)) * distance, y: CGFloat(sin(angle)) * distance)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var liked = false
        var body: some View {
            LikeButton(isLiked: $liked, size: 40)
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding(60)
}

// MARK: - Haptics.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

import SwiftUI

/// The haptics the package plays. `SensoryFeedback` and `sensoryFeedback`
/// need visionOS 26, but the package supports visionOS 1, so call sites use
/// this enum and `.haptic(…)`, which does nothing on visionOS (it has no
/// haptics anyway).
enum Haptic: Equatable {
    case success
    case error
    case lightImpact

    #if !os(visionOS)
    var feedback: SensoryFeedback {
        switch self {
        case .success: .success
        case .error: .error
        case .lightImpact: .impact(weight: .light)
        }
    }
    #endif
}

extension View {
    /// Plays `haptic` every time `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays `haptic` when `trigger` changes and `condition` returns true.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (T, T) -> Bool) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger, condition: condition)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays the haptic returned by `haptic` (if any) when `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(trigger: T, _ haptic: @escaping (T, T) -> Haptic?) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(trigger: trigger) { old, new in haptic(old, new)?.feedback }
        #endif
    }
}
```

## Animated Symbol (`animated-symbol`)

SF Symbols that keep moving: bounce on a beat, pulse, variable colour.

- API: `AnimatedSymbol("…", style:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/AnimatedSymbol.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/AnimatedSymbol.swift

### Usage

```swift
AnimatedSymbol("bell.fill")                      // bounces every 1.5 s
AnimatedSymbol("heart.fill", style: .pulse)
AnimatedSymbol("wifi", style: .variableColor)
AnimatedSymbol("mic.fill", style: .scaleUp, isActive: isRecording)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI AnimatedSymbol view (iOS 17+) wrapping Image(systemName:) with a style enum: .bounce, .pulse, .variableColor and .scaleUp, plus isActive and interval (1.5 s). For .bounce, apply .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: beats) and increment beats in a .task(id: isActive) loop every interval. For the others, use the indefinite effects .symbolEffect(.pulse, isActive:), .symbolEffect(.variableColor.iterative.reversing, isActive:) and .symbolEffect(.scale.up, isActive:). The view inherits font and foregroundStyle like any Image. With Reduce Motion on, treat it as inactive.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// An SF Symbol that keeps playing a symbol effect: a bounce on a beat, or a
/// continuous pulse, variable-colour cycle or scale-up.
public struct AnimatedSymbol: View {
    /// Which symbol effect to play.
    public enum Style: CaseIterable, Sendable {
        /// Bounces once every `interval` seconds.
        case bounce
        /// Fades the symbol's layers in and out.
        case pulse
        /// Lights up the symbol's layers one after another (wifi, speaker…).
        case variableColor
        /// Grows the symbol slightly and holds it.
        case scaleUp
    }

    private let systemName: String
    private let style: Style
    private let isActive: Bool
    private let interval: Double

    @State private var beats = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - systemName: The SF Symbol name.
    ///   - style: The effect to play.
    ///   - isActive: Pauses the effect when false.
    ///   - interval: Seconds between bounces (`.bounce` only).
    public init(_ systemName: String, style: Style = .bounce, isActive: Bool = true, interval: Double = 1.5) {
        self.systemName = systemName
        self.style = style
        self.isActive = isActive
        self.interval = interval
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: the symbol stays still.
        let active = isActive && !reduceMotion
        let image = Image(systemName: systemName)
        Group {
            switch style {
            case .bounce:
                image.symbolEffect(.bounce, value: beats)
            case .pulse:
                image.symbolEffect(.pulse, isActive: active)
            case .variableColor:
                image.symbolEffect(.variableColor.iterative.reversing, isActive: active)
            case .scaleUp:
                image.symbolEffect(.scale.up, isActive: active)
            }
        }
        .task(id: active) {
            guard style == .bounce, active else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                beats += 1
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(max(0.3, interval)))
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    HStack(spacing: 24) {
        AnimatedSymbol("bell.fill")
        AnimatedSymbol("heart.fill", style: .pulse)
        AnimatedSymbol("wifi", style: .variableColor)
        AnimatedSymbol("mic.fill", style: .scaleUp)
    }
    .font(.largeTitle)
    .padding()
}
```

## Liquid Toggle (`liquid-toggle`)

A switch whose knob stretches like a drop of liquid as it slides.

- API: `.toggleStyle(.liquid)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/LiquidToggleStyle.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/LiquidToggleStyle.swift

### Usage

```swift
Toggle("Wi-Fi", isOn: $wifi)
    .toggleStyle(.liquid)

Toggle("Dark mode", isOn: $dark)
    .toggleStyle(.liquid(tint: .purple))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI LiquidToggleStyle (iOS 17+) with a tint (green) and static accessors .liquid and .liquid(tint:). makeBody puts the label, a Spacer and a 52 × 32 pt switch in an HStack. The switch is a plain Button that toggles configuration.isOn inside withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.7)); it shows a ZStack aligned .trailing when on and .leading when off, with a capsule track (tint when on, gray 35 % when off) and a white capsule knob (26 pt tall, 3 pt padding, small shadow). The knob's width runs a keyframeAnimator triggered by isOn: CubicKeyframe to 1.5 × 26 pt over 0.12 s, then SpringKeyframe(.bouncy) back to 26 over 0.35 s, so it stretches as it slides and snaps back round. Give it an "On"/"Off" accessibility value. With Reduce Motion on, don't stretch and use a short ease.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A switch whose knob stretches like a drop of liquid as it slides across,
/// then springs back to a circle.
///
/// ```swift
/// Toggle("Wi-Fi", isOn: $isOn)
///     .toggleStyle(.liquid)
///
/// Toggle("Dark mode", isOn: $dark)
///     .toggleStyle(.liquid(tint: .purple))
/// ```
public struct LiquidToggleStyle: ToggleStyle {
    public var tint: Color

    public init(tint: Color = .green) {
        self.tint = tint
    }

    public func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
        HStack {
            configuration.label
            Spacer(minLength: 12)
            LiquidSwitch(isOn: configuration.$isOn, tint: tint)
        }
    }
}

private struct LiquidSwitch: View {
    @Binding var isOn: Bool
    let tint: Color

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let width: CGFloat = 52
    private let height: CGFloat = 32
    private let knob: CGFloat = 26

    var body: some View {
        let knob = knob
        // Reduce Motion: no stretch.
        let stretch = reduceMotion ? knob : knob * 1.5
        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.7)) {
                isOn.toggle()
            }
        } label: {
            ZStack(alignment: isOn ? .trailing : .leading) {
                Capsule()
                    .fill(isOn ? tint : Color.gray.opacity(0.35))
                Capsule()
                    .fill(.white)
                    .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.2), radius: 2, y: 1)
                    .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: knob, trigger: isOn) { view, knobWidth in
                        view.frame(width: knobWidth, height: knob)
                    } keyframes: { _ in
                        CubicKeyframe(stretch, duration: 0.12)
                        SpringKeyframe(knob, duration: 0.35, spring: .bouncy)
                    }
                    .padding(3)
            }
            .frame(width: width, height: height)
            .contentShape(Capsule())
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityValue(isOn ? "On" : "Off")
    }
}

public extension ToggleStyle where Self == LiquidToggleStyle {
    /// A switch with a stretchy, liquid knob.
    static var liquid: LiquidToggleStyle { LiquidToggleStyle() }

    /// A switch with a stretchy, liquid knob in the given colour.
    static func liquid(tint: Color) -> LiquidToggleStyle { LiquidToggleStyle(tint: tint) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var on = true
        var body: some View {
            Toggle("Notifications", isOn: $on)
                .toggleStyle(.liquid)
                .frame(width: 240)
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```
