## Gooey Menu (`gooey-menu`)

A round button splits into a fan of buttons like a drop of liquid.

- API: `GooeyMenu(symbols:action:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/GooeyMenu.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/GooeyMenu.swift

### Usage

```swift
GooeyMenu(symbols: ["camera.fill", "photo.fill", "mic.fill"], color: .indigo) { index in
    attach(index)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI GooeyMenu(symbols:color:distance:action:) view (iOS 17+). Frame: width 2 × distance + 60, height distance + 66 (distance 76). Behind the buttons, a Canvas adds .alphaThreshold(min: 0.5, color: color) and .blur(radius: 7) and, in drawLayer, draws resolved symbols at the main button's centre (bottom centre, 8 pt up): a 56 pt Circle (tag −1) and one 44 pt Circle per item (tags 0…n−1) offset to its fan position, so the circles fuse like liquid while they separate. Item i of n sits at angle π + π × (i + 1) / (n + 1) on a half-circle of radius distance above the button, or at the centre when closed. Each item animates with .spring(duration: 0.55, bounce: 0.35) delayed 0.04 s × its order (reversed when closing). On top of the canvas, place real Buttons with white SF Symbols at the same offsets (opacity 0 and no hit testing when closed) and the main button with a "plus" that rotates 45° when open. Tapping an item calls action(index) and closes the menu. With Reduce Motion on, hide the goo, draw plain circles and fade items in place.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A round button that splits into a fan of smaller buttons like a drop of
/// liquid, and swallows them back up. The blobs are blurred inside a `Canvas`
/// and cut back with an alpha threshold, so they stretch and merge as they
/// separate (metaballs).
public struct GooeyMenu: View {
    private let symbols: [String]
    private let color: Color
    private let distance: CGFloat
    private let action: (Int) -> Void

    @State private var isOpen = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let mainSize: CGFloat = 56
    private let itemSize: CGFloat = 44

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - symbols: SF Symbol names, one per menu item.
    ///   - color: Colour of the button and the goo.
    ///   - distance: How far items travel from the main button, in points.
    ///   - action: Called with the index of the tapped item. The menu closes.
    public init(symbols: [String], color: Color = .accentColor, distance: CGFloat = 76, action: @escaping (Int) -> Void) {
        self.symbols = symbols
        self.color = color
        self.distance = distance
        self.action = action
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let width = distance * 2 + itemSize + 16
        let height = distance + itemSize / 2 + mainSize / 2 + 16
        ZStack(alignment: .bottom) {
            Canvas { context, _ in
                context.addFilter(.alphaThreshold(min: 0.5, color: color))
                context.addFilter(.blur(radius: 7))
                context.drawLayer { layer in
                    for id in [-1] + Array(symbols.indices) {
                        if let blob = layer.resolveSymbol(id: id) {
                            layer.draw(blob, at: CGPoint(x: width / 2, y: height - 8 - mainSize / 2))
                        }
                    }
                }
            } symbols: {
                Circle().frame(width: mainSize, height: mainSize).tag(-1)
                ForEach(symbols.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                    Circle()
                        .frame(width: itemSize, height: itemSize)
                        .offset(offset(index))
                        .animation(itemAnimation(index), value: isOpen)
                        .tag(index)
                }
            }
            .frame(width: width, height: height)
            .opacity(reduceMotion ? 0 : 1)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)

            // The real, crisp buttons sit on top of the goo.
            ForEach(symbols.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                Button {
                    action(index)
                    isOpen = false
                } label: {
                    Image(systemName: symbols[index])
                        .font(.system(size: 17, weight: .semibold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .frame(width: itemSize, height: itemSize)
                        .background {
                            // Reduce Motion: plain circles that fade in place.
                            if reduceMotion { Circle().fill(color) }
                        }
                        .contentShape(Circle())
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .offset(offset(index))
                .opacity(isOpen ? 1 : 0)
                .animation(itemAnimation(index), value: isOpen)
                .allowsHitTesting(isOpen)
                .padding(.bottom, 8 + (mainSize - itemSize) / 2)
            }

            Button {
                isOpen.toggle()
            } label: {
                Image(systemName: "plus")
                    .font(.system(size: 22, weight: .bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(isOpen ? 45 : 0))
                    .frame(width: mainSize, height: mainSize)
                    .background {
                        if reduceMotion { Circle().fill(color) }
                    }
                    .contentShape(Circle())
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .padding(.bottom, 8)
            .animation(.spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.4), value: isOpen)
            .accessibilityLabel(isOpen ? "Close menu" : "Open menu")
        }
        .frame(width: width, height: height)
    }

    /// Items fan out along the upper half-circle.
    private func offset(_ index: Int) -> CGSize {
        guard isOpen || reduceMotion else { return .zero }
        let angle = Double.pi + Double.pi * Double(index + 1) / Double(symbols.count + 1)
        return CGSize(width: cos(angle) * distance, height: sin(angle) * distance)
    }

    private func itemAnimation(_ index: Int) -> Animation {
        if reduceMotion { return .easeInOut(duration: 0.25) }
        let order = isOpen ? index : symbols.count - 1 - index
        return .spring(duration: 0.55, bounce: 0.35).delay(Double(order) * 0.04)
    }
}

#Preview {
    GooeyMenu(symbols: ["camera.fill", "photo.fill", "mic.fill", "doc.fill"], color: .indigo) { index in
        print("tapped", index)
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Slide to Confirm (`slide-to-confirm`)

Drag the knob all the way across to run the action; let go early and it springs back.

- API: `SlideToConfirm(_:action:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/SlideToConfirm.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/SlideToConfirm.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/Haptics.swift

### Usage

```swift
SlideToConfirm("Slide to pay", color: .green) {
    pay()
}
.frame(width: 280)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI SlideToConfirm(_ title:color:resetAfter:action:) control (iOS 17+), 56 pt tall. In a GeometryReader ZStack(alignment: .leading): a Capsule track (secondary 15 %), the title (headline, secondary) whose opacity is 1 − progress × 1.6, a Capsule fill of width offset + knob + 8 in the colour at 35 %, and a 48 pt knob Circle (inset 4 pt) with a white "chevron.right.2" (or "checkmark" once confirmed, using contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))) and a coloured shadow. A DragGesture on the knob sets offset = clamp(translation.width, 0, maxOffset). On release past 85 % of maxOffset: snap to the end with a 0.3 s spring, mark confirmed, call action and play a success haptic; then after resetAfter (1.5 s, or never if nil) spring back. Otherwise spring back with .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.35). Expose it to accessibility as a button whose action confirms.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A "slide to confirm" control: drag the knob all the way across to run the
/// action. Let go early and it springs back. The label fades as you slide and
/// the track fills behind the knob.
public struct SlideToConfirm: View {
    private let title: String
    private let color: Color
    private let resetAfter: Double?
    private let action: () -> Void

    @State private var offset: CGFloat = 0
    @State private var isConfirmed = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let height: CGFloat = 56
    private let inset: CGFloat = 4

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - title: The label inside the track.
    ///   - color: Knob and fill colour.
    ///   - resetAfter: Seconds after confirming before the control resets;
    ///     `nil` keeps it confirmed.
    ///   - action: Runs once the knob reaches the end.
    public init(_ title: String, color: Color = .accentColor, resetAfter: Double? = 1.5, action: @escaping () -> Void) {
        self.title = title
        self.color = color
        self.resetAfter = resetAfter
        self.action = action
    }

    public var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let knob = height - inset * 2
            let maxOffset = max(0, geometry.size.width - knob - inset * 2)
            let progress = maxOffset > 0 ? offset / maxOffset : 0

            ZStack(alignment: .leading) {
                Capsule().fill(Color.secondary.opacity(0.15))

                Text(title)
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                    .padding(.leading, knob * 0.6)
                    .opacity(1 - progress * 1.6)

                // The fill grows with the knob.
                Capsule()
                    .fill(color.opacity(0.35))
                    .frame(width: offset + knob + inset * 2)

                Circle()
                    .fill(color)
                    .overlay {
                        Image(systemName: isConfirmed ? "checkmark" : "chevron.right.2")
                            .font(.system(size: 18, weight: .bold))
                            .foregroundStyle(.white)
                            .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
                    }
                    .frame(width: knob, height: knob)
                    .shadow(color: color.opacity(0.4), radius: 6, y: 2)
                    .padding(inset)
                    .offset(x: offset)
                    .gesture(
                        DragGesture()
                            .onChanged { value in
                                guard !isConfirmed else { return }
                                offset = min(maxOffset, max(0, value.translation.width))
                            }
                            .onEnded { _ in
                                guard !isConfirmed else { return }
                                if offset > maxOffset * 0.85 {
                                    confirm(maxOffset)
                                } else {
                                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.35)) {
                                        offset = 0
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                    )
            }
        }
        .frame(height: height)
        .haptic(.success, trigger: isConfirmed) { _, new in new }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(title)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
        .accessibilityAction { confirm(nil) }
    }

    private func confirm(_ maxOffset: CGFloat?) {
        withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.3)) {
            if let maxOffset { offset = maxOffset }
            isConfirmed = true
        }
        action()
        guard let resetAfter else { return }
        Task { @MainActor in
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(resetAfter))
            withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.2)) {
                offset = 0
                isConfirmed = false
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    SlideToConfirm("Slide to pay", color: .green) {}
        .frame(width: 280)
        .padding()
}

// MARK: - Haptics.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

import SwiftUI

/// The haptics the package plays. `SensoryFeedback` and `sensoryFeedback`
/// need visionOS 26, but the package supports visionOS 1, so call sites use
/// this enum and `.haptic(…)`, which does nothing on visionOS (it has no
/// haptics anyway).
enum Haptic: Equatable {
    case success
    case error
    case lightImpact

    #if !os(visionOS)
    var feedback: SensoryFeedback {
        switch self {
        case .success: .success
        case .error: .error
        case .lightImpact: .impact(weight: .light)
        }
    }
    #endif
}

extension View {
    /// Plays `haptic` every time `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays `haptic` when `trigger` changes and `condition` returns true.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (T, T) -> Bool) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger, condition: condition)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays the haptic returned by `haptic` (if any) when `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(trigger: T, _ haptic: @escaping (T, T) -> Haptic?) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(trigger: trigger) { old, new in haptic(old, new)?.feedback }
        #endif
    }
}
```

## Download Button (`download-button`)

A capsule shrinks into a progress ring, then pops into a checkmark.

- API: `DownloadButton(progress:) { }`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/DownloadButton.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/DownloadButton.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/Haptics.swift

### Usage

```swift
DownloadButton(progress: download.progress) {
    download.start()
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI DownloadButton(_ title:progress:color:action:) (iOS 17+) with three phases from progress: nil = idle, 0..<1 = loading, ≥ 1 = done. It's a ZStack whose frame is 150 × 44 when idle and 44 × 44 otherwise, over a Capsule filled with the colour (idle), secondary 12 % (loading) or green (done). Idle shows a white Label(title, systemImage: "arrow.down") with a scale 0.8 + opacity transition; loading shows a Circle trimmed to progress, stroked 4 pt with round caps, rotated −90°, padded 3 pt, and a small "stop.fill"; done shows a white "checkmark" with a scale-from-0.2 + opacity transition. Animate phase changes with .spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.35) so the capsule visibly shrinks into the ring, and play a success haptic when it finishes. The action only runs from the idle phase. With Reduce Motion on, use a 0.25 s ease instead of the spring.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A button that morphs through a download: a labelled capsule shrinks into
/// a circle whose ring fills with progress, then pops into a checkmark.
public struct DownloadButton: View {
    private let title: String
    private let progress: Double?
    private let color: Color
    private let action: () -> Void

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private enum Phase: Equatable { case idle, loading, done }

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - title: The label shown before the download starts.
    ///   - progress: `nil` = not started, 0..<1 = downloading, 1 = finished.
    ///   - color: Tint of the button and the ring.
    ///   - action: Called when the idle button is tapped.
    public init(_ title: String = "Download", progress: Double?, color: Color = .accentColor, action: @escaping () -> Void) {
        self.title = title
        self.progress = progress
        self.color = color
        self.action = action
    }

    private var phase: Phase {
        guard let progress else { return .idle }
        return progress >= 1 ? .done : .loading
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let size: CGFloat = 44
        Button {
            if phase == .idle { action() }
        } label: {
            ZStack {
                Capsule()
                    .fill(phase == .loading ? Color.secondary.opacity(0.12) : (phase == .done ? Color.green : color))

                if phase == .loading {
                    Circle()
                        .trim(from: 0, to: progress ?? 0)
                        .stroke(color, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 4, lineCap: .round))
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))
                        .padding(3)
                        .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2), value: progress)
                    Image(systemName: "stop.fill")
                        .font(.system(size: 12))
                        .foregroundStyle(color)
                }

                if phase == .idle {
                    Label(title, systemImage: "arrow.down")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .fixedSize()
                        .transition(.opacity.combined(with: .scale(scale: 0.8)))
                }

                if phase == .done {
                    Image(systemName: "checkmark")
                        .font(.system(size: 18, weight: .bold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .transition(.scale(scale: 0.2).combined(with: .opacity))
                }
            }
            .frame(width: phase == .idle ? 150 : size, height: size)
            .contentShape(Capsule())
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.25) : .spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.35), value: phase)
        .haptic(.success, trigger: phase) { _, new in new == .done }
        .accessibilityLabel(phase == .idle ? title : phase == .done ? "Downloaded" : "Downloading")
        .accessibilityValue(phase == .loading ? "\(Int((progress ?? 0) * 100)) percent" : "")
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var progress: Double?
        var body: some View {
            DownloadButton(progress: progress) {
                Task {
                    progress = 0
                    while let p = progress, p < 1 {
                        try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(60))
                        progress = min(1, p + 0.03)
                    }
                    try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.2))
                    progress = nil
                }
            }
            .padding()
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

/// need visionOS 26, but the package supports visionOS 1, so call sites use
/// this enum and `.haptic(…)`, which does nothing on visionOS (it has no
/// haptics anyway).
enum Haptic: Equatable {
    case success
    case error
    case lightImpact

    #if !os(visionOS)
    var feedback: SensoryFeedback {
        switch self {
        case .success: .success
        case .error: .error
        case .lightImpact: .impact(weight: .light)
        }
    }
    #endif
}

extension View {
    /// Plays `haptic` every time `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays `haptic` when `trigger` changes and `condition` returns true.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (T, T) -> Bool) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger, condition: condition)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays the haptic returned by `haptic` (if any) when `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(trigger: T, _ haptic: @escaping (T, T) -> Haptic?) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(trigger: trigger) { old, new in haptic(old, new)?.feedback }
        #endif
    }
}

## Star Rating (`star-rating`)

Stars fill one after another with a springy pop and a burst of sparks.

- API: `StarRating(rating:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/StarRating.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/StarRating.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/Haptics.swift

### Usage

```swift
StarRating(rating: $rating)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI StarRating(rating: Binding<Int>, maximum:color:size:) control (iOS 17+): an HStack (spacing size × 0.25) of SF Symbols "star.fill" (filled, yellow) or "star" (secondary 50 %), size 28 pt. Tapping star i sets rating = i. Each filled star runs keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 1, trigger: rating) on its scale: hold 1 for (i − 1) × 0.06 s, SpringKeyframe to 1.4 (0.15 s, .snappy), then to 1 (0.4 s, .bouncy), so they pop in sequence. Behind the tapped star, eight 4 pt dots at 45° steps fly out from size × 0.3 to size × 0.95 over 0.45 s while fading (after the same delay). Play a light haptic on change. Make the whole control one adjustable accessibility element ("Rating", "3 of 5"). With Reduce Motion on, skip the pops and sparks.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A star rating control. Tapping a star fills the stars up to it one after
/// another, each with a springy pop, and the tapped star bursts a ring of
/// sparks.
public struct StarRating: View {
    @Binding private var rating: Int
    private let maximum: Int
    private let color: Color
    private let size: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - rating: The number of filled stars, 0…maximum.
    ///   - maximum: How many stars to show.
    ///   - color: Colour of filled stars and sparks.
    ///   - size: Point size of each star.
    public init(rating: Binding<Int>, maximum: Int = 5, color: Color = .yellow, size: CGFloat = 28) {
        _rating = rating
        self.maximum = max(1, maximum)
        self.color = color
        self.size = size
    }

    public var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: size * 0.25) {
            ForEach(1...maximum, id: \.self) { index in
                star(index)
            }
        }
        .haptic(.lightImpact, trigger: rating)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Rating")
        .accessibilityValue("\(rating) of \(maximum)")
        .accessibilityAdjustableAction { direction in
            switch direction {
            case .increment: rating = min(maximum, rating + 1)
            case .decrement: rating = max(0, rating - 1)
            @unknown default: break
            }
        }
    }

    private func star(_ index: Int) -> some View {
        let filled = index <= rating
        // Keyframes must have a positive duration, so the first star waits a hair.
        let delay = max(0.001, Double(index - 1) * 0.06)
        let animate = filled && !reduceMotion
        return Image(systemName: filled ? "star.fill" : "star")
            .font(.system(size: size))
            .foregroundStyle(filled ? color : Color.secondary.opacity(0.5))
            .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 1.0, trigger: rating) { view, scale in
                view.scaleEffect(animate ? scale : 1)
            } keyframes: { _ in
                LinearKeyframe(1, duration: delay)
                SpringKeyframe(1.4, duration: 0.15, spring: .snappy)
                SpringKeyframe(1, duration: 0.4, spring: .bouncy)
            }
            .background {
                if index == rating && !reduceMotion {
                    StarSparks(color: color, size: size, trigger: rating, delay: delay)
                }
            }
            .contentShape(Rectangle())
            .onTapGesture { rating = index }
    }
}

/// Eight short dots that shoot out from the star and fade.
private struct StarSparks: View {
    let color: Color
    let size: CGFloat
    let trigger: Int
    let delay: Double

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(0..<8, id: \.self) { spark in
                Circle()
                    .fill(color)
                    .frame(width: 4, height: 4)
                    .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: SparkValues(), trigger: trigger) { view, value in
                        view
                            .offset(y: -value.distance)
                            .rotationEffect(.degrees(Double(spark) * 45))
                            .opacity(value.opacity)
                    } keyframes: { _ in
                        KeyframeTrack(\.distance) {
                            LinearKeyframe(size * 0.3, duration: delay)
                            CubicKeyframe(size * 0.95, duration: 0.45)
                        }
                        KeyframeTrack(\.opacity) {
                            LinearKeyframe(0, duration: delay)
                            LinearKeyframe(1, duration: 0.05)
                            LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.4)
                        }
                    }
            }
        }
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

private struct SparkValues {
    var distance: CGFloat = 0
    var opacity: Double = 0
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var rating = 3
        var body: some View {
            StarRating(rating: $rating).padding()
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - Haptics.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

/// need visionOS 26, but the package supports visionOS 1, so call sites use
/// this enum and `.haptic(…)`, which does nothing on visionOS (it has no
/// haptics anyway).
enum Haptic: Equatable {
    case success
    case error
    case lightImpact

    #if !os(visionOS)
    var feedback: SensoryFeedback {
        switch self {
        case .success: .success
        case .error: .error
        case .lightImpact: .impact(weight: .light)
        }
    }
    #endif
}

extension View {
    /// Plays `haptic` every time `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays `haptic` when `trigger` changes and `condition` returns true.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (T, T) -> Bool) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger, condition: condition)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays the haptic returned by `haptic` (if any) when `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(trigger: T, _ haptic: @escaping (T, T) -> Haptic?) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(trigger: trigger) { old, new in haptic(old, new)?.feedback }
        #endif
    }
}

## Bouncy Tab Bar (`bouncy-tab-bar`)

A pill glides to the selected tab and its icon squashes and hops.

- API: `BouncyTabBar(selection:items:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/BouncyTabBar.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/BouncyTabBar.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/Haptics.swift

### Usage

```swift
BouncyTabBar(selection: $tab, items: [
    .init("house.fill", "Home"),
    .init("magnifyingglass", "Search"),
    .init("person.fill", "Profile"),
])
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI BouncyTabBar(selection: Binding<Int>, items:color:) (iOS 17+) where each item is an SF Symbol and a title. Lay the tabs out in an HStack (spacing 4, padding 6) on a .regularMaterial Capsule with a soft shadow. Each tab is a plain Button with a VStack of the 18 pt semibold symbol and a caption2 title, tinted with the colour when selected (secondary otherwise), and a Capsule at 15 % of the colour behind the selected tab, shared with matchedGeometryEffect so it glides; selection changes use .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3). The selected icon runs keyframeAnimator(trigger: selection), anchored at the bottom: scaleX 1.25 → 0.9 → spring 1, scaleY 0.75 → 1.12 → spring 1, y 0 → −7 → spring 0 (0.08 s, 0.14 s, 0.3 s .bouncy). Play a light haptic. With Reduce Motion on, skip the hop.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A floating tab bar: a pill glides to the selected tab and its icon does a
/// little squash-and-hop.
public struct BouncyTabBar: View {
    /// One tab: an SF Symbol and a short title.
    public struct Item: Hashable, Sendable {
        public var symbol: String
        public var title: String

        public init(_ symbol: String, _ title: String) {
            self.symbol = symbol
            self.title = title
        }
    }

    @Binding private var selection: Int
    private let items: [Item]
    private let color: Color

    @Namespace private var namespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - selection: Index of the selected tab.
    ///   - items: The tabs, in order.
    ///   - color: Tint of the selected tab.
    public init(selection: Binding<Int>, items: [Item], color: Color = .accentColor) {
        _selection = selection
        self.items = items
        self.color = color
    }

    public var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 4) {
            ForEach(items.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                tab(index)
            }
        }
        .padding(6)
        .background(.regularMaterial, in: Capsule())
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.12), radius: 12, y: 4)
        .haptic(.lightImpact, trigger: selection)
    }

    private func tab(_ index: Int) -> some View {
        let selected = index == selection
        let bounce = selected && !reduceMotion
        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3)) {
                selection = index
            }
        } label: {
            VStack(spacing: 2) {
                Image(systemName: items[index].symbol)
                    .font(.system(size: 18, weight: .semibold))
                    .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: HopValues(), trigger: selection) { view, value in
                        view
                            .scaleEffect(x: bounce ? value.scaleX : 1, y: bounce ? value.scaleY : 1, anchor: .bottom)
                            .offset(y: bounce ? value.y : 0)
                    } keyframes: { _ in
                        KeyframeTrack(\.scaleX) {
                            CubicKeyframe(1.25, duration: 0.08)
                            CubicKeyframe(0.9, duration: 0.14)
                            SpringKeyframe(1, duration: 0.3, spring: .bouncy)
                        }
                        KeyframeTrack(\.scaleY) {
                            CubicKeyframe(0.75, duration: 0.08)
                            CubicKeyframe(1.12, duration: 0.14)
                            SpringKeyframe(1, duration: 0.3, spring: .bouncy)
                        }
                        KeyframeTrack(\.y) {
                            LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.08)
                            CubicKeyframe(-7, duration: 0.14)
                            SpringKeyframe(0, duration: 0.3, spring: .bouncy)
                        }
                    }
                Text(items[index].title)
                    .font(.caption2.weight(.semibold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(selected ? color : Color.secondary)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .padding(.vertical, 6)
            .background {
                if selected {
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(color.opacity(0.15))
                        .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "pill", in: namespace)
                }
            }
            .contentShape(Capsule())
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(items[index].title)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(selected ? [.isButton, .isSelected] : .isButton)
    }
}

private struct HopValues {
    var scaleX: CGFloat = 1
    var scaleY: CGFloat = 1
    var y: CGFloat = 0
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var tab = 0
        var body: some View {
            BouncyTabBar(selection: $tab, items: [
                .init("house.fill", "Home"),
                .init("magnifyingglass", "Search"),
                .init("heart.fill", "Saved"),
                .init("person.fill", "Profile"),
            ])
            .padding()
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - Haptics.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

/// The haptics the package plays. `SensoryFeedback` and `sensoryFeedback`
/// need visionOS 26, but the package supports visionOS 1, so call sites use
/// this enum and `.haptic(…)`, which does nothing on visionOS (it has no
/// haptics anyway).
enum Haptic: Equatable {
    case success
    case error
    case lightImpact

    #if !os(visionOS)
    var feedback: SensoryFeedback {
        switch self {
        case .success: .success
        case .error: .error
        case .lightImpact: .impact(weight: .light)
        }
    }
    #endif
}

extension View {
    /// Plays `haptic` every time `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays `haptic` when `trigger` changes and `condition` returns true.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (T, T) -> Bool) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger, condition: condition)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays the haptic returned by `haptic` (if any) when `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(trigger: T, _ haptic: @escaping (T, T) -> Haptic?) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(trigger: trigger) { old, new in haptic(old, new)?.feedback }
        #endif
    }
}

## Pull Cord (`pull-cord`)

A lamp cord toggle: pull the knob down, it clicks and springs back swinging.

- API: `PullCord(isOn:)`
- Component: Button
- Trigger: Drag / Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/PullCord.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Button/PullCord.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/Haptics.swift

### Usage

```swift
HStack(alignment: .top) {
    Image(systemName: lightsOn ? "lightbulb.max.fill" : "lightbulb")
    PullCord(isOn: $lightsOn)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI PullCord(isOn:length:color:) toggle (iOS 17+). A VStack(spacing: 0) of a 2 pt wide Rectangle (height length + stretch, default length 70) and a 16 × 26 Capsule knob, yellow with a yellow shadow (radius 8) when on. Rotate the whole cord with .rotationEffect(swing, anchor: .top) inside a 60 pt wide frame with room below to stretch. A DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) sets stretch = 1.6c × (1 − e^(−pull / 1.6c)) with c = 0.45 × length (rubber-band resistance) and swing = −translation.width / 6 clamped to ±18°. On release, toggle when stretch passed c or the drag was a tap (moved < 4 pt), play a light haptic, then spring stretch back to 0 with .spring(duration: 0.55, bounce: 0.6) and swing back with .spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.7). With Reduce Motion on, no swing and an ease-out return. Make it one accessibility element with the button trait, value On/Off and an action that toggles.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A toggle you pull like a lamp cord: drag the knob down, it stretches with
/// rubber-band resistance, and past the catch point it clicks, flips the
/// value and springs back up, swinging. A tap also toggles it.
///
/// ```swift
/// PullCord(isOn: $lightsOn)
/// ```
public struct PullCord: View {
    @Binding private var isOn: Bool
    private let length: CGFloat
    private let color: Color

    @State private var stretch: CGFloat = 0
    @State private var swing: Double = 0
    @State private var clicks = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isOn: The value the cord toggles.
    ///   - length: Length of the cord at rest, in points.
    ///   - color: Colour of the cord and knob.
    public init(isOn: Binding<Bool>, length: CGFloat = 70, color: Color = .primary) {
        _isOn = isOn
        self.length = length
        self.color = color
    }

    private var catchPoint: CGFloat { length * 0.45 }

    public var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 0) {
            Rectangle()
                .fill(color.opacity(0.7))
                .frame(width: 2, height: length + stretch)
            Capsule()
                .fill(isOn ? Color.yellow : color)
                .overlay(Capsule().strokeBorder(color.opacity(0.4), lineWidth: 1))
                .frame(width: 16, height: 26)
                .shadow(color: isOn ? .yellow.opacity(0.7) : .clear, radius: 8)
        }
        .rotationEffect(.degrees(swing), anchor: .top)
        .frame(width: 60, height: length + 26 + catchPoint * 1.6, alignment: .top)
        .contentShape(Rectangle())
        .gesture(
            DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
                .onChanged { value in
                    // Rubber band: easy at first, then stiffer.
                    let pull = max(0, value.translation.height)
                    stretch = catchPoint * 1.6 * (1 - exp(-pull / (catchPoint * 1.6)))
                    swing = reduceMotion ? 0 : Double(-value.translation.width / 6).clamped(to: -18...18)
                }
                .onEnded { value in
                    let pulled = stretch > catchPoint || (abs(value.translation.height) < 4 && abs(value.translation.width) < 4)
                    if pulled { toggle() }
                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.55, bounce: 0.6)) {
                        stretch = 0
                    }
                    if reduceMotion {
                        swing = 0
                    } else {
                        // Swing out a little the other way, then settle.
                        withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.7)) { swing = 0 }
                    }
                }
        )
        .haptic(.lightImpact, trigger: clicks)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Pull cord")
        .accessibilityValue(isOn ? "On" : "Off")
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
        .accessibilityAction { toggle() }
    }

    private func toggle() {
        isOn.toggle()
        clicks += 1
    }
}

private extension Double {
    func clamped(to range: ClosedRange<Double>) -> Double { Swift.min(range.upperBound, Swift.max(range.lowerBound, self)) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var on = false
        var body: some View {
            ZStack(alignment: .top) {
                (on ? Color.yellow.opacity(0.15) : Color.black.opacity(0.05))
                PullCord(isOn: $on)
            }
            .frame(width: 200, height: 220)
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - Haptics.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

import SwiftUI

/// The haptics the package plays. `SensoryFeedback` and `sensoryFeedback`
/// need visionOS 26, but the package supports visionOS 1, so call sites use
/// this enum and `.haptic(…)`, which does nothing on visionOS (it has no
/// haptics anyway).
enum Haptic: Equatable {
    case success
    case error
    case lightImpact

    #if !os(visionOS)
    var feedback: SensoryFeedback {
        switch self {
        case .success: .success
        case .error: .error
        case .lightImpact: .impact(weight: .light)
        }
    }
    #endif
}

extension View {
    /// Plays `haptic` every time `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays `haptic` when `trigger` changes and `condition` returns true.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(_ haptic: Haptic, trigger: T, condition: @escaping (T, T) -> Bool) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(haptic.feedback, trigger: trigger, condition: condition)
        #endif
    }

    /// Plays the haptic returned by `haptic` (if any) when `trigger` changes.
    func haptic<T: Equatable>(trigger: T, _ haptic: @escaping (T, T) -> Haptic?) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        self
        #else
        sensoryFeedback(trigger: trigger) { old, new in haptic(old, new)?.feedback }
        #endif
    }
}
```

## Staggered Entrance (`staggered-appear`)

List items fade and rise into place one after another.

- API: `.staggeredAppear(index:)`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/StaggeredAppear.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/StaggeredAppear.swift

### Usage

```swift
ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
    CardView(item)
        .staggeredAppear(index: index)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .staggeredAppear(index:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for list and grid entrances. Each item starts at opacity 0, offset 24 pt down and scale 0.96, then on appear animates to its resting state with .spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.8), delayed by index × 0.08 s so the items cascade in. Delay per item and travel distance are configurable.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Items fade, rise and settle into place one after another when they first
/// appear.
struct StaggeredAppearModifier: ViewModifier {
    var index: Int
    var delayPerItem: Double
    var distance: CGFloat

    @State private var visible = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .opacity(visible ? 1 : 0)
            // Reduce Motion: fade only.
            .offset(y: visible || reduceMotion ? 0 : distance)
            .scaleEffect(visible || reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.96)
            .onAppear {
                withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.8).delay(Double(index) * delayPerItem)) {
                    visible = true
                }
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Staggered entrance. Give each item in a list its position.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
    ///     CardView(item)
    ///         .staggeredAppear(index: index)
    /// }
    /// ```
    func staggeredAppear(index: Int, delayPerItem: Double = 0.08, distance: CGFloat = 24) -> some View {
        modifier(StaggeredAppearModifier(index: index, delayPerItem: delayPerItem, distance: distance))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 12) {
        ForEach(0..<5, id: \.self) { index in
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                .fill(Color.accentColor.opacity(0.2 + Double(index) * 0.15))
                .frame(height: 56)
                .staggeredAppear(index: index)
        }
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## 3D Tilt (`tilt`)

Card tilts in 3D toward the finger with a moving glare, then springs flat.

- API: `.tiltOnDrag()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/Tilt.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/Tilt.swift

### Usage

```swift
CardView()
    .tiltOnDrag(maxAngle: 15, cornerRadius: 20)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .tiltOnDrag() view modifier (iOS 17+). While the user drags on the view, convert the drag translation into a normalised -1…1 value per axis (120 pt = full tilt) and apply two rotation3DEffects (x axis from vertical drag, y axis from horizontal drag) up to a max angle of ~12°, plus a 1.03 scale. Overlay a white glare gradient whose start/end points follow the tilt and which is only visible while dragging, clipped to the card's corner radius. Use .interactiveSpring while dragging and a bouncy spring back to flat on release.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// 3D card tilt that follows the finger, with a moving glare, then springs
/// back flat on release.
struct TiltModifier: ViewModifier {
    var maxAngle: Double
    var glare: Bool
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat

    /// Normalised drag, each axis in -1...1.
    @State private var tilt: CGSize = .zero
    @State private var isDragging = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// Translation (in points) that maps to the maximum angle.
    private let range: CGFloat = 120

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                if glare {
                    LinearGradient(
                        colors: [.white.opacity(isDragging ? 0.35 : 0), .clear],
                        startPoint: UnitPoint(x: 0.5 - tilt.width * 0.5, y: 0.5 - tilt.height * 0.5),
                        endPoint: UnitPoint(x: 0.5 + tilt.width * 0.5, y: 0.5 + tilt.height * 0.5)
                    )
                    .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
                }
            }
            // Reduce Motion: keep the glare and the lift, drop the rotation.
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(Double(-tilt.height) * angle), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0))
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(Double(tilt.width) * angle), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0))
            .scaleEffect(isDragging ? 1.03 : 1)
            .gesture(
                DragGesture()
                    .onChanged { value in
                        withAnimation(.interactiveSpring()) {
                            isDragging = true
                            tilt = CGSize(
                                width: clamp(value.translation.width / range),
                                height: clamp(value.translation.height / range)
                            )
                        }
                    }
                    .onEnded { _ in
                        withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.55)) {
                            isDragging = false
                            tilt = .zero
                        }
                    }
            )
    }

    private var angle: Double { reduceMotion ? 0 : maxAngle }

    private func clamp(_ value: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        min(1, max(-1, value))
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Tilts the view in 3D while it is dragged.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// CardView()
    ///     .tiltOnDrag(maxAngle: 15, cornerRadius: 20)
    /// ```
    func tiltOnDrag(maxAngle: Double = 12, glare: Bool = true, cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16) -> some View {
        modifier(TiltModifier(maxAngle: maxAngle, glare: glare, cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)
        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.purple, .blue], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
        .frame(width: 220, height: 300)
        .tiltOnDrag(cornerRadius: 20)
        .padding(40)
}
```

## Scroll Reveal (`scroll-reveal`)

Rows scale up and come into focus as they enter the visible area.

- API: `.scrollReveal()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ScrollReveal.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ScrollReveal.swift

### Usage

```swift
ScrollView {
    LazyVStack {
        ForEach(items) { item in
            Row(item).scrollReveal()
        }
    }
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .scrollReveal() view modifier (iOS 17+) using scrollTransition(.interactive). When an item is fully inside the scroll view (phase.isIdentity) it is at full opacity, scale 1 and no blur; as it moves toward the top or bottom edge it interpolates to opacity 0.3, scale 0.85 and a 2 pt blur. Axis, minimum scale, minimum opacity and blur amount should be parameters.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

public extension View {
    /// Items scale up and come into focus as they scroll into the visible
    /// area, and fade back out as they leave. Use inside a `ScrollView`.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ScrollView {
    ///     LazyVStack {
    ///         ForEach(items) { item in
    ///             Row(item).scrollReveal()
    ///         }
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    func scrollReveal(
        axis: Axis = .vertical,
        minScale: CGFloat = 0.85,
        minOpacity: Double = 0.3,
        blur: CGFloat = 2
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ScrollRevealModifier(axis: axis, minScale: minScale, minOpacity: minOpacity, blur: blur))
    }
}

struct ScrollRevealModifier: ViewModifier {
    var axis: Axis
    var minScale: CGFloat
    var minOpacity: Double
    var blur: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: keep the fade, drop the scaling and blur.
        let minScale = reduceMotion ? 1 : minScale
        let blur = reduceMotion ? 0 : blur
        let minOpacity = minOpacity
        return content.scrollTransition(.interactive, axis: axis) { view, phase in
            view
                .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : minOpacity)
                .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : minScale)
                .blur(radius: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : blur)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollView {
        LazyVStack(spacing: 12) {
            ForEach(0..<30, id: \.self) { index in
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14)
                    .fill(Color.accentColor.gradient)
                    .frame(height: 80)
                    .overlay(Text("Row \(index)").foregroundStyle(.white))
                    .scrollReveal()
            }
        }
        .padding()
    }
}
```

## Flip Card (`flip-card`)

A two-sided card turns over in 3D with a spring.

- API: `FlipCard(isFlipped:) { } back: { }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/FlipCard.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/FlipCard.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var flipped = false

FlipCard(isFlipped: flipped) {
    QuestionView()
} back: {
    AnswerView()
}
.frame(width: 220, height: 300)
.onTapGesture { flipped.toggle() }
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI FlipCard<Front, Back> view (iOS 17+) with isFlipped and axis (horizontal or vertical) parameters and front/back view builders. Stack both faces in a ZStack and give each an Animatable view modifier holding the animated angle (0 or 180°). The back face uses angle − 180 so it reads correctly once turned. Each face applies rotation3DEffect around the y axis (or x for vertical) with perspective 0.5 and sets opacity to 1 only while |faceAngle| < 90°, so the faces swap exactly at the halfway point and the back never shows mirrored. Animate isFlipped changes with spring(response 0.6, damping 0.75). Hide the hidden face from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, cross-fade instead of rotating.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A two-sided card that turns over in 3D, showing `back` when `isFlipped`
/// is true. The faces swap exactly at 90°, so the back never shows mirrored.
public struct FlipCard<Front: View, Back: View>: View {
    private let isFlipped: Bool
    private let axis: Axis
    private let front: Front
    private let back: Back

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isFlipped: Shows the back when true.
    ///   - axis: `.horizontal` turns like a page (around the vertical axis),
    ///     `.vertical` tumbles top over bottom.
    public init(
        isFlipped: Bool,
        axis: Axis = .horizontal,
        @ViewBuilder front: () -> Front,
        @ViewBuilder back: () -> Back
    ) {
        self.isFlipped = isFlipped
        self.axis = axis
        self.front = front()
        self.back = back()
    }

    public var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            // Cross-fade instead of turning.
            ZStack {
                front.opacity(isFlipped ? 0 : 1)
                back.opacity(isFlipped ? 1 : 0)
            }
            .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: isFlipped)
        } else {
            ZStack {
                front.modifier(FlipFace(angle: isFlipped ? 180 : 0, axis: axis, isBack: false))
                back.modifier(FlipFace(angle: isFlipped ? 180 : 0, axis: axis, isBack: true))
            }
            .animation(.spring(response: 0.6, dampingFraction: 0.75), value: isFlipped)
        }
    }
}

/// Rotates one face by `angle` and hides it while it faces away.
private struct FlipFace: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var angle: Double
    var axis: Axis
    var isBack: Bool

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { angle }
        set { angle = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // The back starts already turned 180° so it reads correctly when shown.
        let faceAngle = isBack ? angle - 180 : angle
        let visible = abs(faceAngle) < 90
        content
            .opacity(visible ? 1 : 0)
            .accessibilityHidden(!visible)
            .rotation3DEffect(
                .degrees(faceAngle),
                axis: axis == .horizontal ? (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0) : (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0),
                perspective: 0.5
            )
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var flipped = false

        var body: some View {
            FlipCard(isFlipped: flipped) {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20).fill(.blue.gradient)
                    .overlay(Text("Front").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
            } back: {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20).fill(.orange.gradient)
                    .overlay(Text("Back").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
            }
            .frame(width: 200, height: 260)
            .onTapGesture { flipped.toggle() }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Swipe Card Stack (`swipe-stack`)

Tinder-style deck: drag the top card away and the pile moves up.

- API: `SwipeCardStack(items) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/SwipeCardStack.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/SwipeCardStack.swift

### Usage

```swift
SwipeCardStack(profiles) { profile, direction in
    direction == .right ? like(profile) : pass(profile)
} card: { profile in
    ProfileCard(profile)
        .frame(width: 300, height: 420)
}
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI SwipeCardStack (iOS 17+) over a collection of Identifiable items with a card view builder and an onSwipe(item, direction) callback. Show the top 3 cards from the current position (looping by default). Cards behind are scaled down 5% per level and moved down 12 pt per level. The top card follows a DragGesture: offset by the translation, rotate by translation.width / 20 degrees around the bottom anchor, and overlay a green (right) or red (left) wash, masked by the card, whose opacity grows to 25% at the threshold. On release, if the predicted end translation passes 110 pt, fly the card 600 pt off in that direction with easeIn(0.25), then reset the drag without animation, advance the position with a spring so the pile moves up, and call onSwipe. Otherwise spring back. Add Swipe left and Swipe right accessibility actions.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Which way a card left the stack.
public enum SwipeDirection: Sendable {
    case left
    case right
}

/// A Tinder-style deck. The top card follows the finger and tilts; past a
/// threshold it flies off and the cards behind move up. Drag less and it
/// springs back.
public struct SwipeCardStack<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Card: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    private let items: Data
    private let visibleCount: Int
    private let loops: Bool
    private let onSwipe: (Data.Element, SwipeDirection) -> Void
    private let card: (Data.Element) -> Card

    @State private var position = 0
    @State private var drag: CGSize = .zero
    @State private var flyingOff: SwipeDirection?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let threshold: CGFloat = 110

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: The cards, top card first.
    ///   - visibleCount: How many cards are drawn in the pile.
    ///   - loops: Starts over from the first card when the deck runs out.
    ///   - onSwipe: Called after a card leaves, with the direction it went.
    ///   - card: Builds the view for one item.
    public init(
        _ items: Data,
        visibleCount: Int = 3,
        loops: Bool = true,
        onSwipe: @escaping (Data.Element, SwipeDirection) -> Void = { _, _ in },
        @ViewBuilder card: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Card
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.visibleCount = visibleCount
        self.loops = loops
        self.onSwipe = onSwipe
        self.card = card
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let elements = Array(items)
        ZStack {
            ForEach(Array(visibleCards(elements).enumerated()).reversed(), id: \.element.id) { depth, item in
                card(item)
                    .modifier(StackedCard(depth: depth, drag: depth == 0 ? drag : .zero, threshold: threshold))
                    .allowsHitTesting(depth == 0)
                    .gesture(depth == 0 ? dragGesture(for: item) : nil)
                    .accessibilityHidden(depth != 0)
                    .accessibilityActions {
                        Button("Swipe left") { swipe(item, .left) }
                        Button("Swipe right") { swipe(item, .right) }
                    }
            }
        }
    }

    private func visibleCards(_ elements: [Data.Element]) -> [Data.Element] {
        guard !elements.isEmpty else { return [] }
        let remaining = loops ? elements.count : max(0, elements.count - position)
        return (0..<min(visibleCount, remaining)).map { elements[(position + $0) % elements.count] }
    }

    private func dragGesture(for item: Data.Element) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture()
            .onChanged { value in
                guard flyingOff == nil else { return }
                drag = value.translation
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                guard flyingOff == nil else { return }
                // Use the predicted end so a quick flick counts too.
                let x = value.predictedEndTranslation.width
                if abs(x) > threshold {
                    swipe(item, x > 0 ? .right : .left)
                } else {
                    withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.6)) { drag = .zero }
                }
            }
    }

    private func swipe(_ item: Data.Element, _ direction: SwipeDirection) {
        flyingOff = direction
        let distance: CGFloat = direction == .right ? 600 : -600
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.2) : .easeIn(duration: 0.25)) {
            drag = CGSize(width: distance, height: drag.height + 40)
        }
        DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.25) {
            var transaction = Transaction()
            transaction.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(transaction) { drag = .zero }
            withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.8)) { position += 1 }
            flyingOff = nil
            onSwipe(item, direction)
        }
    }
}

/// Places a card in the pile: deeper cards are smaller and lower; the top
/// card follows the drag and tilts away from it.
private struct StackedCard: ViewModifier {
    var depth: Int
    var drag: CGSize
    var threshold: CGFloat

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                // Green or red wash that grows as the card nears the threshold.
                let progress = min(1, abs(drag.width) / threshold)
                (drag.width > 0 ? Color.green : Color.red)
                    .opacity(depth == 0 ? Double(progress) * 0.25 : 0)
                    .mask { content }
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
            .scaleEffect(1 - CGFloat(depth) * 0.05)
            .offset(y: CGFloat(depth) * 12)
            .offset(drag)
            .rotationEffect(.degrees(Double(drag.width / 20)), anchor: .bottom)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Item: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let color: Color
    }
    let items = [Color.pink, .orange, .teal, .indigo].enumerated().map { Item(id: $0, color: $1) }
    return SwipeCardStack(items) { item in
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)
            .fill(item.color.gradient)
            .frame(width: 220, height: 300)
            .overlay(Text("Card \(item.id + 1)").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
    }
    .padding(40)
}
```

## Parallax Carousel (`parallax-carousel`)

Paging cards whose images slide slower than the cards, for depth.

- API: `ParallaxCarousel(items) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ParallaxCarousel.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ParallaxCarousel.swift

### Usage

```swift
ParallaxCarousel(places) { place in
    Image(place.photo)
        .resizable()
        .scaledToFill()
}
.frame(height: 240)
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI ParallaxCarousel (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with an optional selection binding. Use a horizontal ScrollView with a LazyHStack (14 pt spacing), .scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), hidden indicators, .scrollPosition(id:anchor: .center), and horizontal contentMargins so each card (78% of the width) snaps to the centre with neighbours peeking. Draw each card's content wider than the card by the parallax factor (0.35), then use .visualEffect to read the card's frame in the .scrollView coordinate space and offset the content by −(distance of the card centre from the viewport centre) × parallax. Finally frame it to the card size and clip it with a continuous rounded rectangle (22 pt), so the image appears to move slower than its frame. With Reduce Motion on, set parallax to 0.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A paging carousel whose card contents slide slower than the cards
/// themselves, so images seem to sit deeper than the frame around them.
/// Neighbouring cards peek in from both sides.
public struct ParallaxCarousel<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Content: View>: View where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    private let items: Data
    private let selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>?
    private let cardWidth: CGFloat
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let cornerRadius: CGFloat
    private let parallax: CGFloat
    private let content: (Data.Element) -> Content

    @State private var internalSelection: Data.Element.ID?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: One card per item.
    ///   - selection: Optional binding to the centred card; set it to scroll.
    ///   - cardWidth: Card width as a fraction of the carousel's width.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between cards.
    ///   - cornerRadius: Corner radius of each card.
    ///   - parallax: How much slower the content moves than its card (0…1).
    ///   - content: The card's content, usually an image. It is drawn wider
    ///     than the card so the parallax never reveals an edge.
    public init(
        _ items: Data,
        selection: Binding<Data.Element.ID?>? = nil,
        cardWidth: CGFloat = 0.78,
        spacing: CGFloat = 14,
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 22,
        parallax: CGFloat = 0.35,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.selection = selection
        self.cardWidth = cardWidth
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.cornerRadius = cornerRadius
        self.parallax = parallax
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let width = geometry.size.width * cardWidth
            let strength = reduceMotion ? 0 : parallax
            ScrollView(.horizontal) {
                LazyHStack(spacing: spacing) {
                    ForEach(items) { item in
                        content(item)
                            // Extra width on both sides for the content to slide into.
                            .frame(width: width * (1 + strength), height: geometry.size.height)
                            .visualEffect { view, proxy in
                                // How far this card's centre is from the carousel's centre.
                                let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))
                                let viewport = proxy.bounds(of: .scrollView(axis: .horizontal))?.width ?? frame.width
                                let distance = frame.midX - viewport / 2
                                return view.offset(x: -distance * strength)
                            }
                            .frame(width: width, height: geometry.size.height)
                            .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                            .id(item.id)
                    }
                }
                .scrollTargetLayout()
            }
            .contentMargins(.horizontal, (geometry.size.width - width) / 2, for: .scrollContent)
            .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
            .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
            .scrollPosition(id: selection ?? $internalSelection, anchor: .center)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Place: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let colors: [Color]
    }
    let places = [
        Place(id: 0, colors: [.orange, .pink]),
        Place(id: 1, colors: [.teal, .blue]),
        Place(id: 2, colors: [.purple, .indigo]),
        Place(id: 3, colors: [.mint, .green]),
    ]
    return ParallaxCarousel(places) { place in
        LinearGradient(colors: place.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
            .overlay(Image(systemName: "mountain.2.fill").font(.system(size: 60)).foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.8)))
    }
    .frame(height: 220)
}
```

## Expandable Card (`expandable-card`)

Tap the header and the card springs open, un-blurring its detail.

- API: `ExpandableCard(isExpanded:) { } detail: { }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ExpandableCard.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ExpandableCard.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var isOpen = false

ExpandableCard(isExpanded: $isOpen) {
    Text("Shipping").font(.headline)
} detail: {
    Text("Arrives Thursday. Free returns within 30 days.")
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ExpandableCard<Header, Detail> (iOS 17+) bound to isExpanded. A VStack holds a plain-style Button containing the header, a spacer and a chevron.down that rotates −180° when open, then, if expanded, the detail view. Toggle inside withAnimation(.spring(response 0.45, damping 0.8)) so the card's height springs. Insert the detail with a combined transition of opacity, an 8 pt upward offset and a custom blur transition (radius 6 → 0). The background is a continuous rounded rectangle (16 pt) filled with the background style whose shadow deepens when open. Expose Expanded/Collapsed as the accessibility value. With Reduce Motion on, use a short ease and an opacity transition only.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A card with a tappable header that expands to reveal its detail. The
/// height springs open, the chevron turns, and the detail un-blurs into place.
/// Stack several for an accordion.
public struct ExpandableCard<Header: View, Detail: View>: View {
    @Binding private var isExpanded: Bool
    private let cornerRadius: CGFloat
    private let header: Header
    private let detail: Detail

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isExpanded: Whether the detail is showing.
    ///   - cornerRadius: Corner radius of the card.
    ///   - header: Always visible; tapping it toggles the card.
    ///   - detail: Shown below the header when expanded.
    public init(
        isExpanded: Binding<Bool>,
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16,
        @ViewBuilder header: () -> Header,
        @ViewBuilder detail: () -> Detail
    ) {
        _isExpanded = isExpanded
        self.cornerRadius = cornerRadius
        self.header = header()
        self.detail = detail()
    }

    public var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
            Button {
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.8)) {
                    isExpanded.toggle()
                }
            } label: {
                HStack {
                    header
                    Spacer(minLength: 8)
                    Image(systemName: "chevron.down")
                        .font(.footnote.weight(.semibold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(isExpanded ? -180 : 0))
                }
                .padding()
                .contentShape(Rectangle())
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .accessibilityValue(isExpanded ? Text("Expanded") : Text("Collapsed"))

            if isExpanded {
                detail
                    .padding([.horizontal, .bottom])
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                    .transition(
                        reduceMotion
                            ? .opacity
                            : .opacity.combined(with: .offset(y: -8)).combined(with: BlurTransition.blur)
                    )
            }
        }
        .background(
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous)
                .fill(.background)
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(isExpanded ? 0.12 : 0.06), radius: isExpanded ? 12 : 4, y: isExpanded ? 6 : 2)
        )
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
    }
}

/// Blurs a view while it is inserted or removed.
private struct BlurTransition: ViewModifier {
    var radius: CGFloat

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.blur(radius: radius)
    }

    static var blur: AnyTransition {
        .modifier(active: BlurTransition(radius: 6), identity: BlurTransition(radius: 0))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var open = [true, false, false]

        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 12) {
                ForEach(0..<3) { index in
                    ExpandableCard(isExpanded: $open[index]) {
                        Text("Question \(index + 1)").font(.headline)
                    } detail: {
                        Text("Answers expand smoothly with a spring, and the detail fades and un-blurs into place.")
                            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    }
                }
            }
            .padding()
            .background(Color.gray.opacity(0.1))
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Hero Expand (`hero-expand`)

A thumbnail grows into a full detail card, morphing with matchedGeometryEffect.

- API: `HeroGrid(items) { thumbnail } detail: { }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/HeroGrid.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/HeroGrid.swift

### Usage

```swift
HeroGrid(photos, columns: 3) { photo in
    Image(photo.thumbnail).resizable().scaledToFill().frame(height: 90)
} detail: { photo in
    PhotoDetail(photo)
}
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI HeroGrid (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with columns (3), spacing (10), cornerRadius (14) and two view builders: thumbnail and detail. Keep @State selected: Item.ID? and a @Namespace. In a ZStack, show a LazyVGrid of flexible columns; for each item, if it isn't selected show a plain Button with the thumbnail clipped to a continuous rounded rectangle and .matchedGeometryEffect(id: item.id, in: namespace), otherwise show the thumbnail .hidden() to keep the slot. Dim the grid to 30 % while something is selected. Above it, if selected, show the detail in a Button sized maxWidth/maxHeight .infinity, clipped the same way, with the same matchedGeometryEffect id and zIndex 1. Open with withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.82)) and close by tapping the detail. Both views get an .opacity transition so their content cross-fades while the frame morphs. With Reduce Motion on, pass properties: [] to matchedGeometryEffect so it only cross-fades.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A grid of thumbnails where tapping one grows it into a detail card that
/// fills the grid, morphing frame and corners with `matchedGeometryEffect`.
/// Tapping the detail shrinks it back into its slot.
public struct HeroGrid<Item: Identifiable, Thumbnail: View, Detail: View>: View {
    private let items: [Item]
    private let columns: Int
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let cornerRadius: CGFloat
    private let thumbnail: (Item) -> Thumbnail
    private let detail: (Item) -> Detail

    @State private var selected: Item.ID?
    @Namespace private var namespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: The items to show.
    ///   - columns: Number of grid columns.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between cells, in points.
    ///   - cornerRadius: Corner radius of thumbnails and the detail card.
    ///   - thumbnail: The small cell for an item. Give it a background so the
    ///     morph has something to stretch.
    ///   - detail: The expanded card for an item.
    public init(
        _ items: [Item],
        columns: Int = 3,
        spacing: CGFloat = 10,
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 14,
        @ViewBuilder thumbnail: @escaping (Item) -> Thumbnail,
        @ViewBuilder detail: @escaping (Item) -> Detail
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.columns = columns
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.cornerRadius = cornerRadius
        self.thumbnail = thumbnail
        self.detail = detail
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: cross-fade in place of the morph.
        let morph: MatchedGeometryProperties = reduceMotion ? [] : .frame
        ZStack {
            LazyVGrid(columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: spacing), count: max(1, columns)), spacing: spacing) {
                ForEach(items) { item in
                    ZStack {
                        if selected != item.id {
                            Button { open(item.id) } label: {
                                thumbnail(item)
                                    .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                            }
                            .buttonStyle(.plain)
                            .matchedGeometryEffect(id: item.id, in: namespace, properties: morph)
                            .transition(.opacity.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.15)))
                        } else {
                            // Keep the slot so the grid doesn't reflow.
                            thumbnail(item).hidden()
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            .opacity(selected == nil ? 1 : 0.3)

            if let id = selected, let item = items.first(where: { $0.id == id }) {
                Button { close() } label: {
                    detail(item)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
                        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .matchedGeometryEffect(id: id, in: namespace, properties: morph)
                .transition(.opacity.animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.15)))
                .zIndex(1)
            }
        }
    }

    private func open(_ id: Item.ID) {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.25) : .spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.82)) {
            selected = id
        }
    }

    private func close() {
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.25) : .spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.85)) {
            selected = nil
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Tile: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let color: Color
    }
    let tiles = [Color.pink, .orange, .teal, .indigo, .mint, .purple].enumerated().map { Tile(id: $0.offset, color: $0.element) }
    return HeroGrid(tiles) { tile in
        tile.color.frame(height: 70)
    } detail: { tile in
        tile.color.overlay(Text("Tile \(tile.id + 1)").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
    }
    .frame(width: 300, height: 160)
    .padding()
}
```
