## Spotlight Card (`spotlight-card`)

A soft glow follows the pointer across the card, like a torch.

- API: `.spotlight()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Hover / Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/Spotlight.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/Spotlight.swift

### Usage

```swift
FeatureCard()
    .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))
    .spotlight()

PricingCard()
    .spotlight(color: .purple.opacity(0.4), radius: 160)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .spotlight(color:radius:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Track the pointer with .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) and a finger with a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0); store the location in @State (nil when the pointer leaves or the drag ends) and remember the last location so the glow can fade out where it was. In an overlay GeometryReader, draw a RadialGradient from color (white 35 %) to clear, centred at the location converted to a UnitPoint, endRadius = radius (120 pt), and mask it with the content so it only lights the card. Move with .interactiveSpring(response: 0.2, dampingFraction: 0.9) and fade out with easeOut(0.35 s). Disable hit testing on the glow. With Reduce Motion on, move the glow without animation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A soft glow that follows the pointer (or a dragging finger) across the
/// view, like a torch shone on the card. Fades out when the pointer leaves.
struct SpotlightModifier: ViewModifier {
    var color: Color
    var radius: CGFloat

    @State private var location: CGPoint?
    @State private var lastLocation: CGPoint = .zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                GeometryReader { geometry in
                    let size = geometry.size
                    let point = location ?? lastLocation
                    RadialGradient(
                        colors: [color, color.opacity(0)],
                        center: UnitPoint(x: size.width > 0 ? point.x / size.width : 0.5,
                                          y: size.height > 0 ? point.y / size.height : 0.5),
                        startRadius: 0,
                        endRadius: radius
                    )
                    .opacity(location == nil ? 0 : 1)
                }
                .mask { content }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) { phase in
                switch phase {
                case let .active(point): move(to: point)
                case .ended: hide()
                }
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0, coordinateSpace: .local)
                    .onChanged { move(to: $0.location) }
                    .onEnded { _ in hide() }
            )
    }

    private func move(to point: CGPoint) {
        // Reduce Motion: no glide, the glow jumps with the pointer.
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .interactiveSpring(response: 0.2, dampingFraction: 0.9)) {
            location = point
            lastLocation = point
        }
    }

    private func hide() {
        withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.35)) { location = nil }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shines a soft glow on the view where the pointer or finger is.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// FeatureCard()
    ///     .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))
    ///     .spotlight()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - color: Colour at the centre of the glow.
    ///   - radius: Radius of the glow, in points.
    func spotlight(color: Color = .white.opacity(0.35), radius: CGFloat = 120) -> some View {
        modifier(SpotlightModifier(color: color, radius: radius))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)
        .fill(Color(white: 0.1))
        .frame(width: 260, height: 160)
        .overlay(Text("Hover me").font(.headline).foregroundStyle(.white))
        .spotlight()
        .padding()
}
```

## Magnifying Dock (`dock`)

Icons swell as the pointer passes over them, like the macOS Dock.

- API: `MagnifyingDock(items) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Hover / Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/MagnifyingDock.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/MagnifyingDock.swift

### Usage

```swift
MagnifyingDock(apps) { app in
    Image(app.icon).resizable()
}
.background(.ultraThinMaterial, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16))
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI MagnifyingDock (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with size (40 pt), magnification (1.8), range (110 pt), spacing (8) and a content builder. Lay the items out in an HStack(alignment: .bottom) and frame each icon to size × scale(i). Put the HStack in a frame exactly as wide as the resting row (count × size + gaps) and size × magnification tall, aligned to the bottom, so the magnified row overflows it evenly; track the pointer x on that frame with .onContinuousHover and a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0). scale(i) = 1 + (magnification − 1) × cos(d / range × π/2) where d is the distance from the pointer to the icon's resting centre (i × (size + spacing) + size/2), or 1 beyond range. Animate pointer changes with .interactiveSpring(response: 0.2) and the release with .spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.75). Add horizontal padding for the overflow. With Reduce Motion on, don't magnify.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A row of icons that swell as the pointer (or a dragging finger) passes
/// over them, like the macOS Dock. Neighbours grow a little too.
public struct MagnifyingDock<Item: Identifiable, Content: View>: View {
    private let items: [Item]
    private let size: CGFloat
    private let magnification: CGFloat
    private let range: CGFloat
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let content: (Item) -> Content

    @State private var pointerX: CGFloat?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: The items to show.
    ///   - size: Resting icon size, in points.
    ///   - magnification: Scale of the icon right under the pointer.
    ///   - range: Distance in points over which neighbours still grow.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between icons.
    ///   - content: The icon for an item; it is sized to fill a square.
    public init(
        _ items: [Item],
        size: CGFloat = 40,
        magnification: CGFloat = 1.8,
        range: CGFloat = 110,
        spacing: CGFloat = 8,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Item) -> Content
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.size = size
        self.magnification = magnification
        self.range = range
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing: spacing) {
            ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
                let side = size * scale(for: index)
                content(item)
                    .frame(width: side, height: side)
            }
        }
        // A frame the size of the resting row: the magnified row overflows it
        // evenly on both sides, and the pointer is measured in resting
        // coordinates, so the icons don't run away from it.
        .frame(width: restingWidth, height: size * magnification, alignment: .bottom)
        .contentShape(Rectangle())
        .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) { phase in
            switch phase {
            case let .active(point): track(point.x)
            case .ended: track(nil)
            }
        }
        .simultaneousGesture(
            DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0, coordinateSpace: .local)
                .onChanged { track($0.location.x) }
                .onEnded { _ in track(nil) }
        )
        .padding(.horizontal, size * (magnification - 1) + spacing)
        .padding(.vertical, 6)
    }

    private var restingWidth: CGFloat {
        CGFloat(items.count) * size + CGFloat(max(0, items.count - 1)) * spacing
    }

    /// Scale of the icon at `index`: a cosine falloff of the distance between
    /// its resting centre and the pointer.
    private func scale(for index: Int) -> CGFloat {
        guard let pointerX, !reduceMotion else { return 1 }
        let restingCentre = CGFloat(index) * (size + spacing) + size / 2
        let distance = abs(pointerX - restingCentre)
        guard distance < range else { return 1 }
        let falloff = cos(distance / range * .pi / 2)
        return 1 + (magnification - 1) * falloff
    }

    private func track(_ x: CGFloat?) {
        withAnimation(x == nil ? .spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.75) : .interactiveSpring(response: 0.2, dampingFraction: 0.85)) {
            pointerX = x
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct App: Identifiable {
        let id: String
        let color: Color
    }
    let apps = [("message.fill", Color.green), ("safari.fill", .blue), ("music.note", .pink), ("photo.fill", .orange), ("gearshape.fill", .gray)]
        .map { App(id: $0.0, color: $0.1) }
    return MagnifyingDock(apps) { app in
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 10, style: .continuous)
            .fill(app.color.gradient)
            .overlay(Image(systemName: app.id).foregroundStyle(.white))
    }
    .background(.ultraThinMaterial, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16))
    .padding()
}
```

## Jiggle (`jiggle`)

The home-screen edit-mode wiggle, each item slightly out of step.

- API: `.jiggle(isActive:)`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Loop / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/Jiggle.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/Jiggle.swift

### Usage

```swift
ForEach(apps) { app in
    AppIcon(app)
        .jiggle(isActive: isEditing)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .jiggle(isActive:angle:) view modifier (iOS 17+) that wiggles a view like an app icon in edit mode. Give each instance a random @State phase (0–1) and rate (0.9–1.1) so neighbours never move in lockstep. In TimelineView(.animation(paused: !isActive)), let t = (time × rate + phase) × 2π × 3.6, rotate by sin(t) × angle (2.5°) and offset y by cos(t/2) × 0.8 pt. When inactive, return to 0 with a 0.15 s ease. With Reduce Motion on, don't move.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The home-screen "edit mode" wiggle: a quick, slightly irregular rotation
/// and bob. Each view gets its own phase so a grid never moves in lockstep.
struct JiggleModifier: ViewModifier {
    var isActive: Bool
    var angle: Double

    @State private var phase = Double.random(in: 0..<1)
    @State private var rate = Double.random(in: 0.9..<1.1)
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: stay still.
        let running = isActive && !reduceMotion
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: !running)) { timeline in
            let t = (timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * rate + phase) * 2 * .pi * 3.6
            content
                .rotationEffect(.degrees(running ? sin(t) * angle : 0))
                .offset(y: running ? CGFloat(cos(t * 0.5)) * 0.8 : 0)
                .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.15), value: running)
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Wiggles the view like an app icon in edit mode while `isActive` is true.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ForEach(apps) { app in
    ///     AppIcon(app)
    ///         .jiggle(isActive: isEditing)
    /// }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameter angle: Peak rotation, in degrees.
    func jiggle(isActive: Bool = true, angle: Double = 2.5) -> some View {
        modifier(JiggleModifier(isActive: isActive, angle: angle))
    }
}

#Preview {
    HStack(spacing: 16) {
        ForEach([Color.blue, .green, .orange, .pink], id: \.self) { color in
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous)
                .fill(color.gradient)
                .frame(width: 54, height: 54)
                .jiggle()
        }
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Fan Stack (`fan-stack`)

A pile of cards fans out like a hand of playing cards, and gathers back.

- API: `FanStack(items, isSpread:) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/FanStack.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/FanStack.swift

### Usage

```swift
FanStack(cards, isSpread: isSpread) { card in
    CardView(card).frame(width: 80, height: 120)
}
.onTapGesture { isSpread.toggle() }
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI FanStack (iOS 17+) over Identifiable items with isSpread, angle (10°) and spacing (34 pt). Draw the cards in a ZStack, bottom first. For card i, let c = i − (count − 1)/2. Fanned: rotate by c × angle around the bottom anchor, offset x by c × spacing and y by c² × 4 pt so the outer cards dip along an arc. Stacked: rotate by c × 1.5° around the centre and offset y by −2 pt × i for a neat pile. Animate each card with .spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.7).delay(i × 0.03) on isSpread so they follow each other. With Reduce Motion on, use a 0.25 s ease without the stagger.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A stack of cards that fans out like a hand of playing cards, and gathers
/// back into a neat pile. Cards follow each other with a short stagger.
public struct FanStack<Item: Identifiable, Content: View>: View {
    private let items: [Item]
    private let isSpread: Bool
    private let angle: Double
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let content: (Item) -> Content

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: The cards, bottom first.
    ///   - isSpread: Fanned out (true) or stacked (false).
    ///   - angle: Rotation between neighbouring cards when fanned, in degrees.
    ///   - spacing: Horizontal distance between neighbouring cards when fanned.
    ///   - content: The card for an item.
    public init(
        _ items: [Item],
        isSpread: Bool,
        angle: Double = 10,
        spacing: CGFloat = 34,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Item) -> Content
    ) {
        self.items = items
        self.isSpread = isSpread
        self.angle = angle
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
                let centred = Double(index) - Double(items.count - 1) / 2
                content(item)
                    .rotationEffect(
                        .degrees(isSpread ? centred * angle : centred * 1.5),
                        anchor: isSpread ? .bottom : .center
                    )
                    .offset(
                        x: isSpread ? CGFloat(centred) * spacing : 0,
                        // The outer cards dip, following the arc of the fan.
                        y: isSpread ? CGFloat(abs(centred) * abs(centred)) * 4 : CGFloat(-index) * 2
                    )
                    .animation(
                        reduceMotion
                            ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.25)
                            : .spring(response: 0.45, dampingFraction: 0.7).delay(Double(index) * 0.03),
                        value: isSpread
                    )
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Card: Identifiable {
        let id: Int
        let color: Color
    }
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var spread = false
        let cards = [Color.pink, .orange, .yellow, .mint, .blue].enumerated().map { Card(id: $0.offset, color: $0.element) }
        var body: some View {
            FanStack(cards, isSpread: spread) { card in
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 10).fill(card.color.gradient).frame(width: 60, height: 86)
            }
            .onTapGesture { spread.toggle() }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding(60)
}
```

## Scratch Card (`scratch-card`)

Rub away a scratch-off cover to reveal what's underneath.

- API: `.scratchToReveal(_:onReveal:)`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ScratchCard.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ScratchCard.swift

### Usage

```swift
PrizeView()
    .scratchToReveal(Color.gray) {
        didReveal = true
    }
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .scratchToReveal(_ cover:lineWidth:threshold:onReveal:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Overlay a Rectangle filled with the cover style (with a faint "hand.draw.fill" hint until the first stroke) and mask it with a compositingGroup of a full Rectangle plus a stroked Path of every finger stroke (lineWidth 34, round caps and joins) using .blendMode(.destinationOut), so strokes punch holes in the cover. A DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) starts a new stroke when translation is zero and appends locations otherwise. Track coverage on a 12 × 12 grid: mark every cell within lineWidth / 2 of each point; once 55 % of cells are marked, fade the cover out over 0.4 s, disable its hit testing and call onReveal once. Give the view a new .id to reset it. Accessibility: a button whose action reveals.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Covers the view with a scratch-off layer. Dragging a finger erases the
/// cover along its path; once enough of it is scratched away, the rest
/// fades out and `onReveal` runs.
struct ScratchModifier<Cover: ShapeStyle>: ViewModifier {
    var cover: Cover
    var lineWidth: CGFloat
    var threshold: Double
    var onReveal: () -> Void

    @State private var strokes: [[CGPoint]] = []
    @State private var scratched: Set<Int> = []
    @State private var isRevealed = false

    /// The cover is split into a grid to estimate how much has been scratched.
    private let grid = 12

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                Rectangle()
                    .fill(cover)
                    .overlay {
                        Image(systemName: "hand.draw.fill")
                            .font(.title)
                            .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.7))
                            .opacity(strokes.isEmpty ? 1 : 0)
                            .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.2), value: strokes.isEmpty)
                    }
                    .mask {
                        ZStack {
                            Rectangle()
                            ScratchPath(strokes: strokes)
                                .stroke(style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
                                .blendMode(.destinationOut)
                        }
                        .compositingGroup()
                    }
                    .opacity(isRevealed ? 0 : 1)
                    .contentShape(Rectangle())
                    .gesture(
                        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
                            .onChanged { value in
                                guard !isRevealed else { return }
                                if value.translation == .zero || strokes.isEmpty {
                                    strokes.append([value.location])
                                } else {
                                    strokes[strokes.count - 1].append(value.location)
                                }
                                mark(value.location, in: geometry.size)
                            }
                    )
                    .allowsHitTesting(!isRevealed)
            }
            .accessibilityElement()
            .accessibilityLabel("Scratch card")
            .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
            .accessibilityAction { reveal() }
            .accessibilityHidden(isRevealed)
        }
    }

    /// Marks every grid cell the brush touches at `point`.
    private func mark(_ point: CGPoint, in size: CGSize) {
        guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return }
        let cellW = size.width / CGFloat(grid), cellH = size.height / CGFloat(grid)
        let r = lineWidth / 2
        let minC = max(0, Int((point.x - r) / cellW)), maxC = min(grid - 1, Int((point.x + r) / cellW))
        let minR = max(0, Int((point.y - r) / cellH)), maxR = min(grid - 1, Int((point.y + r) / cellH))
        guard minC <= maxC, minR <= maxR else { return }
        for row in minR...maxR {
            for column in minC...maxC {
                scratched.insert(row * grid + column)
            }
        }
        if Double(scratched.count) / Double(grid * grid) >= threshold {
            reveal()
        }
    }

    private func reveal() {
        guard !isRevealed else { return }
        withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.4)) { isRevealed = true }
        onReveal()
    }
}

struct ScratchPath: Shape {
    var strokes: [[CGPoint]]

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        for stroke in strokes {
            guard let first = stroke.first else { continue }
            path.move(to: first)
            // A single tap still leaves a round dot.
            path.addLine(to: stroke.count > 1 ? stroke[1] : CGPoint(x: first.x + 0.1, y: first.y))
            if stroke.count > 2 { path.addLines(Array(stroke.dropFirst())) }
        }
        return path
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Hides the view under a scratch-off cover that the user rubs away.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// PrizeView()
    ///     .scratchToReveal(LinearGradient(colors: [.gray, .secondary], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)) {
    ///         didReveal = true
    ///     }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Give the view a new `.id` to reset the cover.
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - cover: The scratch-off layer's fill.
    ///   - lineWidth: Width of the "coin", in points.
    ///   - threshold: Fraction of the cover to scratch before it clears itself.
    ///   - onReveal: Called once when the cover clears.
    func scratchToReveal<Cover: ShapeStyle>(
        _ cover: Cover = Color.gray,
        lineWidth: CGFloat = 34,
        threshold: Double = 0.55,
        onReveal: @escaping () -> Void = {}
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ScratchModifier(cover: cover, lineWidth: lineWidth, threshold: threshold, onReveal: onReveal))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 6) {
        Text("🎉").font(.system(size: 44))
        Text("You won!").font(.headline)
    }
    .frame(width: 220, height: 140)
    .background(Color.yellow.opacity(0.3))
    .scratchToReveal(LinearGradient(colors: [Color(white: 0.62), Color(white: 0.78)], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
    .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16))
    .padding()
}
```

## Stacking Cards (`stacking-cards`)

Cards stick at the top while scrolling and shrink as the next one covers them.

- API: `.stackingCard()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/StackingCards.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/StackingCards.swift

### Usage

```swift
ScrollView {
    VStack(spacing: 16) {
        ForEach(cards) { card in
            CardView(card).stackingCard()
        }
    }
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .stackingCard(top:scale:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for cards in a VStack inside a vertical ScrollView, built with visualEffect so it needs no layout passes. From proxy.frame(in: .scrollView): overshoot = max(0, top − minY) (top 16 pt), covered = min(1, overshoot / height), gone = clamp(overshoot / height − 1, 0, 1). Apply offset(y: overshoot) so the card sticks at the top, scaleEffect(1 − (1 − scale) × covered, anchor: .top) with scale 0.88, brightness(−0.25 × covered) and opacity(1 − gone). Later cards naturally draw on top in the VStack, so they slide over the pinned ones like a wallet. With Reduce Motion on, skip the scaling.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// While scrolling, each card sticks at the top of the scroll view, then
/// shrinks and dims as the next card slides over it, so the cards pile up
/// like a deck (Apple Wallet style). Uses `visualEffect`, so it costs no
/// layout passes.
struct StackingCardModifier: ViewModifier {
    var top: CGFloat
    var scale: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let top = top, scale = scale, reduceMotion = reduceMotion
        return content.visualEffect { effect, proxy in
            let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView)
            let height = max(1, frame.height)
            // How far the card has scrolled past its pin line.
            let overshoot = max(0, top - frame.minY)
            let covered = min(1, overshoot / height)
            // Once fully covered, fade it so the pile stays tidy.
            let gone = min(1, max(0, overshoot / height - 1))
            return effect
                .offset(y: overshoot)
                .scaleEffect(reduceMotion ? 1 : 1 - (1 - scale) * covered, anchor: .top)
                .brightness(-0.25 * covered)
                .opacity(1 - gone)
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Pins the card at the top of its scroll view and shrinks it as the
    /// next card slides over it. Apply to every card in a `VStack` inside a
    /// vertical `ScrollView`.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ScrollView {
    ///     VStack(spacing: 16) {
    ///         ForEach(cards) { card in
    ///             CardView(card).stackingCard()
    ///         }
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - top: Distance from the top of the scroll view where cards stick.
    ///   - scale: How small a fully covered card gets.
    func stackingCard(top: CGFloat = 16, scale: CGFloat = 0.88) -> some View {
        modifier(StackingCardModifier(top: top, scale: scale))
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollView {
        VStack(spacing: 16) {
            ForEach([Color.pink, .orange, .teal, .indigo, .mint, .purple], id: \.self) { color in
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20)
                    .fill(color.gradient)
                    .frame(height: 180)
                    .stackingCard()
            }
        }
        .padding()
        .padding(.bottom, 300)
    }
}
```

## Deck Shuffle (`deck-shuffle`)

A deck splits in two, mixes, and springs back into a messy stack.

- API: `DeckShuffle(items, trigger:) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Value change / Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/DeckShuffle.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/DeckShuffle.swift

### Usage

```swift
DeckShuffle(cards, trigger: shuffles) { card in
    CardFace(card)
}
.onTapGesture { shuffles += 1 }
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI DeckShuffle(_ items:trigger:spread:content:) view (iOS 17+) for Identifiable items. Keep the order as @State [ID]. Draw the cards in a ZStack with zIndex = stack position, offset y = −2 pt × position and a small hand-made tilt per position (0, −2.5, 2, −1, 3, −2, 1.5, −3°). When trigger changes: animate isSplit = true with .easeOut(0.28 s), which moves even positions to x −spread (70 pt) rotated −8° and odd ones to +spread rotated +8°; after 0.3 s, in one .spring(duration: 0.55, bounce: 0.3) animation, shuffle the order and set isSplit = false, so cards change sides and visibly cross over as they come together. With Reduce Motion on, just re-order with a 0.3 s ease.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A small deck of cards that riffle-shuffles every time `trigger` changes:
/// the deck splits into two halves that slide apart, the order is mixed, and
/// the cards spring back together into a slightly messy stack.
public struct DeckShuffle<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Trigger: Equatable, Content: View>: View
where Data.Element: Identifiable {
    private let items: Data
    private let trigger: Trigger
    private let spread: CGFloat
    private let content: (Data.Element) -> Content

    @State private var order: [Data.Element.ID] = []
    @State private var isSplit = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: The cards, bottom to top.
    ///   - trigger: Shuffles whenever it changes.
    ///   - spread: How far each half slides out, in points.
    ///   - content: Draws one card.
    public init(_ items: Data, trigger: Trigger, spread: CGFloat = 70, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content) {
        self.items = items
        self.trigger = trigger
        self.spread = spread
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let ids = order.isEmpty ? items.map(\.id) : order
        ZStack {
            ForEach(Array(items)) { item in
                let position = ids.firstIndex(of: item.id) ?? 0
                let tilt = Self.tilt(for: position)
                content(item)
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(isSplit ? (position.isMultiple(of: 2) ? -8 : 8) : tilt))
                    .offset(
                        x: isSplit ? (position.isMultiple(of: 2) ? -spread : spread) : 0,
                        y: isSplit ? 0 : -CGFloat(position) * 2
                    )
                    .zIndex(Double(position))
            }
        }
        .onAppear { if order.isEmpty { order = items.map(\.id) } }
        .onChange(of: trigger) { shuffle() }
    }

    /// A small, stable tilt per stack position so the deck looks hand-made.
    private static func tilt(for position: Int) -> Double {
        let values: [Double] = [0, -2.5, 2, -1, 3, -2, 1.5, -3]
        return values[position % values.count]
    }

    private func shuffle() {
        let shuffled = (order.isEmpty ? items.map(\.id) : order).shuffled()
        if reduceMotion {
            withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) { order = shuffled }
            return
        }
        withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.28)) { isSplit = true }
        Task { @MainActor in
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.3))
            // Re-ordering while apart changes which half each card is in, so
            // cards visibly cross over as they come back together.
            withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.55, bounce: 0.3)) {
                order = shuffled
                isSplit = false
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Card: Identifiable { let id: Int; let color: Color }
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shuffles = 0
        let cards = [Card(id: 0, color: .pink), Card(id: 1, color: .orange), Card(id: 2, color: .teal), Card(id: 3, color: .indigo), Card(id: 4, color: .mint)]
        var body: some View {
            DeckShuffle(cards, trigger: shuffles) { card in
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12).fill(card.color.gradient).frame(width: 80, height: 112)
            }
            .onTapGesture { shuffles += 1 }
            .padding(80)
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Looping Carousel (`looping-carousel`)

A paging carousel that wraps around forever, with peeking neighbours.

- API: `LoopingCarousel(items) { item in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Drag / Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/LoopingCarousel.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/LoopingCarousel.swift

### Usage

```swift
LoopingCarousel(banners, autoplay: 3) { banner in
    BannerCard(banner)
}
.frame(height: 200)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI LoopingCarousel(_ items:spacing:peek:autoplay:content:) view (iOS 17+). Inside a horizontal ScrollView, a LazyHStack(spacing: 12) lays the items out three times (index 0..<3n, item = items[index % n]), each .containerRelativeFrame(.horizontal) with .scrollTransition(.interactive) scaling to 1 − |phase| × 0.12 and fading to 1 − |phase| × 0.4, and .id(index). Use .scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), .contentMargins(.horizontal, peek + spacing) (peek 36 pt) and .scrollPosition(id:), starting at n (the middle copy). In .task(id: position), wait 0.45 s for scrolling to settle; if the position is outside the middle copy, jump to n + position % n inside a transaction with animations disabled, which looks identical. For autoplay, loop: sleep autoplay seconds, then position += 1 with .spring(duration: 0.6, bounce: 0.15). With Reduce Motion on, skip the scaling.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A horizontally paging carousel that never ends: it wraps from the last
/// card back to the first. Neighbours peek in from the sides, shrunk and
/// faded, and it can advance on its own.
///
/// The items are laid out three times; after scrolling settles, the
/// position silently jumps back to the middle copy.
public struct LoopingCarousel<Data: RandomAccessCollection, Content: View>: View where Data.Index == Int {
    private let items: Data
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let peek: CGFloat
    private let autoplay: Double?
    private let content: (Data.Element) -> Content

    @State private var position: Int?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - items: The cards, in order.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between cards, in points.
    ///   - peek: How much of each neighbour shows at the sides, in points.
    ///   - autoplay: Seconds between automatic advances; `nil` to disable.
    ///   - content: Draws one card.
    public init(_ items: Data, spacing: CGFloat = 12, peek: CGFloat = 36, autoplay: Double? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content) {
        self.items = items
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.peek = peek
        self.autoplay = autoplay
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let count = items.count
        let reduceMotion = reduceMotion
        ScrollView(.horizontal) {
            LazyHStack(spacing: spacing) {
                ForEach(0..<(count * 3), id: \.self) { index in
                    content(items[items.startIndex + index % max(1, count)])
                        .containerRelativeFrame(.horizontal)
                        .scrollTransition(.interactive, axis: .horizontal) { view, phase in
                            view
                                .scaleEffect(reduceMotion ? 1 : 1 - abs(phase.value) * 0.12)
                                .opacity(1 - abs(phase.value) * 0.4)
                        }
                        .id(index)
                }
            }
            .scrollTargetLayout()
        }
        .contentMargins(.horizontal, peek + spacing, for: .scrollContent)
        .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
        .scrollIndicators(.hidden)
        .scrollPosition(id: $position)
        .onAppear { if position == nil { position = count } }
        .task(id: position) {
            // Once scrolling has settled, recentre on the middle copy.
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.45))
            guard count > 0, let current = position, current < count || current >= count * 2 else { return }
            var jump = Transaction()
            jump.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(jump) { position = count + current % count }
        }
        .task(id: autoplay) {
            guard let autoplay, count > 1 else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(autoplay))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.6, bounce: 0.15)) {
                    position = (position ?? count) + 1
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    LoopingCarousel([Color.pink, .orange, .teal, .indigo], autoplay: 2) { color in
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20).fill(color.gradient).frame(height: 180)
    }
    .frame(height: 200)
}
```

## Drag to Dismiss (`drag-to-dismiss`)

Fling a card away; it flies off with your throw or springs back.

- API: `.dragToDismiss(isPresented:)`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/DragToDismiss.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/DragToDismiss.swift

### Usage

```swift
if showPhoto {
    PhotoView()
        .dragToDismiss(isPresented: $showPhoto)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .dragToDismiss(isPresented:threshold:) view modifier (iOS 17+). While dragging, offset the view by the translation, scale it to 1 − min(0.2, distance / 1200) and rotate it by translation.width / 25 degrees. On release, if the drag distance exceeds threshold (120 pt) or the predicted end translation exceeds 2.5 × threshold, fly it off along the predicted direction normalised to 700 pt with .easeOut(0.3 s) while fading out, then set isPresented = false and reset the offset without animation. Otherwise spring back with .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.4). Add an accessibility action "Dismiss". With Reduce Motion on, skip the scale and rotation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Lets the user fling a view away. While dragging it follows the finger,
/// shrinking and tilting a little; released past a distance (or flicked fast
/// enough) it flies off in the throw direction and `isPresented` turns
/// false; otherwise it springs back.
struct DragToDismissModifier: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    var threshold: CGFloat

    @State private var drag: CGSize = .zero
    @State private var isLeaving = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let distance = hypot(drag.width, drag.height)
        content
            .scaleEffect(reduceMotion ? 1 : 1 - min(0.2, distance / 1200))
            .rotationEffect(.degrees(reduceMotion ? 0 : Double(drag.width) / 25))
            .offset(drag)
            .opacity(isLeaving ? 0 : 1)
            .gesture(
                DragGesture()
                    .onChanged { value in
                        guard !isLeaving else { return }
                        drag = value.translation
                    }
                    .onEnded { value in
                        guard !isLeaving else { return }
                        let predicted = value.predictedEndTranslation
                        let thrown = hypot(predicted.width, predicted.height) > threshold * 2.5
                        if hypot(value.translation.width, value.translation.height) > threshold || thrown {
                            dismiss(towards: predicted)
                        } else {
                            withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.4)) { drag = .zero }
                        }
                    }
            )
            .accessibilityAction(named: "Dismiss") { isPresented = false }
    }

    private func dismiss(towards predicted: CGSize) {
        let length = max(1, hypot(predicted.width, predicted.height))
        // Keep the throw direction but make sure it leaves the screen.
        let fly = CGSize(width: predicted.width / length * 700, height: predicted.height / length * 700)
        withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.3)) {
            drag = fly
            isLeaving = true
        }
        Task { @MainActor in
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.3))
            isPresented = false
            var reset = Transaction()
            reset.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(reset) {
                drag = .zero
                isLeaving = false
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Lets the user drag the view away to dismiss it, with a spring back if
    /// they don't drag far enough.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showPhoto {
    ///     PhotoView()
    ///         .dragToDismiss(isPresented: $showPhoto)
    /// }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isPresented: Set to `false` once the view has flown off.
    ///   - threshold: Drag distance, in points, that dismisses on release.
    func dragToDismiss(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, threshold: CGFloat = 120) -> some View {
        modifier(DragToDismissModifier(isPresented: isPresented, threshold: threshold))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            ZStack {
                if shown {
                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 24)
                        .fill(Color.indigo.gradient)
                        .frame(width: 220, height: 300)
                        .dragToDismiss(isPresented: $shown)
                } else {
                    Button("Show again") { shown = true }
                }
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Shrinking Header (`shrinking-header`)

The header sticks to the top and shrinks as content scrolls under it.

- API: `.shrinkingHeader()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ScrollHeaders.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ScrollHeaders.swift

### Usage

```swift
ScrollView {
    VStack(spacing: 0) {
        ProfileHeader().shrinkingHeader()
        ForEach(posts) { PostRow($0) }
    }
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .shrinkingHeader(minScale:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for the first view in a vertical ScrollView, built with visualEffect. From proxy.frame(in: .scrollView): scrolled = max(0, −minY), progress = min(1, scrolled / (height × (1 − minScale))). Apply scaleEffect(1 − (1 − minScale) × progress, anchor: .top) with minScale 0.6 first, then offset(y: scrolled) so it stays pinned at the top (offset first and the scale would shrink the offset too, letting the header drift away), and give the view .zIndex(1) so the content scrolls underneath it. With Reduce Motion on, pin it without scaling.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Headers that react to the scroll position, driven by `visualEffect` so
// they cost no extra layout passes. Apply them to the first view inside a
// vertical `ScrollView`.

// MARK: - Shrinking header

struct ShrinkingHeaderModifier: ViewModifier {
    var minScale: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let minScale = minScale, reduceMotion = reduceMotion
        return content
            .visualEffect { effect, proxy in
                let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView)
                let scrolled = max(0, -frame.minY)
                // Shrinks over the distance it loses in height, then stays put.
                let range = max(1, frame.height * (1 - minScale))
                let progress = min(1, scrolled / range)
                // Scale first, then offset: the other way round the scale
                // would shrink the pinning offset too and the header would
                // drift off the top.
                return effect
                    .scaleEffect(reduceMotion ? 1 : 1 - (1 - minScale) * progress, anchor: .top)
                    .offset(y: scrolled)
            }
            // Stay above the content that scrolls underneath.
            .zIndex(1)
    }
}

// MARK: - Stretchy header

struct StretchyHeaderModifier: ViewModifier {
    var parallax: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let parallax = reduceMotion ? 0 : parallax
        return content.visualEffect { effect, proxy in
            let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView)
            let pull = max(0, frame.minY)
            let height = max(1, frame.height)
            return effect
                // Pulled down: grow from the bottom so it fills the gap.
                .scaleEffect(1 + pull / height, anchor: .bottom)
                // Scrolled up: lag behind the content for a parallax feel.
                .offset(y: min(0, frame.minY) * -parallax)
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Pins the header to the top of its scroll view and shrinks it as the
    /// content scrolls up underneath.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ScrollView {
    ///     VStack(spacing: 0) {
    ///         ProfileHeader().shrinkingHeader()
    ///         ForEach(posts) { PostRow($0) }
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameter minScale: The header's scale once fully collapsed.
    func shrinkingHeader(minScale: CGFloat = 0.6) -> some View {
        modifier(ShrinkingHeaderModifier(minScale: minScale))
    }

    /// Makes a header image stretch when the scroll view is pulled down past
    /// the top, and drift with a parallax when scrolled up.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ScrollView {
    ///     Image("cover")
    ///         .resizable()
    ///         .scaledToFill()
    ///         .frame(height: 260)
    ///         .clipped()
    ///         .stretchyHeader()
    ///     ArticleBody()
    /// }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameter parallax: How much slower than the content it moves when
    ///   scrolled up (0 = none, 0.5 = half speed).
    func stretchyHeader(parallax: CGFloat = 0.5) -> some View {
        modifier(StretchyHeaderModifier(parallax: parallax))
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollView {
        VStack(spacing: 0) {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .frame(height: 200)
                .overlay(Text("Stretch me").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
                .stretchyHeader()
            ForEach(0..<20, id: \.self) { index in
                Text("Row \(index)")
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                    .padding()
                    .background(.background)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Stretchy Header (`stretchy-header`)

A header image stretches when pulled down and drifts with parallax when scrolled.

- API: `.stretchyHeader()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ScrollHeaders.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/ScrollHeaders.swift

### Usage

```swift
ScrollView {
    Image("cover")
        .resizable()
        .scaledToFill()
        .frame(height: 260)
        .clipped()
        .stretchyHeader()
    ArticleBody()
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .stretchyHeader(parallax:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for a header image at the top of a vertical ScrollView, built with visualEffect. From proxy.frame(in: .scrollView): when pulled past the top (minY > 0), scaleEffect(1 + minY / height, anchor: .bottom) so it grows upward to fill the gap; when scrolled up (minY < 0), offset(y: minY × −parallax) with parallax 0.5 so it moves at half speed. With Reduce Motion on, skip the parallax.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Headers that react to the scroll position, driven by `visualEffect` so
// they cost no extra layout passes. Apply them to the first view inside a
// vertical `ScrollView`.

// MARK: - Shrinking header

struct ShrinkingHeaderModifier: ViewModifier {
    var minScale: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let minScale = minScale, reduceMotion = reduceMotion
        return content
            .visualEffect { effect, proxy in
                let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView)
                let scrolled = max(0, -frame.minY)
                // Shrinks over the distance it loses in height, then stays put.
                let range = max(1, frame.height * (1 - minScale))
                let progress = min(1, scrolled / range)
                // Scale first, then offset: the other way round the scale
                // would shrink the pinning offset too and the header would
                // drift off the top.
                return effect
                    .scaleEffect(reduceMotion ? 1 : 1 - (1 - minScale) * progress, anchor: .top)
                    .offset(y: scrolled)
            }
            // Stay above the content that scrolls underneath.
            .zIndex(1)
    }
}

// MARK: - Stretchy header

struct StretchyHeaderModifier: ViewModifier {
    var parallax: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let parallax = reduceMotion ? 0 : parallax
        return content.visualEffect { effect, proxy in
            let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView)
            let pull = max(0, frame.minY)
            let height = max(1, frame.height)
            return effect
                // Pulled down: grow from the bottom so it fills the gap.
                .scaleEffect(1 + pull / height, anchor: .bottom)
                // Scrolled up: lag behind the content for a parallax feel.
                .offset(y: min(0, frame.minY) * -parallax)
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Pins the header to the top of its scroll view and shrinks it as the
    /// content scrolls up underneath.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ScrollView {
    ///     VStack(spacing: 0) {
    ///         ProfileHeader().shrinkingHeader()
    ///         ForEach(posts) { PostRow($0) }
    ///     }
    /// }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameter minScale: The header's scale once fully collapsed.
    func shrinkingHeader(minScale: CGFloat = 0.6) -> some View {
        modifier(ShrinkingHeaderModifier(minScale: minScale))
    }

    /// Makes a header image stretch when the scroll view is pulled down past
    /// the top, and drift with a parallax when scrolled up.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ScrollView {
    ///     Image("cover")
    ///         .resizable()
    ///         .scaledToFill()
    ///         .frame(height: 260)
    ///         .clipped()
    ///         .stretchyHeader()
    ///     ArticleBody()
    /// }
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameter parallax: How much slower than the content it moves when
    ///   scrolled up (0 = none, 0.5 = half speed).
    func stretchyHeader(parallax: CGFloat = 0.5) -> some View {
        modifier(StretchyHeaderModifier(parallax: parallax))
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollView {
        VStack(spacing: 0) {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .frame(height: 200)
                .overlay(Text("Stretch me").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
                .stretchyHeader()
            ForEach(0..<20, id: \.self) { index in
                Text("Row \(index)")
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                    .padding()
                    .background(.background)
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Island Pill (`island-pill`)

A black pill springs open into a card and back, its contents blurring across.

- API: `IslandPill(isExpanded:) { } expanded: { }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/IslandPill.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/IslandPill.swift

### Usage

```swift
IslandPill(isExpanded: showsPlayer) {
    Image(systemName: "waveform")
} expanded: {
    NowPlayingView()
}
.onTapGesture { showsPlayer.toggle() }
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI IslandPill(isExpanded:compactSize:expandedSize:color:compact:expanded:) view (iOS 17+): a black shape that morphs between a pill (default 126 × 37, corner radius half its height) and a card (default 340 × 160, corner radius min(44, height / 2)), using a continuous RoundedRectangle as background and clip shape. Inside, a ZStack holds both contents: the compact one fades out while blurring to 8 pt and scaling to 1.6; the expanded one fades in from blur 10 pt and scale 0.6 (anchored top). Force the dark colour scheme inside. Animate every change of isExpanded with .spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.32). With Reduce Motion on, skip the blur and scale and use .easeInOut(duration: 0.25).

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A black pill that springs open into a larger rounded card and back, like a
/// live activity growing out of the top of the screen. The compact and
/// expanded contents cross-fade with a blur while the shape morphs.
///
/// ```swift
/// IslandPill(isExpanded: showsPlayer) {
///     Image(systemName: "waveform")
/// } expanded: {
///     NowPlayingView()
/// }
/// ```
public struct IslandPill<Compact: View, Expanded: View>: View {
    private let isExpanded: Bool
    private let compactSize: CGSize
    private let expandedSize: CGSize
    private let color: Color
    private let compact: Compact
    private let expanded: Expanded

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isExpanded: Shows the expanded content when true. Changes animate.
    ///   - compactSize: Size of the closed pill.
    ///   - expandedSize: Size of the open card.
    ///   - color: Fill of the pill.
    ///   - compact: Content of the closed pill.
    ///   - expanded: Content of the open card.
    public init(
        isExpanded: Bool,
        compactSize: CGSize = CGSize(width: 126, height: 37),
        expandedSize: CGSize = CGSize(width: 340, height: 160),
        color: Color = .black,
        @ViewBuilder compact: () -> Compact,
        @ViewBuilder expanded: () -> Expanded
    ) {
        self.isExpanded = isExpanded
        self.compactSize = compactSize
        self.expandedSize = expandedSize
        self.color = color
        self.compact = compact()
        self.expanded = expanded()
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let size = isExpanded ? expandedSize : compactSize
        let radius = isExpanded ? min(44, expandedSize.height / 2) : compactSize.height / 2
        ZStack {
            compact
                .opacity(isExpanded ? 0 : 1)
                .blur(radius: isExpanded && !reduceMotion ? 8 : 0)
                .scaleEffect(isExpanded && !reduceMotion ? 1.6 : 1)
            expanded
                .opacity(isExpanded ? 1 : 0)
                .blur(radius: isExpanded || reduceMotion ? 0 : 10)
                .scaleEffect(isExpanded || reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.6, anchor: .top)
        }
        .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)
        .background(color, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: radius, style: .continuous))
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: radius, style: .continuous))
        .environment(\.colorScheme, .dark)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.25) : .spring(duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.32), value: isExpanded)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var open = false
        var body: some View {
            IslandPill(isExpanded: open) {
                HStack {
                    Image(systemName: "music.note")
                    Spacer()
                    Image(systemName: "waveform").foregroundStyle(.green)
                }
                .padding(.horizontal, 14)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
            } expanded: {
                HStack(spacing: 14) {
                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12).fill(.orange.gradient).frame(width: 64, height: 64)
                    VStack(alignment: .leading) {
                        Text("Now Playing").font(.headline)
                        Text("Motion Library").foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    }
                    Spacer()
                }
                .padding(20)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
            }
            .onTapGesture { open.toggle() }
            .frame(height: 220, alignment: .top)
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Hover Lift (`hover-lift`)

Cards rise, grow and lean towards the pointer on iPad and Mac.

- API: `.hoverLift(isActive:)`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Hover
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/HoverLift.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/HoverLift.swift

### Usage

```swift
LazyVGrid(columns: columns) {
    ForEach(projects) { project in
        ProjectCard(project)
            .hoverLift()
    }
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .hoverLift(scale:tilt:cornerRadius:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for pointer hover on iPad and Mac. Track the pointer with .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) and the view size with a background GeometryReader. While hovered, scale to 1.05, offset y −4 and deepen the shadow (black 22 %, radius 18, y 12; at rest 8 %, radius 6, y 3), all with .spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.3). Lean towards the pointer: with lean = location / size × 2 − 1, apply rotation3DEffect(tilt × lean.x around y) and (−tilt × lean.y around x), tilt 6°, perspective 0.6, animated with .interactiveSpring(duration: 0.25). With Reduce Motion on, don't move or scale; brighten by 0.05 instead. Add isActive (default false) to lift the view without a pointer too, for the focused or selected card. On visionOS, where apps can't see the gaze, use .contentShape(.hoverEffect, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:)) and the system .hoverEffect().

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Lifts the view towards the pointer on hover (iPad trackpad or mouse, Mac):
/// it grows a little, rises, casts a deeper shadow and leans slightly
/// towards the pointer. On visionOS, where apps can't see the gaze, it uses
/// the system hover effect instead.
struct HoverLiftModifier: ViewModifier {
    var scale: CGFloat
    var tilt: Double
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat
    var isActive: Bool

    @State private var location: CGPoint?
    @State private var size: CGSize = .zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        #if os(visionOS)
        content
            .contentShape(.hoverEffect, RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous))
            .hoverEffect()
            .scaleEffect(isActive && !reduceMotion ? scale : 1)
            .animation(.spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.3), value: isActive)
        #else
        let hovering = location != nil || isActive
        // -1…1 from the centre, for the lean.
        let lean = location.map { CGPoint(x: size.width > 0 ? $0.x / size.width * 2 - 1 : 0, y: size.height > 0 ? $0.y / size.height * 2 - 1 : 0) } ?? .zero
        let moves = !reduceMotion
        content
            .scaleEffect(hovering && moves ? scale : 1)
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(moves ? tilt * Double(lean.x) : 0), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(moves ? -tilt * Double(lean.y) : 0), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
            .offset(y: hovering && moves ? -4 : 0)
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(hovering ? 0.22 : 0.08), radius: hovering ? 18 : 6, y: hovering ? 12 : 3)
            .brightness(hovering && !moves ? 0.05 : 0)
            .animation(.spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.3), value: hovering)
            .animation(.interactiveSpring(duration: 0.25), value: lean)
            .background {
                GeometryReader { proxy in
                    Color.clear
                        .onAppear { size = proxy.size }
                        .onChange(of: proxy.size) { _, new in size = new }
                }
            }
            .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) { phase in
                switch phase {
                case let .active(point): location = point
                case .ended: location = nil
                }
            }
        #endif
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Lifts the view under the pointer: it scales up, rises, deepens its
    /// shadow and leans towards the pointer. For iPad pointers and the Mac;
    /// visionOS gets the system hover highlight.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ProjectCard(project)
    ///     .hoverLift()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - scale: Scale while hovered.
    ///   - tilt: Maximum lean towards the pointer, in degrees.
    ///   - cornerRadius: Corner radius of the hover shape on visionOS.
    ///   - isActive: Also lifts the view while true, for example for the
    ///     focused or selected card (without the lean, which follows the pointer).
    func hoverLift(scale: CGFloat = 1.05, tilt: Double = 6, cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16, isActive: Bool = false) -> some View {
        modifier(HoverLiftModifier(scale: scale, tilt: tilt, cornerRadius: cornerRadius, isActive: isActive))
    }
}

#Preview {
    HStack(spacing: 20) {
        ForEach(0..<3) { index in
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16, style: .continuous)
                .fill([Color.orange, .pink, .indigo][index].gradient)
                .frame(width: 90, height: 120)
                .hoverLift()
        }
    }
    .padding(40)
}
```

## Marquee Wall (`marquee-wall`)

A tilted wall of cards, columns scrolling endlessly up and down.

- API: `MarqueeWall(count:) { index in }`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/MarqueeWall.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/MarqueeWall.swift

### Usage

```swift
MarqueeWall(count: shots.count, columns: 4) { index in
    Image(shots[index]).resizable().scaledToFill()
}
.frame(height: 320)
.clipped()
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI MarqueeWall(count:columns:itemSize:spacing:speed:angle:content:) view (iOS 17+), the scrolling showcase wall from landing pages. Each of the columns (default 4) shows perColumn = max(3, ceil(count / columns)) items twice in a VStack, cards of itemSize (110 × 140) with 14 pt continuous corners and 12 pt spacing, so the loop height is perColumn × (height + spacing). In TimelineView(.animation), distance = (time × speed × (1 + 0.15 × (column % 3))) mod loopHeight (speed 24 pt/s); even columns offset by −distance (moving up), odd ones by distance − loopHeight (moving down). Lay the columns in an HStack, rotate the whole thing by −14° and let the caller clip it. Disable hit testing. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A tilted wall of cards whose columns scroll endlessly in alternating
/// directions, the showcase backdrop of portfolio and landing pages.
///
/// ```swift
/// MarqueeWall(count: 12, columns: 4) { index in
///     Image("shot-\(index)").resizable().scaledToFill()
/// }
/// .frame(height: 300)
/// .clipped()
/// ```
public struct MarqueeWall<Content: View>: View {
    private let count: Int
    private let columns: Int
    private let itemSize: CGSize
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let speed: Double
    private let angle: Angle
    private let content: (Int) -> Content

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of distinct items; they're shared out between the columns.
    ///   - columns: Number of columns.
    ///   - itemSize: Size of each card.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between cards.
    ///   - speed: Scroll speed, in points per second.
    ///   - angle: Rotation of the whole wall.
    ///   - content: Builds the card for an index in `0..<count`.
    public init(
        count: Int,
        columns: Int = 4,
        itemSize: CGSize = CGSize(width: 110, height: 140),
        spacing: CGFloat = 12,
        speed: Double = 24,
        angle: Angle = .degrees(-14),
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Int) -> Content
    ) {
        self.count = max(1, count)
        self.columns = max(1, columns)
        self.itemSize = itemSize
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.speed = speed
        self.angle = angle
        self.content = content
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Each column shows its items twice over, so the loop is seamless.
        let perColumn = max(3, Int(ceil(Double(count) / Double(columns))))
        let loopHeight = CGFloat(perColumn) * (itemSize.height + spacing)
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: spacing) {
                ForEach(0..<columns, id: \.self) { column in
                    let distance = CGFloat((time * speed * (1 + Double(column % 3) * 0.15)).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: Double(loopHeight)))
                    let offset = column.isMultiple(of: 2) ? -distance : distance - loopHeight
                    VStack(spacing: spacing) {
                        ForEach(0..<(perColumn * 2), id: \.self) { row in
                            content((column * perColumn + row % perColumn) % count)
                                .frame(width: itemSize.width, height: itemSize.height)
                                .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14, style: .continuous))
                        }
                    }
                    .offset(y: offset)
                    .frame(height: loopHeight, alignment: .top)
                }
            }
            .rotationEffect(angle)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        }
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
    }
}

#Preview {
    let colors: [Color] = [.orange, .pink, .purple, .blue, .teal, .green, .yellow, .red]
    return MarqueeWall(count: 8, columns: 4, itemSize: CGSize(width: 80, height: 100)) { index in
        Rectangle().fill(colors[index].gradient)
    }
    .frame(width: 340, height: 240)
    .clipped()
    .background(.black)
}
```

## Photo Develop (`photo-develop`)

The view develops like an instant photo, from murky dark to full colour.

- API: `.photoDevelop()`
- Component: Card & Group
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/PhotoDevelop.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Card/PhotoDevelop.swift

### Usage

```swift
Image("snapshot")
    .resizable()
    .scaledToFill()
    .frame(width: 200, height: 200)
    .photoDevelop(trigger: shotCount)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .photoDevelop(trigger:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+) that develops the view like an instant photo on appear and whenever trigger changes. Reset progress to 0 without animation, then animate it to 1 with .easeOut(duration: 3.5). Apply the look in an Animatable modifier so each quality keeps its own pace: light = min(1, 1.6p), colour = max(0, (p − 0.25) / 0.75), focus = min(1, 1.3p); .saturation(colour), .contrast(0.55 + 0.45 × light), .brightness(−0.45 × (1 − light)), .blur(radius: 5 × (1 − focus)), and an overlay LinearGradient from blue-grey (0.2, 0.25, 0.35) to brown (0.35, 0.25, 0.18) with opacity 0.75 × (1 − colour) and .blendMode(.multiply). With Reduce Motion on, develop over 0.4 s.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The view develops like an instant photo: it starts as a dark, murky,
/// blue-brown smudge and over a few seconds the light, contrast, colour and
/// focus come in.
struct PhotoDevelopModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var duration: Double

    @State private var progress: Double = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .modifier(DevelopEffect(progress: progress))
            .onAppear(perform: develop)
            .onChange(of: trigger) { develop() }
    }

    private func develop() {
        var reset = Transaction()
        reset.disablesAnimations = true
        withTransaction(reset) { progress = 0 }
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.4) : .easeOut(duration: duration)) { progress = 1 }
    }
}

/// The look at a point of the development, 0 (blank) to 1 (developed).
/// Animatable, so each quality keeps its own pace during the animation.
struct DevelopEffect: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var progress: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Each quality arrives at its own pace: light first, colour last.
        let light = min(1, progress * 1.6)
        let colour = max(0, (progress - 0.25) / 0.75)
        let focus = min(1, progress * 1.3)
        content
            .saturation(colour)
            .contrast(0.55 + 0.45 * light)
            .brightness(-0.45 * (1 - light))
            .blur(radius: 5 * (1 - focus))
            .overlay {
                // The murky blue-brown cast of an undeveloped print.
                LinearGradient(colors: [Color(red: 0.2, green: 0.25, blue: 0.35), Color(red: 0.35, green: 0.25, blue: 0.18)], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                    .opacity(0.75 * (1 - colour))
                    .blendMode(.multiply)
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Develops the view like an instant photo on appear, and again whenever
    /// `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("snapshot")
    ///     .resizable()
    ///     .scaledToFill()
    ///     .photoDevelop()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - trigger: Develops the photo again whenever it changes.
    ///   - duration: Seconds from blank to fully developed.
    func photoDevelop(trigger: some Equatable = 0, duration: Double = 3.5) -> some View {
        modifier(PhotoDevelopModifier(trigger: trigger, duration: duration))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shots = 0
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .purple], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                    .overlay(Image(systemName: "sun.max.fill").font(.system(size: 50)).foregroundStyle(.yellow))
                    .frame(width: 160, height: 160)
                    .photoDevelop(trigger: shots)
                Color.white.frame(height: 40)
            }
            .padding([.top, .horizontal], 10)
            .background(.white)
            .shadow(radius: 6)
            .onTapGesture { shots += 1 }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Pulse Rings (`pulse-rings`)

Concentric rings expand and fade continuously, like a radar or live dot.

- API: `PulseRings()`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/PulseRings.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/PulseRings.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    PulseRings(color: .green, count: 3)
        .frame(width: 120, height: 120)
    Circle().fill(.green).frame(width: 24, height: 24)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI PulseRings view (iOS 17+). Draw N stroked circles (default 3, 2 pt line) that each grow from 20% to 100% of the frame while fading from opacity 1 to 0 over a 2 s cycle, evenly phase-offset so a new ring is always emerging. Drive it with TimelineView(.animation) and compute each ring's progress from the timeline date (no @State or repeatForever), so it never drifts and stops when off screen. Hide it from accessibility.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Concentric rings that continuously expand and fade, like a radar or a
/// "live" indicator. Place it behind an icon or avatar.
///
/// ```swift
/// ZStack {
///     PulseRings(color: .green)
///         .frame(width: 120, height: 120)
///     Circle().fill(.green).frame(width: 24, height: 24)
/// }
/// ```
public struct PulseRings: View {
    private let color: Color
    private let count: Int
    private let duration: Double
    private let lineWidth: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    public init(color: Color = .accentColor, count: Int = 3, duration: Double = 2, lineWidth: CGFloat = 2) {
        self.color = color
        self.count = max(1, count)
        self.duration = duration
        self.lineWidth = lineWidth
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: frozen rings at evenly spaced sizes.
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? duration * 0.5 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            ZStack {
                ForEach(0..<count, id: \.self) { index in
                    ring(progress: progress(time: time, index: index))
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func progress(time: TimeInterval, index: Int) -> Double {
        let offset = Double(index) / Double(count)
        return (time / duration + offset).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
    }

    private func ring(progress: Double) -> some View {
        Circle()
            .stroke(color, lineWidth: lineWidth)
            .scaleEffect(0.2 + progress * 0.8)
            .opacity(1 - progress)
    }
}

#Preview {
    ZStack {
        PulseRings(color: .green)
            .frame(width: 160, height: 160)
        Circle()
            .fill(.green)
            .frame(width: 28, height: 28)
    }
}
```

## Like Burst (`burst`)

Particles fly outward from the centre when a value changes.

- API: `.burst(trigger:)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/Burst.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/Burst.swift

### Usage

```swift
Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
    .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
    .burst(trigger: isLiked, color: .pink, isEnabled: isLiked)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .burst(trigger:) view modifier (iOS 17+) for "like" feedback. Every time the Equatable trigger changes (and isEnabled is true), spawn a burst in an overlay: 12 small circles (alternating 7 pt and 4 pt) placed evenly around a circle, which move outward from the centre to a ~36 pt radius while shrinking to 30% and fading out with easeOut over 0.6 s. Remove each burst after it finishes, allow overlapping bursts, and never intercept touches. Color, count and radius are parameters.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Small dots that fly outward from the centre of the view, e.g. on a "like"
/// tap. Plays every time `trigger` changes.
struct BurstModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var color: Color
    var count: Int
    var radius: CGFloat
    var isEnabled: Bool

    @State private var bursts: [UUID] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                ZStack {
                    ForEach(bursts, id: \.self) { _ in
                        BurstParticles(color: color, count: count, radius: radius)
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
            .onChange(of: trigger) {
                // Reduce Motion: skip the particles.
                guard isEnabled, !reduceMotion else { return }
                let id = UUID()
                bursts.append(id)
                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.8) {
                    bursts.removeAll { $0 == id }
                }
            }
    }
}

private struct BurstParticles: View {
    let color: Color
    let count: Int
    let radius: CGFloat

    @State private var exploded = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(0..<max(1, count), id: \.self) { index in
                particle(angle: Double(index) / Double(max(1, count)) * 2 * .pi, index: index)
            }
        }
        .onAppear {
            withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.6)) {
                exploded = true
            }
        }
    }

    private func particle(angle: Double, index: Int) -> some View {
        // Alternate particle size and distance so the burst feels organic.
        let size: CGFloat = index.isMultiple(of: 2) ? 7 : 4
        let distance = radius * (index.isMultiple(of: 3) ? 0.75 : 1)
        return Circle()
            .fill(color)
            .frame(width: size, height: size)
            // Scale before offsetting, otherwise the scale also shrinks the
            // travel distance and the particles never leave the icon.
            .scaleEffect(exploded ? 0.3 : 1)
            .offset(
                x: exploded ? CGFloat(cos(angle)) * distance : 0,
                y: exploded ? CGFloat(sin(angle)) * distance : 0
            )
            .opacity(exploded ? 0 : 1)
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Emits a burst of particles every time `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image(systemName: isLiked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
    ///     .burst(trigger: isLiked, color: .pink, isEnabled: isLiked)
    /// ```
    func burst<Trigger: Equatable>(
        trigger: Trigger,
        color: Color = .pink,
        count: Int = 12,
        radius: CGFloat = 36,
        isEnabled: Bool = true
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(BurstModifier(trigger: trigger, color: color, count: count, radius: radius, isEnabled: isEnabled))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var liked = false
        var body: some View {
            Button {
                liked.toggle()
            } label: {
                Image(systemName: liked ? "heart.fill" : "heart")
                    .font(.system(size: 44))
                    .foregroundStyle(liked ? Color.pink : Color.secondary)
                    .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .burst(trigger: liked, isEnabled: liked)
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```
