## Checkmark Draw (`checkmark`)

A success mark draws itself: circle stroke, fill, then a popping check.

- API: `AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked:)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/AnimatedCheckmark.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/AnimatedCheckmark.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/CheckmarkShape.swift

### Usage

```swift
AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked: isDone)
    .frame(width: 80, height: 80)

AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked: saved, color: .blue, lineWidth: 3)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI AnimatedCheckmark view (iOS 17+) with isChecked, color (green) and lineWidth (4 at 60 pt, scaled with size). It is square. Layer three parts in a ZStack: a circle stroke trimmed from 0 to 1 and rotated −90° so it draws clockwise from the top (easeInOut 0.45 s); a filled circle that scales from 0.6 and fades in with a spring after 0.35 s; and a white checkmark path (short stroke down-right, long stroke up-right, round caps and joins) trimmed from 0 to 1 with easeOut 0.3 s after 0.55 s. Finish with a small bouncy scale pop at 0.75 s. Unchecking reverses everything without delays. With Reduce Motion on, replace the sequence with a 0.2 s fade.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A success mark that draws itself: the circle strokes around, fills, then
/// the checkmark is drawn on top with a small pop. Unchecking erases it.
public struct AnimatedCheckmark: View {
    private let isChecked: Bool
    private let color: Color
    private let lineWidth: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isChecked: Draws the mark when true, erases it when false.
    ///   - color: Circle colour; the checkmark is white on top of it.
    ///   - lineWidth: Stroke width, scaled with the view's size (at 60 pt).
    public init(isChecked: Bool, color: Color = .green, lineWidth: CGFloat = 4) {
        self.isChecked = isChecked
        self.color = color
        self.lineWidth = lineWidth
    }

    public var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let side = min(geometry.size.width, geometry.size.height)
            let scale = side / 60
            ZStack {
                Circle()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: isChecked ? 1 : 0)
                    .stroke(color, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth * scale, lineCap: .round))
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))
                    .animation(timing(.easeInOut(duration: 0.45)), value: isChecked)
                Circle()
                    .fill(color)
                    .scaleEffect(isChecked ? 1 : 0.6)
                    .opacity(isChecked ? 1 : 0)
                    .animation(timing(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.6).delay(isChecked ? 0.35 : 0)), value: isChecked)
                CheckmarkShape()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: isChecked ? 1 : 0)
                    .stroke(.white, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth * 1.2 * scale, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
                    .frame(width: side * 0.42, height: side * 0.32)
                    .offset(y: side * 0.02)
                    .animation(timing(.easeOut(duration: 0.3).delay(isChecked ? 0.55 : 0)), value: isChecked)
            }
            .frame(width: side, height: side)
            .scaleEffect(isChecked && !reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.95)
            .animation(timing(.spring(response: 0.3, dampingFraction: 0.4).delay(isChecked ? 0.75 : 0)), value: isChecked)
            .frame(width: geometry.size.width, height: geometry.size.height)
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(isChecked ? Text("Done") : Text("Not done"))
    }

    /// Reduce Motion: skip the drawing and just fade.
    private func timing(_ animation: Animation) -> Animation {
        reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : animation
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var checked = false

        var body: some View {
            AnimatedCheckmark(isChecked: checked)
                .frame(width: 80, height: 80)
                .onTapGesture { checked.toggle() }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - CheckmarkShape.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

// Shared by StatusButton and AnimatedCheckmark.

import SwiftUI

/// A checkmark drawn left to right, sized to its frame.
struct CheckmarkShape: Shape {
    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.midY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.minX + rect.width * 0.38, y: rect.maxY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.minY))
        return path
    }
}
```

## Confetti (`confetti`)

Confetti bursts out of the view, tumbles under gravity and fades.

- API: `.confetti(trigger:)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/Confetti.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/Confetti.swift

### Usage

```swift
@State private var orders = 0

Button("Complete order") { orders += 1 }
    .confetti(trigger: orders)

Text("🎉 Level up!")
    .confetti(trigger: level, colors: [.yellow, .orange], count: 120)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .confetti(trigger:colors:count:spread:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Each change of the equatable trigger appends a burst with a start date and 80 random pieces, removed after 2.4 s. Each piece has a velocity fanned ±60° around straight up (speed up to 3.2 × spread), a spin rate, a wobble phase, a 5–9 × 8–14 pt size, a colour index and every fourth one is a circle. Draw all bursts in one Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), in an overlay enlarged by .padding(−spread) (160 pt) so confetti flies beyond the view, with hit testing off. Position = origin + velocity × (1 − e^(−1.6t)) / 1.6 + ½ × gravity × t² (air drag plus gravity), rotate by spin × t, scale x by cos(wobble + 8t) to fake turning over, and fade out over the last 0.6 s. With Reduce Motion on, skip the burst.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Confetti that bursts up and out of the view whenever `trigger` changes,
/// then tumbles down under gravity and fades. Drawn in a single `Canvas`, so
/// a few hundred pieces stay cheap.
struct ConfettiModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Trigger
    var colors: [Color]
    var count: Int
    var spread: CGFloat

    @State private var bursts: [ConfettiBurst] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                if !bursts.isEmpty {
                    TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
                        Canvas { context, size in
                            let now = timeline.date
                            for burst in bursts {
                                burst.draw(in: &context, size: size, time: now.timeIntervalSince(burst.start), colors: colors)
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    // Draw well beyond the view's own bounds.
                    .padding(-spread)
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
            .onChange(of: trigger) {
                guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                let burst = ConfettiBurst(count: count, spread: spread)
                bursts.append(burst)
                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + ConfettiBurst.lifetime) {
                    bursts.removeAll { $0.id == burst.id }
                }
            }
    }
}

struct ConfettiBurst: Identifiable {
    static let lifetime: Double = 2.4

    struct Piece {
        var velocity: CGVector
        var spin: Double
        var wobble: Double
        var size: CGSize
        var colorIndex: Int
        var isCircle: Bool
    }

    let id = UUID()
    let start = Date()
    let pieces: [Piece]

    init(count: Int, spread: CGFloat) {
        pieces = (0..<max(1, count)).map { index in
            // Mostly upward, fanned out ±60° from vertical.
            let angle = -Double.pi / 2 + Double.random(in: -1.05...1.05)
            let speed = Double.random(in: 0.55...1.0) * Double(spread) * 3.2
            return Piece(
                velocity: CGVector(dx: cos(angle) * speed, dy: sin(angle) * speed),
                spin: Double.random(in: -9...9),
                wobble: Double.random(in: 0...(2 * .pi)),
                size: CGSize(width: .random(in: 5...9), height: .random(in: 8...14)),
                colorIndex: index,
                isCircle: index.isMultiple(of: 4)
            )
        }
    }

    func draw(in context: inout GraphicsContext, size: CGSize, time: Double, colors: [Color]) {
        guard time >= 0, time < Self.lifetime, !colors.isEmpty else { return }
        let origin = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
        let gravity = 900.0
        let drag = 1.6
        // Velocity decays with air drag; position integrates it.
        let decay = (1 - exp(-drag * time)) / drag
        let fade = time > Self.lifetime - 0.6 ? (Self.lifetime - time) / 0.6 : 1
        for piece in pieces {
            let x = origin.x + piece.velocity.dx * decay
            let y = origin.y + piece.velocity.dy * decay + 0.5 * gravity * time * time * 0.55
            var copy = context
            copy.opacity = fade
            copy.translateBy(x: x, y: y)
            copy.rotate(by: .radians(piece.spin * time))
            // Squash horizontally to fake the piece turning over in 3D.
            copy.scaleBy(x: CGFloat(cos(piece.wobble + time * 8)), y: 1)
            let rect = CGRect(
                x: -piece.size.width / 2,
                y: -piece.size.height / 2,
                width: piece.size.width,
                height: piece.isCircle ? piece.size.width : piece.size.height
            )
            let shape = piece.isCircle ? Path(ellipseIn: rect) : Path(rect)
            copy.fill(shape, with: .color(colors[piece.colorIndex % colors.count]))
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Fires a confetti burst from the view each time `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Button("Complete order") { orders += 1 }
    ///     .confetti(trigger: orders)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - trigger: Any equatable value; each change fires one burst.
    ///   - colors: Colours the pieces cycle through.
    ///   - count: Pieces per burst.
    ///   - spread: How far beyond the view's bounds confetti may travel.
    func confetti<Trigger: Equatable>(
        trigger: Trigger,
        colors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .green, .blue, .purple],
        count: Int = 80,
        spread: CGFloat = 160
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ConfettiModifier(trigger: trigger, colors: colors, count: count, spread: spread))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var count = 0

        var body: some View {
            Button("Celebrate 🎉") { count += 1 }
                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                .confetti(trigger: count)
                .frame(width: 400, height: 400)
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Loaders (`loaders`)

Five looping activity indicators: spinner, dots, bars, orbit and pulse.

- API: `MotionLoader(.spinner)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/MotionLoader.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/MotionLoader.swift

### Usage

```swift
MotionLoader(.spinner)
    .frame(width: 32, height: 32)

MotionLoader(.dots, color: .secondary)
    .frame(width: 44, height: 44)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI MotionLoader view (iOS 17+) with a style enum (spinner, dots, bars, orbit, pulse), a color and a speed multiplier. It is square and drives everything from TimelineView(.animation) time, sizing parts relative to its side. Spinner: a round-capped arc whose trim length breathes between 15% and 75% while it rotates. Dots: three dots hopping up in sequence (max(0, sin(6t − i·0.9))) and brightening at the top. Bars: five capsules whose heights follow a sine wave offset per bar. Orbit: two dots circling each other, scaled and layered by a fake depth. Pulse: two rings expanding and fading in turn around a centre dot. Label it "Loading" for accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, show a dot that slowly breathes in opacity.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A set of looping activity indicators. Pick a style; size it with `.frame`.
public struct MotionLoader: View {
    /// The look of the loader.
    public enum Style: String, CaseIterable, Sendable {
        /// An arc that spins while its length breathes.
        case spinner
        /// Three dots hopping in sequence.
        case dots
        /// Equaliser bars rising and falling in a wave.
        case bars
        /// Two dots orbiting each other.
        case orbit
        /// A ring that pulses outward.
        case pulse
    }

    private let style: Style
    private let color: Color
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - style: Which loader to draw.
    ///   - color: Fill or stroke colour.
    ///   - speed: Multiplier on the default tempo.
    public init(_ style: Style = .spinner, color: Color = .accentColor, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.style = style
        self.color = color
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
            // Reduce Motion: a slow opacity breathe instead of movement.
            let time = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let side = min(geometry.size.width, geometry.size.height)
                Group {
                    if reduceMotion {
                        Circle()
                            .fill(color)
                            .frame(width: side * 0.4, height: side * 0.4)
                            .opacity(0.4 + 0.4 * (0.5 + 0.5 * sin(time * 2)))
                    } else {
                        loader(time: time, side: side)
                    }
                }
                .frame(width: geometry.size.width, height: geometry.size.height)
            }
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently)
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private func loader(time: Double, side: CGFloat) -> some View {
        switch style {
        case .spinner:
            let breathe = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(time * 3)
            Circle()
                .trim(from: 0, to: 0.15 + 0.6 * breathe)
                .stroke(color, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: side * 0.1, lineCap: .round))
                .rotationEffect(.radians(time * 5))
                .padding(side * 0.05)

        case .dots:
            HStack(spacing: side * 0.1) {
                ForEach(0..<3, id: \.self) { index in
                    let hop = max(0, sin(time * 6 - Double(index) * 0.9))
                    Circle()
                        .fill(color)
                        .frame(width: side * 0.22, height: side * 0.22)
                        .offset(y: -side * 0.25 * hop)
                        .opacity(0.5 + 0.5 * hop)
                }
            }
            .offset(y: side * 0.1)

        case .bars:
            HStack(alignment: .center, spacing: side * 0.07) {
                ForEach(0..<5, id: \.self) { index in
                    let level = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(time * 5 - Double(index) * 0.7)
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(color)
                        .frame(width: side * 0.12, height: side * (0.25 + 0.65 * level))
                }
            }

        case .orbit:
            ZStack {
                ForEach(0..<2, id: \.self) { index in
                    let angle = time * 4 + Double(index) * .pi
                    let depth = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(angle)
                    Circle()
                        .fill(color)
                        .frame(width: side * 0.3, height: side * 0.3)
                        .scaleEffect(0.7 + 0.3 * depth)
                        .opacity(0.6 + 0.4 * depth)
                        .offset(x: cos(angle) * side * 0.3)
                        .zIndex(depth)
                }
            }

        case .pulse:
            ZStack {
                ForEach(0..<2, id: \.self) { index in
                    let phase = (time * 0.8 + Double(index) * 0.5).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
                    Circle()
                        .stroke(color, lineWidth: side * 0.06)
                        .scaleEffect(0.2 + 0.8 * phase)
                        .opacity(1 - phase)
                }
                Circle()
                    .fill(color)
                    .frame(width: side * 0.2, height: side * 0.2)
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    HStack(spacing: 24) {
        ForEach(MotionLoader.Style.allCases, id: \.self) { style in
            MotionLoader(style)
                .frame(width: 44, height: 44)
        }
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Morphing Blob (`morphing-blob`)

An organic, lava-lamp blob whose outline never stops changing.

- API: `MorphingBlob()`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/MorphingBlob.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/MorphingBlob.swift

### Usage

```swift
MorphingBlob(colors: [.purple, .pink, .orange])
    .frame(width: 200, height: 200)

MorphingBlob(fill: Color.blue.opacity(0.3), points: 8, wobble: 0.1)
    .overlay(Image(systemName: "mic.fill"))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI MorphingBlob view (iOS 17+) generic over a ShapeStyle fill, with a convenience initializer taking colours for a diagonal LinearGradient. Draw a custom Shape in TimelineView(.animation): place N control points (6) evenly around the centre, each at radius base × (1 + wobble × (0.6·sin(1.1t + 1.7i) + 0.4·sin(0.7t + 2.9i))), where base = half the side × (1 − wobble) and wobble is 0.18. Connect them into a smooth closed curve with a Catmull-Rom spline converted to cubic Béziers (control points p1 + (p2 − p0)/6 and p2 − (p3 − p1)/6). Keep a 1:1 aspect ratio and hide it from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, freeze the shape.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// An organic blob whose outline keeps morphing, like a lava lamp. Use it as
/// an avatar backdrop, a "listening" indicator or a hero decoration.
public struct MorphingBlob<Fill: ShapeStyle>: View {
    private let fill: Fill
    private let points: Int
    private let wobble: CGFloat
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - fill: Any shape style: a colour, gradient or material.
    ///   - points: Number of lobes around the outline (4…10 looks organic).
    ///   - wobble: How far the outline moves in and out, as a fraction of the radius.
    ///   - speed: Multiplier on the morphing tempo.
    public init(fill: Fill, points: Int = 6, wobble: CGFloat = 0.18, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.fill = fill
        self.points = points
        self.wobble = wobble
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            BlobShape(
                time: reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed,
                points: points,
                wobble: wobble
            )
            .fill(fill)
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

public extension MorphingBlob where Fill == LinearGradient {
    /// A blob filled with a diagonal gradient.
    init(colors: [Color] = [.purple, .pink, .orange], points: Int = 6, wobble: CGFloat = 0.18, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.init(
            fill: LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing),
            points: points,
            wobble: wobble,
            speed: speed
        )
    }
}

/// A closed, smooth outline through `points` control points whose distance
/// from the centre is a sum of slow sine waves.
struct BlobShape: Shape {
    var time: Double
    var points: Int
    var wobble: CGFloat

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let count = max(3, points)
        let centre = CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
        let baseRadius = min(rect.width, rect.height) / 2 * (1 - wobble)
        let vertices: [CGPoint] = (0..<count).map { index in
            let angle = Double(index) / Double(count) * 2 * .pi
            let i = Double(index)
            // Two waves with unrelated frequencies so the motion never visibly repeats.
            let offset = sin(time * 1.1 + i * 1.7) * 0.6 + sin(time * 0.7 + i * 2.9) * 0.4
            let radius = baseRadius * (1 + wobble * CGFloat(offset))
            return CGPoint(x: centre.x + CGFloat(cos(angle)) * radius, y: centre.y + CGFloat(sin(angle)) * radius)
        }
        return smoothClosedPath(through: vertices)
    }

    /// Catmull-Rom spline through the points, as cubic Béziers.
    private func smoothClosedPath(through p: [CGPoint]) -> Path {
        var path = Path()
        let n = p.count
        path.move(to: p[0])
        for i in 0..<n {
            let p0 = p[(i - 1 + n) % n], p1 = p[i], p2 = p[(i + 1) % n], p3 = p[(i + 2) % n]
            let c1 = CGPoint(x: p1.x + (p2.x - p0.x) / 6, y: p1.y + (p2.y - p0.y) / 6)
            let c2 = CGPoint(x: p2.x - (p3.x - p1.x) / 6, y: p2.y - (p3.y - p1.y) / 6)
            path.addCurve(to: p2, control1: c1, control2: c2)
        }
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

#Preview {
    MorphingBlob()
        .frame(width: 200, height: 200)
        .padding()
}
```

## Draw On (`draw-on`)

Any Shape strokes itself on like a pen, and erases back.

- API: `Shape.drawOn()`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/DrawOn.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/DrawOn.swift

### Usage

```swift
Circle()
    .drawOn()
    .frame(width: 80, height: 80)

SignaturePath()
    .drawOn(isDrawn: signed, style: .blue, lineWidth: 3, duration: 1.6)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Shape extension drawOn(isDrawn:style:lineWidth:duration:) (iOS 17+) returning a DrawOnShape view. It strokes shape.trim(from: 0, to: progress) with the given ShapeStyle (accent colour), a StrokeStyle with lineWidth (3 pt), round caps and round joins, and pads by lineWidth / 2 so the stroke isn't clipped. Keep progress in @State; on appear and whenever isDrawn changes, animate it to 1 (draw) or 0 (erase) with easeInOut over duration (1.2 s). Works with any Shape, including custom paths, which are drawn in path order. With Reduce Motion on, use a 0.2 s ease.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Strokes any `Shape` as if a pen were drawing it, from the start of its
/// path to the end. Draws on appear and whenever `isDrawn` turns on; erases
/// back when it turns off.
public struct DrawOnShape<S: Shape>: View {
    private let shape: S
    private let isDrawn: Bool
    private let style: AnyShapeStyle
    private let lineWidth: CGFloat
    private let duration: Double

    @State private var progress: CGFloat = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    init(shape: S, isDrawn: Bool, style: AnyShapeStyle, lineWidth: CGFloat, duration: Double) {
        self.shape = shape
        self.isDrawn = isDrawn
        self.style = style
        self.lineWidth = lineWidth
        self.duration = duration
    }

    public var body: some View {
        shape
            .trim(from: 0, to: progress)
            .stroke(style, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
            .padding(lineWidth / 2)
            .onAppear { update(isDrawn) }
            .onChange(of: isDrawn) { _, newValue in update(newValue) }
    }

    private func update(_ drawn: Bool) {
        // Reduce Motion: the stroke appears all at once.
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .easeInOut(duration: duration)) {
            progress = drawn ? 1 : 0
        }
    }
}

public extension Shape {
    /// Draws the shape's outline like a pen stroke.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Circle()
    ///     .drawOn()
    ///     .frame(width: 80, height: 80)
    ///
    /// SignaturePath()
    ///     .drawOn(isDrawn: signed, style: .blue, lineWidth: 3, duration: 1.6)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - isDrawn: Draws when true, erases when false.
    ///   - style: Stroke colour or gradient.
    ///   - lineWidth: Stroke width, in points.
    ///   - duration: Time to draw the whole path, in seconds.
    @MainActor
    func drawOn<Style: ShapeStyle>(
        isDrawn: Bool = true,
        style: Style = Color.accentColor,
        lineWidth: CGFloat = 3,
        duration: Double = 1.2
    ) -> DrawOnShape<Self> {
        DrawOnShape(shape: self, isDrawn: isDrawn, style: AnyShapeStyle(style), lineWidth: lineWidth, duration: duration)
    }
}

#Preview {
    HStack(spacing: 24) {
        Circle().drawOn().frame(width: 70, height: 70)
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14).drawOn(style: .pink, duration: 2).frame(width: 90, height: 70)
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Progress Ring (`progress-ring`)

A gradient ring springs to each value as the percentage rolls.

- API: `ProgressRing(progress:)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/ProgressRing.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/ProgressRing.swift

### Usage

```swift
ProgressRing(progress: uploaded)
    .frame(width: 120, height: 120)

ProgressRing(progress: steps / goal, colors: [.green, .mint]) {
    Image(systemName: "figure.walk").font(.title)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ProgressRing (iOS 17+) with progress (0…1), lineWidth (12 pt), colors (cyan, blue, purple) and an optional label view builder (default: the percentage). In a ZStack, stroke a full Circle in secondary at 18 % opacity, then a Circle().trim(from: 0, to: progress) stroked with AngularGradient(colors:) over 0–360° and a round line cap, rotated −90° so it starts at twelve o'clock. Pad by lineWidth / 2. Animate progress changes with .spring(response: 0.6, dampingFraction: 0.75). The default label is the percentage as .title2.bold().monospacedDigit() with .contentTransition(.numericText(value:)), so the digits roll. Expose the percentage as the accessibility value. With Reduce Motion on, use a short ease.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A circular progress ring with a gradient stroke and rounded cap that
/// springs to each new value, with the percentage counting in the middle.
public struct ProgressRing<Label: View>: View {
    private let progress: Double
    private let lineWidth: CGFloat
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let label: Label

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - progress: 0…1.
    ///   - lineWidth: Ring thickness, in points.
    ///   - colors: Gradient along the ring, from start to end.
    ///   - label: What sits inside the ring.
    public init(
        progress: Double,
        lineWidth: CGFloat = 12,
        colors: [Color] = [.cyan, .blue, .purple],
        @ViewBuilder label: () -> Label
    ) {
        self.progress = progress
        self.lineWidth = lineWidth
        self.colors = colors
        self.label = label()
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let clamped = min(1, max(0, progress))
        ZStack {
            Circle()
                .stroke(Color.secondary.opacity(0.18), lineWidth: lineWidth)
            Circle()
                .trim(from: 0, to: clamped)
                .stroke(
                    AngularGradient(colors: colors, center: .center, startAngle: .degrees(0), endAngle: .degrees(360)),
                    style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round)
                )
                .rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))
            label
        }
        .padding(lineWidth / 2)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(response: 0.6, dampingFraction: 0.75), value: clamped)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityValue(clamped.formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(0))))
    }
}

public extension ProgressRing where Label == ProgressRingPercent {
    /// A ring with the percentage in the middle.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ProgressRing(progress: uploaded)
    ///     .frame(width: 120, height: 120)
    /// ```
    init(progress: Double, lineWidth: CGFloat = 12, colors: [Color] = [.cyan, .blue, .purple]) {
        self.init(progress: progress, lineWidth: lineWidth, colors: colors) {
            ProgressRingPercent(progress: progress)
        }
    }
}

/// The default label: a percentage that rolls to each new value.
public struct ProgressRingPercent: View {
    let progress: Double

    public var body: some View {
        let value = min(1, max(0, progress))
        Text(value.formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(0))))
            .font(.title2.bold().monospacedDigit())
            .contentTransition(.numericText(value: value))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var progress = 0.35
        var body: some View {
            ProgressRing(progress: progress)
                .frame(width: 120, height: 120)
                .onTapGesture { progress = progress >= 1 ? 0.1 : progress + 0.3 }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```

## Skeleton (`skeleton`)

A shimmering placeholder of the view's own layout while it loads.

- API: `.skeleton(isLoading:)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Loop / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/Skeleton.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/Skeleton.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Text/Shimmer.swift

### Usage

```swift
ArticleRow(article)
    .skeleton(isLoading: isLoading)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .skeleton(isLoading:) view modifier (iOS 17+). While loading, apply .redacted(reason: .placeholder) so text and images become grey blocks in the view's real layout, then the shimmer modifier (a white 80 % highlight band, 35 % of the width, sweeping left to right every 1.6 s, masked by the content), disable hit testing and hide the view from accessibility. When loading ends, remove both and animate with easeInOut(0.3 s) so the real content fades in. The shimmer pauses for Reduce Motion.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Swaps a view for a shimmering grey placeholder of the same layout while
/// it loads, then fades the real content in.
struct SkeletonModifier: ViewModifier {
    var isLoading: Bool

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .redacted(reason: isLoading ? .placeholder : [])
            // `.shimmer()` already pauses itself for Reduce Motion.
            .shimmer(isActive: isLoading)
            .allowsHitTesting(!isLoading)
            .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: isLoading)
            // Placeholder text is meaningless to VoiceOver.
            .accessibilityHidden(isLoading)
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shows a shimmering placeholder of the view's own layout while
    /// `isLoading` is true.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ArticleRow(article)
    ///     .skeleton(isLoading: article.isPlaceholder)
    /// ```
    func skeleton(isLoading: Bool) -> some View {
        modifier(SkeletonModifier(isLoading: isLoading))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var loading = true
        var body: some View {
            HStack(spacing: 12) {
                Image(systemName: "person.crop.circle.fill").font(.largeTitle)
                VStack(alignment: .leading) {
                    Text("Taylor Appleseed").font(.headline)
                    Text("Shipped a new build").font(.subheadline)
                }
            }
            .skeleton(isLoading: loading)
            .onTapGesture { loading.toggle() }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}

// MARK: - Shimmer.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

import SwiftUI

/// A band of light that sweeps across the view, clipped to the view's own
/// shape. Works on text, images, and skeleton placeholders.
struct ShimmerModifier: ViewModifier {
    var isActive: Bool
    var duration: Double
    var bandWidth: CGFloat
    var highlight: Color

    @State private var animating = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                if isActive {
                    GeometryReader { geometry in
                        let width = geometry.size.width
                        let band = max(1, width * bandWidth)
                        LinearGradient(
                            colors: [.clear, highlight, .clear],
                            startPoint: .leading,
                            endPoint: .trailing
                        )
                        .frame(width: band, height: geometry.size.height)
                        .offset(x: animating ? width : -band)
                    }
                    .mask { content }
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
                    .onAppear {
                        animating = false
                        // Reduce Motion: no sweep; the band stays parked off-screen.
                        guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                        withAnimation(.linear(duration: duration).repeatForever(autoreverses: false)) {
                            animating = true
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Sweeps a highlight across the view.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text("Loading…").font(.title).shimmer()
    /// RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8).fill(.gray.opacity(0.3)).shimmer()
    /// ```
    func shimmer(
        isActive: Bool = true,
        duration: Double = 1.6,
        bandWidth: CGFloat = 0.35,
        highlight: Color = .white.opacity(0.8)
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ShimmerModifier(
            isActive: isActive,
            duration: duration,
            bandWidth: bandWidth,
            highlight: highlight
        ))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 16) {
        Text("Shimmering title")
            .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            .foregroundStyle(.gray)
            .shimmer()
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
            .fill(.gray.opacity(0.25))
            .frame(height: 60)
            .shimmer()
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Sliding Tabs (`sliding-tabs`)

A segmented control whose pill or underline glides to the selection.

- API: `SlidingTabs([…], selection:)`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Tap
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/SlidingTabs.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/SlidingTabs.swift

### Usage

```swift
SlidingTabs(["Day", "Week", "Month"], selection: $range)

SlidingTabs(Category.allCases, selection: $category, indicator: .underline) { $0.title }
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI SlidingTabs control (iOS 17+) over Hashable options with a selection binding, an indicator style (.pill or .underline), a tint and a title closure (plus a convenience init for [String]). Show the options as plain Buttons in an HStack inside a 4 pt padded capsule tinted secondary at 12 % (pill style only). Behind the selected title only, draw the indicator — a capsule filled with the tint (title turns white), or a 3 pt capsule at the bottom inset 10 pt (title turns tint) — with .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "indicator", in: namespace), so it glides between options. Change the selection inside withAnimation(.spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.8)), and add the .isSelected trait. With Reduce Motion on, use a 0.15 s ease.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A segmented control whose selection indicator (a pill or an underline)
/// glides to the tapped option with `matchedGeometryEffect`.
public struct SlidingTabs<Value: Hashable>: View {
    /// How the selected option is marked.
    public enum Indicator: Sendable {
        /// A filled capsule behind the selected title.
        case pill
        /// A short bar under the selected title.
        case underline
    }

    @Binding private var selection: Value
    private let options: [Value]
    private let title: (Value) -> String
    private let indicator: Indicator
    private let tint: Color

    @Namespace private var namespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - options: The options, in order.
    ///   - selection: The selected option.
    ///   - indicator: `.pill` or `.underline`.
    ///   - tint: Colour of the indicator.
    ///   - title: The title of an option.
    public init(
        _ options: [Value],
        selection: Binding<Value>,
        indicator: Indicator = .pill,
        tint: Color = .accentColor,
        title: @escaping (Value) -> String
    ) {
        self.options = options
        _selection = selection
        self.indicator = indicator
        self.tint = tint
        self.title = title
    }

    public var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 4) {
            ForEach(options, id: \.self) { option in
                let selected = option == selection
                Button {
                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.15) : .spring(response: 0.35, dampingFraction: 0.8)) {
                        selection = option
                    }
                } label: {
                    Text(title(option))
                        .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                        .padding(.horizontal, 14)
                        .padding(.vertical, 8)
                        .foregroundStyle(indicator == .pill && selected ? Color.white : selected ? tint : Color.secondary)
                        .background { marker(selected) }
                        .contentShape(Rectangle())
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .accessibilityAddTraits(selected ? .isSelected : [])
            }
        }
        .padding(4)
        .background {
            if indicator == .pill {
                Capsule().fill(Color.secondary.opacity(0.12))
            }
        }
    }

    @ViewBuilder
    private func marker(_ selected: Bool) -> some View {
        if selected {
            switch indicator {
            case .pill:
                Capsule()
                    .fill(tint)
                    .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "indicator", in: namespace)
            case .underline:
                VStack {
                    Spacer()
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(tint)
                        .frame(height: 3)
                        .padding(.horizontal, 10)
                }
                .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "indicator", in: namespace)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension SlidingTabs where Value == String {
    /// Tabs whose options are their own titles.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// SlidingTabs(["Day", "Week", "Month"], selection: $range)
    /// ```
    init(_ options: [String], selection: Binding<String>, indicator: Indicator = .pill, tint: Color = .accentColor) {
        self.init(options, selection: selection, indicator: indicator, tint: tint) { $0 }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var range = "Week"
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 24) {
                SlidingTabs(["Day", "Week", "Month"], selection: $range)
                SlidingTabs(["Day", "Week", "Month"], selection: $range, indicator: .underline)
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```

## Reading Progress (`reading-progress`)

A bar along the top fills as you scroll through the content.

- API: `ReadingProgressScrollView { … }`
- Component: Shape
- Trigger: Scroll
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/ReadingProgress.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Shape/ReadingProgress.swift

### Usage

```swift
ReadingProgressScrollView(color: .pink) {
    ArticleBody()
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ReadingProgressScrollView(color:height:content:) (iOS 17+): a vertical ScrollView whose content gets a top overlay holding a Color.clear layer with a Capsule (4 pt tall, the colour, a soft glow shadow) at its top-leading edge. Drive the layer with visualEffect, not state or a PreferenceKey (preferences don't reliably leave an iOS scroll view): frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView), viewport = proxy.bounds(of: .scrollView)?.size, progress = clamp(−frame.minY / (frame.height − viewport.height), 0, 1); scaleEffect(x: viewport.width × progress / frame.width, anchor: .topLeading), then offset(x: −frame.minX, y: −frame.minY) to pin it to the top. Disable hit testing.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A vertical scroll view with a reading-progress bar along its top edge
/// that fills as you scroll from the top to the bottom of the content.
public struct ReadingProgressScrollView<Content: View>: View {
    private let color: Color
    private let height: CGFloat
    private let content: Content

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - color: Bar colour.
    ///   - height: Bar thickness, in points.
    ///   - content: The scrolling content.
    public init(color: Color = .accentColor, height: CGFloat = 4, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) {
        self.color = color
        self.height = height
        self.content = content()
    }

    public var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            content.overlay(alignment: .top) { bar }
        }
    }

    /// The bar lives inside the scrolled content and is pinned and sized by
    /// `visualEffect`, so it needs no state, no preferences (they don't reach
    /// out of an iOS scroll view reliably) and no extra layout passes.
    private var bar: some View {
        Color.clear
            .overlay(alignment: .topLeading) {
                Capsule()
                    .fill(color)
                    .frame(height: height)
                    .shadow(color: color.opacity(0.5), radius: 4)
            }
            .visualEffect { effect, proxy in
                let frame = proxy.frame(in: .scrollView)
                let viewport = proxy.bounds(of: .scrollView)?.size ?? frame.size
                let scrollable = max(1, frame.height - viewport.height)
                let progress = min(1, max(0, -frame.minY / scrollable))
                return effect
                    // Span the scroll view's width, filled to `progress`.
                    .scaleEffect(x: viewport.width * progress / max(1, frame.width), y: 1, anchor: .topLeading)
                    // Stay pinned to the top of the visible area.
                    .offset(x: -frame.minX, y: -frame.minY)
            }
            .allowsHitTesting(false)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

#Preview {
    ReadingProgressScrollView(color: .pink) {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
            ForEach(0..<30, id: \.self) { index in
                Text("Paragraph \(index + 1). Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.")
            }
        }
        .padding()
    }
}
```

## Aurora (`aurora`)

Soft, blurred colour blobs drift slowly behind your content.

- API: `AuroraBackground()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/AuroraBackground.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/AuroraBackground.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    AuroraBackground(colors: [.purple, .blue, .teal, .pink])
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    Text("Welcome").font(.largeTitle.bold())
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI AuroraBackground view (iOS 17+). On a dark base color, draw one large circle per palette color (default purple, blue, teal, pink; 80% opacity, diameter 70% of the larger side). Each circle drifts on its own Lissajous path, x = cos(t·0.6 + phase)·30% width and y = sin(t·0.8 + phase·1.3)·30% height, where phase differs per index. Drive time from TimelineView(.animation) scaled by a speed parameter, blur the whole group with a ~60 pt radius, clip to bounds and hide it from accessibility.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Soft, slowly drifting colour blobs, heavily blurred. A calm animated
/// backdrop for onboarding screens, paywalls, or hero sections.
///
/// ```swift
/// ZStack {
///     AuroraBackground()
///         .ignoresSafeArea()
///     Text("Welcome").font(.largeTitle.bold())
/// }
/// ```
public struct AuroraBackground: View {
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let speed: Double
    private let blurRadius: CGFloat
    private let baseColor: Color

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    public init(
        colors: [Color] = [.purple, .blue, .teal, .pink],
        speed: Double = 0.4,
        blurRadius: CGFloat = 60,
        baseColor: Color = .black
    ) {
        self.colors = colors
        self.speed = speed
        self.blurRadius = blurRadius
        self.baseColor = baseColor
    }

    public var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: a still frame of the same blobs.
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                blobs(time: time, size: geometry.size)
            }
        }
        .background(baseColor)
        .clipped()
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func blobs(time: Double, size: CGSize) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(colors.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                blob(color: colors[index], index: index, time: time, size: size)
            }
        }
        .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)
        .blur(radius: blurRadius)
    }

    private func blob(color: Color, index: Int, time: Double, size: CGSize) -> some View {
        let phase = Double(index) * 1.7
        let diameter = max(size.width, size.height) * 0.7
        let x = CGFloat(cos(time * 0.6 + phase)) * size.width * 0.3
        let y = CGFloat(sin(time * 0.8 + phase * 1.3)) * size.height * 0.3
        return Circle()
            .fill(color.opacity(0.8))
            .frame(width: diameter, height: diameter)
            .offset(x: x, y: y)
    }
}

#Preview {
    ZStack {
        AuroraBackground()
            .ignoresSafeArea()
        Text("Welcome")
            .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
    }
}
```

## Mesh Gradient (`mesh-gradient`)

A 3×3 MeshGradient whose points drift so the colours flow like liquid.

- API: `AnimatedMeshGradient()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 18+ · macOS 15+ · visionOS 2+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/AnimatedMeshGradient.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/AnimatedMeshGradient.swift

### Usage

```swift
if #available(iOS 18, *) {
    AnimatedMeshGradient()
        .ignoresSafeArea()
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI AnimatedMeshGradient view for iOS 18+ (mark it @available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)) with nine colours (indigo, purple, pink / blue, purple, orange / teal, mint, yellow by default; fewer are repeated) and a speed. Inside TimelineView(.animation), draw MeshGradient(width: 3, height: 3, points:colors:). Keep the four corners fixed; slide the four edge midpoints along their own edge by sin(t × 2π / period + offset) × 0.2, and move the centre point in both axes by 0.25, giving each a different period between 6 and 10 s so the motion never repeats visibly. Hide it from accessibility, and with Reduce Motion on, pause it.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A 3×3 `MeshGradient` whose inner points drift in slow loops, so the
/// colours flow into each other like liquid.
@available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *)
public struct AnimatedMeshGradient: View {
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - colors: Nine colours, row by row from the top left. Fewer are
    ///     repeated; more are ignored.
    ///   - speed: 1 = default pace; 0.5 is half as fast.
    public init(
        colors: [Color] = [
            .indigo, .purple, .pink,
            .blue, .purple, .orange,
            .teal, .mint, .yellow,
        ],
        speed: Double = 1
    ) {
        let palette = colors.isEmpty ? [Color.blue] : colors
        self.colors = (0..<9).map { palette[$0 % palette.count] }
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let t = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            MeshGradient(width: 3, height: 3, points: Self.points(at: t), colors: colors)
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// Corners stay put; edge midpoints slide along their edge and the
    /// centre wanders, each on its own period.
    static func points(at t: Double) -> [SIMD2<Float>] {
        func wave(_ period: Double, _ amount: Double, _ offset: Double = 0) -> Float {
            Float(sin(t * 2 * .pi / period + offset) * amount)
        }
        return [
            [0, 0], [0.5 + wave(7, 0.2), 0], [1, 0],
            [0, 0.5 + wave(9, 0.2, 1)], [0.5 + wave(6, 0.25, 2), 0.5 + wave(8, 0.25)], [1, 0.5 + wave(10, 0.2, 3)],
            [0, 1], [0.5 + wave(8, 0.2, 4), 1], [1, 1],
        ]
    }
}

#Preview {
    if #available(iOS 18, macOS 15, visionOS 2, *) {
        AnimatedMeshGradient()
            .frame(width: 300, height: 200)
            .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 24))
    }
}
```

## Retro Grid (`retro-grid`)

A synthwave floor: a perspective grid scrolling toward you.

- API: `RetroGrid()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/RetroGrid.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/RetroGrid.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    Color.black
    RetroGrid(color: .pink)
    Text("NEON").font(.system(size: 60, weight: .black))
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI RetroGrid view (iOS 17+) with color (pink), spacing (40 pt), speed (0.8 rows per second) and horizon (0.35 of the height). In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation): with top = height × horizon and depth = height − top, draw horizontal lines at y = top + depth / z for z = n + 1 − fract(time × speed), n = 0…39, so the bottom edge is z = 1, rows bunch up toward the horizon and every row moves toward the viewer; draw lines from the vanishing point (centre, top) to (centre + k × spacing, bottom) for enough k to cover the width. Stroke the path twice: 3 pt at 35 % opacity for a glow, then 1 pt solid. Mask the view with a vertical gradient that is clear down to the horizon and opaque 45 % lower, so lines fade into the distance. Hide from accessibility; Reduce Motion pauses it.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A synthwave floor: a perspective grid that scrolls toward the viewer and
/// fades into the horizon.
public struct RetroGrid: View {
    private let color: Color
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let speed: Double
    private let horizon: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - color: Line colour.
    ///   - spacing: Distance between lines at the bottom edge, in points.
    ///   - speed: Grid rows passed per second.
    ///   - horizon: Height of the horizon, as a fraction of the view (0 = top).
    public init(color: Color = .pink, spacing: CGFloat = 40, speed: Double = 0.8, horizon: CGFloat = 0.35) {
        self.color = color
        self.spacing = spacing
        self.speed = speed
        self.horizon = horizon
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                draw(in: &context, size: size, time: time)
            }
        }
        .mask {
            LinearGradient(
                stops: [.init(color: .clear, location: horizon), .init(color: .black, location: min(1, horizon + 0.45))],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func draw(in context: inout GraphicsContext, size: CGSize, time: Double) {
        let top = size.height * horizon
        let depth = size.height - top
        guard depth > 0, spacing > 0 else { return }
        let centre = size.width / 2
        var path = Path()

        // Horizontal lines at depths z = 1, 2, 3…; y = top + depth / z puts
        // z = 1 at the bottom edge and z → ∞ at the horizon. Shifting z by the
        // fractional time moves every row toward the viewer.
        let shift = time * speed
        let scroll = shift - shift.rounded(.down)
        for row in 0..<40 {
            let z = CGFloat(Double(row) + 1 - scroll)
            guard z > 0.05 else { continue }
            let y = top + depth / z
            guard y <= size.height + 1 else { continue }
            path.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: y))
            path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: size.width, y: y))
        }

        // Lines running into the distance all meet at the vanishing point.
        let columns = Int(size.width / spacing) + 4
        for column in -columns...columns {
            let x = centre + CGFloat(column) * spacing
            path.move(to: CGPoint(x: centre, y: top))
            path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: size.height))
        }

        context.stroke(path, with: .color(color.opacity(0.35)), lineWidth: 3)
        context.stroke(path, with: .color(color), lineWidth: 1)
    }
}

#Preview {
    RetroGrid()
        .background(Color(red: 0.08, green: 0.02, blue: 0.15))
        .frame(width: 320, height: 200)
}
```

## Border Beam (`border-beam`)

A short comet of light runs around the card's border forever.

- API: `.borderBeam()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/BorderBeam.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/BorderBeam.swift

### Usage

```swift
PlanCard()
    .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))
    .borderBeam(cornerRadius: 20)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .borderBeam(cornerRadius:colors:lineWidth:length:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+). In an overlay TimelineView(.animation), compute head = fract(time / duration) (4 s per lap). Stroke RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:, style: .continuous).trim(from: head − length, to: head) with a LinearGradient of the colours (orange, pink, purple), lineWidth 2 pt and round caps; when head − length is negative, also stroke trim(from: 1 + head − length, to: 1) so the beam wraps past the path's start seamlessly. Draw the beam twice, once blurred by 2 × lineWidth underneath for a glow. Pad by lineWidth / 2, disable hit testing and hide from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on, park the beam.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A short comet of light that runs around the view's rounded border forever.
struct BorderBeamModifier: ViewModifier {
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat
    var colors: [Color]
    var lineWidth: CGFloat
    var length: CGFloat
    var duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            // Reduce Motion: the beam is parked at the top-left corner.
            TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
                let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
                let head = CGFloat((time / max(0.1, duration)).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1))
                ZStack {
                    beam(head: head).blur(radius: lineWidth * 2)
                    beam(head: head)
                }
            }
            .allowsHitTesting(false)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }

    /// The beam from `head - length` to `head`, split in two when it wraps
    /// past the start of the path.
    private func beam(head: CGFloat) -> some View {
        let shape = RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius, style: .continuous)
        let tail = head - length
        let style = StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round)
        let gradient = LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
        return ZStack {
            shape.trim(from: max(0, tail), to: head).stroke(gradient, style: style)
            if tail < 0 {
                shape.trim(from: 1 + tail, to: 1).stroke(gradient, style: style)
            }
        }
        .padding(lineWidth / 2)
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Sends a beam of light around the view's border, forever.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// PlanCard()
    ///     .background(.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))
    ///     .borderBeam(cornerRadius: 20)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - cornerRadius: Match the view's own corner radius.
    ///   - colors: Gradient of the beam.
    ///   - lineWidth: Beam thickness, in points.
    ///   - length: Fraction of the border the beam covers (0…1).
    ///   - duration: Seconds per lap.
    func borderBeam(
        cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16,
        colors: [Color] = [.orange, .pink, .purple],
        lineWidth: CGFloat = 2,
        length: CGFloat = 0.2,
        duration: Double = 4
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(BorderBeamModifier(
            cornerRadius: cornerRadius,
            colors: colors,
            lineWidth: lineWidth,
            length: min(1, max(0.01, length)),
            duration: duration
        ))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20, style: .continuous)
        .fill(Color(white: 0.08))
        .frame(width: 240, height: 140)
        .overlay(Text("Pro plan").font(.headline).foregroundStyle(.white))
        .borderBeam(cornerRadius: 20)
        .padding()
}
```

## Waves (`waves`)

Layered sine waves roll across the bottom, back layers slower and paler.

- API: `WaveBackground()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/WaveBackground.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/WaveBackground.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack(alignment: .top) {
    WaveBackground()
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    Text("Ocean").font(.largeTitle.bold()).padding(.top, 80)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI WaveBackground view (iOS 17+) with colors (one per layer, back to front: cyan 35 %, blue 45 %, indigo 70 %), amplitude (12 pt) and speed. In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), for each layer with depth d = layer / (count − 1): baseline at height × (0.45 + 0.2 d), wavelength width × (0.9 − 0.3 d), phase = time × (0.6 + 0.5 d), alternating direction per layer. Build a path from the bottom-left corner along y = baseline + sin(x / wavelength × 2π + phase + layer) × amplitude × (0.7 + 0.3 d) sampled every 4 pt, down to the bottom-right corner, close it and fill it with the layer's colour. Hide from accessibility; Reduce Motion pauses it.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Layered sine waves rolling across the bottom of the view, each layer a
/// little slower and paler than the one in front, like an ocean horizon.
public struct WaveBackground: View {
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let amplitude: CGFloat
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - colors: One colour per layer, back to front.
    ///   - amplitude: Wave height, in points.
    ///   - speed: 1 = default pace.
    public init(
        colors: [Color] = [.cyan.opacity(0.35), .blue.opacity(0.45), .indigo.opacity(0.7)],
        amplitude: CGFloat = 12,
        speed: Double = 1
    ) {
        self.colors = colors
        self.amplitude = amplitude
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            Canvas { context, size in
                for (layer, color) in colors.enumerated() {
                    let depth = CGFloat(layer) / CGFloat(max(1, colors.count - 1))
                    // Back layers sit higher, move slower and have longer waves.
                    let baseline = size.height * (0.45 + 0.2 * depth)
                    let wavelength = size.width * (0.9 - 0.3 * depth)
                    let phase = time * (0.6 + 0.5 * depth) * (layer.isMultiple(of: 2) ? 1 : -1)
                    var path = Path()
                    path.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height))
                    for x in stride(from: 0, through: size.width, by: 4) {
                        let angle = Double(x / wavelength) * 2 * .pi + phase + Double(layer)
                        let y = baseline + CGFloat(sin(angle)) * amplitude * (0.7 + 0.3 * depth)
                        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: y))
                    }
                    path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height))
                    path.closeSubpath()
                    context.fill(path, with: .color(color))
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

#Preview {
    WaveBackground()
        .frame(width: 320, height: 200)
        .background(Color.cyan.opacity(0.08))
}
```

## Film Grain (`grain`)

Flickering film grain over any view, from a tiled noise texture.

- API: `.grain()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/Grain.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/Grain.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/SeededRandom.swift

### Usage

```swift
LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
    .grain()

HeroImage()
    .grain(opacity: 0.2, isAnimated: false)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .grain(opacity:isAnimated:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Generate a 128 × 128 grey noise CGImage once (8-bit DeviceGray, random bytes from a seeded generator, no interpolation). In an overlay, show it with Image(decorative:scale: 2).resizable(resizingMode: .tile) in a frame 64 pt larger than the view in each direction, clipped, and shift it by a different offset (frame × 37 mod 64, frame × 53 mod 64) 12 times a second using TimelineView(.periodic(by: 1/12)), so the grain flickers like film. Use .blendMode(.overlay) at opacity (0.35), disable hit testing and hide it from accessibility. With Reduce Motion on (or isAnimated false), keep the grain still.

### Source

```swift
import CoreGraphics
import SwiftUI

/// Film grain: a tiled noise texture over the view, re-positioned a few times
/// a second so it flickers like real film.
struct GrainModifier: ViewModifier {
    var opacity: Double
    var isAnimated: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            if let noise = NoiseTexture.image {
                // Reduce Motion: still grain.
                let animated = isAnimated && !reduceMotion
                TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: 1.0 / 12)) { timeline in
                    let frame = animated ? Int(timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * 12) : 0
                    GeometryReader { geometry in
                        Image(decorative: noise, scale: 2)
                            .resizable(resizingMode: .tile)
                            // One tile larger than the view in each direction so
                            // the random shift never uncovers an edge.
                            .frame(width: geometry.size.width + 64, height: geometry.size.height + 64)
                            .offset(x: -CGFloat(frame * 37 % 64), y: -CGFloat(frame * 53 % 64))
                    }
                    .clipped()
                }
                .blendMode(.overlay)
                .opacity(opacity)
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A 128×128 grey noise image, generated once.
enum NoiseTexture {
    static let image: CGImage? = {
        let side = 128
        var generator = SplitMix64(seed: 7)
        var pixels = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: side * side)
        for index in pixels.indices {
            pixels[index] = UInt8(truncatingIfNeeded: generator.next() >> 56)
        }
        guard let provider = CGDataProvider(data: Data(pixels) as CFData) else { return nil }
        return CGImage(
            width: side,
            height: side,
            bitsPerComponent: 8,
            bitsPerPixel: 8,
            bytesPerRow: side,
            space: CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceGray(),
            bitmapInfo: CGBitmapInfo(rawValue: CGImageAlphaInfo.none.rawValue),
            provider: provider,
            decode: nil,
            shouldInterpolate: false,
            intent: .defaultIntent
        )
    }()
}

public extension View {
    /// Lays flickering film grain over the view.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
    ///     .grain()
    ///
    /// HeroImage()
    ///     .grain(opacity: 0.25, isAnimated: false)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - opacity: Strength of the grain (0…1).
    ///   - isAnimated: Re-rolls the grain 12 times a second when true.
    func grain(opacity: Double = 0.35, isAnimated: Bool = true) -> some View {
        modifier(GrainModifier(opacity: opacity, isAnimated: isAnimated))
    }
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .purple], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
        .grain()
        .frame(width: 300, height: 200)
}

// MARK: - SeededRandom.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

// Shared by the particle and background effects that need stable random
// layouts. Copy this file along with any effect that uses `SplitMix64`.

import SwiftUI

/// Small deterministic random generator, so particle layouts are stable
/// between launches and previews.
struct SplitMix64: RandomNumberGenerator {
    private var state: UInt64

    init(seed: UInt64) { state = seed }

    mutating func next() -> UInt64 {
        state &+= 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15
        var z = state
        z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) &* 0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9
        z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) &* 0x94D0_49BB_1331_11EB
        return z ^ (z >> 31)
    }

    /// A Double in 0..<1.
    mutating func unit() -> Double { Double.random(in: 0..<1, using: &self) }
}

extension CGFloat {
    /// Wraps the value into 0..<length.
    func wrapped(to length: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        let r = truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: length)
        return r < 0 ? r + length : r
    }
}
```

## Flashlight (`flashlight`)

The view goes dark except a soft circle of light around the pointer.

- API: `.flashlight()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Hover / Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/Flashlight.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/Flashlight.swift

### Usage

```swift
TreasureMap()
    .flashlight(radius: 100)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .flashlight(radius:darkness:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Track the pointer with .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) and a finger with a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0), storing the location in @State (nil on exit) plus the last location. In an overlay GeometryReader, draw a RadialGradient from clear to black at darkness (0.85) opacity, centred on the location as a UnitPoint, from startRadius 0.55 × radius to endRadius radius (90 pt), so everything outside the circle is dark with a soft edge. Fade the whole overlay out when the pointer leaves (lights back on) with easeOut(0.4 s), and follow the pointer with .interactiveSpring(response: 0.18). Disable hit testing. With Reduce Motion on, move without animation.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Darkens the view except for a soft circle of light around the pointer (or
/// a dragging finger), like exploring a dark room with a torch.
struct FlashlightModifier: ViewModifier {
    var radius: CGFloat
    var darkness: Double

    @State private var location: CGPoint?
    @State private var lastLocation: CGPoint?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                GeometryReader { geometry in
                    let size = geometry.size
                    let point = location ?? lastLocation ?? CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                    RadialGradient(
                        colors: [.black.opacity(0), .black.opacity(darkness)],
                        center: UnitPoint(x: size.width > 0 ? point.x / size.width : 0.5,
                                          y: size.height > 0 ? point.y / size.height : 0.5),
                        startRadius: radius * 0.55,
                        endRadius: radius
                    )
                    // Lights come back on when the pointer leaves.
                    .opacity(location == nil ? 0 : 1)
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .onContinuousHover(coordinateSpace: .local) { phase in
                switch phase {
                case let .active(point): move(to: point)
                case .ended: release()
                }
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(
                DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0, coordinateSpace: .local)
                    .onChanged { move(to: $0.location) }
                    .onEnded { _ in release() }
            )
    }

    private func move(to point: CGPoint) {
        // Reduce Motion: the light jumps with the pointer instead of trailing it.
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .interactiveSpring(response: 0.18, dampingFraction: 0.9)) {
            location = point
            lastLocation = point
        }
    }

    private func release() {
        withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.4)) { location = nil }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Dims the view except around the pointer or finger.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// TreasureMap()
    ///     .flashlight(radius: 100)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - radius: Radius of the lit circle, in points.
    ///   - darkness: Opacity of the darkness outside the light (0…1).
    func flashlight(radius: CGFloat = 90, darkness: Double = 0.85) -> some View {
        modifier(FlashlightModifier(radius: radius, darkness: darkness))
    }
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [.yellow, .orange, .red], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
        .overlay(Text("Find me").font(.largeTitle.bold()))
        .frame(width: 300, height: 200)
        .flashlight()
}
```

## Lava Lamp (`lava-lamp`)

Soft blobs drift up and down, stretching and merging like hot wax.

- API: `LavaLamp()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/LavaLamp.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/LavaLamp.swift

### Usage

```swift
LavaLamp(colors: [.yellow, .orange, .pink])
    .ignoresSafeArea()
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI LavaLamp(colors:background:blobs:speed:) view (iOS 17+). In TimelineView(.animation), fill a vertical LinearGradient of the colours, masked by a Canvas that adds .alphaThreshold(min: 0.5, color: .black) then .blur(radius: 7 % of the smaller side), and in drawLayer fills 7 black ellipses: blob i (seed = i × 1.618) at x = width × (0.2 + 0.6 × (0.5 + 0.5 sin(seed × 3.1 + t × 0.13))), y = height × (0.5 + 0.48 sin(t × (0.18 + 0.05 × (i % 3)) + seed × 2.3)), radius = min side × (0.11 + 0.07 × (0.5 + 0.5 sin(seed × 5.7))), stretched vertically by 1 + 0.25 |cos(t × 0.2 + seed × 2.3)|, plus wide pools of wax at the bottom and top. The threshold fuses the blurred blobs into liquid shapes (metaballs). Put the background colour (deep purple) behind. With Reduce Motion on, show one still frame.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A lava lamp: soft blobs drift up and down, stretching and merging when
/// they meet. The blobs are blurred and cut back with an alpha threshold
/// (metaballs), then used as a mask over a gradient.
public struct LavaLamp: View {
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let background: Color
    private let blobs: Int
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - colors: Gradient of the wax, top to bottom.
    ///   - background: Colour behind the wax.
    ///   - blobs: Number of blobs.
    ///   - speed: Multiplier on the drifting speed.
    public init(colors: [Color] = [.yellow, .orange, .pink], background: Color = Color(red: 0.16, green: 0.05, blue: 0.25), blobs: Int = 7, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.colors = colors
        self.background = background
        self.blobs = max(1, blobs)
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            // Reduce Motion: a still frame.
            let time = reduceMotion ? 12 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .mask {
                    Canvas { context, size in
                        context.addFilter(.alphaThreshold(min: 0.5, color: .black))
                        context.addFilter(.blur(radius: min(size.width, size.height) * 0.07))
                        context.drawLayer { layer in
                            let unit = min(size.width, size.height)
                            for index in 0..<blobs {
                                let seed = Double(index) * 1.618
                                let x = size.width * (0.2 + 0.6 * (0.5 + 0.5 * sin(seed * 3.1 + time * 0.13)))
                                let y = size.height * (0.5 + 0.48 * sin(time * (0.18 + 0.05 * Double(index % 3)) + seed * 2.3))
                                let r = unit * (0.11 + 0.07 * (0.5 + 0.5 * sin(seed * 5.7)))
                                // Blobs stretch vertically while they move fastest.
                                let stretch = 1 + 0.25 * abs(cos(time * 0.2 + seed * 2.3))
                                layer.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: x - r, y: y - r * stretch, width: r * 2, height: r * 2 * stretch)), with: .color(.black))
                            }
                            // Pools of wax at the bottom and top of the lamp.
                            layer.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: -size.width * 0.1, y: size.height * 0.9, width: size.width * 1.2, height: size.height * 0.3)), with: .color(.black))
                            layer.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: size.width * 0.1, y: -size.height * 0.22, width: size.width * 0.8, height: size.height * 0.28)), with: .color(.black))
                        }
                    }
                }
                .background(background)
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

#Preview {
    LavaLamp()
        .frame(width: 200, height: 320)
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 30))
}
```
