## Matrix Rain (`matrix-rain`)

Columns of glyphs rain down with bright heads and fading trails.

- API: `MatrixRain()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/MatrixRain.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/MatrixRain.swift

### Usage

```swift
MatrixRain(color: .green)
    .background(.black)
    .ignoresSafeArea()
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI MatrixRain(color:fontSize:speed:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Resolve every glyph (half-width katakana plus digits, monospaced, 14 pt) once per frame in the trail colour and in white. Columns are fontSize × 0.9 wide, rows fontSize × 1.1 tall. For each column, a stable random seed sets the trail length (8–22), the speed (6–16 rows/s) and a phase; the head row = (time × speed + seed × 97) mod (rows + length). Draw the head white at full opacity and each trail cell below it with opacity 0.85 × (1 − offset / length), picking the glyph from a hash of (column, row, floor(time × (2 + seed × 4))) so characters flicker. With Reduce Motion on, show one still frame.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Falling columns of glyphs, like the digital rain from the films: each
/// column has a bright head and a fading trail, and characters flicker as
/// they fall.
public struct MatrixRain: View {
    private let color: Color
    private let fontSize: CGFloat
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private static let glyphs = Array("ｱｲｳｴｵｶｷｸｹｺｻｼｽｾｿﾀﾁﾂﾃﾄﾅﾆﾇﾈﾉﾊﾋﾌﾍﾎﾏﾐﾑﾒﾓﾔﾕﾖﾗﾘﾙﾚﾛﾜ0123456789").map(String.init)

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - color: Colour of the trails. Heads are drawn white.
    ///   - fontSize: Glyph size; also sets the column width.
    ///   - speed: Multiplier on the falling speed.
    public init(color: Color = .green, fontSize: CGFloat = 14, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.color = color
        self.fontSize = fontSize
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 7 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            Canvas { context, size in
                let glyphs = Self.glyphs
                let font = Font.system(size: fontSize, weight: .medium, design: .monospaced)
                // Resolve every glyph once per frame, then stamp them.
                let trail = glyphs.map { context.resolve(Text($0).font(font).foregroundStyle(color)) }
                let head = glyphs.map { context.resolve(Text($0).font(font).foregroundStyle(.white)) }
                let columnWidth = fontSize * 0.9
                let rowHeight = fontSize * 1.1
                let columns = Int(size.width / columnWidth) + 1
                let rows = Int(size.height / rowHeight) + 1
                for column in 0..<columns {
                    let seed = Self.hash(column, 0)
                    let length = 8 + Int(seed * 14)
                    let velocity = 6 + seed * 10 // rows per second
                    let cycle = Double(rows + length)
                    let headRow = Int((time * velocity + seed * 97).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: cycle))
                    for offset in 0..<length {
                        let row = headRow - offset
                        guard row >= 0 && row < rows else { continue }
                        // Characters change a few times a second.
                        let flicker = Int(time * (2 + seed * 4))
                        let pick = Int(Self.hash(column * 131 + row, flicker) * Double(glyphs.count)) % glyphs.count
                        var copy = context
                        copy.opacity = offset == 0 ? 1 : 0.85 * (1 - Double(offset) / Double(length))
                        copy.draw(offset == 0 ? head[pick] : trail[pick], at: CGPoint(x: CGFloat(column) * columnWidth + columnWidth / 2, y: CGFloat(row) * rowHeight + rowHeight / 2))
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// A stable pseudo-random value in 0..<1.
    static func hash(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 374_761_393 &+ b &* 668_265_263)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 13)) &* 1_274_126_177
        x ^= x >> 16
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

#Preview {
    MatrixRain()
        .frame(width: 300, height: 220)
        .background(.black)
}
```

## Interactive Dot Grid (`dot-grid`)

A grid of dots scatters away from your finger and eases back.

- API: `InteractiveDotGrid()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Drag / Hover / Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/InteractiveDotGrid.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/InteractiveDotGrid.swift

### Usage

```swift
InteractiveDotGrid(spacing: 18)
    .ignoresSafeArea()
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI InteractiveDotGrid(spacing:color:highlight:radius:) view (iOS 17+). Track the pointer from a DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) and onContinuousHover (nil when released). In a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), smooth the pointer and a 0…1 strength each frame with exponential easing (k = 1 − e^(−14 dt) while active, strength decays with e^(−6 dt) after release) in a plain reference-type model. Draw a centred grid of dots every spacing points (18 pt): within radius (70 pt) of the pointer, near = (1 − d / radius)² × strength; push the dot away by near × spacing × 1.6, grow it by 2 × near and tint it with the highlight colour above 0.15. At rest, a faint wave sin((column + row) × 0.45 − time × 2) varies the radius by 0.5 pt. With Reduce Motion on, keep the highlight but don't move dots or run the wave.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A grid of dots that scatter away from your finger or pointer and ease
/// back when you let go. At rest a faint wave ripples through the dot sizes.
public struct InteractiveDotGrid: View {
    private let spacing: CGFloat
    private let color: Color
    private let highlight: Color
    private let radius: CGFloat

    @State private var pointer: CGPoint?
    @State private var model = DotGridModel()
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - spacing: Distance between dots, in points.
    ///   - color: Dot colour at rest.
    ///   - highlight: Dot colour near the pointer.
    ///   - radius: How far the pointer's push reaches, in points.
    public init(spacing: CGFloat = 18, color: Color = .secondary.opacity(0.45), highlight: Color = .accentColor, radius: CGFloat = 70) {
        self.spacing = max(4, spacing)
        self.color = color
        self.highlight = highlight
        self.radius = radius
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
            let time = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                let state = model.step(towards: pointer)
                let columns = Int(size.width / spacing) + 1
                let rows = Int(size.height / spacing) + 1
                let originX = (size.width - CGFloat(columns - 1) * spacing) / 2
                let originY = (size.height - CGFloat(rows - 1) * spacing) / 2
                for row in 0..<rows {
                    for column in 0..<columns {
                        var p = CGPoint(x: originX + CGFloat(column) * spacing, y: originY + CGFloat(row) * spacing)
                        var near: CGFloat = 0
                        if state.strength > 0.001 {
                            let dx = p.x - state.point.x, dy = p.y - state.point.y
                            let distance = max(0.001, hypot(dx, dy))
                            if distance < radius {
                                near = pow(1 - distance / radius, 2) * state.strength
                                let push = reduceMotion ? 0 : near * spacing * 1.6
                                p.x += dx / distance * push
                                p.y += dy / distance * push
                            }
                        }
                        let wave = reduceMotion ? 0 : 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(Double(column + row) * 0.45 - time * 2)
                        let r = 1.2 + 0.5 * CGFloat(wave) + 2 * near
                        let shading: GraphicsContext.Shading = near > 0.15 ? .color(highlight.opacity(0.4 + 0.6 * Double(near))) : .color(color)
                        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: p.x - r, y: p.y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)), with: shading)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        .contentShape(Rectangle())
        .gesture(
            DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
                .onChanged { pointer = $0.location }
                .onEnded { _ in pointer = nil }
        )
        .onContinuousHover { phase in
            switch phase {
            case .active(let location): pointer = location
            case .ended: pointer = nil
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

/// Smooths the pointer and the push strength from frame to frame, so dots
/// glide out and back instead of snapping. Not observed: it's only read and
/// written while drawing.
final class DotGridModel {
    private var point: CGPoint = .zero
    private var strength: CGFloat = 0
    private var last = Date()

    func step(towards target: CGPoint?) -> (point: CGPoint, strength: CGFloat) {
        let now = Date()
        let dt = min(0.05, now.timeIntervalSince(last))
        last = now
        let k = CGFloat(1 - exp(-dt * 14))
        if let target {
            if strength < 0.01 { point = target }
            point.x += (target.x - point.x) * k
            point.y += (target.y - point.y) * k
            strength += (1 - strength) * k
        } else {
            strength += (0 - strength) * CGFloat(1 - exp(-dt * 6))
        }
        return (point, strength)
    }
}

#Preview {
    InteractiveDotGrid()
        .frame(width: 300, height: 220)
}
```

## Meteors (`meteors`)

Meteors streak across a starry sky with glowing heads and fading tails.

- API: `Meteors()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/Meteors.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/Meteors.swift

### Usage

```swift
Meteors(count: 10)
    .background(Color(red: 0.03, green: 0.04, blue: 0.12))
    .ignoresSafeArea()
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Meteors(count:angle:color:showsStars:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Scatter 60 faint static stars (0.4–1.2 pt, 25–65 % opacity) from a stable hash. Each meteor i has a flight time of 1.6–3.8 s and a pause of 0.5–3 s; when in flight, its head moves from a start point spread along the top edge and the side it comes from along the direction (angle 135° in y-down coordinates, so they travel down and to the left) by (width + height) × 1.2 × progress. Stroke its 50–110 pt tail from the tail point to the head with a linear gradient clear → 90 % colour, 1.5 pt wide, round caps, and draw a 5 pt head with a 2 pt blur. With Reduce Motion on, draw the stars only.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Meteors streak diagonally across a starry sky, each with a glowing head
/// and a fading tail, at random intervals.
public struct Meteors: View {
    private let count: Int
    private let angle: Angle
    private let color: Color
    private let showsStars: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of meteors in flight over a cycle.
    ///   - angle: Direction of travel (0° = right, 90° = down).
    ///   - color: Colour of heads and tails.
    ///   - showsStars: Scatter faint static stars behind the meteors.
    public init(count: Int = 10, angle: Angle = .degrees(135), color: Color = .white, showsStars: Bool = true) {
        self.count = max(1, count)
        self.angle = angle
        self.color = color
        self.showsStars = showsStars
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                if showsStars {
                    for index in 0..<60 {
                        let x = Self.hash(index, 1) * size.width, y = Self.hash(index, 2) * size.height
                        let r = 0.4 + Self.hash(index, 3) * 0.8
                        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: x - r, y: y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)), with: .color(color.opacity(0.25 + 0.4 * Self.hash(index, 4))))
                    }
                }
                // Reduce Motion: stars only.
                guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                let direction = CGPoint(x: cos(angle.radians), y: sin(angle.radians))
                let travel = (size.width + size.height) * 1.2
                for index in 0..<count {
                    let duration = 1.6 + Self.hash(index, 5) * 2.2
                    let cycle = duration + 0.5 + Self.hash(index, 6) * 2.5 // flight + pause
                    let local = (time + Self.hash(index, 7) * 10).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: cycle)
                    guard local < duration else { continue }
                    let progress = local / duration
                    // Start points spread along the top and the side the meteors come from.
                    let spread = Self.hash(index, 8) * (size.width + size.height)
                    let start = direction.x >= 0
                        ? (spread < size.width ? CGPoint(x: spread - size.width * 0.3, y: -20) : CGPoint(x: -20, y: spread - size.width))
                        : (spread < size.width ? CGPoint(x: spread + size.width * 0.3, y: -20) : CGPoint(x: size.width + 20, y: spread - size.width))
                    let head = CGPoint(x: start.x + direction.x * travel * progress, y: start.y + direction.y * travel * progress)
                    let tailLength = 50 + Self.hash(index, 9) * 60
                    let tail = CGPoint(x: head.x - direction.x * tailLength, y: head.y - direction.y * tailLength)
                    var line = Path()
                    line.move(to: tail)
                    line.addLine(to: head)
                    context.stroke(line, with: .linearGradient(Gradient(colors: [color.opacity(0), color.opacity(0.9)]), startPoint: tail, endPoint: head), style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 1.5, lineCap: .round))
                    var glow = context
                    glow.addFilter(.blur(radius: 2))
                    glow.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: head.x - 2.5, y: head.y - 2.5, width: 5, height: 5)), with: .color(color))
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    static func hash(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 73_856_093 ^ b &* 19_349_663 &+ 0x9E37)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

#Preview {
    Meteors()
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
        .background(Color(red: 0.03, green: 0.04, blue: 0.12))
}
```

## Flow Field (`flow-field`)

Generative curves follow a shifting vector field with dashes flowing along them.

- API: `FlowField()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/FlowField.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/FlowField.swift

### Usage

```swift
FlowField(colors: [.cyan, .blue, .purple, .pink])
    .background(Color(white: 0.06))
    .ignoresSafeArea()
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI FlowField(lines:colors:speed:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Define a flow angle field(x, y, t) = (sin(x × 0.012 + t) × cos(y × 0.014 − 0.7t) + sin((x + y) × 0.007 + 0.5t)) × π, with coordinates scaled so the smaller side maps to about 220 units and t = time × 0.25. For each of 140 lines, start at a stable random point and integrate 22 steps of 3.2 pt along the field into a Path. Stroke it in a colour picked from the list at 18 % opacity, then again at 85 % with a dash [5, 40] and dashPhase −((time × 30 + random × 45) mod 45), so short dashes travel along the curves (wrap the phase: a huge dash phase makes Core Graphics hang). With Reduce Motion on, show one still frame.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Generative art: short curves follow a slowly shifting vector field, like
/// wind or water, with dashes travelling along them to show the flow.
public struct FlowField: View {
    private let lines: Int
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - lines: Number of curves.
    ///   - colors: Curves are tinted along this list, left to right.
    ///   - speed: Multiplier on how fast the field shifts.
    public init(lines: Int = 140, colors: [Color] = [.cyan, .blue, .purple, .pink], speed: Double = 1) {
        self.lines = max(1, lines)
        self.colors = colors.isEmpty ? [.primary] : colors
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 3 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            Canvas { context, size in
                let scale = 220 / max(1, min(size.width, size.height))
                for index in 0..<lines {
                    var p = CGPoint(x: Self.hash(index, 1) * size.width, y: Self.hash(index, 2) * size.height)
                    var path = Path()
                    path.move(to: p)
                    for _ in 0..<22 {
                        let angle = Self.field(Double(p.x) * scale, Double(p.y) * scale, time * 0.25)
                        p.x += CGFloat(cos(angle)) * 3.2
                        p.y += CGFloat(sin(angle)) * 3.2
                        path.addLine(to: p)
                    }
                    let tint = colors[min(colors.count - 1, Int(Self.hash(index, 1) * Double(colors.count)))]
                    context.stroke(path, with: .color(tint.opacity(0.18)), lineWidth: 1)
                    // Travelling dashes show the direction of flow. The phase is
                    // wrapped to one dash period: Core Graphics walks the pattern
                    // up to the phase, so a raw clock value would hang it.
                    let phase = (time * 30 + Self.hash(index, 3) * 45).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 45)
                    context.stroke(path, with: .color(tint.opacity(0.85)), style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 1.4, lineCap: .round, dash: [5, 40], dashPhase: -CGFloat(phase)))
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// Flow direction, in radians, at a point: layered sines that drift over time.
    static func field(_ x: Double, _ y: Double, _ t: Double) -> Double {
        let a = sin(x * 0.012 + t) * cos(y * 0.014 - t * 0.7)
        let b = sin((x + y) * 0.007 + t * 0.5)
        return (a + b) * .pi
    }

    static func hash(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 2_246_822_519 &+ b &* 3_266_489_917)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 15)) &* 0x2c1b_3c6d
        x ^= x >> 12
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

#Preview {
    FlowField()
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
        .background(Color(white: 0.06))
}
```

## Network (`network`)

Drifting points link up with lines when close, and gather at your finger.

- API: `NetworkBackground()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop / Hover / Drag
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/NetworkBackground.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/NetworkBackground.swift

### Usage

```swift
NetworkBackground(color: .cyan)
    .background(.black)
    .ignoresSafeArea()
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI NetworkBackground(count:linkDistance:color:interactive:) view (iOS 17+): a plexus of drifting points. In TimelineView(.animation) + Canvas, point i starts at a hashed position, moves at 6–20 pt/s in a hashed direction, and wraps around the edges with 20 pt of slack. Join every pair closer than linkDistance (70 pt) with a line of opacity 0.55 × (1 − d / linkDistance) and width 0.6 + 0.6 × that strength, then draw each point as a 3.6 pt dot. Track the pointer with onContinuousHover and a DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0); points within 110 pt are pulled towards it by (1 − d / 110) × 0.45 of the gap, so the web gathers under the finger. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline. Hide it from accessibility.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Drifting points that link up with thin lines whenever two come close, like
/// a constellation or a network map. Points near the pointer or finger are
/// pulled towards it, so the web gathers where you touch.
///
/// ```swift
/// NetworkBackground(color: .cyan)
///     .background(.black)
///     .ignoresSafeArea()
/// ```
public struct NetworkBackground: View {
    private let count: Int
    private let linkDistance: CGFloat
    private let color: Color
    private let interactive: Bool

    @State private var pointer: CGPoint?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of points.
    ///   - linkDistance: Points closer than this are joined, in points.
    ///   - color: Colour of points and lines.
    ///   - interactive: Pull points towards the pointer or a drag.
    public init(count: Int = 46, linkDistance: CGFloat = 70, color: Color = .white, interactive: Bool = true) {
        self.count = max(2, count)
        self.linkDistance = linkDistance
        self.color = color
        self.interactive = interactive
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                let points = (0..<count).map { position(of: $0, time: time, size: size) }
                for i in points.indices {
                    for j in (i + 1)..<points.count {
                        let distance = hypot(points[i].x - points[j].x, points[i].y - points[j].y)
                        guard distance < linkDistance else { continue }
                        var line = Path()
                        line.move(to: points[i])
                        line.addLine(to: points[j])
                        let strength = 1 - distance / linkDistance
                        context.stroke(line, with: .color(color.opacity(0.55 * strength)), lineWidth: 0.6 + strength * 0.6)
                    }
                }
                for point in points {
                    context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: point.x - 1.8, y: point.y - 1.8, width: 3.6, height: 3.6)), with: .color(color.opacity(0.9)))
                }
            }
        }
        .contentShape(Rectangle())
        .onContinuousHover { phase in
            guard interactive else { return }
            if case let .active(location) = phase { pointer = location } else { pointer = nil }
        }
        .gesture(interactive ? DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
            .onChanged { pointer = $0.location }
            .onEnded { _ in pointer = nil } : nil)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private func position(of index: Int, time: Double, size: CGSize) -> CGPoint {
        let speed = 6 + Self.hash(index, 3) * 14 // points per second
        let heading = Self.hash(index, 4) * 2 * .pi
        let x = wrap(Self.hash(index, 1) * size.width + cos(heading) * speed * time, size.width)
        let y = wrap(Self.hash(index, 2) * size.height + sin(heading) * speed * time, size.height)
        var point = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)
        if let pointer {
            let dx = pointer.x - point.x, dy = pointer.y - point.y
            let distance = hypot(dx, dy)
            let reach: CGFloat = 110
            if distance < reach, distance > 0.1 {
                let pull = (1 - distance / reach) * 0.45
                point.x += dx * pull
                point.y += dy * pull
            }
        }
        return point
    }

    /// Wraps into -20…length+20, so points leave one edge and enter the other.
    private func wrap(_ value: Double, _ length: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
        let span = Double(length) + 40
        let r = (value + 20).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: span)
        return CGFloat((r < 0 ? r + span : r) - 20)
    }

    private static func hash(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 73_856_093 ^ b &* 19_349_663 &+ 0x51ED)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

#Preview {
    NetworkBackground(color: .cyan)
        .frame(width: 340, height: 240)
        .background(Color(red: 0.03, green: 0.05, blue: 0.12))
}
```

## Topographic Lines (`topographic`)

Contour lines of a shifting landscape flow like a living map.

- API: `TopographicLines()`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/TopographicLines.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/TopographicLines.swift

### Usage

```swift
TopographicLines(color: .green)
    .background(Color(white: 0.06))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI TopographicLines(levels:scale:color:speed:) view (iOS 17+). In TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1/30)) + Canvas, sample a height field on an 8 pt grid: h = 0.65 × noise(x + t, y − 0.6t) + 0.35 × noise(2.1x − 0.8t, 2.1y + 7), with x, y in units of scale (90 pt), t = time × speed (0.12), and noise a smoothstep-interpolated value noise from an integer hash. For each of levels (14) thresholds spread over 0.18…0.82, trace the contour with marching squares (16 cases, edge crossings linearly interpolated, saddles drawn as two segments) into one Path and stroke it: every fifth line at 1.4 pt and 85 % opacity, the others 0.7 pt at 45 %. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Contour lines of a slowly shifting landscape, like a topographic map
/// coming alive: hills swell and sink and the lines flow around them, with
/// every fifth line drawn heavier.
///
/// ```swift
/// TopographicLines(color: .green)
///     .background(Color(white: 0.06))
/// ```
public struct TopographicLines: View {
    private let levels: Int
    private let scale: Double
    private let color: Color
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - levels: Number of contour lines between the lowest and highest ground.
    ///   - scale: Size of the hills, in points.
    ///   - color: Colour of the lines.
    ///   - speed: How fast the landscape shifts.
    public init(levels: Int = 14, scale: Double = 90, color: Color = .primary, speed: Double = 0.12) {
        self.levels = max(1, levels)
        self.scale = max(10, scale)
        self.color = color
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 10_000) * speed
            Canvas { context, size in
                let cell: CGFloat = 8
                let columns = Int(size.width / cell) + 2, rows = Int(size.height / cell) + 2
                // Height field on the grid corners.
                var field = [Double](repeating: 0, count: columns * rows)
                for row in 0..<rows {
                    for column in 0..<columns {
                        let x = Double(column) * cell / scale, y = Double(row) * cell / scale
                        field[row * columns + column] = Self.noise(x + time, y - time * 0.6) * 0.65 + Self.noise(x * 2.1 - time * 0.8, y * 2.1 + 7) * 0.35
                    }
                }
                for level in 1...levels {
                    let threshold = 0.18 + 0.64 * Double(level) / Double(levels + 1)
                    var path = Path()
                    for row in 0..<(rows - 1) {
                        for column in 0..<(columns - 1) {
                            Self.contour(in: &path, field: field, columns: columns, column: column, row: row, cell: cell, threshold: threshold)
                        }
                    }
                    let major = level % 5 == 0
                    context.stroke(path, with: .color(color.opacity(major ? 0.85 : 0.45)), lineWidth: major ? 1.4 : 0.7)
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// Marching squares: the segment(s) where the field crosses `threshold`
    /// inside one grid cell.
    private static func contour(in path: inout Path, field: [Double], columns: Int, column: Int, row: Int, cell: CGFloat, threshold t: Double) {
        let a = field[row * columns + column], b = field[row * columns + column + 1]
        let c = field[(row + 1) * columns + column + 1], d = field[(row + 1) * columns + column]
        let index = (a > t ? 8 : 0) | (b > t ? 4 : 0) | (c > t ? 2 : 0) | (d > t ? 1 : 0)
        guard index != 0, index != 15 else { return }
        let x = CGFloat(column) * cell, y = CGFloat(row) * cell
        func lerp(_ v1: Double, _ v2: Double) -> CGFloat { CGFloat((t - v1) / (v2 - v1)) }
        let top = CGPoint(x: x + cell * lerp(a, b), y: y)
        let right = CGPoint(x: x + cell, y: y + cell * lerp(b, c))
        let bottom = CGPoint(x: x + cell * lerp(d, c), y: y + cell)
        let left = CGPoint(x: x, y: y + cell * lerp(a, d))
        func segment(_ p: CGPoint, _ q: CGPoint) { path.move(to: p); path.addLine(to: q) }
        switch index {
        case 1, 14: segment(left, bottom)
        case 2, 13: segment(bottom, right)
        case 3, 12: segment(left, right)
        case 4, 11: segment(top, right)
        case 5: segment(left, top); segment(bottom, right)
        case 6, 9: segment(top, bottom)
        case 7, 8: segment(left, top)
        case 10: segment(top, right); segment(left, bottom)
        default: break
        }
    }

    /// Smooth value noise in 0…1.
    private static func noise(_ x: Double, _ y: Double) -> Double {
        let ix = floor(x), iy = floor(y)
        let fx = x - ix, fy = y - iy
        let ux = fx * fx * (3 - 2 * fx), uy = fy * fy * (3 - 2 * fy)
        let a = hash(ix, iy), b = hash(ix + 1, iy), c = hash(ix, iy + 1), d = hash(ix + 1, iy + 1)
        return (a + (b - a) * ux) + ((c + (d - c) * ux) - (a + (b - a) * ux)) * uy
    }

    private static func hash(_ x: Double, _ y: Double) -> Double {
        var h = UInt64(bitPattern: Int64(x) &* 374_761_393 &+ Int64(y) &* 668_265_263)
        h = (h ^ (h >> 13)) &* 1_274_126_177
        h ^= h >> 16
        return Double(h % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

#Preview {
    TopographicLines(color: .mint)
        .frame(width: 340, height: 240)
        .background(Color(white: 0.06))
}
```

## Day & Night Sky (`day-night-sky`)

A sky runs from starry night through dawn, noon and sunset, sun and moon arcing over.

- API: `DayNightSky(time:)`
- Component: Background
- Trigger: Loop / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/DayNightSky.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Background/DayNightSky.swift

### Usage

```swift
DayNightSky()                // loops a day every 16 s
    .ignoresSafeArea()

DayNightSky(time: hour / 24) // follows the time of day
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI DayNightSky(time:cycle:) view (iOS 17+). time is 0…1 (0 midnight, 0.25 sunrise, 0.5 noon, 0.75 sunset); nil loops it with TimelineView every cycle (16 s). Draw an Animatable scene in a Canvas: a vertical gradient whose top and horizon colours are interpolated between stops (night navy, deep purple dawn, pink-orange sunrise horizon, bright blue noon, golden afternoon, orange sunset horizon under violet, dusk). Fade in 50 hashed stars near night, twinkling. Put the sun and moon on opposite sides of an arc: x = mid − cos(angle) × 0.45w, y = horizon − sin(angle) × 0.75h, sun angle = (t − 0.25) × 2π, each with a blurred halo; the sun turns orange near the horizon. Finish with a band of dark hills tinted from the sky colour. Animate a fixed time with .easeInOut(duration: 1.2). With Reduce Motion on, hold at early evening (0.7).

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A sky that runs through a whole day: deep night with stars, a pink and
/// orange dawn, blue noon, a burning sunset, and back, with the sun and moon
/// arcing across. Loops on its own, or follows a time of day you set.
///
/// ```swift
/// DayNightSky()                 // loops a day every 16 s
/// DayNightSky(time: 0.75)       // fixed at sunset
/// ```
public struct DayNightSky: View {
    private let time: Double?
    private let cycle: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - time: Time of day, 0…1 (0 midnight, 0.25 sunrise, 0.5 noon,
    ///     0.75 sunset). Changes animate. Leave nil to loop.
    ///   - cycle: Seconds per day when looping.
    public init(time: Double? = nil, cycle: Double = 16) {
        self.time = time
        self.cycle = max(1, cycle)
    }

    public var body: some View {
        if let time {
            SkyScene(time: time)
                .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 1.2), value: time)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
        } else {
            TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
                // Reduce Motion: hold at a calm early evening.
                let t = reduceMotion ? 0.7 : (timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate / cycle).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
                SkyScene(time: t)
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }
}

/// The sky at one time of day. Animatable, so a fixed `time` animates
/// through the colours in between.
struct SkyScene: View, Animatable {
    var time: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { time }
        set { time = newValue }
    }

    private typealias RGB = (Double, Double, Double)

    /// Sky colours (top, horizon) at times of day.
    private static let stops: [(time: Double, top: RGB, horizon: RGB)] = [
        (0.00, (0.02, 0.03, 0.10), (0.06, 0.08, 0.20)),
        (0.20, (0.05, 0.06, 0.20), (0.25, 0.15, 0.35)),
        (0.27, (0.30, 0.35, 0.65), (0.98, 0.60, 0.45)),
        (0.35, (0.30, 0.60, 0.95), (0.70, 0.85, 1.00)),
        (0.50, (0.20, 0.50, 0.95), (0.65, 0.85, 1.00)),
        (0.68, (0.30, 0.50, 0.90), (0.95, 0.80, 0.60)),
        (0.75, (0.35, 0.25, 0.55), (1.00, 0.45, 0.20)),
        (0.82, (0.08, 0.08, 0.25), (0.40, 0.20, 0.35)),
        (1.00, (0.02, 0.03, 0.10), (0.06, 0.08, 0.20)),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        let t = time - floor(time)
        let (top, horizon) = Self.colours(at: t)
        Canvas { context, size in
            let rect = CGRect(origin: .zero, size: size)
            context.fill(Path(rect), with: .linearGradient(
                Gradient(colors: [Self.color(top), Self.color(horizon)]),
                startPoint: .zero, endPoint: CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height)))
            // Stars fade in at night and twinkle with the time.
            let night = max(0, 1 - min(abs(t - 0) , abs(t - 1)) / 0.22) // near midnight
            let starOpacity = max(night, max(0, 1 - abs(t - 0.1) / 0.15), max(0, 1 - abs(t - 0.9) / 0.15))
            if starOpacity > 0.01 {
                for index in 0..<50 {
                    let x = Self.hash(index, 1) * size.width, y = Self.hash(index, 2) * size.height * 0.75
                    let r = 0.5 + Self.hash(index, 3) * 1
                    let twinkle = 0.6 + 0.4 * sin(t * 300 + Double(index))
                    context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: x - r, y: y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)), with: .color(.white.opacity(starOpacity * twinkle * 0.9)))
                }
            }
            // Sun and moon on opposite sides of a wide arc.
            let horizonY = size.height * 0.92
            func orb(at angle: Double, radius: Double, color: Color, glow: Double) {
                let p = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2 - cos(angle) * size.width * 0.45, y: horizonY - sin(angle) * size.height * 0.75)
                guard p.y < horizonY + radius else { return }
                var halo = context
                halo.addFilter(.blur(radius: radius * 0.9))
                halo.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: p.x - radius * 1.6, y: p.y - radius * 1.6, width: radius * 3.2, height: radius * 3.2)), with: .color(color.opacity(glow)))
                context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: p.x - radius, y: p.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)), with: .color(color))
            }
            let sunAngle = (t - 0.25) * 2 * .pi
            orb(at: sunAngle, radius: 14, color: Color(red: 1, green: 0.85 - 0.3 * max(0, 1 - sin(sunAngle) * 3), blue: 0.4), glow: 0.6)
            orb(at: sunAngle + .pi, radius: 10, color: Color(red: 0.95, green: 0.95, blue: 0.85), glow: 0.3)
            // A dark band of hills in front.
            var hills = Path()
            hills.move(to: CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height))
            for step in 0...40 {
                let x = size.width * Double(step) / 40
                hills.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: x, y: horizonY - 6 - 8 * sin(Double(step) * 0.45) - 5 * sin(Double(step) * 1.3)))
            }
            hills.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height))
            hills.closeSubpath()
            context.fill(hills, with: .color(Self.color((top.0 * 0.35, top.1 * 0.35, top.2 * 0.4))))
        }
    }

    private static func colours(at t: Double) -> (RGB, RGB) {
        let upper = stops.firstIndex { $0.time >= t } ?? stops.count - 1
        let lower = max(0, upper - 1)
        let a = stops[lower], b = stops[upper]
        let span = b.time - a.time
        let f = span > 0 ? (t - a.time) / span : 0
        func mix(_ x: RGB, _ y: RGB) -> RGB { (x.0 + (y.0 - x.0) * f, x.1 + (y.1 - x.1) * f, x.2 + (y.2 - x.2) * f) }
        return (mix(a.top, b.top), mix(a.horizon, b.horizon))
    }

    private static func color(_ rgb: RGB) -> Color { Color(red: rgb.0, green: rgb.1, blue: rgb.2) }

    private static func hash(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 73_856_093 ^ b &* 19_349_663 &+ 0x5C1E)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

#Preview {
    DayNightSky(cycle: 10)
        .frame(width: 340, height: 220)
}
```

## Rolling Number (`rolling-number`)

Digits roll like an odometer when the value changes.

- API: `RollingNumber(value:)`
- Component: Number
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/RollingNumber.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/RollingNumber.swift

### Usage

```swift
RollingNumber(value: score)
    .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI RollingNumber view (iOS 17+) that displays a number with odometer-style digit rolling. Render Text(value, format:) with monospacedDigit(), apply .contentTransition(.numericText(value:)) so digits roll up when the value increases and down when it decreases, and animate changes with .snappy. Provide initialisers for Int and for Double with a FloatingPointFormatStyle.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A number whose digits roll up or down when the value changes, like an
/// odometer. Built on `contentTransition(.numericText)`.
///
/// ```swift
/// RollingNumber(value: score)
///     .font(.system(size: 48, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
/// ```
public struct RollingNumber: View {
    private let value: Double
    private let format: FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double>
    private let animation: Animation

    public init(
        value: Double,
        format: FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double> = .number.precision(.fractionLength(0)),
        animation: Animation = .snappy
    ) {
        self.value = value
        self.format = format
        self.animation = animation
    }

    public init(value: Int, animation: Animation = .snappy) {
        self.init(value: Double(value), animation: animation)
    }

    public var body: some View {
        Text(value, format: format)
            .monospacedDigit()
            .contentTransition(.numericText(value: value))
            .animation(animation, value: value)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var value = 1280
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                RollingNumber(value: value)
                    .font(.system(size: 56, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
                HStack {
                    Button("-") { value -= Int.random(in: 1...300) }
                    Button("+") { value += Int.random(in: 1...300) }
                }
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Split-Flap Display (`split-flap`)

Characters flip through the alphabet like an airport departures board.

- API: `SplitFlapText(_:)`
- Component: Number
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/SplitFlap.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/SplitFlap.swift

### Usage

```swift
SplitFlapText(departure.time)   // "12:45"
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI SplitFlapText(_ text:size:tile:ink:) view (iOS 17+), upper-casing the text, with one flap cell per character in an HStack. Each cell is size × 0.78 wide and size × 1.3 tall (size 36), drawn from four halves of a monospaced bold character on a rounded dark tile, each half clipped to the top or bottom half: static top = next character, static bottom = current, a top flap showing current rotated with rotation3DEffect about the x axis anchored at .bottom, and a bottom flap showing next anchored at .top; a thin dark line covers the seam. When the target changes, after a 0.05 s × index delay, step through the characters of the board alphabet " A…Z0…9:.-/" from current towards the target (at most the last 6 steps); each step folds the top flap 0 → −90° (.easeIn, 0.07 s), then the bottom flap 90° → 0 (.easeOut, 0.07 s), then commits next as current and resets the angles without animation. With Reduce Motion on, change instantly.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A split-flap display, like an airport departures board. When the text
/// changes, each character flips through a few intermediate characters
/// before landing, with the top flap folding down over the bottom half.
public struct SplitFlapText: View {
    private let text: String
    private let size: CGFloat
    private let tile: Color
    private let ink: Color

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - text: The characters to show. Letters are shown in upper case.
    ///   - size: Font size of each character; tiles are sized from it.
    ///   - tile: Tile colour.
    ///   - ink: Character colour.
    public init(_ text: String, size: CGFloat = 36, tile: Color = Color(white: 0.13), ink: Color = .white) {
        self.text = text.uppercased()
        self.size = size
        self.tile = tile
        self.ink = ink
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let characters = Array(text)
        HStack(spacing: size * 0.08) {
            ForEach(characters.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                FlapCell(target: characters[index], size: size, tile: tile, ink: ink, delay: Double(index) * 0.05)
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(text)
    }
}

/// The order a real board cycles through.
private let flapAlphabet = Array(" ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789:.-/")

private struct FlapCell: View {
    let target: Character
    let size: CGFloat
    let tile: Color
    let ink: Color
    let delay: Double

    @State private var current: Character = " "
    @State private var next: Character = " "
    @State private var topAngle: Double = 0
    @State private var bottomAngle: Double = 90
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let flipTime = 0.07

    var body: some View {
        let width = size * 0.78, height = size * 1.3
        ZStack {
            half(next, top: true)
            half(current, top: false)
            // The flap: the old top folds down…
            half(current, top: true)
                .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(topAngle), axis: (1, 0, 0), anchor: .bottom, perspective: 0.5)
                .opacity(topAngle > -89 ? 1 : 0)
            // …revealing the new bottom as it lands.
            half(next, top: false)
                .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(bottomAngle), axis: (1, 0, 0), anchor: .top, perspective: 0.5)
                .opacity(bottomAngle < 89 ? 1 : 0)
        }
        .frame(width: width, height: height)
        .overlay {
            Rectangle().fill(Color.black.opacity(0.5)).frame(height: max(1, size * 0.03))
        }
        .task(id: target) { await flip(to: target) }
    }

    private func half(_ character: Character, top: Bool) -> some View {
        let width = size * 0.78, height = size * 1.3
        return Text(String(character))
            .font(.system(size: size, weight: .bold, design: .monospaced))
            .foregroundStyle(ink)
            .frame(width: width, height: height)
            .background(tile, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: size * 0.12))
            .frame(height: height / 2, alignment: top ? .top : .bottom)
            .clipped()
            .frame(height: height, alignment: top ? .top : .bottom)
    }

    /// Steps through up to six characters of the alphabet on the way to `target`.
    private func flip(to target: Character) async {
        guard target != current else { return }
        if reduceMotion {
            current = target
            next = target
            return
        }
        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(delay))
        var steps: [Character] = []
        if let from = flapAlphabet.firstIndex(of: current), let to = flapAlphabet.firstIndex(of: target) {
            var index = from
            while index != to && steps.count < 40 {
                index = (index + 1) % flapAlphabet.count
                steps.append(flapAlphabet[index])
            }
        }
        if steps.isEmpty { steps = [target] }
        for step in steps.suffix(6) {
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            await flipOnce(to: step)
        }
    }

    private func flipOnce(to character: Character) async {
        next = character
        withAnimation(.easeIn(duration: flipTime)) { topAngle = -90 }
        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(flipTime))
        withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: flipTime)) { bottomAngle = 0 }
        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(flipTime))
        var reset = Transaction()
        reset.disablesAnimations = true
        withTransaction(reset) {
            current = character
            topAngle = 0
            bottomAngle = 90
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var index = 0
        let words = ["12:45", "BOARD", "08:10"]
        var body: some View {
            SplitFlapText(words[index])
                .onTapGesture { index = (index + 1) % words.count }
                .padding()
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Slot Machine (`slot-machine`)

Number reels spin with motion blur and land one after another.

- API: `SlotMachineNumber(value:)`
- Component: Number
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/SlotMachineNumber.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/SlotMachineNumber.swift

### Usage

```swift
SlotMachineNumber(value: score, digits: 3)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI SlotMachineNumber(value:digits:size:) view (iOS 17+) that zero-pads the value and shows one reel per digit. A reel is a VStack of 40 rows (row % 10, heavy rounded monospaced digits, size × 1.25 tall) offset by −index × rowHeight and clipped to one row, on a rounded secondary-12 % tile with a top/bottom shading gradient like a drum. When its digit changes from old to new: jump (no animation) to index old, set a blur of size × 0.06, and animate index to 30 + new with .timingCurve(0.3, 0, 0.2, 1.08) over 0.9 s + 0.25 s × reel order, so reels land left to right with a small overshoot; ease the blur off over the last 30 %, and on completion jump back to index new without animation. With Reduce Motion on, animate straight to the new digit in 0.3 s.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A number shown on slot-machine reels. When the value changes, every reel
/// spins a few full turns, blurred with speed, and the reels land one after
/// another from left to right with a small bounce.
public struct SlotMachineNumber: View {
    private let value: Int
    private let digits: Int
    private let size: CGFloat

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - value: The number to show. Negative values show as 0.
    ///   - digits: Minimum number of reels; the number is zero-padded.
    ///   - size: Font size of the digits.
    public init(value: Int, digits: Int = 3, size: CGFloat = 40) {
        self.value = max(0, value)
        self.digits = max(1, digits)
        self.size = size
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let text = String(value)
        let padded = String(repeating: "0", count: max(0, digits - text.count)) + text
        let numbers = padded.compactMap(\.wholeNumberValue)
        HStack(spacing: size * 0.12) {
            ForEach(numbers.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                SlotReel(digit: numbers[index], size: size, order: index)
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(String(value))
    }
}

private struct SlotReel: View {
    let digit: Int
    let size: CGFloat
    let order: Int

    /// Index into the strip of 40 digits (four turns of 0–9).
    @State private var index: Int = 0
    @State private var isSpinning = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        let height = size * 1.25
        VStack(spacing: 0) {
            ForEach(0..<40, id: \.self) { row in
                Text("\(row % 10)")
                    .font(.system(size: size, weight: .heavy, design: .rounded))
                    .monospacedDigit()
                    .frame(height: height)
            }
        }
        .offset(y: -CGFloat(index) * height)
        .blur(radius: isSpinning ? size * 0.06 : 0)
        .frame(height: height, alignment: .top)
        .padding(.horizontal, size * 0.12)
        .clipped()
        .background(Color.secondary.opacity(0.12), in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: size * 0.18))
        .overlay {
            // Shading so the strip looks like it wraps around a drum.
            LinearGradient(stops: [
                .init(color: .black.opacity(0.25), location: 0),
                .init(color: .clear, location: 0.3),
                .init(color: .clear, location: 0.7),
                .init(color: .black.opacity(0.25), location: 1),
            ], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
            .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: size * 0.18))
            .allowsHitTesting(false)
        }
        .onAppear { index = digit }
        .onChange(of: digit) { old, new in spin(from: old, to: new) }
    }

    private func spin(from old: Int, to new: Int) {
        guard !reduceMotion else {
            withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3)) { index = new }
            return
        }
        // Start from the old digit on the first turn, land on the fourth.
        var reset = Transaction()
        reset.disablesAnimations = true
        withTransaction(reset) { index = old }
        let duration = 0.9 + Double(order) * 0.25
        isSpinning = true
        withAnimation(.timingCurve(0.3, 0, 0.2, 1.08, duration: duration)) {
            index = 30 + new
        } completion: {
            isSpinning = false
            var settle = Transaction()
            settle.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(settle) { index = new }
        }
        Task { @MainActor in
            // Sharpen up a little before the reel stops.
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(duration * 0.7))
            withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: duration * 0.3)) { isSpinning = false }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var value = 777
        var body: some View {
            SlotMachineNumber(value: value)
                .onTapGesture { value = Int.random(in: 0...999) }
                .padding()
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Price Ticker (`price-ticker`)

Digits roll to the new price as the background flashes green or red.

- API: `PriceTicker(value:)`
- Component: Number
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/PriceTicker.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/PriceTicker.swift

### Usage

```swift
PriceTicker(value: stock.price)
    .font(.title2.bold())
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI PriceTicker(value:fractionDigits:prefix:) view (iOS 17+): an HStack of a 10 pt "arrowtriangle.up.fill" / "arrowtriangle.down.fill" (hidden when flat) and the prefix + value formatted with fractionDigits decimals, monospacedDigit, with .contentTransition(.numericText(value:)) and .snappy(0.35 s) animation so digits roll. On change, record the direction (green up, red down) for the arrow and text colour, and bump a counter that drives keyframeAnimator on a rounded background in that colour: opacity 0 → 0.3 (0.05 s) → 0 (0.9 s), a quick flash. With Reduce Motion on, skip the roll animation and the flash.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A live price: digits roll to the new value, the background flashes green
/// or red, and an arrow shows which way it moved.
public struct PriceTicker: View {
    private let value: Double
    private let fractionDigits: Int
    private let prefix: String

    @State private var direction: Direction = .flat
    @State private var flashes = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private enum Direction { case up, down, flat }

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - value: The current price.
    ///   - fractionDigits: Decimal places to show.
    ///   - prefix: Text before the number, such as a currency symbol.
    public init(value: Double, fractionDigits: Int = 2, prefix: String = "$") {
        self.value = value
        self.fractionDigits = fractionDigits
        self.prefix = prefix
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let color: Color = direction == .up ? .green : direction == .down ? .red : .secondary
        HStack(spacing: 6) {
            Image(systemName: direction == .down ? "arrowtriangle.down.fill" : "arrowtriangle.up.fill")
                .font(.system(size: 10))
                .foregroundStyle(color)
                .opacity(direction == .flat ? 0 : 1)
                .contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))
            Text(prefix + value.formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(fractionDigits))))
                .monospacedDigit()
                .contentTransition(.numericText(value: value))
                .foregroundStyle(direction == .flat ? Color.primary : color)
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, 10)
        .padding(.vertical, 6)
        .background {
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8)
                .fill(color)
                .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0.0, trigger: flashes) { view, opacity in
                    view.opacity(opacity)
                } keyframes: { _ in
                    LinearKeyframe(0.3, duration: 0.05)
                    LinearKeyframe(0, duration: 0.9)
                }
        }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy(duration: 0.35), value: value)
        .onChange(of: value) { old, new in
            direction = new > old ? .up : new < old ? .down : .flat
            if !reduceMotion { flashes += 1 }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var price = 182.40
        var body: some View {
            PriceTicker(value: price)
                .font(.title2.bold())
                .task {
                    while !Task.isCancelled {
                        try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.2))
                        price += Double.random(in: -2...2)
                    }
                }
                .padding()
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Animated Chart (`animated-chart`)

Bars grow up one after another; a line draws itself left to right.

- API: `GrowingBarChart(values:) / DrawingLineChart(values:)`
- Component: Number
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/AnimatedChart.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/AnimatedChart.swift

### Usage

```swift
GrowingBarChart(values: weekly)
    .frame(height: 120)

DrawingLineChart(values: trend, color: .pink)
    .frame(height: 120)
```

### How it works

Create two SwiftUI chart views without Swift Charts (iOS 17+). GrowingBarChart(values:color:spacing:): in a GeometryReader, an HStack(alignment: .bottom) of bars with top-rounded UnevenRoundedRectangles filled with the colour's gradient, bar width = width / (n + (n − 1) × spacing) with spacing 0.35; heights are 0 until onAppear sets grown, then height × value / max with .spring(duration: 0.6, bounce: 0.3) delayed 0.06 s × index, and springing to new heights when values change. DrawingLineChart(values:color:duration:): map values into the rect (5–6 pt inset), smooth with midpoint quadratic curves, stroke it 3 pt with round caps trimmed to progress, fill the closed area under it with a colour 35 % → clear gradient at opacity progress, and pop a 9 pt dot with a white ring onto the last point with a bouncy spring once progress reaches 1. In .task(id: values), reset progress to 0 without animation and animate to 1 with .easeInOut(1.2 s). With Reduce Motion on, use short eases.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A bar chart whose bars grow up from the baseline one after another on
/// appear, and spring to their new heights when the values change.
public struct GrowingBarChart: View {
    private let values: [Double]
    private let color: Color
    private let spacing: CGFloat

    @State private var grown = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - values: Bar values; the tallest fills the height.
    ///   - color: Bar colour.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between bars, as a fraction of a bar's width.
    public init(values: [Double], color: Color = .accentColor, spacing: CGFloat = 0.35) {
        self.values = values
        self.color = color
        self.spacing = spacing
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let top = max(values.max() ?? 1, 0.0001)
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let count = CGFloat(max(1, values.count))
            let barWidth = geometry.size.width / (count + (count - 1) * spacing)
            HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing: barWidth * spacing) {
                ForEach(values.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                    let fraction = grown ? max(0, values[index]) / top : 0
                    UnevenRoundedRectangle(topLeadingRadius: barWidth * 0.25, topTrailingRadius: barWidth * 0.25)
                        .fill(color.gradient)
                        .frame(width: barWidth, height: max(2, geometry.size.height * fraction))
                        .animation(
                            reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.3)
                                : .spring(duration: 0.6, bounce: 0.3).delay(grown ? Double(index) * 0.06 : 0),
                            value: grown
                        )
                        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.6, bounce: 0.3), value: values[index])
                }
            }
            .frame(maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .bottom)
        }
        .onAppear { grown = true }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Bar chart")
        .accessibilityValue(values.map { $0.formatted() }.joined(separator: ", "))
    }
}

/// A line chart that draws itself from left to right, with a gradient area
/// that fades in underneath and a dot that lands on the last point. Redraws
/// when the values change.
public struct DrawingLineChart: View {
    private let values: [Double]
    private let color: Color
    private let duration: Double

    @State private var progress: Double = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - values: The points, left to right.
    ///   - color: Line colour.
    ///   - duration: Seconds to draw the line.
    public init(values: [Double], color: Color = .accentColor, duration: Double = 1.2) {
        self.values = values
        self.color = color
        self.duration = duration
    }

    public var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ChartLine(values: values, closed: true)
                .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [color.opacity(0.35), color.opacity(0)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
                .opacity(progress)
            ChartLine(values: values, closed: false)
                .trim(from: 0, to: progress)
                .stroke(color, style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 3, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round))
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                if let last = ChartLine.points(values, in: CGRect(origin: .zero, size: geometry.size)).last {
                    Circle()
                        .fill(color)
                        .frame(width: 9, height: 9)
                        .overlay(Circle().stroke(.white, lineWidth: 2))
                        .position(last)
                        .scaleEffect(progress >= 1 ? 1 : 0.01, anchor: UnitPoint(x: last.x / max(1, geometry.size.width), y: last.y / max(1, geometry.size.height)))
                        .animation(.spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.5), value: progress >= 1)
                }
            }
        }
        .task(id: values) {
            var reset = Transaction()
            reset.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(reset) { progress = 0 }
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(16))
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.3) : .easeInOut(duration: duration)) { progress = 1 }
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Line chart")
        .accessibilityValue(values.map { $0.formatted() }.joined(separator: ", "))
    }
}

struct ChartLine: Shape {
    var values: [Double]
    var closed: Bool

    static func points(_ values: [Double], in rect: CGRect) -> [CGPoint] {
        guard values.count > 1, let low = values.min(), let high = values.max() else { return [] }
        let range = max(high - low, 0.0001)
        // A little headroom so the stroke and dot aren't clipped.
        let inset = rect.insetBy(dx: 5, dy: 6)
        return values.enumerated().map { index, value in
            CGPoint(
                x: inset.minX + inset.width * CGFloat(index) / CGFloat(values.count - 1),
                y: inset.maxY - inset.height * CGFloat((value - low) / range)
            )
        }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let points = Self.points(values, in: rect)
        var path = Path()
        guard let first = points.first, let last = points.last else { return path }
        path.move(to: first)
        // Smooth the line with midpoint quadratic curves.
        for index in 1..<points.count {
            let previous = points[index - 1], point = points[index]
            let mid = CGPoint(x: (previous.x + point.x) / 2, y: (previous.y + point.y) / 2)
            path.addQuadCurve(to: mid, control: previous)
            if index == points.count - 1 { path.addQuadCurve(to: point, control: point) }
        }
        if closed {
            path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: last.x, y: rect.maxY))
            path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: first.x, y: rect.maxY))
            path.closeSubpath()
        }
        return path
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 30) {
        GrowingBarChart(values: [3, 7, 4, 9, 6, 8]).frame(width: 220, height: 100)
        DrawingLineChart(values: [3, 5, 4, 8, 6, 9, 7, 11]).frame(width: 220, height: 100)
    }
    .padding()
}
```

## Needle Gauge (`needle-gauge`)

A speedometer needle swings to the value, overshoots and settles.

- API: `NeedleGauge(value:)`
- Component: Number
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/NeedleGauge.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/NeedleGauge.swift

### Usage

```swift
NeedleGauge(value: cpuLoad)
    .frame(width: 200, height: 200)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI NeedleGauge(value:colors:label:) view (iOS 17+), value 0…1, square. Draw a 240° arc (from 150° to 30° clockwise, radius 42 % of the side, line width 8 %, round caps): a secondary-15 % track, and on top an animatable arc Shape trimmed to the value and stroked with an AngularGradient of green, yellow, red over the same angles. Add 11 tick capsules (longer every fifth) rotated from −120° to +120°, a primary-coloured needle capsule rotated −120° + 240° × value, and a hub circle. Animate the needle with .spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.45) so it overshoots and settles. Below the hub, show the label or the percentage with .contentTransition(.numericText). With Reduce Motion on, use a 0.3 s ease.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A speedometer-style gauge: a 240° arc that fills with a gradient, tick
/// marks, and a needle that swings to the value on a spring, overshooting a
/// little before it settles.
public struct NeedleGauge: View {
    private let value: Double
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let label: String?

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let sweep = 240.0

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - value: 0 (needle far left) to 1 (far right). Clamped.
    ///   - colors: Gradient along the arc, from 0 to 1.
    ///   - label: Optional caption under the needle; defaults to a percentage.
    public init(value: Double, colors: [Color] = [.green, .yellow, .red], label: String? = nil) {
        self.value = min(1, max(0, value))
        self.colors = colors
        self.label = label
    }

    public var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { geometry in
            let side = min(geometry.size.width, geometry.size.height)
            let lineWidth = side * 0.08
            ZStack {
                arc(to: 1)
                    .stroke(Color.secondary.opacity(0.15), style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round))
                arc(to: value)
                    .stroke(
                        AngularGradient(colors: colors, center: .center, startAngle: .degrees(90 + (360 - sweep) / 2), endAngle: .degrees(90 + (360 - sweep) / 2 + sweep)),
                        style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round)
                    )
                ForEach(0...10, id: \.self) { tick in
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(Color.secondary.opacity(0.6))
                        .frame(width: tick.isMultiple(of: 5) ? 2.5 : 1.5, height: side * (tick.isMultiple(of: 5) ? 0.08 : 0.05))
                        .offset(y: -side * 0.32)
                        .rotationEffect(.degrees(-sweep / 2 + sweep * Double(tick) / 10))
                }
                Capsule()
                    .fill(Color.primary)
                    .frame(width: side * 0.025, height: side * 0.36)
                    .offset(y: -side * 0.14)
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(-sweep / 2 + sweep * value))
                    .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.3) : .spring(duration: 0.9, bounce: 0.45), value: value)
                Circle()
                    .fill(Color.primary)
                    .frame(width: side * 0.08, height: side * 0.08)
                Text(label ?? "\(Int((value * 100).rounded()))%")
                    .font(.system(size: side * 0.11, weight: .bold, design: .rounded))
                    .monospacedDigit()
                    .contentTransition(.numericText(value: value))
                    .animation(.snappy, value: value)
                    .offset(y: side * 0.24)
            }
            .frame(width: side, height: side)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Gauge")
        .accessibilityValue(label ?? "\(Int((value * 100).rounded())) percent")
    }

    /// The arc from the left end to `fraction` of the sweep.
    private func arc(to fraction: Double) -> some Shape {
        GaugeArc(sweep: sweep, fraction: fraction)
    }
}

struct GaugeArc: Shape {
    var sweep: Double
    var fraction: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { fraction }
        set { fraction = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let radius = min(rect.width, rect.height) * 0.42
        let start = 90 + (360 - sweep) / 2
        var path = Path()
        path.addArc(center: CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY), radius: radius, startAngle: .degrees(start), endAngle: .degrees(start + sweep * fraction), clockwise: false)
        return path
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var value = 0.3
        var body: some View {
            NeedleGauge(value: value)
                .frame(width: 200, height: 200)
                .onTapGesture { value = Double.random(in: 0...1) }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Contribution Grid (`contribution-grid`)

Activity squares pop in column by column, shaded by how busy each day was.

- API: `ContributionGrid(values:)`
- Component: Number
- Trigger: Appear / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/ContributionGrid.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Number/ContributionGrid.swift

### Usage

```swift
ContributionGrid(values: commitsPerDay, color: .green)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI ContributionGrid(values:rows:color:cellSize:spacing:) view (iOS 17+) like a contributions calendar: values fill columns of rows (7) top to bottom, left to right, as 11 pt squares with 3 pt gaps and corner radius 0.22 × size. Shade each square by its share of the largest value, rounded up to quarters: 0 is secondary at 15 %, otherwise the colour at 0.25 + 0.75 × level. On appear, scale each square from 0.2 and fade it in with .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.45) delayed by 0.035 s per column + 0.02 s per row, so it sweeps in diagonally; changes of shade use the same staggered spring. With Reduce Motion on, no scaling and a plain 0.3 s ease. Make it one accessibility element whose value is "N of M days active".

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A grid of small squares shaded by value, like a contributions calendar.
/// On appear the squares pop in column by column in a diagonal wave, and
/// when the values change the new shades ripple through the same way.
///
/// ```swift
/// ContributionGrid(values: commitsPerDay, color: .green)
/// ```
public struct ContributionGrid: View {
    private let values: [Double]
    private let rows: Int
    private let color: Color
    private let cellSize: CGFloat
    private let spacing: CGFloat

    @State private var shown = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - values: One value per day, filled top to bottom, then left to right.
    ///     Shades are relative to the largest value.
    ///   - rows: Squares per column (7 for a week).
    ///   - color: Colour of the busiest squares.
    ///   - cellSize: Side of a square, in points.
    ///   - spacing: Gap between squares.
    public init(values: [Double], rows: Int = 7, color: Color = .green, cellSize: CGFloat = 11, spacing: CGFloat = 3) {
        self.values = values
        self.rows = max(1, rows)
        self.color = color
        self.cellSize = cellSize
        self.spacing = spacing
    }

    public var body: some View {
        let columns = Int(ceil(Double(values.count) / Double(rows)))
        let peak = max(values.max() ?? 0, .leastNonzeroMagnitude)
        HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: spacing) {
            ForEach(0..<columns, id: \.self) { column in
                VStack(spacing: spacing) {
                    ForEach(0..<rows, id: \.self) { row in
                        let index = column * rows + row
                        if index < values.count {
                            let level = shade(values[index] / peak)
                            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cellSize * 0.22, style: .continuous)
                                .fill(level == 0 ? Color.secondary.opacity(0.15) : color.opacity(0.25 + 0.75 * level))
                                .frame(width: cellSize, height: cellSize)
                                .scaleEffect(shown || reduceMotion ? 1 : 0.2)
                                .opacity(shown ? 1 : 0)
                                .animation(wave(column: column, row: row), value: shown)
                                .animation(wave(column: column, row: row), value: level)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        .onAppear { shown = true }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Activity grid")
        .accessibilityValue("\(values.filter { $0 > 0 }.count) of \(values.count) days active")
    }

    /// Rounds a 0…1 share to one of five shades, like a contributions calendar.
    private func shade(_ share: Double) -> Double {
        guard share > 0 else { return 0 }
        return min(1, ceil(share * 4) / 4)
    }

    private func wave(column: Int, row: Int) -> Animation {
        if reduceMotion { return .easeInOut(duration: 0.3) }
        return .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.45).delay(Double(column) * 0.035 + Double(row) * 0.02)
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var seed = 1
        var body: some View {
            ContributionGrid(values: (0..<(7 * 20)).map { index in
                let x = sin(Double(index * seed) * 12.9898) * 43758.5453
                let r = x - floor(x)
                return r < 0.3 ? 0 : r * 10
            })
            .onTapGesture { seed += 1 }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```
