## Dot Globe (`dot-globe`)

A globe of evenly spread dots spins on a tilted axis, with pulsing cities.

- API: `DotGlobe()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/DotGlobe.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/DotGlobe.swift

### Usage

```swift
DotGlobe(dots: 700, color: .cyan)
    .frame(width: 260, height: 260)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI DotGlobe(dots:color:accent:speed:) view (iOS 17+), square, drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Place 700 points on a unit sphere with the Fibonacci method (y = 1 − 2(i + 0.5)/n, ring = √(1 − y²), θ = golden angle × i + time × 0.6), tilt them 0.35 rad around the x axis, and project orthographically onto a circle of radius 45 % of the side. With depth = (z + 1) / 2, draw each dot with radius (0.6 + 1.2 × depth) and opacity 0.12 + 0.88 × depth², so the back is faint. Every 61st dot is a "city" in the accent colour (on the front half) whose radius pulses with sin(time × 3 + i). Add a faint 15 % rim circle. With Reduce Motion on, don't rotate.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A globe made of evenly spread dots, spinning slowly on a tilted axis.
/// Dots on the far side are smaller and fainter, which sells the depth,
/// and a few "cities" pulse.
public struct DotGlobe: View {
    private let dots: Int
    private let color: Color
    private let accent: Color
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - dots: Number of dots on the sphere.
    ///   - color: Dot colour.
    ///   - accent: Colour of the pulsing cities.
    ///   - speed: Turns per minute ÷ 6 (1 = one turn every 10 s… roughly).
    public init(dots: Int = 700, color: Color = .cyan, accent: Color = .pink, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.dots = max(10, dots)
        self.color = color
        self.accent = accent
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            Canvas { context, size in
                let radius = min(size.width, size.height) * 0.45
                let centre = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                let spin = time * 0.6
                let tilt = 0.35
                let golden = Double.pi * (3 - sqrt(5))
                for index in 0..<dots {
                    // Fibonacci sphere: evenly spread points.
                    let y = 1 - 2 * (Double(index) + 0.5) / Double(dots)
                    let ring = sqrt(1 - y * y)
                    let theta = golden * Double(index) + spin
                    var x = cos(theta) * ring, z = sin(theta) * ring
                    // Tilt the axis towards the viewer.
                    let ty = y * cos(tilt) - z * sin(tilt)
                    z = y * sin(tilt) + z * cos(tilt)
                    x *= 1
                    let depth = (z + 1) / 2 // 0 = back, 1 = front
                    let isCity = index % 61 == 0
                    let pulse = isCity ? 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(time * 3 + Double(index)) : 0
                    let r = (0.6 + 1.2 * depth) * (isCity ? 1.8 + pulse : 1)
                    let p = CGPoint(x: centre.x + CGFloat(x) * radius, y: centre.y - CGFloat(ty) * radius)
                    let tint = isCity && depth > 0.5 ? accent : color
                    context.fill(
                        Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: p.x - r, y: p.y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)),
                        with: .color(tint.opacity(0.12 + 0.88 * depth * depth))
                    )
                }
                // A faint rim light.
                context.stroke(
                    Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: centre.x - radius, y: centre.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)),
                    with: .color(color.opacity(0.15)), lineWidth: 1
                )
            }
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

#Preview {
    DotGlobe()
        .frame(width: 260, height: 260)
        .background(Color(red: 0.03, green: 0.05, blue: 0.12))
}
```

## Bubbles (`bubbles`)

Soap bubbles rise and wobble with rainbow rims and glossy highlights.

- API: `Bubbles()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Bubbles.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Bubbles.swift

### Usage

```swift
Bubbles(count: 18)
    .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.blue.opacity(0.5), .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Bubbles(count:color:speed:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Each of 18 bubbles has a stable random radius (6–22 pt), rise time (4–8 s), phase and x; progress = ((time + phase) / duration) mod 1 moves it from below the bottom to above the top while x wobbles by 14 pt × sin(time × (1 + r) + i). Fade in over the first ~17 % and out over the last 20 %. Fill each with a radial gradient (2 % → 12 % → 35 % of the tint, transparent centre), stroke a 1 pt rim with a diagonal pink → tint → purple gradient, and add a small white oval highlight at the top-left. With Reduce Motion on, show one still frame.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Soap bubbles rise from the bottom, wobbling side to side, with a
/// rainbow-tinted rim and a glossy highlight, and fade out near the top.
public struct Bubbles: View {
    private let count: Int
    private let color: Color
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of bubbles in flight.
    ///   - color: Rim tint.
    ///   - speed: Multiplier on the rising speed.
    public init(count: Int = 18, color: Color = .cyan, speed: Double = 1) {
        self.count = max(1, count)
        self.color = color
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 5 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed
            Canvas { context, size in
                for index in 0..<count {
                    let seed = Double(index)
                    let r = CGFloat(6 + Self.hash(index, 1) * 16)
                    let duration = 4 + Self.hash(index, 2) * 4
                    let progress = ((time + Self.hash(index, 3) * duration) / duration).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
                    let baseX = Self.hash(index, 4) * size.width
                    let x = baseX + sin(time * (1 + Self.hash(index, 5)) + seed) * 14
                    let y = size.height + r - (size.height + r * 2) * progress
                    let fade = progress > 0.8 ? (1 - progress) / 0.2 : min(1, progress * 6)
                    let rect = CGRect(x: x - r, y: y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)
                    var bubble = context
                    bubble.opacity = fade
                    bubble.fill(Path(ellipseIn: rect), with: .radialGradient(
                        Gradient(colors: [color.opacity(0.02), color.opacity(0.12), color.opacity(0.35)]),
                        center: CGPoint(x: x, y: y), startRadius: 0, endRadius: r
                    ))
                    bubble.stroke(Path(ellipseIn: rect), with: .linearGradient(
                        Gradient(colors: [.pink.opacity(0.7), color.opacity(0.8), .purple.opacity(0.6)]),
                        startPoint: CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.minY), endPoint: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.maxY)
                    ), lineWidth: 1)
                    let shine = CGRect(x: x - r * 0.55, y: y - r * 0.6, width: r * 0.45, height: r * 0.3)
                    bubble.fill(Path(ellipseIn: shine), with: .color(.white.opacity(0.75)))
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    static func hash(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 1_103_515_245 &+ b &* 12_345 &+ 777)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 16)) &* 0x45d9_f3b
        x ^= x >> 16
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

#Preview {
    Bubbles()
        .frame(width: 300, height: 220)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.blue.opacity(0.5), .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
}
```

## Fireflies (`fireflies`)

Glowing fireflies drift lazily and blink on their own rhythms.

- API: `Fireflies()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Fireflies.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Fireflies.swift

### Usage

```swift
Fireflies(count: 24)
    .background(Color(red: 0.02, green: 0.06, blue: 0.05))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Fireflies(count:color:speed:) view (iOS 17+) drawn in a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation). Each firefly has three stable random values a, b, c; its position is the view centre plus two layered sines per axis (x: 0.38 sin(t(0.13 + 0.12a) + 20a) + 0.1 sin(t(0.5 + 0.3b) + 9b); y: 0.36 sin(t(0.11 + 0.1b) + 17b) + 0.1 cos(t(0.45 + 0.3c) + 5c), as fractions of the size), giving slow wandering loops. Its blink = (0.5 + 0.5 sin(t(0.8 + 1.6c) + 30a))³. Draw a glow circle 8 × r wide in a context with .blur(radius: 6) at opacity 0.25 + 0.75 × blink, then a white core of radius r (1.6–2.8 pt) at 0.35 + 0.65 × blink. Warm yellow by default. With Reduce Motion on, freeze positions but keep the blinking.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Fireflies drift lazily on looping paths, each glowing and dimming on its
/// own rhythm. Lovely over dark, quiet backgrounds.
public struct Fireflies: View {
    private let count: Int
    private let color: Color
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of fireflies.
    ///   - color: Glow colour.
    ///   - speed: Multiplier on the drifting speed.
    public init(count: Int = 24, color: Color = Color(red: 1, green: 0.9, blue: 0.45), speed: Double = 1) {
        self.count = max(1, count)
        self.color = color
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
            let real = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            // Reduce Motion: they stay put but keep glowing softly.
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : real * speed
            Canvas { context, size in
                var glow = context
                glow.addFilter(.blur(radius: 6))
                for index in 0..<count {
                    let a = Self.hash(index, 1), b = Self.hash(index, 2), c = Self.hash(index, 3)
                    // Two layered sines per axis give slow, wandering loops.
                    let x = size.width * (0.5 + 0.38 * sin(time * (0.13 + a * 0.12) + a * 20) + 0.1 * sin(time * (0.5 + b * 0.3) + b * 9))
                    let y = size.height * (0.5 + 0.36 * sin(time * (0.11 + b * 0.1) + b * 17) + 0.1 * cos(time * (0.45 + c * 0.3) + c * 5))
                    let blink = pow(0.5 + 0.5 * sin(real * (0.8 + c * 1.6) + a * 30), 3)
                    let r = 1.6 + 1.2 * c
                    glow.opacity = 0.25 + 0.75 * blink
                    glow.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: x - r * 4, y: y - r * 4, width: r * 8, height: r * 8)), with: .color(color.opacity(0.7)))
                    var core = context
                    core.opacity = 0.35 + 0.65 * blink
                    core.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: x - r, y: y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2)), with: .color(.white))
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    static func hash(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 9_301 &+ b &* 49_297 &+ 233_280)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 15)) &* 0x2c1b_3c6d
        x ^= x >> 12
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

#Preview {
    Fireflies()
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
        .background(Color(red: 0.02, green: 0.06, blue: 0.05))
}
```

## Flock (`flock`)

Little arrows swim together like birds or fish, and chase your finger.

- API: `Flock()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop / Drag / Hover
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Flock.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Flock.swift

### Usage

```swift
Flock(count: 60, color: .white)
    .background(.indigo.gradient)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Flock(count:color:speed:) view (iOS 17+) that simulates boids. Keep the boids (position, velocity) in a reference-type model stored in @State and advance it from a Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation), with dt = time since the last frame capped at 1/20 s. For each boid, look at neighbours within 46 pt: steer 5 % towards their average velocity, 1.2 % towards their centre, and away from any closer than 16 pt by 0.14 × the overlap. If there's a target (from onContinuousHover or a DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)), add 2 % of the gap to it. Push back by 9 within 24 pt of an edge. Clamp speed between 0.6 and 1.3 × cruise (90 pt/s, 1.5× when chasing). Draw each boid as a small arrowhead path rotated to atan2 of its velocity. With Reduce Motion on, freeze them. Hide it from accessibility.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A flock of little arrows that swim together like birds or fish: each one
/// steers to keep its distance, match its neighbours' heading and stay with
/// the group (boids). Drag or hover and the flock chases the pointer.
///
/// ```swift
/// Flock(count: 60, color: .white)
///     .background(.indigo.gradient)
/// ```
public struct Flock: View {
    private let count: Int
    private let color: Color
    private let speed: Double

    @State private var model = FlockModel()
    @State private var target: CGPoint?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - count: Number of boids.
    ///   - color: Colour of the boids.
    ///   - speed: Cruising speed, in points per second.
    public init(count: Int = 50, color: Color = .white, speed: Double = 90) {
        self.count = max(1, count)
        self.color = color
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            Canvas { context, size in
                model.step(to: timeline.date, size: size, count: count, speed: speed, target: target, frozen: reduceMotion)
                for boid in model.boids {
                    let angle = atan2(boid.velocity.dy, boid.velocity.dx)
                    var arrow = Path()
                    arrow.move(to: CGPoint(x: 7, y: 0))
                    arrow.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: -5, y: 4))
                    arrow.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: -2.5, y: 0))
                    arrow.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: -5, y: -4))
                    arrow.closeSubpath()
                    let transform = CGAffineTransform(translationX: boid.position.x, y: boid.position.y).rotated(by: angle)
                    context.fill(arrow.applying(transform), with: .color(color))
                }
            }
        }
        .contentShape(Rectangle())
        .onContinuousHover { phase in
            if case let .active(location) = phase { target = location } else { target = nil }
        }
        .gesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
            .onChanged { target = $0.location }
            .onEnded { _ in target = nil })
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

/// The simulation. A class so the canvas can advance it every frame without
/// invalidating the view.
final class FlockModel {
    struct Boid {
        var position: CGPoint
        var velocity: CGVector
    }

    private(set) var boids: [Boid] = []
    private var last: Date?

    func step(to date: Date, size: CGSize, count: Int, speed: Double, target: CGPoint?, frozen: Bool) {
        if boids.count != count { seed(count: count, size: size, speed: speed) }
        let dt = min(1.0 / 20, last.map { date.timeIntervalSince($0) } ?? 0)
        last = date
        guard !frozen, dt > 0 else { return }

        let neighbourhood: CGFloat = 46, personalSpace: CGFloat = 16
        var next = boids
        for i in boids.indices {
            var separation = CGVector.zero, alignment = CGVector.zero, centre = CGVector.zero
            var neighbours: CGFloat = 0
            for j in boids.indices where j != i {
                let dx = boids[j].position.x - boids[i].position.x
                let dy = boids[j].position.y - boids[i].position.y
                let distance = hypot(dx, dy)
                guard distance < neighbourhood else { continue }
                neighbours += 1
                alignment.dx += boids[j].velocity.dx; alignment.dy += boids[j].velocity.dy
                centre.dx += dx; centre.dy += dy
                if distance < personalSpace, distance > 0.01 {
                    separation.dx -= dx / distance * (personalSpace - distance)
                    separation.dy -= dy / distance * (personalSpace - distance)
                }
            }
            var v = boids[i].velocity
            if neighbours > 0 {
                v.dx += (alignment.dx / neighbours - v.dx) * 0.05 + centre.dx / neighbours * 0.012 + separation.dx * 0.14
                v.dy += (alignment.dy / neighbours - v.dy) * 0.05 + centre.dy / neighbours * 0.012 + separation.dy * 0.14
            }
            let p = boids[i].position
            if let target {
                v.dx += (target.x - p.x) * 0.02
                v.dy += (target.y - p.y) * 0.02
            }
            // Turn back from the edges.
            let margin: CGFloat = 24, turn: CGFloat = 9
            if p.x < margin { v.dx += turn }
            if p.x > size.width - margin { v.dx -= turn }
            if p.y < margin { v.dy += turn }
            if p.y > size.height - margin { v.dy -= turn }
            // Hold the cruising speed (a little faster when chasing).
            let cruise = CGFloat(speed) * (target == nil ? 1 : 1.5)
            let length = max(0.01, hypot(v.dx, v.dy))
            let clamped = min(max(length, cruise * 0.6), cruise * 1.3)
            v = CGVector(dx: v.dx / length * clamped, dy: v.dy / length * clamped)
            next[i].velocity = v
            next[i].position = CGPoint(x: p.x + v.dx * dt, y: p.y + v.dy * dt)
        }
        boids = next
    }

    private func seed(count: Int, size: CGSize, speed: Double) {
        var generator = SystemRandomNumberGenerator()
        boids = (0..<count).map { _ in
            let angle = Double.random(in: 0..<(2 * .pi), using: &generator)
            return Boid(
                position: CGPoint(x: .random(in: 0...max(1, size.width), using: &generator), y: .random(in: 0...max(1, size.height), using: &generator)),
                velocity: CGVector(dx: cos(angle) * speed, dy: sin(angle) * speed)
            )
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    Flock()
        .frame(width: 340, height: 240)
        .background(Color.indigo.gradient)
}
```

## Ink Trail (`ink-trail`)

The pointer or finger leaves puffs of ink that swell, drift up and fade.

- API: `.inkTrail(color:)`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Drag / Hover
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/InkTrail.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/InkTrail.swift

### Usage

```swift
Color.black
    .inkTrail(color: .purple)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .inkTrail(color:lifetime:size:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Record puffs (point, time, random seed) from onContinuousHover and a simultaneous DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0), skipping points closer than 0.18 × size to the last one within 50 ms and dropping puffs older than lifetime (1.2 s). Draw them in an overlay Canvas inside TimelineView(.animation) with a blur of 0.35 × size: at age a (0…1) a puff has radius size × (0.35 + 0.9a) (size 26 pt), rises 34a pt, sways sideways by sin(seed × 9 + 3a) × 14a pt, and has opacity 0.85 × (1 − a)². Disable hit testing on the overlay. With Reduce Motion on, record nothing.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The pointer or finger leaves a soft trail of ink, like smoke from a
/// sparkler: puffs swell, drift upwards and fade.
struct InkTrailModifier: ViewModifier {
    var color: Color
    var lifetime: Double
    var size: CGFloat

    struct Puff {
        var point: CGPoint
        var time: Date
        var seed: Double
    }

    @State private var puffs: [Puff] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion || puffs.isEmpty)) { timeline in
                    Canvas { context, _ in
                        context.addFilter(.blur(radius: size * 0.35))
                        for puff in puffs {
                            let age = timeline.date.timeIntervalSince(puff.time) / lifetime
                            guard age >= 0, age < 1 else { continue }
                            let radius = size * (0.35 + age * 0.9)
                            // Drift up and sideways, a little differently per puff.
                            let x = puff.point.x + CGFloat(sin(puff.seed * 9 + age * 3) * 14 * age)
                            let y = puff.point.y - CGFloat(age * 34)
                            let opacity = (1 - age) * (1 - age) * 0.85
                            context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: x - radius, y: y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)), with: .color(color.opacity(opacity)))
                        }
                    }
                }
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .onContinuousHover { phase in
                if case let .active(location) = phase { add(location) }
            }
            .simultaneousGesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { add($0.location) })
    }

    private func add(_ point: CGPoint) {
        guard !reduceMotion else { return }
        let now = Date()
        // Space puffs out so a slow drag doesn't stack hundreds in one spot.
        if let last = puffs.last, hypot(last.point.x - point.x, last.point.y - point.y) < size * 0.18, now.timeIntervalSince(last.time) < 0.05 { return }
        puffs.removeAll { now.timeIntervalSince($0.time) > lifetime }
        puffs.append(Puff(point: point, time: now, seed: Double.random(in: 0...1)))
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Leaves a fading trail of ink or smoke wherever the pointer moves or a
    /// finger drags over the view.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Color.black
    ///     .inkTrail(color: .purple)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - color: Colour of the ink.
    ///   - lifetime: Seconds before a puff fades away.
    ///   - size: Diameter of a fresh puff, in points.
    func inkTrail(color: Color = .purple, lifetime: Double = 1.2, size: CGFloat = 26) -> some View {
        modifier(InkTrailModifier(color: color, lifetime: lifetime, size: size))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Color(red: 0.06, green: 0.05, blue: 0.1)
        .frame(width: 340, height: 240)
        .inkTrail(color: .pink)
}
```

## Rain on Glass (`rain-on-glass`)

Raindrops cling to a window while bigger drops slide down in fits and starts.

- API: `RainOnGlass()`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/RainOnGlass.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/RainOnGlass.swift

### Usage

```swift
Image("city-night")
    .blur(radius: 6)
    .overlay(RainOnGlass())
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI RainOnGlass(drops:tint:) overlay (iOS 17+) in TimelineView(.animation) + Canvas. Scatter one static bead per 900 pt² at hashed positions with radius 0.8–2.6 pt. Each of the sliding drops (9) has a cycle of 3.5–7.5 s; its progress l through the cycle becomes stick-slip motion with five steps, (floor(5l) + frac(5l)³) / 5, carrying it from a hashed start near the top past the bottom edge, with a 3 pt sideways wobble and radius 3.2–5.8 pt, stretched 1.25× vertically. Behind it, leave a trail of tiny beads every 9 pt with hashed jitter. Draw every drop like a tiny lens: an ellipse filled with a diagonal gradient (tint 35 % → tint 5 % → black 35 %) plus a bright fleck at the top-left. Disable hit testing. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Raindrops on a window: tiny beads cling to the glass while bigger drops
/// slide down in fits and starts, leaving a dotted trail behind them. Put it
/// over a blurred photo or a dark gradient.
///
/// ```swift
/// Image("city-night")
///     .blur(radius: 6)
///     .overlay(RainOnGlass())
/// ```
public struct RainOnGlass: View {
    private let drops: Int
    private let tint: Color

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - drops: Number of sliding drops.
    ///   - tint: Colour of the drops' highlights.
    public init(drops: Int = 9, tint: Color = .white) {
        self.drops = max(0, drops)
        self.tint = tint
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                // Beads that cling to the glass.
                let beads = Int(size.width * size.height / 900)
                for index in 0..<beads {
                    let x = Self.hash(index, 1) * size.width, y = Self.hash(index, 2) * size.height
                    drawDrop(&context, at: CGPoint(x: x, y: y), radius: 0.8 + Self.hash(index, 3) * 1.8)
                }
                // Drops that slide down in fits and starts, then start over.
                for index in 0..<drops {
                    let cycle = 3.5 + Self.hash(index, 4) * 4
                    let local = (time + Self.hash(index, 5) * 20).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: cycle) / cycle
                    // Stick-slip: a staircase smoothed with a little ease.
                    let steps = 5.0
                    let stepped = (floor(local * steps) + pow(local * steps - floor(local * steps), 3)) / steps
                    let startY = -20 + Self.hash(index, 6) * size.height * 0.4
                    let y = startY + stepped * (size.height + 40 - startY)
                    let wobble = sin(local * 9 + Double(index)) * 3
                    let x = Self.hash(index, 7) * size.width + wobble
                    let radius = 3.2 + Self.hash(index, 8) * 2.6
                    // The trail of tiny beads left behind.
                    let trailCount = Int((y - startY) / 9)
                    for t in 0..<max(0, trailCount) {
                        let ty = startY + Double(t) * 9 + Self.hash(index * 31 + t, 9) * 5
                        let tx = Self.hash(index, 7) * size.width + sin(Double(t) * 1.7 + Double(index)) * 1.5
                        drawDrop(&context, at: CGPoint(x: tx, y: ty), radius: 0.7 + Self.hash(index * 31 + t, 10) * 0.8)
                    }
                    drawDrop(&context, at: CGPoint(x: x, y: y), radius: radius, stretch: 1.25)
                }
            }
        }
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    /// A drop: darker rim at the bottom, bright fleck at the top-left, like a
    /// tiny lens.
    private func drawDrop(_ context: inout GraphicsContext, at p: CGPoint, radius r: Double, stretch: Double = 1) {
        let rect = CGRect(x: p.x - r, y: p.y - r * stretch, width: r * 2, height: r * 2 * stretch)
        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: rect), with: .linearGradient(
            Gradient(colors: [tint.opacity(0.35), tint.opacity(0.05), Color.black.opacity(0.35)]),
            startPoint: CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.minY), endPoint: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.maxY)))
        let fleck = r * 0.35
        context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: p.x - r * 0.45 - fleck / 2, y: p.y - r * stretch * 0.5 - fleck / 2, width: fleck, height: fleck)), with: .color(tint.opacity(0.8)))
    }

    private static func hash(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 73_856_093 ^ b &* 19_349_663 &+ 0x7A1D)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [Color(red: 0.1, green: 0.15, blue: 0.3), Color(red: 0.35, green: 0.2, blue: 0.4)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
        .overlay(RainOnGlass())
        .frame(width: 340, height: 240)
}
```

## Orbits (`orbits`)

Planets circle a glowing star on tilted orbits, passing behind it and in front.

- API: `Orbits(colors:)`
- Component: Particle & 3D
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Orbits.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Particle/Orbits.swift

### Usage

```swift
Orbits(colors: [.orange, .cyan, .pink])
    .frame(width: 240, height: 160)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Orbits(colors:tilt:centerColor:) view (iOS 17+) in TimelineView(.animation) + Canvas. Each colour is a planet on its own orbit, radius spread from 0.38 to 1 × the largest radius that fits (an ellipse squashed vertically by tilt, 0.38). Period = 2.4 × (2r / maxR)^1.5 s so inner planets move faster; angle = time / period × 2π + 2.1 × index; position = centre + (cos a × r, sin a × r × tilt); depth = sin a. Stroke each orbit at white 14 %. Draw the planets with depth < 0 first, then the star (a 20 pt circle over a 32 pt blurred halo at 70 %), then the ones in front, so they pass behind and in front of it. Scale planets by 0.75 + 0.25 × (depth + 1) / 2 and dim the far ones. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Planets circle a glowing star on tilted orbits, passing behind it and in
/// front of it, getting smaller and dimmer on the far side, like a little
/// solar system or an atom.
///
/// ```swift
/// Orbits(colors: [.orange, .cyan, .pink])
///     .frame(width: 240, height: 160)
/// ```
public struct Orbits: View {
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let tilt: Double
    private let centerColor: Color

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - colors: One planet per colour, from the innermost orbit out.
    ///   - tilt: How flat the orbits look: 0 is seen edge-on, 1 from above.
    ///   - centerColor: Colour of the central star.
    public init(colors: [Color] = [.orange, .cyan, .pink, .mint], tilt: Double = 0.38, centerColor: Color = .yellow) {
        self.colors = colors
        self.tilt = min(1, max(0.05, tilt))
        self.centerColor = centerColor
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
            Canvas { context, size in
                let centre = CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2)
                let maxRadius = min(size.width / 2, size.height / 2 / tilt) * 0.92
                let planets = colors.enumerated().map { index, color in
                    let radius = maxRadius * (0.38 + 0.62 * Double(index + 1) / Double(colors.count))
                    // Inner planets go round faster (roughly Kepler's third law).
                    let period = 2.4 * pow(radius / maxRadius * 2, 1.5)
                    let angle = time / period * 2 * .pi + Double(index) * 2.1
                    let depth = sin(angle) // > 0: in front of the star
                    let point = CGPoint(x: centre.x + cos(angle) * radius, y: centre.y + sin(angle) * radius * tilt)
                    return (radius: radius, point: point, depth: depth, color: color, size: 5 + Double(index % 3) * 2)
                }
                // Orbit rings.
                for planet in planets {
                    let r = planet.radius
                    context.stroke(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: centre.x - r, y: centre.y - r * tilt, width: r * 2, height: r * 2 * tilt)), with: .color(.white.opacity(0.14)), lineWidth: 1)
                }
                func draw(_ planet: (radius: Double, point: CGPoint, depth: Double, color: Color, size: Double)) {
                    let scale = 0.75 + 0.25 * (planet.depth + 1) / 2
                    let s = planet.size * scale
                    context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: planet.point.x - s, y: planet.point.y - s, width: s * 2, height: s * 2)),
                                 with: .color(planet.color.opacity(0.55 + 0.45 * (planet.depth + 1) / 2)))
                }
                for planet in planets where planet.depth < 0 { draw(planet) }
                // The star, with a soft glow.
                var glow = context
                glow.addFilter(.blur(radius: 10))
                glow.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: centre.x - 16, y: centre.y - 16, width: 32, height: 32)), with: .color(centerColor.opacity(0.7)))
                context.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: centre.x - 10, y: centre.y - 10, width: 20, height: 20)), with: .color(centerColor))
                for planet in planets where planet.depth >= 0 { draw(planet) }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

#Preview {
    Orbits()
        .frame(width: 320, height: 200)
        .background(Color(red: 0.04, green: 0.05, blue: 0.12))
}
```

## Iris (`iris`)

A circle opens from a point to reveal the view, like a camera iris.

- API: `.transition(.iris)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
if showPhoto {
    PhotoView()
        .transition(.iris)
}

DetailView()
    .transition(.iris(origin: .topTrailing))
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+, the Transition protocol) called IrisTransition with an origin UnitPoint (centre), exposed as .iris and .iris(origin:). In body(content:phase:), mask the content with a GeometryReader containing a Circle whose radius is the distance from the origin point to the furthest corner, positioned at the origin, with scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin). The circle grows from the origin to cover the view on insertion and closes back on removal, timed by whatever animation drives the change, e.g. withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.6)). It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that reveal or hide a view through an animated mask. Masks
// don't move the content, so they need no Reduce Motion fallback.

// MARK: - Iris

/// A circle that opens from a point to reveal the view, and closes back to
/// it on removal, like a camera iris.
public struct IrisTransition: Transition {
    public var origin: UnitPoint

    public init(origin: UnitPoint = .center) {
        self.origin = origin
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let size = geometry.size
                let o = CGPoint(x: size.width * origin.x, y: size.height * origin.y)
                // Far enough to cover the corner furthest from the origin.
                let radius = [CGPoint.zero, CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 0), CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height), CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height)]
                    .map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }
                    .max() ?? 0
                Circle()
                    .frame(width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
                    .position(o)
                    .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == IrisTransition {
    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from its centre.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showPhoto {
    ///     PhotoView().transition(.iris)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var iris: IrisTransition { IrisTransition() }

    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from `origin`.
    static func iris(origin: UnitPoint) -> IrisTransition { IrisTransition(origin: origin) }
}

// MARK: - Blinds

/// Horizontal slats that open together, like Venetian blinds.
public struct BlindsTransition: Transition {
    public var slats: Int

    public init(slats: Int = 8) {
        self.slats = max(1, slats)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                ForEach(0..<slats, id: \.self) { _ in
                    Rectangle()
                        .scaleEffect(y: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: .top)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == BlindsTransition {
    /// Reveals the view through opening blinds.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Banner().transition(.blinds)
    /// ```
    static var blinds: BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition() }

    /// Reveals the view through `slats` opening blinds.
    static func blinds(slats: Int) -> BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition(slats: slats) }
}

// MARK: - Clock wipe

/// A wedge that sweeps clockwise from twelve o'clock, like a clock hand.
public struct ClockWipeTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            ClockWipeShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
        }
    }
}

struct ClockWipeShape: Shape {
    var progress: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard progress < 1 else { return Path(rect) }
        guard progress > 0 else { return Path() }
        let centre = CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
        let radius = hypot(rect.width, rect.height)
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: centre)
        // In SwiftUI's y-down space, clockwise: false sweeps clockwise on screen.
        path.addArc(center: centre, radius: radius, startAngle: .degrees(-90), endAngle: .degrees(-90 + 360 * progress), clockwise: false)
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == ClockWipeTransition {
    /// Sweeps the view in like the hand of a clock.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Badge().transition(.clockWipe)
    /// ```
    static var clockWipe: ClockWipeTransition { ClockWipeTransition() }
}

// MARK: - Dissolve

/// The view appears and disappears in square pixels, in random order.
public struct DissolveTransition: Transition {
    public var cellSize: CGFloat

    public init(cellSize: CGFloat = 10) {
        self.cellSize = max(2, cellSize)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            DissolveShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0, cellSize: cellSize)
        }
    }
}

struct DissolveShape: Shape {
    var progress: Double
    var cellSize: CGFloat

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard progress < 1 else { return Path(rect) }
        var path = Path()
        guard progress > 0 else { return path }
        let columns = Int((rect.width / cellSize).rounded(.up))
        let rows = Int((rect.height / cellSize).rounded(.up))
        for row in 0..<rows {
            for column in 0..<columns where Self.threshold(column, row) < progress {
                // A hair larger than the cell so neighbours don't leave seams.
                path.addRect(CGRect(x: rect.minX + CGFloat(column) * cellSize, y: rect.minY + CGFloat(row) * cellSize, width: cellSize, height: cellSize).insetBy(dx: -0.25, dy: -0.25))
            }
        }
        return path
    }

    /// A stable pseudo-random value in 0..<1 for each cell.
    static func threshold(_ column: Int, _ row: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: column &* 73_856_093 ^ row &* 19_349_663)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == DissolveTransition {
    /// Dissolves the view in and out in random square pixels.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Avatar().transition(.dissolve)
    /// ```
    static var dissolve: DissolveTransition { DissolveTransition() }

    /// Dissolves the view in and out in random pixels of `cellSize` points.
    static func dissolve(cellSize: CGFloat) -> DissolveTransition { DissolveTransition(cellSize: cellSize) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                HStack(spacing: 12) {
                    ForEach(0..<4, id: \.self) { index in
                        ZStack {
                            if shown {
                                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                                    .fill(Color.blue.gradient)
                                    .transition(index == 0 ? AnyTransition(.iris) : index == 1 ? AnyTransition(.blinds) : index == 2 ? AnyTransition(.clockWipe) : AnyTransition(.dissolve))
                            }
                        }
                        .frame(width: 64, height: 64)
                    }
                }
                Button("Toggle") { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { shown.toggle() } }
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```

## Blinds (`blinds`)

Horizontal slats open together to reveal the view, like Venetian blinds.

- API: `.transition(.blinds)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
Banner()
    .transition(.blinds)

Poster()
    .transition(.blinds(slats: 12))
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called BlindsTransition with a slats count (8), exposed as .blinds and .blinds(slats:). In body(content:phase:), mask the content with a VStack(spacing: 0) of slats Rectangles, each with scaleEffect(y: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: .top), so every slat grows down from its top edge at the same time on insertion and folds back up on removal. It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that reveal or hide a view through an animated mask. Masks
// don't move the content, so they need no Reduce Motion fallback.

// MARK: - Iris

/// A circle that opens from a point to reveal the view, and closes back to
/// it on removal, like a camera iris.
public struct IrisTransition: Transition {
    public var origin: UnitPoint

    public init(origin: UnitPoint = .center) {
        self.origin = origin
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let size = geometry.size
                let o = CGPoint(x: size.width * origin.x, y: size.height * origin.y)
                // Far enough to cover the corner furthest from the origin.
                let radius = [CGPoint.zero, CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 0), CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height), CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height)]
                    .map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }
                    .max() ?? 0
                Circle()
                    .frame(width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
                    .position(o)
                    .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == IrisTransition {
    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from its centre.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showPhoto {
    ///     PhotoView().transition(.iris)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var iris: IrisTransition { IrisTransition() }

    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from `origin`.
    static func iris(origin: UnitPoint) -> IrisTransition { IrisTransition(origin: origin) }
}

// MARK: - Blinds

/// Horizontal slats that open together, like Venetian blinds.
public struct BlindsTransition: Transition {
    public var slats: Int

    public init(slats: Int = 8) {
        self.slats = max(1, slats)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                ForEach(0..<slats, id: \.self) { _ in
                    Rectangle()
                        .scaleEffect(y: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: .top)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == BlindsTransition {
    /// Reveals the view through opening blinds.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Banner().transition(.blinds)
    /// ```
    static var blinds: BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition() }

    /// Reveals the view through `slats` opening blinds.
    static func blinds(slats: Int) -> BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition(slats: slats) }
}

// MARK: - Clock wipe

/// A wedge that sweeps clockwise from twelve o'clock, like a clock hand.
public struct ClockWipeTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            ClockWipeShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
        }
    }
}

struct ClockWipeShape: Shape {
    var progress: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard progress < 1 else { return Path(rect) }
        guard progress > 0 else { return Path() }
        let centre = CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
        let radius = hypot(rect.width, rect.height)
        var path = Path()
        path.move(to: centre)
        // In SwiftUI's y-down space, clockwise: false sweeps clockwise on screen.
        path.addArc(center: centre, radius: radius, startAngle: .degrees(-90), endAngle: .degrees(-90 + 360 * progress), clockwise: false)
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == ClockWipeTransition {
    /// Sweeps the view in like the hand of a clock.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Badge().transition(.clockWipe)
    /// ```
    static var clockWipe: ClockWipeTransition { ClockWipeTransition() }
}

// MARK: - Dissolve

/// The view appears and disappears in square pixels, in random order.
public struct DissolveTransition: Transition {
    public var cellSize: CGFloat

    public init(cellSize: CGFloat = 10) {
        self.cellSize = max(2, cellSize)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            DissolveShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0, cellSize: cellSize)
        }
    }
}

struct DissolveShape: Shape {
    var progress: Double
    var cellSize: CGFloat

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard progress < 1 else { return Path(rect) }
        var path = Path()
        guard progress > 0 else { return path }
        let columns = Int((rect.width / cellSize).rounded(.up))
        let rows = Int((rect.height / cellSize).rounded(.up))
        for row in 0..<rows {
            for column in 0..<columns where Self.threshold(column, row) < progress {
                // A hair larger than the cell so neighbours don't leave seams.
                path.addRect(CGRect(x: rect.minX + CGFloat(column) * cellSize, y: rect.minY + CGFloat(row) * cellSize, width: cellSize, height: cellSize).insetBy(dx: -0.25, dy: -0.25))
            }
        }
        return path
    }

    /// A stable pseudo-random value in 0..<1 for each cell.
    static func threshold(_ column: Int, _ row: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: column &* 73_856_093 ^ row &* 19_349_663)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == DissolveTransition {
    /// Dissolves the view in and out in random square pixels.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Avatar().transition(.dissolve)
    /// ```
    static var dissolve: DissolveTransition { DissolveTransition() }

    /// Dissolves the view in and out in random pixels of `cellSize` points.
    static func dissolve(cellSize: CGFloat) -> DissolveTransition { DissolveTransition(cellSize: cellSize) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                HStack(spacing: 12) {
                    ForEach(0..<4, id: \.self) { index in
                        ZStack {
                            if shown {
                                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                                    .fill(Color.blue.gradient)
                                    .transition(index == 0 ? AnyTransition(.iris) : index == 1 ? AnyTransition(.blinds) : index == 2 ? AnyTransition(.clockWipe) : AnyTransition(.dissolve))
                            }
                        }
                        .frame(width: 64, height: 64)
                    }
                }
                Button("Toggle") { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { shown.toggle() } }
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```

---

## Clock Wipe (`clock-wipe`)

A wedge sweeps clockwise from twelve o'clock, like a clock hand.

- API: `.transition(.clockWipe)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
Badge()
    .transition(.clockWipe)
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called ClockWipeTransition, exposed as .clockWipe. Mask the content with an animatable Shape whose animatableData is progress (0…1): it returns the full rect at 1, an empty path at 0, and otherwise a pie wedge from the centre with radius equal to the rect's diagonal, from −90° to −90° + 360° × progress (clockwise: false, which sweeps clockwise on screen in SwiftUI's y-down space). Pass progress 1 when phase.isIdentity and 0 otherwise, so the animation interpolates the angle. It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that reveal or hide a view through an animated mask. Masks
// don't move the content, so they need no Reduce Motion fallback.

// MARK: - Iris

/// A circle that opens from a point to reveal the view, and closes back to
/// it on removal, like a camera iris.
public struct IrisTransition: Transition {
    public var origin: UnitPoint

    public init(origin: UnitPoint = .center) {
        self.origin = origin
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let size = geometry.size
                let o = CGPoint(x: size.width * origin.x, y: size.height * origin.y)
                // Far enough to cover the corner furthest from the origin.
                let radius = [CGPoint.zero, CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 0), CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height), CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height)]
                    .map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }
                    .max() ?? 0
                Circle()
                    .frame(width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
                    .position(o)
                    .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == IrisTransition {
    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from its centre.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showPhoto {
    ///     PhotoView().transition(.iris)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var iris: IrisTransition { IrisTransition() }

    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from `origin`.
    static func iris(origin: UnitPoint) -> IrisTransition { IrisTransition(origin: origin) }
}

// MARK: - Blinds

/// Horizontal slats that open together, like Venetian blinds.
public struct BlindsTransition: Transition {
    public var slats: Int

    public init(slats: Int = 8) {
        self.slats = max(1, slats)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {

                ForEach(0..<slats, id: \.self) { _ in

                }
            }
        }
    }
}

    /// Reveals the view through opening blinds.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Banner().transition(.blinds)
    /// ```
    static var blinds: BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition() }

    /// Reveals the view through `slats` opening blinds.
    static func blinds(slats: Int) -> BlindsTransition { BlindsTransition(slats: slats) }
}

            ClockWipeShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)

## Pixel Dissolve (`dissolve`)

The view appears and vanishes in square pixels, in random order.

- API: `.transition(.dissolve)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/MaskTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
Avatar()
    .transition(.dissolve)

Artwork()
    .transition(.dissolve(cellSize: 6))
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called DissolveTransition with a cellSize (10 pt), exposed as .dissolve and .dissolve(cellSize:). Mask the content with an animatable Shape whose animatableData is progress (0…1): divide the rect into a grid of cellSize squares, give each cell a stable pseudo-random threshold in 0…1 from an integer hash of (column, row), and add the cells whose threshold is below progress (outset by 0.25 pt so neighbours don't leave seams); return the full rect at 1 and an empty path at 0. Pass progress 1 when phase.isIdentity and 0 otherwise. It only masks, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that reveal or hide a view through an animated mask. Masks
// don't move the content, so they need no Reduce Motion fallback.

// MARK: - Iris

/// A circle that opens from a point to reveal the view, and closes back to
/// it on removal, like a camera iris.
public struct IrisTransition: Transition {
    public var origin: UnitPoint

    public init(origin: UnitPoint = .center) {
        self.origin = origin
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.mask {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                let size = geometry.size
                let o = CGPoint(x: size.width * origin.x, y: size.height * origin.y)
                // Far enough to cover the corner furthest from the origin.
                let radius = [CGPoint.zero, CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 0), CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height), CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height)]
                    .map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }
                    .max() ?? 0
                Circle()
                    .frame(width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2)
                    .position(o)
                    .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.001, anchor: origin)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == IrisTransition {
    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from its centre.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showPhoto {
    ///     PhotoView().transition(.iris)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var iris: IrisTransition { IrisTransition() }

    /// Opens the view in a growing circle from `origin`.
    static func iris(origin: UnitPoint) -> IrisTransition { IrisTransition(origin: origin) }
}

    public var slats: Int

    public init(slats: Int = 8) {
        self.slats = max(1, slats)

    /// ```

            ClockWipeShape(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)

## Poof (`poof`)

The view puffs away like smoke: it swells and blurs out.

- API: `.transition(.poof)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/StyleTransitions.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/StyleTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
ForEach(notes) { note in
    NoteRow(note)
        .transition(.poof)
}
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called PoofTransition, exposed as .poof. Return a small view that reads Reduce Motion and applies: scale 1.35 when phase == .didDisappear, 0.7 when .willAppear, 1 at identity; blur radius 14 when not identity, 0 at identity; opacity 0 when not identity. Removal swells and blurs away like smoke, insertion condenses in from a smaller blur. With Reduce Motion on, keep the scale at 1 (blur and fade only).

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that change how the view itself looks (scale, blur, skew,
// exposure) on its way in and out.

// MARK: - Poof

/// The view puffs away like smoke: it swells and blurs out on removal, and
/// condenses from a blur on insertion.
public struct PoofTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        PoofBody(content: content, phase: phase)
    }
}

private struct PoofBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: blur and fade only, no scaling.
        let scale: CGFloat = reduceMotion ? 1 : phase == .didDisappear ? 1.35 : phase == .willAppear ? 0.7 : 1
        content
            .scaleEffect(scale)
            .blur(radius: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 14)
            .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == PoofTransition {
    /// Puffs the view away like smoke (and condenses it back in).
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ForEach(notes) { note in
    ///     NoteRow(note).transition(.poof)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var poof: PoofTransition { PoofTransition() }
}

// MARK: - Swoosh

/// The view whooshes in from the leading edge leaning forward, and out to
/// the trailing edge, with a motion blur.
public struct SwooshTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        SwooshBody(content: content, phase: phase)
    }
}

private struct SwooshBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // TransitionPhase.value is -1 before insertion, 0 at rest and 1 after removal.
        let value = CGFloat(phase.value)
        content
            // Reduce Motion: fade only.
            .modifier(SkewSlide(progress: reduceMotion ? 0 : value))
            .blur(radius: abs(value) * 6)
            .opacity(1 - abs(Double(value)))
    }
}

/// Slides the view by `progress` × its width while skewing it in the
/// direction of travel.
struct SkewSlide: GeometryEffect {
    var progress: CGFloat

    var animatableData: CGFloat {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func effectValue(size: CGSize) -> ProjectionTransform {
        let skew = -progress * 0.6
        // Skew around the vertical centre so the view doesn't drift sideways.
        let transform = CGAffineTransform(a: 1, b: 0, c: skew, d: 1, tx: progress * size.width - skew * size.height / 2, ty: 0)
        return ProjectionTransform(transform)
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == SwooshTransition {
    /// Whooshes the view in from the leading edge and out to the trailing edge.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Toast().transition(.swoosh)
    /// ```
    static var swoosh: SwooshTransition { SwooshTransition() }
}

// MARK: - Film exposure

/// The view develops like a photo: it starts blown out to white and
/// colourless, then the exposure and colour settle in.
public struct FilmExposureTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content
            .brightness(phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 0.9)
            .saturation(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
            .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == FilmExposureTransition {
    /// Develops the view from an over-exposed white, like a photo.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// AsyncImage(url: url) { image in
    ///     image.resizable().transition(.filmExposure)
    /// } placeholder: { ProgressView() }
    /// ```
    static var filmExposure: FilmExposureTransition { FilmExposureTransition() }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                HStack(spacing: 12) {
                    ForEach(0..<3, id: \.self) { index in
                        ZStack {
                            if shown {
                                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                                    .fill(Color.orange.gradient)
                                    .transition(index == 0 ? AnyTransition(.poof) : index == 1 ? AnyTransition(.swoosh) : AnyTransition(.filmExposure))
                            }
                        }
                        .frame(width: 70, height: 70)
                    }
                }
                Button("Toggle") { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.6)) { shown.toggle() } }
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}
```

## Swoosh (`swoosh`)

The view whooshes in leaning forward, with a motion blur.

- API: `.transition(.swoosh)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/StyleTransitions.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/StyleTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
if let toast {
    ToastView(toast)
        .transition(.swoosh)
}
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called SwooshTransition, exposed as .swoosh. Use phase.value (−1 before insertion, 0 at rest, +1 after removal) as v and apply a GeometryEffect whose animatableData is v: a CGAffineTransform with c = −0.6 v (a horizontal skew) and tx = v × width − c × height / 2 (slide by the view's own width, skewing around the vertical centre). Add blur 6 × |v| and opacity 1 − |v|, so it whooshes in from the leading edge leaning into the motion and leaves to the trailing edge. With Reduce Motion on, skip the slide and skew (fade only).

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that change how the view itself looks (scale, blur, skew,
// exposure) on its way in and out.

// MARK: - Poof

/// The view puffs away like smoke: it swells and blurs out on removal, and
/// condenses from a blur on insertion.
public struct PoofTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        PoofBody(content: content, phase: phase)
    }
}

private struct PoofBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: blur and fade only, no scaling.
        let scale: CGFloat = reduceMotion ? 1 : phase == .didDisappear ? 1.35 : phase == .willAppear ? 0.7 : 1
        content
            .scaleEffect(scale)
            .blur(radius: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 14)
            .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == PoofTransition {
    /// Puffs the view away like smoke (and condenses it back in).
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ForEach(notes) { note in
    ///     NoteRow(note).transition(.poof)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var poof: PoofTransition { PoofTransition() }
}

// MARK: - Swoosh

/// The view whooshes in from the leading edge leaning forward, and out to
/// the trailing edge, with a motion blur.
public struct SwooshTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        SwooshBody(content: content, phase: phase)
    }
}

private struct SwooshBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // TransitionPhase.value is -1 before insertion, 0 at rest and 1 after removal.
        let value = CGFloat(phase.value)
        content
            // Reduce Motion: fade only.
            .modifier(SkewSlide(progress: reduceMotion ? 0 : value))
            .blur(radius: abs(value) * 6)
            .opacity(1 - abs(Double(value)))
    }
}

/// Slides the view by `progress` × its width while skewing it in the
/// direction of travel.
struct SkewSlide: GeometryEffect {
    var progress: CGFloat

    var animatableData: CGFloat {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func effectValue(size: CGSize) -> ProjectionTransform {
        let skew = -progress * 0.6
        // Skew around the vertical centre so the view doesn't drift sideways.
        let transform = CGAffineTransform(a: 1, b: 0, c: skew, d: 1, tx: progress * size.width - skew * size.height / 2, ty: 0)
        return ProjectionTransform(transform)
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == SwooshTransition {
    /// Whooshes the view in from the leading edge and out to the trailing edge.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Toast().transition(.swoosh)
    /// ```
    static var swoosh: SwooshTransition { SwooshTransition() }
}

// MARK: - Film exposure

/// The view develops like a photo: it starts blown out to white and
/// colourless, then the exposure and colour settle in.
public struct FilmExposureTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content
            .brightness(phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 0.9)
            .saturation(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
            .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == FilmExposureTransition {
    /// Develops the view from an over-exposed white, like a photo.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// AsyncImage(url: url) { image in
    ///     image.resizable().transition(.filmExposure)
    /// } placeholder: { ProgressView() }
    /// ```
    static var filmExposure: FilmExposureTransition { FilmExposureTransition() }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                HStack(spacing: 12) {
                    ForEach(0..<3, id: \.self) { index in
                        ZStack {
                            if shown {
                                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                                    .fill(Color.orange.gradient)
                                    .transition(index == 0 ? AnyTransition(.poof) : index == 1 ? AnyTransition(.swoosh) : AnyTransition(.filmExposure))
                            }
                        }
                        .frame(width: 70, height: 70)
                    }
                }
                Button("Toggle") { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.6)) { shown.toggle() } }
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo().padding()
}

## Film Exposure (`film-exposure`)

The view develops like a photo, from over-exposed white to full colour.

- API: `.transition(.filmExposure)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Appear
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/StyleTransitions.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/StyleTransitions.swift

### Usage

```swift
AsyncImage(url: url) { image in
    image.resizable()
        .transition(.filmExposure)
} placeholder: {
    ProgressView()
}
```

### How it works

Create a custom SwiftUI Transition (iOS 17+) called FilmExposureTransition, exposed as .filmExposure. When the phase isn't identity, apply brightness 0.9, saturation 0 and opacity 0; at identity, brightness 0, saturation 1 and opacity 1. Inserting the view develops it like a photo, from blown-out colourless white to full colour, and removing it fades it back out to white. Nothing moves, so it needs no Reduce Motion fallback.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

// Transitions that change how the view itself looks (scale, blur, skew,
// exposure) on its way in and out.

// MARK: - Poof

/// The view puffs away like smoke: it swells and blurs out on removal, and
/// condenses from a blur on insertion.
public struct PoofTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        PoofBody(content: content, phase: phase)
    }
}

private struct PoofBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // Reduce Motion: blur and fade only, no scaling.
        let scale: CGFloat = reduceMotion ? 1 : phase == .didDisappear ? 1.35 : phase == .willAppear ? 0.7 : 1
        content
            .scaleEffect(scale)
            .blur(radius: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 14)
            .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == PoofTransition {
    /// Puffs the view away like smoke (and condenses it back in).
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ForEach(notes) { note in
    ///     NoteRow(note).transition(.poof)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var poof: PoofTransition { PoofTransition() }
}

// MARK: - Swoosh

/// The view whooshes in from the leading edge leaning forward, and out to
/// the trailing edge, with a motion blur.
public struct SwooshTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        SwooshBody(content: content, phase: phase)
    }
}

    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        // TransitionPhase.value is -1 before insertion, 0 at rest and 1 after removal.
        let value = CGFloat(phase.value)
        content
            // Reduce Motion: fade only.
            .modifier(SkewSlide(progress: reduceMotion ? 0 : value))
            .blur(radius: abs(value) * 6)
            .opacity(1 - abs(Double(value)))
    }
}

/// Slides the view by `progress` × its width while skewing it in the
/// direction of travel.
struct SkewSlide: GeometryEffect {
    var progress: CGFloat

    var animatableData: CGFloat {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func effectValue(size: CGSize) -> ProjectionTransform {
        let skew = -progress * 0.6
        // Skew around the vertical centre so the view doesn't drift sideways.
        let transform = CGAffineTransform(a: 1, b: 0, c: skew, d: 1, tx: progress * size.width - skew * size.height / 2, ty: 0)
        return ProjectionTransform(transform)

    /// ```swift
    /// Toast().transition(.swoosh)
    /// ```

}

/// colourless, then the exposure and colour settle in.

        content
            .brightness(phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 0.9)
            .saturation(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
            .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

    /// Develops the view from an over-exposed white, like a photo.
