## Circular Reveal (`circular-reveal`)

New content spreads out in a circle from where you tapped.

- API: `CircularReveal(value:) { value in }`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/CircularReveal.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/CircularReveal.swift

### Usage

```swift
CircularReveal(value: isDark, origin: tapPoint) { dark in
    ThemePreview(dark: dark)
}
```

### How it works

Create a generic SwiftUI CircularReveal(value:origin:duration:content:) view (iOS 17+) where origin is a UnitPoint. Keep @State shown (initially value), incoming (optional) and progress. When value changes: if a reveal is in flight, commit it; set incoming = new and progress = 0 without animation, then animate progress to 1 with .easeInOut(0.7 s) and, on completion, set shown = new and incoming = nil without animation. Render ZStack { content(shown); content(incoming) masked by an animatable circle Shape centred at origin whose radius is progress × the distance to the furthest corner }, with hit testing off on the incoming layer. To start at a tap, convert the location with UnitPoint(x: x / width, y: y / height). With Reduce Motion on, cross-fade the incoming layer instead of growing the circle.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Swaps content with a circle that grows from a point (typically where the
/// user tapped) until it covers everything, like switching to dark mode by
/// "painting" it in. The old content stays underneath until it's covered.
public struct CircularReveal<Value: Equatable, Content: View>: View {
    private let value: Value
    private let origin: UnitPoint
    private let duration: Double
    private let content: (Value) -> Content

    @State private var shown: Value
    @State private var incoming: Value?
    @State private var progress: Double = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - value: Whenever it changes, the content for the new value is revealed.
    ///   - origin: Where the circle starts, in unit coordinates. Convert a tap
    ///     location with `UnitPoint(x: x / width, y: y / height)`.
    ///   - duration: Seconds for the circle to cover the view.
    ///   - content: Builds the content for a value.
    public init(value: Value, origin: UnitPoint = .center, duration: Double = 0.7, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Value) -> Content) {
        self.value = value
        self.origin = origin
        self.duration = duration
        self.content = content
        _shown = State(initialValue: value)
    }

    public var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            content(shown)
            if let incoming {
                content(incoming)
                    .mask {
                        RevealCircle(progress: reduceMotion ? 1 : progress, origin: origin)
                    }
                    .opacity(reduceMotion ? progress : 1)
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
            }
        }
        .onChange(of: value) { _, new in reveal(new) }
    }

    private func reveal(_ new: Value) {
        // A reveal in flight finishes instantly so the next one starts clean.
        if let current = incoming { shown = current }
        var reset = Transaction()
        reset.disablesAnimations = true
        withTransaction(reset) {
            incoming = new
            progress = 0
        }
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.3) : .easeInOut(duration: duration)) {
            progress = 1
        } completion: {
            guard incoming == new else { return }
            var settle = Transaction()
            settle.disablesAnimations = true
            withTransaction(settle) {
                shown = new
                incoming = nil
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A circle around `origin` whose radius reaches the furthest corner at 1.
struct RevealCircle: Shape {
    var progress: Double
    var origin: UnitPoint

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let o = CGPoint(x: rect.minX + rect.width * origin.x, y: rect.minY + rect.height * origin.y)
        let corners = [CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.minY), CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.minY), CGPoint(x: rect.minX, y: rect.maxY), CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.maxY)]
        let reach = corners.map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }.max() ?? 0
        let r = reach * progress
        return Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: o.x - r, y: o.y - r, width: r * 2, height: r * 2))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var dark = false
        @State private var origin = UnitPoint.center
        var body: some View {
            GeometryReader { geometry in
                CircularReveal(value: dark, origin: origin) { isDark in
                    ZStack {
                        isDark ? Color.black : Color.white
                        Image(systemName: isDark ? "moon.stars.fill" : "sun.max.fill")
                            .font(.system(size: 60))
                            .foregroundStyle(isDark ? .yellow : .orange)
                    }
                }
                .onTapGesture { location in
                    origin = UnitPoint(x: location.x / geometry.size.width, y: location.y / geometry.size.height)
                    dark.toggle()
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

---

## Liquid Swipe (`liquid-swipe`)

The next page pours in from the edge behind a bulging liquid wave.

- API: `.transition(.liquidSwipe)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/LiquidSwipe.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/LiquidSwipe.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    OnboardingPage(page)
        .id(page)
        .transition(.liquidSwipe)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI LiquidSwipeTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with a .liquidSwipe accessor. Mask the content with an animatable Shape whose progress is 0 on willAppear and 1 otherwise: at progress p it covers the view from the trailing edge to edge = maxX − (width + a) × p, where the bulge a = 0.35 × width × sin(πp); the leading boundary is straight except for a wave from midY − 0.45h to midY + 0.45h drawn with two cubic curves that bulge out to edge − a at midY. Darken the outgoing view with brightness −0.15 and give the incoming view zIndex 1 so it draws on top. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View and use no bulge.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The incoming view pours in from the trailing edge behind a liquid wave
/// with a bulge in the middle, covering the outgoing view, which darkens
/// slightly as it disappears. Great for onboarding pages.
public struct LiquidSwipeTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        LiquidSwipeBody(content: content, phase: phase)
    }
}

private struct LiquidSwipeBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        content
            .mask {
                LiquidEdge(progress: phase == .willAppear ? 0 : 1, bulge: reduceMotion ? 0 : 1)
            }
            .brightness(phase == .didDisappear ? -0.15 : 0)
            // The incoming page always draws on top of the outgoing one.
            .zIndex(phase == .didDisappear ? 0 : 1)
    }
}

/// Covers the view from the trailing edge; the leading edge of the covered
/// area is a wave whose bulge peaks halfway through.
struct LiquidEdge: Shape {
    var progress: Double
    var bulge: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        guard progress < 1 else { return Path(rect) }
        var path = Path()
        guard progress > 0 else { return path }
        let p = CGFloat(progress)
        let amplitude = rect.width * 0.35 * CGFloat(sin(progress * .pi) * bulge)
        // The straight part of the edge, pushed far enough left that the
        // bulge has fully left the view by the end.
        let edge = rect.maxX - (rect.width + amplitude) * p
        let midY = rect.midY
        let reach = rect.height * 0.45
        path.move(to: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.minY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: edge, y: rect.minY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: edge, y: midY - reach))
        path.addCurve(
            to: CGPoint(x: edge - amplitude, y: midY),
            control1: CGPoint(x: edge, y: midY - reach * 0.45),
            control2: CGPoint(x: edge - amplitude, y: midY - reach * 0.5)
        )
        path.addCurve(
            to: CGPoint(x: edge, y: midY + reach),
            control1: CGPoint(x: edge - amplitude, y: midY + reach * 0.5),
            control2: CGPoint(x: edge, y: midY + reach * 0.45)
        )
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: edge, y: rect.maxY))
        path.addLine(to: CGPoint(x: rect.maxX, y: rect.maxY))
        path.closeSubpath()
        return path
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == LiquidSwipeTransition {
    /// Pours the new view in from the trailing edge behind a liquid wave.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ZStack {
    ///     OnboardingPage(page)
    ///         .id(page)
    ///         .transition(.liquidSwipe)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var liquidSwipe: LiquidSwipeTransition { LiquidSwipeTransition() }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var page = 0
        let colors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .teal, .indigo]
        var body: some View {
            ZStack {
                colors[page]
                    .overlay(Text("Page \(page + 1)").font(.largeTitle.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
                    .id(page)
                    .transition(.liquidSwipe)
            }
            .frame(width: 260, height: 360)
            .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 24))
            .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.9)) { page = (page + 1) % colors.count } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

---

## Page Turn (`page-turn`)

The old page swings away like a book page, revealing the next one.

- API: `.transition(.pageTurn)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/PageTurn.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/PageTurn.swift

### Usage

```swift
ZStack {
    ChapterView(chapter)
        .id(chapter)
        .transition(.pageTurn)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI PageTurnTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with a .pageTurn accessor. The outgoing view gets zIndex 1 and an Animatable ViewModifier with progress 0 → 1: rotation3DEffect(−90° × p, axis y, anchor .leading, perspective 0.6), an overlay LinearGradient from clear to black at 45 % × p (leading → trailing) so the free edge darkens as it turns, a shadow of opacity 0.3 × sin(πp), radius 12, x 6, and opacity 0 at the very end. The incoming view sits underneath and brightens from −0.25 to 0. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View and simply fade the page out.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Like turning a page in a book: the outgoing view swings away around its
/// leading edge in 3D, shading as it turns, and reveals the incoming view
/// underneath, which brightens up from the page's shadow.
public struct PageTurnTransition: Transition {
    public init() {}

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        PageTurnBody(content: content, phase: phase)
    }
}

private struct PageTurnBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        content
            .modifier(PageTurnEffect(progress: phase == .didDisappear ? 1 : 0, reduceMotion: reduceMotion))
            .brightness(phase == .willAppear ? -0.25 : 0)
            // The turning page is on top of the one it reveals.
            .zIndex(phase == .didDisappear ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

struct PageTurnEffect: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var progress: Double
    var reduceMotion: Bool

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            // Reduce Motion: fade the page away.
            content.opacity(1 - progress)
        } else {
            content
                .overlay {
                    // The page darkens towards its free edge as it turns.
                    LinearGradient(colors: [.black.opacity(0), .black.opacity(0.45 * progress)], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
                        .allowsHitTesting(false)
                }
                .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(-90 * progress), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), anchor: .leading, perspective: 0.6)
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.3 * sin(progress * .pi)), radius: 12, x: 6)
                .opacity(progress > 0.98 ? 0 : 1)
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == PageTurnTransition {
    /// Turns the old view away like a book page, revealing the new one.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// ZStack {
    ///     ChapterView(chapter)
    ///         .id(chapter)
    ///         .transition(.pageTurn)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var pageTurn: PageTurnTransition { PageTurnTransition() }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var page = 0
        let colors: [Color] = [.orange, .teal, .indigo]
        var body: some View {
            ZStack {
                RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                    .fill(colors[page].gradient)
                    .overlay(Text("Chapter \(page + 1)").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
                    .id(page)
                    .transition(.pageTurn)
            }
            .frame(width: 220, height: 300)
            .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.9)) { page = (page + 1) % colors.count } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Glitch Transition (`glitch-transition`)

The view breaks up like a bad signal on its way in or out.

- API: `.transition(.glitch)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/GlitchTransition.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/GlitchTransition.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/GlitchSlice.swift

### Usage

```swift
if showAlert {
    AlertBanner()
        .transition(.glitch)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI GlitchTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with .glitch and .glitch(slices:) accessors that applies an Animatable ViewModifier with amount 0 (identity) → 1 (inserted or removed). At 0 render the content as is. Otherwise, with frame = Int(amount × 16) so the pattern changes in steps: stack a red copy (colorMultiply(.red), offset x −amount × 10, 60 %), a cyan copy (offset +amount × 10, 60 %) and 7 horizontal slices of the content, each masked to its band and offset sideways by (random(slice, frame) − 0.5) × 60 × amount; composite them and set opacity to 1 − 0.6 × amount, or 0.15 when random(frame) ≤ 0.9 × amount, reaching 0 at the end. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View and fade instead.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The view breaks up like a bad signal on its way in or out: horizontal
/// slices jump sideways, red and cyan copies split apart, and it flickers in
/// steps rather than fading smoothly.
public struct GlitchTransition: Transition {
    public var slices: Int

    /// - Parameter slices: Number of horizontal slices that jump around.
    public init(slices: Int = 7) {
        self.slices = max(1, slices)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        GlitchTransitionBody(content: content, phase: phase, slices: slices)
    }
}

private struct GlitchTransitionBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase
    let slices: Int

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            // Reduce Motion: a plain fade.
            content.opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
        } else {
            content.modifier(GlitchEffect(amount: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 1, slices: slices))
        }
    }
}

struct GlitchEffect: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    /// 0 = intact, 1 = gone.
    var amount: Double
    var slices: Int

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { amount }
        set { amount = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        if amount <= 0.001 {
            content
        } else {
            // The glitch pattern changes in discrete "frames", not smoothly.
            let frame = Int(amount * 16)
            let split = CGFloat(amount) * 10
            // Stepped flicker on the way out.
            let visible = Self.random(frame, 99) > amount * 0.9 ? 1 - amount * 0.6 : 0.15
            ZStack {
                content
                    .colorMultiply(.red)
                    .offset(x: -split)
                    .opacity(0.6)
                content
                    .colorMultiply(.cyan)
                    .offset(x: split)
                    .opacity(0.6)
                ForEach(0..<slices, id: \.self) { slice in
                    content
                        .mask(GlitchSlice(index: slice, count: slices))
                        .offset(x: CGFloat(Self.random(slice, frame) - 0.5) * 60 * CGFloat(amount))
                }
            }
            .compositingGroup()
            .opacity(amount >= 0.999 ? 0 : visible)
            .allowsHitTesting(false)
        }
    }

    static func random(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 73_856_093 ^ b &* 19_349_663)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == GlitchTransition {
    /// Glitches the view in and out like a broken signal.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showAlert {
    ///     AlertBanner().transition(.glitch)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var glitch: GlitchTransition { GlitchTransition() }

    /// Glitches the view in and out with `slices` jumping bands.
    static func glitch(slices: Int) -> GlitchTransition { GlitchTransition(slices: slices) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            ZStack {
                if shown {
                    Text("SIGNAL")
                        .font(.system(size: 40, weight: .black, design: .monospaced))
                        .padding()
                        .background(Color.black, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12))
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .transition(.glitch)
                }
            }
            .frame(width: 280, height: 160)
            .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.linear(duration: 0.6)) { shown.toggle() } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - GlitchSlice.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

// Shared by GlitchTransition and OrigamiFold.

import SwiftUI

/// One horizontal band of the view.
struct GlitchSlice: Shape {
    var index: Int
    var count: Int

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let height = rect.height / CGFloat(count)
        return Path(CGRect(x: rect.minX - rect.width, y: rect.minY + CGFloat(index) * height, width: rect.width * 3, height: height + 0.5))
    }
}
```

## Origami Fold (`origami`)

The view folds up into creased panels like a paper map.

- API: `.transition(.origami)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/OrigamiFold.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/OrigamiFold.swift, Sources/MotionLibrary/Support/GlitchSlice.swift

### Usage

```swift
if showTicket {
    TicketView()
        .transition(.origami)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI OrigamiTransition (iOS 17+, Transition) with .origami and .origami(folds:) accessors applying an Animatable ViewModifier with progress 0 (flat) → 1 (folded). At 0 render the content. Otherwise keep the footprint with content.hidden() and, in a top-aligned overlay GeometryReader, draw 4 copies of the content, each masked to its horizontal panel. With angle = 90° × p and c = cos(angle): even panels hinge on their top edge (rotation3DEffect +angle about x, anchor at y = i / n), odd panels on their bottom edge (−angle, anchor (i + 1) / n), and each is offset by hinge × panelHeight × (c − 1) so it starts where the previous one ends, collapsing like an accordion towards the top. Shade panels with black at (0.1 even, 0.4 odd) × (1 − c), perspective 0.4, and fade out over the last 15 %. Read Reduce Motion in an inner View and fade instead.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The view folds up like a paper map: it's split into horizontal panels
/// that crease in alternating directions and collapse towards the top, with
/// the panels facing away shaded darker. Insertion unfolds it again.
public struct OrigamiTransition: Transition {
    public var folds: Int

    /// - Parameter folds: Number of panels (2…8 looks right).
    public init(folds: Int = 4) {
        self.folds = max(2, folds)
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        OrigamiBody(content: content, phase: phase, folds: folds)
    }
}

private struct OrigamiBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase
    let folds: Int

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            // Reduce Motion: a plain fade.
            content.opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
        } else {
            content.modifier(OrigamiEffect(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 1, folds: folds))
        }
    }
}

struct OrigamiEffect: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    /// 0 = flat, 1 = folded away.
    var progress: Double
    var folds: Int

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        if progress <= 0.001 {
            content
        } else {
            // Keep the original footprint while panels are drawn on top.
            content
                .hidden()
                .overlay(alignment: .top) {
                    GeometryReader { geometry in
                        let panel = geometry.size.height / CGFloat(folds)
                        let angle = 90 * min(progress, 0.999)
                        let c = CGFloat(cos(angle * .pi / 180))
                        ZStack(alignment: .top) {
                            ForEach(0..<folds, id: \.self) { index in
                                let even = index.isMultiple(of: 2)
                                // Even panels hinge on their top edge, odd ones on their bottom edge,
                                // and each is moved up so it starts where the previous one ends.
                                let hinge = CGFloat(even ? index : index + 1)
                                let shift = hinge * panel * (c - 1)
                                content
                                    .frame(width: geometry.size.width, height: geometry.size.height)
                                    .mask(GlitchSlice(index: index, count: folds))
                                    .overlay {
                                        Color.black
                                            .opacity((even ? 0.1 : 0.4) * (1 - Double(c)))
                                            .mask(GlitchSlice(index: index, count: folds))
                                            .allowsHitTesting(false)
                                    }
                                    .rotation3DEffect(
                                        .degrees(even ? angle : -angle),
                                        axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0),
                                        anchor: UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: hinge / CGFloat(folds)),
                                        perspective: 0.4
                                    )
                                    .offset(y: shift)
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                .opacity(progress > 0.85 ? (1 - progress) / 0.15 : 1)
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
        }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == OrigamiTransition {
    /// Folds the view up like a paper map (and unfolds it on insertion).
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showTicket {
    ///     TicketView().transition(.origami)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var origami: OrigamiTransition { OrigamiTransition() }

    /// Folds the view into `folds` panels.
    static func origami(folds: Int) -> OrigamiTransition { OrigamiTransition(folds: folds) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            ZStack(alignment: .top) {
                if shown {
                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12)
                        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
                        .frame(width: 200, height: 240)
                        .transition(.origami)
                }
            }
            .frame(width: 280, height: 300)
            .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.9)) { shown.toggle() } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - GlitchSlice.swift
// Needed by this effect: save it as its own file next to the one above.

// Shared by GlitchTransition and OrigamiFold.

import SwiftUI

/// One horizontal band of the view.
struct GlitchSlice: Shape {
    var index: Int
    var count: Int

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let height = rect.height / CGFloat(count)
        return Path(CGRect(x: rect.minX - rect.width, y: rect.minY + CGFloat(index) * height, width: rect.width * 3, height: height + 0.5))
    }
}
```

## Ink Bleed (`ink-bleed`)

New content spreads in like a blot of ink on wet paper, with a ragged edge.

- API: `.transition(.inkBleed)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/InkBleed.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/InkBleed.swift

### Usage

```swift
if showsDetail {
    DetailCard()
        .transition(.inkBleed(from: .topLeading))
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Transition .inkBleed / .inkBleed(from: UnitPoint) (iOS 17+) that masks the content with an Animatable blot view whose progress is 1 when the phase is identity and 0 otherwise. The blot is a Canvas with .alphaThreshold(min: 0.5) and a blur of max(2, 0.06r), drawing into a layer: a circle of radius 0.82r at the origin plus 26 circles around it, at angle i / 26 × 2π + hashed jitter, distance r × (0.62–0.92) and radius r × (0.12–0.32). r = (1.25 × distance to the furthest corner + 30) × progress, so blurring then thresholding melts them into one ragged blot that clears the corners at 1. With Reduce Motion on, fade instead.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Reveals the view like ink dropped on wet paper: a blot spreads from a
/// point with a blotchy, organic edge until it covers everything.
public struct InkBleedTransition: Transition {
    public var origin: UnitPoint

    public init(origin: UnitPoint = .center) {
        self.origin = origin
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        InkBleedBody(content: content, progress: phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0, origin: origin)
    }
}

private struct InkBleedBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let progress: Double
    let origin: UnitPoint

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            content.opacity(progress)
        } else {
            content.mask { InkBlot(progress: progress, origin: origin) }
        }
    }
}

/// The blot: a circle ringed by smaller circles, merged into one ragged
/// shape by blurring and thresholding the alpha.
struct InkBlot: View, Animatable {
    var progress: Double
    var origin: UnitPoint

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    var body: some View {
        Canvas { context, size in
            let o = CGPoint(x: size.width * origin.x, y: size.height * origin.y)
            let corners = [CGPoint.zero, CGPoint(x: size.width, y: 0), CGPoint(x: 0, y: size.height), CGPoint(x: size.width, y: size.height)]
            let reach = corners.map { hypot($0.x - o.x, $0.y - o.y) }.max() ?? 0
            // Overshoot so the ragged edge clears the corners at 1.
            let r = (reach * 1.25 + 30) * progress
            guard r > 0.5 else { return }
            context.addFilter(.alphaThreshold(min: 0.5))
            context.addFilter(.blur(radius: max(2, r * 0.06)))
            context.drawLayer { layer in
                layer.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: o.x - r * 0.82, y: o.y - r * 0.82, width: r * 1.64, height: r * 1.64)), with: .color(.black))
                for index in 0..<26 {
                    let angle = Double(index) / 26 * 2 * .pi + Self.hash(index, 1) * 0.4
                    let distance = r * (0.62 + 0.3 * Self.hash(index, 2))
                    let blob = r * (0.12 + 0.2 * Self.hash(index, 3))
                    let c = CGPoint(x: o.x + cos(angle) * distance, y: o.y + sin(angle) * distance)
                    layer.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: c.x - blob, y: c.y - blob, width: blob * 2, height: blob * 2)), with: .color(.black))
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private static func hash(_ a: Int, _ b: Int) -> Double {
        var x = UInt64(truncatingIfNeeded: a &* 73_856_093 ^ b &* 19_349_663 &+ 0x1A4B)
        x = (x ^ (x >> 33)) &* 0xff51_afd7_ed55_8ccd
        x ^= x >> 33
        return Double(x % 10_000) / 10_000
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == InkBleedTransition {
    /// Spreads the view in (and out) like a blot of ink on wet paper.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if showsDetail {
    ///     DetailCard().transition(.inkBleed)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var inkBleed: InkBleedTransition { InkBleedTransition() }

    /// Spreads the view in from `origin` like a blot of ink.
    static func inkBleed(from origin: UnitPoint) -> InkBleedTransition { InkBleedTransition(origin: origin) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            ZStack {
                Color(white: 0.95)
                if shown {
                    LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                        .overlay(Text("Ink").font(.largeTitle.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
                        .transition(.inkBleed(from: .topLeading))
                }
            }
            .frame(width: 280, height: 180)
            .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16))
            .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 1.1)) { shown.toggle() } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Zoom Blur (`zoom-blur`)

Content rushes in from the camera, blurred and trailed by echoes, then snaps sharp.

- API: `.transition(.zoomBlur)`
- Component: Transition
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/ZoomBlur.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionLibrary/Transition/ZoomBlur.swift

### Usage

```swift
Text(title)
    .id(title)
    .transition(.zoomBlur)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI Transition .zoomBlur / .zoomBlur(scale:) (iOS 17+). In an Animatable modifier with amount 0 (in place) … 1 (away), scale the content to 1 + (scale − 1) × amount (scale 1.6), blur it by 14 × amount and fade it to 1 − amount. While 0 < amount < 1, add three echo copies behind it, each a little larger (+ 0.12 × step × amount), blurrier (6 + 6 × step × amount) and fainter ((1 − amount) × 0.28 / step), as a cheap radial zoom blur. The phase maps identity to 0 and both insertion and removal to 1, so it rushes in from the camera and out past it. With Reduce Motion on, fade instead.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Rushes the view in from the camera with a zoom blur: it arrives large and
/// out of focus, trailed by fading echoes, and snaps sharp as it lands. On
/// removal it flies past the viewer the same way.
public struct ZoomBlurTransition: Transition {
    public var scale: CGFloat

    public init(scale: CGFloat = 1.6) {
        self.scale = scale
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        ZoomBlurBody(content: content, phase: phase, scale: scale)
    }
}

private struct ZoomBlurBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase
    let scale: CGFloat

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        let away = phase.isIdentity ? 0.0 : 1.0
        if reduceMotion {
            content.opacity(1 - away)
        } else {
            content.modifier(ZoomBlurEffect(amount: away, scale: scale, content: content))
        }
    }
}

/// The look at `amount` 0 (in place) to 1 (fully zoomed away). The echoes
/// are fainter, larger copies, a cheap stand-in for a radial blur.
private struct ZoomBlurEffect<Echo: View>: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var amount: Double
    var scale: CGFloat
    let content: Echo

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { amount }
        set { amount = newValue }
    }

    func body(content view: Content) -> some View {
        let a = CGFloat(amount)
        view
            .scaleEffect(1 + (scale - 1) * a)
            .blur(radius: 14 * a)
            .opacity(1 - amount)
            .background {
                if amount > 0.01 && amount < 0.99 {
                    ZStack {
                        ForEach(1...3, id: \.self) { step in
                            content
                                .scaleEffect(1 + (scale - 1) * a + CGFloat(step) * 0.12 * a)
                                .blur(radius: 6 + 6 * CGFloat(step) * a)
                                .opacity((1 - amount) * 0.28 / Double(step))
                        }
                    }
                    .allowsHitTesting(false)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == ZoomBlurTransition {
    /// Zooms the view in from the camera, blurred and trailed by echoes,
    /// and out past the viewer on removal.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if let photo = selected {
    ///     PhotoView(photo).transition(.zoomBlur)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var zoomBlur: ZoomBlurTransition { ZoomBlurTransition() }

    /// Zooms the view in from `scale` times its size.
    static func zoomBlur(scale: CGFloat) -> ZoomBlurTransition { ZoomBlurTransition(scale: scale) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var shown = true
        var body: some View {
            ZStack {
                if shown {
                    Text("WARP")
                        .font(.system(size: 54, weight: .black, design: .rounded))
                        .foregroundStyle(.indigo)
                        .transition(.zoomBlur)
                }
            }
            .frame(width: 280, height: 180)
            .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.6)) { shown.toggle() } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}
```

## Water Ripple (`water-ripple`)

A real ripple distorts the view's pixels outward from a tap.

- API: `.waterRippleOnTap() / .waterRipple(at:trigger:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Tap / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/WaterRipple.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/WaterRipple.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/WaterRipple.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Image("pond")
    .waterRippleOnTap()

Card()
    .waterRipple(at: tapLocation, trigger: tapCount)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .waterRipple(at:trigger:amplitude:duration:) view modifier (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] layer shader. The shader takes (float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float2 origin, float time, float amplitude, float frequency, float decay, float speed): distance = length(position − origin), local = max(0, time − distance / speed), wave = amplitude × sin(frequency × local) × exp(−decay × local); sample the layer at position + wave × normalize(position − origin) and add 0.25 × wave / amplitude to rgb (times alpha) so crests brighten. In Swift, run keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0, trigger:) with MoveKeyframe(0) and a LinearKeyframe to duration (3 s) over duration, and apply .visualEffect { $0.layerEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionRipple(.float2(origin), .float(elapsed), .float(12), .float(15), .float(8), .float(1200)), maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: 12, height: 12), isEnabled: 0 < elapsed < duration) }. Add .waterRippleOnTap() that records a SpatialTapGesture location (as a simultaneous gesture) and bumps the trigger. With Reduce Motion on, disable the effect.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A water ripple that spreads from a point across the view's pixels: a
/// ring wave pushes them in and out and brightens the crests, ringing a
/// few times before it fades. Rendered with a Metal `layerEffect`
/// (`Shaders/WaterRipple.metal`).
struct WaterRippleModifier<Trigger: Equatable>: ViewModifier {
    var origin: CGPoint
    var trigger: Trigger
    var amplitude: Double
    var duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let origin = origin, amplitude = amplitude, duration = duration
        let enabled = !reduceMotion
        return content.keyframeAnimator(initialValue: 0.0, trigger: trigger) { view, elapsed in
            view.visualEffect { effect, _ in
                effect.layerEffect(
                    motionShaders.motionRipple(
                        .float2(origin),
                        .float(elapsed),
                        .float(amplitude),
                        .float(15), // frequency
                        .float(8), // decay
                        .float(1200) // speed, points per second
                    ),
                    maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: amplitude, height: amplitude),
                    isEnabled: enabled && elapsed > 0 && elapsed < duration
                )
            }
        } keyframes: { _ in
            MoveKeyframe(0)
            LinearKeyframe(duration, duration: duration)
        }
    }
}

/// Starts a ripple wherever the view is tapped.
struct WaterRippleOnTapModifier: ViewModifier {
    var amplitude: Double

    @State private var origin: CGPoint = .zero
    @State private var taps = 0

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .modifier(WaterRippleModifier(origin: origin, trigger: taps, amplitude: amplitude, duration: 3))
            .simultaneousGesture(
                SpatialTapGesture().onEnded { value in
                    origin = value.location
                    taps += 1
                }
            )
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Sends a water ripple across the view from `origin` every time
    /// `trigger` changes.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("photo")
    ///     .waterRipple(at: tapLocation, trigger: tapCount)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - origin: Where the ripple starts, in the view's coordinates.
    ///   - trigger: Starts a new ripple whenever it changes.
    ///   - amplitude: How far pixels are pushed, in points.
    ///   - duration: How long the ripple lasts, in seconds.
    func waterRipple<Trigger: Equatable>(at origin: CGPoint, trigger: Trigger, amplitude: Double = 12, duration: Double = 3) -> some View {
        modifier(WaterRippleModifier(origin: origin, trigger: trigger, amplitude: amplitude, duration: duration))
    }

    /// Sends a water ripple out from wherever the view is tapped.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("pond")
    ///     .waterRippleOnTap()
    /// ```
    func waterRippleOnTap(amplitude: Double = 12) -> some View {
        modifier(WaterRippleOnTapModifier(amplitude: amplitude))
    }
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [.cyan, .blue, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
        .overlay(Image(systemName: "fish.fill").font(.system(size: 60)).foregroundStyle(.white))
        .frame(width: 280, height: 200)
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))
        .waterRippleOnTap()
}

// MARK: - WaterRipple.metal
// Save the shader below as WaterRipple.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for WaterRipple.swift (SwiftUI layer/distortion/colour effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// A ring wave travels out from `origin`, pushing pixels along the radius;
/// it rings at `frequency`, fades with `decay`, and brightens its crests.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionRipple(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer,
                                    float2 origin, float time,
                                    float amplitude, float frequency, float decay, float speed) {
    float distance = length(position - origin);
    // Each pixel starts moving once the wave front reaches it.
    float local = max(0.0, time - distance / speed);
    float wave = amplitude * sin(frequency * local) * exp(-decay * local);
    float2 direction = distance > 0.001 ? (position - origin) / distance : float2(0);
    half4 color = layer.sample(position + wave * direction);
    color.rgb += half(0.25 * (wave / max(amplitude, 0.001))) * color.a;
    return color;
}
*/
```

## Pixellate (`pixellate`)

The view melts into a mosaic of square blocks and back.

- API: `.pixellate(_:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/Pixellate.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/Pixellate.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/Pixellate.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Avatar()
    .pixellate(isHidden ? 18 : 1)
    .animation(.easeInOut, value: isHidden)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .pixellate(_ size:) view modifier (iOS 17+) as an Animatable ViewModifier over size, so withAnimation interpolates the block size. It applies .layerEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionPixellate(.float(size)), maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: size, height: size), isEnabled: size > 1). The Metal [[stitchable]] shader (float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float size) returns layer.sample(position) when size ≤ 1, otherwise layer.sample((floor(position / size) + 0.5) × size), one colour per block.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Breaks the view into square blocks of one colour each. The block size is
/// animatable, so the view can melt into or out of a mosaic. Rendered with a
/// Metal `layerEffect` (`Shaders/Pixellate.metal`).
struct PixellateModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var size: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { size }
        set { size = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.layerEffect(
            motionShaders.motionPixellate(.float(size)),
            maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: size, height: size),
            isEnabled: size > 1
        )
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shows the view as a mosaic of `size`-point blocks. Animate `size`
    /// to pixellate in or out.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Avatar()
    ///     .pixellate(isHidden ? 18 : 1)
    ///     .animation(.easeInOut, value: isHidden)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameter size: Block size in points; 1 or less shows the view as is.
    func pixellate(_ size: Double) -> some View {
        modifier(PixellateModifier(size: size))
    }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var blocky = false
        var body: some View {
            Image(systemName: "photo.artframe")
                .font(.system(size: 120))
                .foregroundStyle(.orange, .blue)
                .pixellate(blocky ? 16 : 1)
                .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { blocky.toggle() } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - Pixellate.metal
// Save the shader below as Pixellate.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for Pixellate.swift (SwiftUI layer/distortion/colour effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// Samples one colour per `size` × `size` cell.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionPixellate(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float size) {
    if (size <= 1.0) { return layer.sample(position); }
    float2 cell = (floor(position / size) + 0.5) * size;
    return layer.sample(cell);
}
*/
```

## Chromatic Aberration (`chromatic-aberration`)

Red and blue split sideways like a cheap lens; animate it on a beat.

- API: `.chromaticAberration(_:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Value change / Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/ChromaticAberration.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/ChromaticAberration.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/ChromaticAberration.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Text("BASS DROP")
    .font(.largeTitle.weight(.black))
    .chromaticAberration(isPlaying ? 6 : 0)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .chromaticAberration(_ amount:) view modifier (iOS 17+) as an Animatable ViewModifier over amount, applying .layerEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionChromatic(.float(amount)), maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: |amount|, height: 0), isEnabled: |amount| > 0.01). The Metal [[stitchable]] shader (float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float amount) samples red at position + (amount, 0), green at position and blue at position − (amount, 0), with alpha = the max of the three samples' alpha. For a beat, spike amount to 7 pt with withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.12)) and, in its completion, ease back to 1.5 over 0.5 s.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Splits the red and blue channels sideways like a cheap lens or a glitchy
/// screen. The amount is animatable, so it can pulse on a beat or spike on
/// an event. Rendered with a Metal `layerEffect`
/// (`Shaders/ChromaticAberration.metal`).
struct ChromaticAberrationModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var amount: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { amount }
        set { amount = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.layerEffect(
            motionShaders.motionChromatic(.float(amount)),
            maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: abs(amount), height: 0),
            isEnabled: abs(amount) > 0.01
        )
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shifts the red channel right and the blue channel left by `amount`
    /// points. Animate it for a pulsing RGB split.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text("BASS DROP")
    ///     .chromaticAberration(isPlaying ? 6 : 0)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    func chromaticAberration(_ amount: Double = 4) -> some View {
        modifier(ChromaticAberrationModifier(amount: amount))
    }
}

#Preview {
    Text("RGB SPLIT")
        .font(.system(size: 44, weight: .black))
        .chromaticAberration(5)
        .padding()
}

// MARK: - ChromaticAberration.metal
// Save the shader below as ChromaticAberration.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for ChromaticAberration.swift (SwiftUI layer/distortion/colour effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// Splits red and blue apart horizontally by `amount` points, like a cheap lens.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionChromatic(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float amount) {
    half4 base = layer.sample(position);
    half4 red = layer.sample(position + float2(amount, 0));
    half4 blue = layer.sample(position - float2(amount, 0));
    half alpha = max(base.a, max(red.a, blue.a));
    return half4(red.r, base.g, blue.b, alpha);
}
*/
```

## CRT Screen (`crt`)

Curved glass, scanlines, a rolling band and flicker, like an old monitor.

- API: `.crtScreen()`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/CRT.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/CRT.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/CRT.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

GameView()
    .crtScreen()
    .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 24))
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .crtScreen(curvature:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Inside TimelineView(.animation), apply .visualEffect { $0.layerEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionCRT(.float2(proxy.size), .float(time), .float(curvature)), maxSampleOffset: size × curvature) } with curvature 0.06. The Metal [[stitchable]] shader (position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float2 size, float time, float curvature): map to centred uv in −1…1, barrel-distort with uv × (1 + curvature × dot(uv, uv)), return black outside 0…1; sample red at +0.8 pt and blue at −0.8 pt for fringing; multiply by scanlines 0.8 + 0.2 sin(y × π × 0.66), a rolling band 1 + 0.08 × smoothstep(0.92, 1, sin(uv.y × 3 − time × 1.5)), a vignette smoothstep(1.25, 0.4, length(centred)) and a flicker 0.97 + 0.03 sin(time × 60). With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline at time 0.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Makes the view look like it's on an old CRT monitor: curved glass,
/// scanlines, a slow rolling band, slight colour fringing, a vignette and a
/// faint flicker. Rendered with a Metal `layerEffect` (`Shaders/CRT.metal`).
struct CRTModifier: ViewModifier {
    var curvature: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let curvature = curvature
        // Reduce Motion: the screen stays, the band and flicker stop.
        return TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1000)
            content.visualEffect { effect, proxy in
                effect.layerEffect(
                    motionShaders.motionCRT(.float2(proxy.size), .float(time), .float(curvature)),
                    maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: proxy.size.width * curvature, height: proxy.size.height * curvature)
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shows the view on a retro CRT screen.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// GameView()
    ///     .crtScreen()
    ///     .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 24))
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameter curvature: How much the glass bulges (0 = flat).
    func crtScreen(curvature: Double = 0.06) -> some View {
        modifier(CRTModifier(curvature: curvature))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 8) {
        Text("READY.").font(.system(size: 28, weight: .bold, design: .monospaced))
        Text("LOAD \"*\",8,1").font(.system(size: 18, design: .monospaced))
    }
    .foregroundStyle(.green)
    .frame(width: 300, height: 200)
    .background(Color(red: 0.02, green: 0.08, blue: 0.04))
    .crtScreen()
    .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))
}

// MARK: - CRT.metal
// Save the shader below as CRT.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for CRT.swift (SwiftUI layer/distortion/colour effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// An old CRT screen: barrel-curved glass, scanlines, a rolling bright band,
/// slight colour fringing, a dark vignette and a faint flicker.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionCRT(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float2 size, float time, float curvature) {
    float2 uv = position / size;
    float2 centred = uv * 2.0 - 1.0;
    // Barrel distortion: push points outward by their squared distance.
    centred *= 1.0 + curvature * dot(centred, centred);
    uv = (centred + 1.0) * 0.5;
    if (uv.x < 0.0 || uv.x > 1.0 || uv.y < 0.0 || uv.y > 1.0) { return half4(0, 0, 0, 1); }
    float2 p = uv * size;
    half4 color;
    color.r = layer.sample(p + float2(0.8, 0)).r;
    color.g = layer.sample(p).g;
    color.b = layer.sample(p - float2(0.8, 0)).b;
    color.a = 1.0;
    float scanline = 0.8 + 0.2 * sin(p.y * 3.14159 * 0.66);
    float band = 1.0 + 0.08 * smoothstep(0.92, 1.0, sin(uv.y * 3.0 - time * 1.5));
    float vignette = smoothstep(1.25, 0.4, length(centred));
    float flicker = 0.97 + 0.03 * sin(time * 60.0);
    color.rgb *= half(scanline * band * vignette * flicker);
    return color;
}
*/
```

## Heat Haze (`heat-haze`)

The view shimmers like hot air over a desert road.

- API: `.heatHaze(strength:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/HeatHaze.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/HeatHaze.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/HeatHaze.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Image("desert-road")
    .heatHaze()
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .heatHaze(strength:) view modifier (iOS 17+). Inside TimelineView(.animation), apply .visualEffect { $0.distortionEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionHeatHaze(.float2(proxy.size), .float(time), .float(strength)), maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: strength, height: strength)) } with strength 6 pt. The Metal [[stitchable]] distortion shader (float2 position, float2 size, float time, float strength) uses smooth value noise: rise = y × 0.05 + time × 2, n = noise(x × 0.04, rise) − 0.5, m = noise(x × 0.09 + 10, rise × 1.7) − 0.5, weight = 0.35 + 0.65 × y / height (stronger at the bottom), and returns position + ((n + 0.5m) × strength × weight, n × strength × 0.3 × weight). With Reduce Motion on, use strength 0.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Makes the view shimmer like air over hot asphalt or a desert road:
/// layered noise wobbles pixels sideways, rising over time, stronger towards
/// the bottom. Rendered with a Metal `distortionEffect`
/// (`Shaders/HeatHaze.metal`).
struct HeatHazeModifier: ViewModifier {
    var strength: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        // Reduce Motion: no shimmer.
        let strength = reduceMotion ? 0 : strength
        return TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1000)
            content.visualEffect { effect, proxy in
                effect.distortionEffect(
                    motionShaders.motionHeatHaze(.float2(proxy.size), .float(time), .float(strength)),
                    maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: strength, height: strength),
                    isEnabled: strength > 0
                )
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Makes the view shimmer like hot air.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("desert-road")
    ///     .heatHaze()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameter strength: How far pixels wobble, in points.
    func heatHaze(strength: Double = 6) -> some View {
        modifier(HeatHazeModifier(strength: strength))
    }
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .yellow, .brown], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
        .overlay(Image(systemName: "sun.max.fill").font(.system(size: 70)).foregroundStyle(.white))
        .frame(width: 280, height: 200)
        .heatHaze(strength: 8)
        .clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20))
}

// MARK: - HeatHaze.metal
// Save the shader below as HeatHaze.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for HeatHaze.swift (SwiftUI layer/distortion/colour effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// A cheap, stable hash of a 2D point into 0...1.
static float motionHash(float2 p) {
    p = fract(p * float2(123.34, 456.21));
    p += dot(p, p + 45.32);
    return fract(p.x * p.y);
}

/// Smooth value noise in 0...1.
static float motionNoise(float2 p) {
    float2 i = floor(p);
    float2 f = fract(p);
    float a = motionHash(i);
    float b = motionHash(i + float2(1, 0));
    float c = motionHash(i + float2(0, 1));
    float d = motionHash(i + float2(1, 1));
    float2 u = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
    return mix(mix(a, b, u.x), mix(c, d, u.x), u.y);
}

/// Wobbles pixels sideways with layered noise rising over time, like air
/// shimmering over hot asphalt. Stronger towards the bottom.
[[ stitchable ]] float2 motionHeatHaze(float2 position, float2 size, float time, float strength) {
    float rise = position.y * 0.05 + time * 2.0;
    float n = motionNoise(float2(position.x * 0.04, rise)) - 0.5;
    float m = motionNoise(float2(position.x * 0.09 + 10.0, rise * 1.7)) - 0.5;
    float weight = 0.35 + 0.65 * (position.y / max(size.y, 1.0));
    return position + float2((n + 0.5 * m) * strength * weight, n * strength * 0.3 * weight);
}
*/
```

## Noise Dissolve (`noise-dissolve`)

The view burns away in organic blotches with a glowing edge.

- API: `.noiseDissolve(_:) / .transition(.noiseDissolve)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/NoiseDissolve.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/NoiseDissolve.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/NoiseDissolve.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Card()
    .noiseDissolve(isDeleting ? 1 : 0)
    .animation(.easeIn(duration: 1), value: isDeleting)

if !isDeleted {
    NoteCard().transition(.noiseDissolve)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .noiseDissolve(_ progress:scale:edge:) view modifier (iOS 17+) as an Animatable ViewModifier over progress, applying .colorEffect(ShaderLibrary.motionDissolve(.float(progress), .float(scale), .color(edge)), isEnabled: progress > 0) with scale 18 pt and an orange edge, plus a NoiseDissolveTransition (.noiseDissolve) that uses progress 1 when not identity. The Metal [[stitchable]] colour shader (float2 position, half4 color, float progress, float scale, half4 edge): n = 0.7 × noise(position / scale) + 0.3 × noise(position / (0.35 × scale)) using smooth value noise; threshold = progress × 1.1 − 0.05; return transparent where n < threshold, and mix towards edge × alpha by 1 − smoothstep(threshold, threshold + 0.06, n) so a thin band glows just before it burns. With Reduce Motion on, the transition fades instead.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Burns the view away in organic noise blotches with a glowing edge, like
/// paper catching fire. `progress` is animatable, and there's a matching
/// transition. Rendered with a Metal `colorEffect`
/// (`Shaders/NoiseDissolve.metal`).
struct NoiseDissolveModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var progress: Double
    var scale: Double
    var edge: Color

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.colorEffect(
            motionShaders.motionDissolve(.float(progress), .float(scale), .color(edge)),
            isEnabled: progress > 0
        )
    }
}

/// Burns the view away on removal and un-burns it on insertion.
public struct NoiseDissolveTransition: Transition {
    public var edge: Color

    public init(edge: Color = .orange) {
        self.edge = edge
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        NoiseDissolveBody(content: content, phase: phase, edge: edge)
    }
}

private struct NoiseDissolveBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase
    let edge: Color

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            // Reduce Motion: a plain fade.
            content.opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
        } else {
            content.modifier(NoiseDissolveModifier(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 1, scale: 18, edge: edge))
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Dissolves the view in noise: 0 shows it all, 1 hides it all.
    /// Animate `progress` to burn it away.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Card()
    ///     .noiseDissolve(isDeleting ? 1 : 0)
    ///     .animation(.easeIn(duration: 1), value: isDeleting)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - progress: 0…1.
    ///   - scale: Size of the noise blotches, in points.
    ///   - edge: Colour of the burning edge.
    func noiseDissolve(_ progress: Double, scale: Double = 18, edge: Color = .orange) -> some View {
        modifier(NoiseDissolveModifier(progress: progress, scale: scale, edge: edge))
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == NoiseDissolveTransition {
    /// Burns the view away in glowing noise (and back in on insertion).
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if !isDeleted {
    ///     NoteCard().transition(.noiseDissolve)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var noiseDissolve: NoiseDissolveTransition { NoiseDissolveTransition() }

    /// Burns the view away with an `edge`-coloured glow.
    static func noiseDissolve(edge: Color) -> NoiseDissolveTransition { NoiseDissolveTransition(edge: edge) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var burnt = false
        var body: some View {
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 16)
                .fill(Color.indigo.gradient)
                .frame(width: 220, height: 150)
                .noiseDissolve(burnt ? 1 : 0)
                .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 1.2)) { burnt.toggle() } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - NoiseDissolve.metal
// Save the shader below as NoiseDissolve.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for NoiseDissolve.swift (SwiftUI layer/distortion/colour effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// A cheap, stable hash of a 2D point into 0...1.
static float motionHash(float2 p) {
    p = fract(p * float2(123.34, 456.21));
    p += dot(p, p + 45.32);
    return fract(p.x * p.y);
}

/// Smooth value noise in 0...1.
static float motionNoise(float2 p) {
    float2 i = floor(p);
    float2 f = fract(p);
    float a = motionHash(i);
    float b = motionHash(i + float2(1, 0));
    float c = motionHash(i + float2(0, 1));
    float d = motionHash(i + float2(1, 1));
    float2 u = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
    return mix(mix(a, b, u.x), mix(c, d, u.x), u.y);
}

/// Burns the view away in organic noise blotches. Pixels whose noise is
/// below `progress` vanish; a thin band just above it glows in `edge`.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionDissolve(float2 position, half4 color, float progress, float scale, half4 edge) {
    float n = motionNoise(position / scale) * 0.7 + motionNoise(position / (scale * 0.35)) * 0.3;
    // Stretch the range so 0 shows everything and 1 hides everything.
    float threshold = progress * 1.1 - 0.05;
    if (n < threshold) { return half4(0); }
    float glow = 1.0 - smoothstep(threshold, threshold + 0.06, n);
    if (progress <= 0.0) { glow = 0.0; }
    half4 burnt = mix(color, edge * color.a, half(glow));
    return burnt;
}
*/
```

---

## Disintegrate (`disintegrate`)

The view crumbles into grains of sand that blow away on the wind.

- API: `.disintegrate(_:) / .transition(.disintegrate)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/Disintegrate.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/Disintegrate.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/Disintegrate.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Avatar()
    .disintegrate(isGone ? 1 : 0)
    .animation(.easeIn(duration: 1.6), value: isGone)

if !isDeleted {
    MessageRow().transition(.disintegrate)
}
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .disintegrate(_ progress:wind:grain:) view modifier and matching Transition (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] layer shader with (position, layer, float2 size, float progress, float grain, float2 wind). Split the view into grain-sized cells (2 pt) with two hashes n, n2 per cell. along = dot(position / size, normalize(wind)) × 0.5 + 0.5; delay = (1 − along) × 0.55 + 0.3n; local = clamp((1.4 × progress − delay) / 0.5, 0, 1). If local is 0, return the layer unchanged; if n2 < 1.15 × local, return clear (the grain is gone); otherwise sample the layer at position − (wind × local² + (sin 40n, cos 31n) × local × 6 × grain) and multiply by 1 − local. Apply it through .visualEffect so the shader gets the size, with maxSampleOffset |wind| + 6 × grain, in an Animatable modifier on progress. The transition maps identity to 0 and removal/insertion to 1 (default wind (140, −60)); with Reduce Motion on it fades instead.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Crumbles the view into grains of sand that blow away on the wind, the
/// grains nearest the wind's source going first. `progress` is animatable,
/// and there's a matching transition. Rendered with a Metal `layerEffect`
/// (`Shaders/Disintegrate.metal`).
struct DisintegrateModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var progress: Double
    var wind: CGVector
    var grain: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let progress = Float(progress), grain = Float(max(1, grain))
        let wind = CGPoint(x: wind.dx, y: wind.dy)
        let reach = CGSize(width: abs(wind.x) + Double(grain) * 6, height: abs(wind.y) + Double(grain) * 6)
        return content.visualEffect { effect, proxy in
            effect.layerEffect(
                motionShaders.motionDisintegrate(.float2(proxy.size), .float(progress), .float(grain), .float2(wind)),
                maxSampleOffset: reach,
                isEnabled: progress > 0
            )
        }
    }
}

/// Blows the view away as sand on removal and gathers it back on insertion.
public struct DisintegrateTransition: Transition {
    public var wind: CGVector

    public init(wind: CGVector = CGVector(dx: 140, dy: -60)) {
        self.wind = wind
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        DisintegrateBody(content: content, phase: phase, wind: wind)
    }
}

private struct DisintegrateBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase
    let wind: CGVector

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            content.opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
        } else {
            content.modifier(DisintegrateModifier(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 1, wind: wind, grain: 2))
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Crumbles the view into blowing sand: 0 shows it whole, 1 has blown
    /// it all away. Animate `progress` to make it go.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Avatar()
    ///     .disintegrate(isGone ? 1 : 0)
    ///     .animation(.easeIn(duration: 1.6), value: isGone)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - progress: 0…1.
    ///   - wind: Where the grains blow, and how far, in points.
    ///   - grain: Size of a grain, in points.
    func disintegrate(_ progress: Double, wind: CGVector = CGVector(dx: 140, dy: -60), grain: Double = 2) -> some View {
        modifier(DisintegrateModifier(progress: progress, wind: wind, grain: grain))
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == DisintegrateTransition {
    /// Blows the view away as sand (and gathers it back in on insertion).
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if !isDeleted {
    ///     MessageRow().transition(.disintegrate)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var disintegrate: DisintegrateTransition { DisintegrateTransition() }

    /// Blows the view away as sand along `wind`, in points.
    static func disintegrate(wind: CGVector) -> DisintegrateTransition { DisintegrateTransition(wind: wind) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var gone = false
        var body: some View {
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 20)
                .fill(Color.orange.gradient)
                .overlay(Image(systemName: "person.fill").font(.system(size: 60)).foregroundStyle(.white))
                .frame(width: 160, height: 160)
                .disintegrate(gone ? 1 : 0)
                .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.easeIn(duration: 1.6)) { gone.toggle() } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - Disintegrate.metal
// Save the shader below as Disintegrate.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for Disintegrate.swift (SwiftUI layer effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// A cheap, stable hash of a 2D point into 0...1.
static float motionHash(float2 p) {
    p = fract(p * float2(123.34, 456.21));
    p += dot(p, p + 45.32);
    return fract(p.x * p.y);
}

/// Crumbles the layer into grains of sand that blow away on the wind,
/// sweeping from the leading edge to the trailing one as `progress` goes
/// from 0 to 1.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionDisintegrate(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float2 size, float progress, float grain, float2 wind) {
    float2 cell = floor(position / grain);
    float n = motionHash(cell);
    float n2 = motionHash(cell + 17.0);
    // Grains leave in a sweep along the wind, with some randomness.
    float2 direction = normalize(wind);
    float along = dot(position / max(size, float2(1.0)), direction) * 0.5 + 0.5;
    float delay = (1.0 - along) * 0.55 + n * 0.3;
    float local = clamp((progress * 1.4 - delay) / 0.5, 0.0, 1.0);
    if (local <= 0.0) { return layer.sample(position); }
    // A grain that has left: some vanish, the rest are drawn from upwind.
    if (n2 < local * 1.15) { return half4(0); }
    float2 drift = wind * local * local + float2(sin(n * 40.0), cos(n * 31.0)) * local * grain * 6.0;
    half4 colour = layer.sample(position - drift);
    return colour * half(1.0 - local);
}
*/
```

## Genie (`genie`)

The view pinches and pours into a point below it, like minimising a window.

- API: `.genie(_:toward:) / .transition(.genie)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/Genie.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/Genie.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/Genie.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Panel()
    .genie(isMinimised ? 1 : 0, toward: 0.8)
    .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.7), value: isMinimised)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .genie(_ progress:toward:) view modifier and matching Transition (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] distortion shader (position, float2 size, float progress, float target) that returns where to sample. pinch = clamp(2p, 0, 1), slide = clamp(2p − 1, 0, 1). Return an off-view point below the bottom edge (that part has gone into the target, and maxSampleOffset widens the drawn area). y = position.y − slide × height (return an off-view point if y < 0). bend = smoothstep(0, 1, clamp(y / height + slide, 0, 1)) and squeeze = pinch × bend; the row's edges move from 0 and width towards target × width ∓ 3 pt by squeeze. Return off-view for x outside them, else x = (position.x − left) / (right − left) × width. So the bottom first pinches towards the target in an S-curve, then the whole shape slides down into it. Apply through .visualEffect for the size, maxSampleOffset = size, in an Animatable modifier on progress. The transition defaults to the middle of the bottom edge; with Reduce Motion on it fades instead.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// The "genie" minimise: the view pinches towards a point on its bottom edge
/// and pours down into it. `progress` is animatable, and there's a matching
/// transition. Rendered with a Metal `distortionEffect`
/// (`Shaders/Genie.metal`).
struct GenieModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var progress: Double
    var target: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let progress = Float(progress), target = Float(target)
        return content.visualEffect { effect, proxy in
            effect.distortionEffect(
                motionShaders.motionGenie(.float2(proxy.size), .float(progress), .float(target)),
                maxSampleOffset: proxy.size,
                isEnabled: progress > 0
            )
        }
    }
}

/// Sucks the view into a point below it on removal, and pours it back out on
/// insertion.
public struct GenieTransition: Transition {
    public var target: Double

    public init(target: Double = 0.5) {
        self.target = target
    }

    public func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        GenieBody(content: content, phase: phase, target: target)
    }
}

private struct GenieBody<Content: View>: View {
    let content: Content
    let phase: TransitionPhase
    let target: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            content.opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
        } else {
            content.modifier(GenieModifier(progress: phase.isIdentity ? 0 : 1, target: target))
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Pours the view into a point on its bottom edge: 0 shows it, 1 has it
    /// fully minimised.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Window()
    ///     .genie(isMinimised ? 1 : 0, toward: 0.8)
    ///     .animation(.easeIn(duration: 0.6), value: isMinimised)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - progress: 0…1.
    ///   - target: Where along the bottom edge it goes, 0 (left) to 1 (right).
    func genie(_ progress: Double, toward target: Double = 0.5) -> some View {
        modifier(GenieModifier(progress: progress, target: min(1, max(0, target))))
    }
}

public extension Transition where Self == GenieTransition {
    /// Minimises the view into the middle of its bottom edge, genie style.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// if isOpen {
    ///     Panel().transition(.genie)
    /// }
    /// ```
    static var genie: GenieTransition { GenieTransition() }

    /// Minimises the view into a point on its bottom edge, 0 (left) to 1 (right).
    static func genie(toward target: Double) -> GenieTransition { GenieTransition(target: min(1, max(0, target))) }
}

#Preview {
    struct Demo: View {
        @State private var minimised = false
        var body: some View {
            RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14)
                .fill(Color.blue.gradient)
                .overlay(Text("Window").font(.title.bold()).foregroundStyle(.white))
                .frame(width: 220, height: 150)
                .genie(minimised ? 1 : 0, toward: 0.8)
                .frame(height: 260, alignment: .top)
                .onTapGesture { withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { minimised.toggle() } }
        }
    }
    return Demo()
}

// MARK: - Genie.metal
// Save the shader below as Genie.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for Genie.swift (SwiftUI distortion effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// The macOS-style "genie" minimise: the bottom of the view pinches towards
/// `target` (0...1 along the bottom edge) while the rest bends after it,
/// then the whole shape slides down and into that point.
[[ stitchable ]] float2 motionGenie(float2 position, float2 size, float progress, float target) {
    float pinch = clamp(progress * 2.0, 0.0, 1.0);
    float slide = clamp(progress * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
    // Anything that has slid past the bottom edge has gone into the target.
    if (position.y > size.y) { return float2(-1e5); }
    // Slide: content moves down by up to the full height.
    float y = position.y - slide * size.y;
    if (y < 0.0) { return float2(-1e5); }
    float v = clamp(y / size.y, 0.0, 1.0);
    // The pinch grows towards the bottom with an S-curve, and reaches higher
    // up as the slide progresses.
    float bend = smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, clamp(v + slide, 0.0, 1.0));
    float squeeze = pinch * bend;
    float targetX = target * size.x;
    float narrow = 6.0;
    float left = mix(0.0, targetX - narrow * 0.5, squeeze);
    float right = mix(size.x, targetX + narrow * 0.5, squeeze);
    if (position.x < left || position.x > right) { return float2(-1e5); }
    float x = (position.x - left) / max(right - left, 0.001) * size.x;
    return float2(x, y);
}
*/
```
