## Glass Lens (`glass-lens`)

A round glass lens magnifies what's under it, bending light at its rim.

- API: `.glassLensOnDrag() / .glassLens(at:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Drag / Hover
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/GlassLens.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/GlassLens.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/GlassLens.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

ArticleView()
    .glassLensOnDrag(radius: 60)
```

### How it works

Create SwiftUI .glassLens(at:radius:magnification:) and .glassLensOnDrag() view modifiers (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] layer shader (position, layer, float2 centre, float radius, float magnification). u = distance from centre / radius. Outside (u ≥ 1), darken the layer by up to 22 % in a soft ring that fades out by u = 1.12. Inside, sample at centre + offset × scale with scale = mix(1 / magnification, 1, u³), so the middle is magnified (1.8×) and the rim isn't; sample red at scale + 0.035u⁴ and blue at scale − 0.035u⁴ for colour fringing. Brighten towards white by a rim term smoothstep(0.86, 1, u) × 0.35 plus a specular spot centred at (−0.38, −0.42) × radius that fades over 0.32 × radius. maxSampleOffset = radius. The drag version follows a DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0) and the hover location, starting in the middle.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A round glass lens over the view: it magnifies what's under it, bends the
/// light harder towards the rim with a hint of colour fringing, and casts a
/// soft shadow. Rendered with a Metal `layerEffect`
/// (`Shaders/GlassLens.metal`).
struct GlassLensModifier: ViewModifier {
    var centre: CGPoint
    var radius: Double
    var magnification: Double

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.layerEffect(
            motionShaders.motionGlassLens(.float2(centre), .float(radius), .float(max(1, magnification))),
            maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: radius, height: radius)
        )
    }
}

/// A lens that follows a dragging finger or the pointer.
struct GlassLensOnDragModifier: ViewModifier {
    var radius: Double
    var magnification: Double

    @State private var centre: CGPoint?
    @State private var size: CGSize = .zero

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .modifier(GlassLensModifier(centre: centre ?? CGPoint(x: size.width / 2, y: size.height / 2), radius: radius, magnification: magnification))
            .background {
                GeometryReader { proxy in
                    Color.clear
                        .onAppear { size = proxy.size }
                        .onChange(of: proxy.size) { _, new in size = new }
                }
            }
            .gesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { value in
                withAnimation(.interactiveSpring(duration: 0.2)) { centre = value.location }
            })
            .onContinuousHover { phase in
                if case let .active(location) = phase { centre = location }
            }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Puts a glass lens over the view at `centre`.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// MapView()
    ///     .glassLens(at: point, radius: 60)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - centre: Centre of the lens, in the view's coordinates.
    ///   - radius: Radius of the lens, in points.
    ///   - magnification: Zoom at the middle of the lens.
    func glassLens(at centre: CGPoint, radius: Double = 56, magnification: Double = 1.8) -> some View {
        modifier(GlassLensModifier(centre: centre, radius: radius, magnification: magnification))
    }

    /// Puts a glass lens over the view that follows a dragging finger or the
    /// pointer. It starts in the middle.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Text(article).glassLensOnDrag()
    /// ```
    func glassLensOnDrag(radius: Double = 56, magnification: Double = 1.8) -> some View {
        modifier(GlassLensOnDragModifier(radius: radius, magnification: magnification))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
        ForEach(0..<6) { _ in
            Text("Drag the lens over this text to read it.").font(.caption)
        }
    }
    .padding()
    .frame(width: 280, height: 180)
    .background(.white)
    .glassLensOnDrag()
}

// MARK: - GlassLens.metal
// Save the shader below as GlassLens.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for GlassLens.swift (SwiftUI layer effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// A round glass lens over the layer: magnifies the middle, bends the light
/// harder towards the rim (splitting the colours a little), adds a bright rim
/// and specular highlight, and drops a soft shadow just outside.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionGlassLens(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float2 centre, float radius, float magnification) {
    float2 offset = position - centre;
    float d = length(offset);
    float u = d / radius;
    if (u >= 1.0) {
        half4 colour = layer.sample(position);
        // Soft shadow ring outside the rim.
        float shadow = (1.0 - smoothstep(1.0, 1.12, u)) * 0.22;
        return half4(colour.rgb * half(1.0 - shadow), colour.a);
    }
    // Strong magnification in the middle easing to none at the rim.
    float scale = mix(1.0 / magnification, 1.0, pow(u, 3.0));
    float split = 0.035 * pow(u, 4.0);
    half4 g = layer.sample(centre + offset * scale);
    half r = layer.sample(centre + offset * (scale + split)).r;
    half b = layer.sample(centre + offset * (scale - split)).b;
    half4 colour = half4(r, g.g, b, g.a);
    // Bright rim, and a highlight up and to the left.
    float rim = smoothstep(0.86, 1.0, u) * 0.35;
    float2 light = centre + float2(-0.38, -0.42) * radius;
    float spec = (1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, radius * 0.32, length(position - light))) * 0.45;
    half glow = half(rim + spec);
    colour.rgb = colour.rgb + glow * (1.0h - colour.rgb);
    colour.a = max(colour.a, glow);
    return colour;
}
*/
```

## Swirl (`swirl`)

The view twists around a point like water going down a drain.

- API: `.swirlOnDrag() / .swirl(at:strength:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Drag / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/Swirl.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/Swirl.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/Swirl.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Image("galaxy")
    .swirlOnDrag()

Logo()
    .swirl(at: centre, strength: isStirred ? 4 : 0)
    .animation(.spring(duration: 1), value: isStirred)
```

### How it works

Create SwiftUI .swirl(at:radius:strength:) and .swirlOnDrag(radius:strength:) view modifiers (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] distortion shader (position, float2 centre, float radius, float strength): within radius (110 pt), rotate the offset from the centre by strength × t² where t = 1 − distance / radius, so it twists most at the centre and not at all at the edge; outside, return the position unchanged. Animate strength in an Animatable modifier, maxSampleOffset = radius. The drag version moves the centre to the finger and sets strength to 4 × min(1, 0.35 + travel / 160) with an interactive spring, then springs back to 0 with .spring(duration: 0.8, bounce: 0.45) on release. With Reduce Motion on, the drag doesn't twist.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Twists the view around a point like water going down a drain.
/// `strength` is animatable. Rendered with a Metal `distortionEffect`
/// (`Shaders/Swirl.metal`).
struct SwirlModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var centre: CGPoint
    var radius: Double
    var strength: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { strength }
        set { strength = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.distortionEffect(
            motionShaders.motionSwirl(.float2(centre), .float(radius), .float(strength)),
            maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: radius, height: radius),
            isEnabled: abs(strength) > 0.001
        )
    }
}

/// Swirls wherever a finger drags, and untwists with a spring on release.
struct SwirlOnDragModifier: ViewModifier {
    var radius: Double
    var strength: Double

    @State private var centre: CGPoint = .zero
    @State private var amount: Double = 0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .modifier(SwirlModifier(centre: centre, radius: radius, strength: amount))
            .gesture(
                DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
                    .onChanged { value in
                        guard !reduceMotion else { return }
                        centre = value.location
                        // Twist harder the further the finger travels.
                        let travel = hypot(value.translation.width, value.translation.height)
                        withAnimation(.interactiveSpring(duration: 0.3)) {
                            amount = strength * min(1, 0.35 + travel / 160)
                        }
                    }
                    .onEnded { _ in
                        withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.8, bounce: 0.45)) { amount = 0 }
                    }
            )
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Twists the view around `centre`. Animate `strength` to stir it.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("latte")
    ///     .swirl(at: point, strength: isStirred ? 4 : 0)
    ///     .animation(.spring(duration: 1), value: isStirred)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - centre: Centre of the twist, in the view's coordinates.
    ///   - radius: Reach of the twist, in points.
    ///   - strength: Twist at the centre, in radians (negative turns the other way).
    func swirl(at centre: CGPoint, radius: Double = 110, strength: Double) -> some View {
        modifier(SwirlModifier(centre: centre, radius: radius, strength: strength))
    }

    /// Swirls the view under a dragging finger and springs back on release.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("galaxy")
    ///     .swirlOnDrag()
    /// ```
    func swirlOnDrag(radius: Double = 110, strength: Double = 4) -> some View {
        modifier(SwirlOnDragModifier(radius: radius, strength: strength))
    }
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [.blue, .purple, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
        .overlay(Text("SWIRL").font(.system(size: 50, weight: .black)).foregroundStyle(.white))
        .frame(width: 280, height: 200)
        .swirlOnDrag()
}

// MARK: - Swirl.metal
// Save the shader below as Swirl.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for Swirl.swift (SwiftUI distortion effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// Twists the view around `centre` like water going down a drain: pixels
/// within `radius` are rotated, most at the centre and none at the edge.
[[ stitchable ]] float2 motionSwirl(float2 position, float2 centre, float radius, float strength) {
    float2 offset = position - centre;
    float d = length(offset);
    if (d >= radius) { return position; }
    float t = 1.0 - d / radius;
    float angle = strength * t * t;
    float c = cos(angle), s = sin(angle);
    return centre + float2(c * offset.x - s * offset.y, s * offset.x + c * offset.y);
}
*/
```

## Kaleidoscope (`kaleidoscope`)

One wedge of the view mirrored round the centre, turning into new patterns.

- API: `.kaleidoscope(segments:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Loop / Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/Kaleidoscope.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/Kaleidoscope.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/Kaleidoscope.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Image("flowers")
    .kaleidoscope(segments: 8)
    .clipShape(Circle())
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .kaleidoscope(segments:rotation:spins:) view modifier (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] layer shader (position, layer, float2 size, float segments, float rotation). Around the centre, take the polar angle modulo the wedge 2π / segments and mirror the second half of each wedge (a > wedge / 2 → wedge − a), add rotation, and sample at centre + r' × (cos a, sin a), where r' folds the radius back into the view (reach − |r mod 2 reach − reach|, reach = half the shorter side) so the corners aren't empty. Pass the size through .visualEffect with maxSampleOffset = size, in an Animatable modifier on rotation. When spins is on, add time × 0.25 rad from TimelineView(.animation) so the pattern keeps blooming. With Reduce Motion on, don't spin.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Turns the view into a kaleidoscope: one wedge is mirrored around the
/// centre, and turning the wedge makes the pattern bloom and fold.
/// Rendered with a Metal `layerEffect` (`Shaders/Kaleidoscope.metal`).
struct KaleidoscopeModifier: ViewModifier {
    var segments: Int
    var rotation: Angle
    var spins: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        if spins && !reduceMotion {
            TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
                let turn = timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 3600) * 0.25
                content.modifier(KaleidoscopeEffect(segments: segments, rotation: rotation.radians + turn))
            }
        } else {
            content.modifier(KaleidoscopeEffect(segments: segments, rotation: rotation.radians))
        }
    }
}

struct KaleidoscopeEffect: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var segments: Int
    var rotation: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { rotation }
        set { rotation = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let segments = Float(max(2, segments)), rotation = Float(rotation)
        return content.visualEffect { effect, proxy in
            effect.layerEffect(
                motionShaders.motionKaleidoscope(.float2(proxy.size), .float(segments), .float(rotation)),
                maxSampleOffset: proxy.size
            )
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Mirrors the view into a kaleidoscope with `segments` reflections.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("flowers")
    ///     .kaleidoscope(segments: 8)           // turns on its own
    /// Pattern()
    ///     .kaleidoscope(segments: 6, rotation: angle, spins: false)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - segments: Number of mirrored wedges.
    ///   - rotation: Which part of the view the wedge samples; animatable.
    ///   - spins: Keep turning the wedge, so the pattern keeps changing.
    func kaleidoscope(segments: Int = 8, rotation: Angle = .zero, spins: Bool = true) -> some View {
        modifier(KaleidoscopeModifier(segments: segments, rotation: rotation, spins: spins))
    }
}

#Preview {
    AngularGradient(colors: [.red, .orange, .yellow, .green, .blue, .purple, .red], center: .topLeading)
        .overlay(Image(systemName: "leaf.fill").font(.system(size: 60)).foregroundStyle(.white).offset(x: 40, y: 20))
        .frame(width: 240, height: 240)
        .kaleidoscope(segments: 8)
}

// MARK: - Kaleidoscope.metal
// Save the shader below as Kaleidoscope.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for Kaleidoscope.swift (SwiftUI layer effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// Mirrors one wedge of the layer around the centre, `segments` times, like
/// a kaleidoscope. `rotation` turns the wedge being sampled, so animating it
/// makes the pattern bloom and fold.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionKaleidoscope(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float2 size, float segments, float rotation) {
    float2 centre = size * 0.5;
    float2 p = position - centre;
    float r = length(p);
    float wedge = 2.0 * M_PI_F / max(segments, 1.0);
    float a = atan2(p.y, p.x);
    a = a - wedge * floor(a / wedge);
    if (a > wedge * 0.5) { a = wedge - a; } // mirror every other half
    a += rotation;
    // Fold the sample radius back into the view so the edges don't go blank.
    float reach = min(size.x, size.y) * 0.5;
    float folded = reach - abs(fmod(r, 2.0 * reach) - reach);
    return layer.sample(centre + folded * float2(cos(a), sin(a)));
}
*/
```

## Halftone (`halftone`)

The view is printed in round dots, bigger where it's darker, like newsprint.

- API: `.halftone(dotSize:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/Halftone.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/Halftone.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/Halftone.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Image("portrait")
    .halftone(dotSize: isPrinted ? 8 : 1)
    .animation(.easeInOut, value: isPrinted)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .halftone(dotSize:angle:paper:) view modifier (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] layer shader (position, layer, float dotSize, float angle, half4 paper). Rotate the position into a grid at angle (45°), find the centre of its dotSize cell (8 pt), rotate that back and sample the layer there for the dot's colour. Un-premultiply, take luminance L, coverage = (1 − 0.85L) × alpha, dot radius = √coverage × 0.72 × dotSize, and draw the dot with a 0.8 pt smoothstep edge over the paper colour, keeping the alpha of the layer at the pixel so transparent areas stay transparent. Animate dotSize in an Animatable modifier and disable the effect below 1.5 pt, so animating from 1 brings the dots in. maxSampleOffset = dotSize.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Redraws the view as round printing dots on paper, like newsprint or a
/// comic: darker areas get bigger dots, each in the colour underneath.
/// `dotSize` is animatable. Rendered with a Metal `layerEffect`
/// (`Shaders/Halftone.metal`).
struct HalftoneModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var dotSize: Double
    var angle: Angle
    var paper: Color

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { dotSize }
        set { dotSize = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let size = max(1, dotSize)
        content.layerEffect(
            motionShaders.motionHalftone(.float(size), .float(angle.radians), .color(paper)),
            maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: size, height: size),
            isEnabled: dotSize >= 1.5
        )
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Prints the view in halftone dots. Animate `dotSize` from 1 (off) up
    /// to bring the dots in.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("portrait")
    ///     .halftone(dotSize: 8)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - dotSize: Spacing of the dot grid, in points. Below 1.5 the effect is off.
    ///   - angle: Rotation of the dot grid (print screens use 45°).
    ///   - paper: Colour between the dots.
    func halftone(dotSize: Double = 8, angle: Angle = .degrees(45), paper: Color = .white) -> some View {
        modifier(HalftoneModifier(dotSize: dotSize, angle: angle, paper: paper))
    }
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .purple], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
        .overlay(Image(systemName: "star.fill").font(.system(size: 80)).foregroundStyle(.yellow))
        .frame(width: 260, height: 180)
        .halftone(dotSize: 7)
}

// MARK: - Halftone.metal
// Save the shader below as Halftone.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for Halftone.swift (SwiftUI layer effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// Redraws the layer as a grid of round dots on paper, like newsprint: the
/// grid is rotated by `angle`, each dot takes the colour under its centre,
/// and darker areas get bigger dots.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionHalftone(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float dotSize, float angle, half4 paper) {
    float c = cos(angle), s = sin(angle);
    // Into the rotated grid and back out again.
    float2 p = float2(c * position.x + s * position.y, -s * position.x + c * position.y);
    float2 cell = (floor(p / dotSize) + 0.5) * dotSize;
    float2 centre = float2(c * cell.x - s * cell.y, s * cell.x + c * cell.y);
    half4 ink = layer.sample(centre);
    half alpha = layer.sample(position).a;
    if (alpha <= 0.0h) { return half4(0); }
    float3 rgb = ink.a > 0.0h ? float3(ink.rgb / ink.a) : float3(1);
    float luminance = dot(rgb, float3(0.299, 0.587, 0.114));
    float coverage = (1.0 - luminance * 0.85) * float(ink.a);
    float radius = sqrt(coverage) * dotSize * 0.72;
    float d = length(p - cell);
    float inside = 1.0 - smoothstep(radius - 0.8, radius + 0.8, d);
    half3 colour = mix(paper.rgb, half3(rgb), half(inside));
    return half4(colour * alpha, alpha);
}
*/
```

## Dither (`dither`)

Chunky pixels in a few flat colours with a Bayer cross-hatch, like a retro handheld.

- API: `.dither(pixelSize:palette:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/Dither.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/Dither.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/Dither.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

GameScene()
    .dither(pixelSize: 3)                             // four greens
Avatar()
    .dither(pixelSize: 2, palette: DitherPalette.mono) // 1-bit
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .dither(pixelSize:palette:) view modifier (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] layer shader (position, layer, float pixelSize, device const half4 *palette, int count). Sample the layer at the centre of the position's pixelSize block (3 pt), un-premultiply, take luminance, and add a 4 × 4 Bayer threshold ((bayer[i] + 0.5) / 16 − 0.5) / (levels − 1) indexed by the block coordinates mod 4. Round to the nearest of the palette's colours (darkest first) and return it premultiplied by the sample's alpha. Pass the palette with .colorArray. Ship palettes: four greens like an early handheld (0.06, 0.22, 0.06) … (0.61, 0.74, 0.06), mono black/white, and sepia. Animate pixelSize in an Animatable modifier; maxSampleOffset = pixelSize.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Retro ordered dithering: the view is cut into chunky pixels and drawn in
/// a few flat colours with a Bayer cross-hatch between them, like an old
/// handheld console screen. Rendered with a Metal `layerEffect`
/// (`Shaders/Dither.metal`).
struct DitherModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var pixelSize: Double
    var palette: [Color]

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { pixelSize }
        set { pixelSize = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let size = max(1, pixelSize)
        content.layerEffect(
            motionShaders.motionDither(.float(size), .colorArray(palette)),
            maxSampleOffset: CGSize(width: size, height: size),
            isEnabled: palette.count >= 2
        )
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Draws the view in a handful of colours with ordered (Bayer) dithering.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("level")
    ///     .dither(pixelSize: 3)                         // four-shade green
    /// Avatar()
    ///     .dither(pixelSize: 2, palette: [.black, .white]) // 1-bit
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - pixelSize: Size of one chunky pixel, in points.
    ///   - palette: Two or more colours from darkest to lightest. The default
    ///     is a four-shade green, like an early handheld console.
    func dither(pixelSize: Double = 3, palette: [Color] = DitherPalette.green) -> some View {
        modifier(DitherModifier(pixelSize: pixelSize, palette: palette))
    }
}

/// Palettes for `.dither(pixelSize:palette:)`, darkest first.
public enum DitherPalette {
    /// Four greens, like an early handheld console's screen.
    public static let green: [Color] = [
        Color(red: 0.06, green: 0.22, blue: 0.06), Color(red: 0.19, green: 0.38, blue: 0.19),
        Color(red: 0.55, green: 0.67, blue: 0.06), Color(red: 0.61, green: 0.74, blue: 0.06),
    ]
    /// Black and white.
    public static let mono: [Color] = [.black, .white]
    /// Four warm browns, like an old photograph.
    public static let sepia: [Color] = [
        Color(red: 0.17, green: 0.11, blue: 0.07), Color(red: 0.44, green: 0.3, blue: 0.2),
        Color(red: 0.75, green: 0.6, blue: 0.43), Color(red: 0.96, green: 0.9, blue: 0.78),
    ]
}

#Preview {
    LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .white], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
        .overlay(Image(systemName: "gamecontroller.fill").font(.system(size: 70)).foregroundStyle(.gray))
        .frame(width: 260, height: 160)
        .dither(pixelSize: 3)
}

// MARK: - Dither.metal
// Save the shader below as Dither.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for Dither.swift (SwiftUI layer effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// Retro ordered dithering: the layer is cut into `pixelSize` blocks, each
/// block's brightness is nudged by a 4x4 Bayer pattern and snapped to one of
/// the palette's colours (darkest first).
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionDither(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float pixelSize, device const half4 *palette, int count) {
    float2 block = floor(position / pixelSize);
    half4 colour = layer.sample((block + 0.5) * pixelSize);
    if (colour.a <= 0.01h) { return half4(0); }
    float3 rgb = float3(colour.rgb / colour.a);
    float luminance = dot(rgb, float3(0.299, 0.587, 0.114));
    const float bayer[16] = { 0, 8, 2, 10, 12, 4, 14, 6, 3, 11, 1, 9, 15, 7, 13, 5 };
    int2 b = int2(fmod(block, 4.0));
    float threshold = (bayer[b.y * 4 + b.x] + 0.5) / 16.0 - 0.5;
    int levels = max(count, 2);
    float level = clamp(luminance + threshold / float(levels - 1), 0.0, 1.0);
    int index = clamp(int(round(level * float(levels - 1))), 0, levels - 1);
    half4 shade = palette[min(index, count - 1)];
    return half4(shade.rgb * colour.a, colour.a);
}
*/
```

## Thermal Vision (`thermal`)

Brightness turns into heat colours, from cold indigo to white hot.

- API: `.thermal(_:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Value change
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/Thermal.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/Thermal.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/Thermal.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

CameraFeed()
    .thermal(isScanning ? 1 : 0)
    .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.6), value: isScanning)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .thermal(_ intensity:) view modifier (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] colour shader (position, half4 colour, float intensity). Un-premultiply, take luminance as heat, and map it through seven evenly spaced stops: (0, 0, 0.05), (0.2, 0.05, 0.45), (0.65, 0.05, 0.6), (0.95, 0.15, 0.2), (1, 0.5, 0), (1, 0.9, 0.2), (1, 1, 1), interpolating linearly. Mix the original colour with the heat colour by intensity and premultiply again. Animate intensity in an Animatable modifier and disable the effect at 0, so the view can switch into heat vision.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// False-colour "heat vision": brightness becomes temperature, from cold
/// black and indigo through magenta and red to hot yellow and white.
/// `intensity` is animatable, so the view can switch into heat vision.
/// Rendered with a Metal `colorEffect` (`Shaders/Thermal.metal`).
struct ThermalModifier: ViewModifier, Animatable {
    var intensity: Double

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { intensity }
        set { intensity = newValue }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.colorEffect(motionShaders.motionThermal(.float(intensity)), isEnabled: intensity > 0)
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Shows the view through a heat camera. Animate `intensity` between 0
    /// and 1 to switch it on and off.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("street")
    ///     .thermal(isScanning ? 1 : 0)
    ///     .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.6), value: isScanning)
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameter intensity: 0 shows the original colours, 1 the full heat palette.
    func thermal(_ intensity: Double = 1) -> some View {
        modifier(ThermalModifier(intensity: intensity))
    }
}

#Preview {
    RadialGradient(colors: [.white, .gray, .black], center: .center, startRadius: 10, endRadius: 140)
        .frame(width: 260, height: 180)
        .thermal()
}

// MARK: - Thermal.metal
// Save the shader below as Thermal.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for Thermal.swift (SwiftUI colour effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// Maps brightness to a heat-camera palette, from cold black and indigo
/// through magenta and red to hot yellow and white. `intensity` blends from
/// the original colours (0) to the full false colour (1).
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionThermal(float2 position, half4 colour, float intensity) {
    if (colour.a <= 0.0h) { return colour; }
    float3 rgb = float3(colour.rgb / colour.a);
    float heat = dot(rgb, float3(0.299, 0.587, 0.114));
    const float3 stops[7] = {
        float3(0.0, 0.0, 0.05), float3(0.2, 0.05, 0.45), float3(0.65, 0.05, 0.6),
        float3(0.95, 0.15, 0.2), float3(1.0, 0.5, 0.0), float3(1.0, 0.9, 0.2), float3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    };
    float scaled = clamp(heat, 0.0, 1.0) * 6.0;
    int i = min(int(floor(scaled)), 5);
    float3 thermal = mix(stops[i], stops[i + 1], scaled - float(i));
    float3 result = mix(rgb, thermal, clamp(intensity, 0.0, 1.0));
    return half4(half3(result) * colour.a, colour.a);
}
*/
```

## Flag Wave (`flag-wave`)

The view ripples like a flag on a pole, its folds catching the light.

- API: `.flagWave()`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/FlagWave.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/FlagWave.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/FlagWave.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

Image("banner")
    .flagWave(amplitude: 10)
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI .flagWave(amplitude:wavelength:speed:) view modifier (iOS 17+) using a Metal [[stitchable]] layer shader (position, layer, float2 size, float time, float amplitude, float wavelength). reach = x / width (0 at the pole on the leading edge, 1 at the free end); phase = x / wavelength × 2π − 4 × time; wave = sin(phase) + 0.35 sin(2.3 phase + 1.1). Sample at (x + 0.25 × amplitude × reach × cos(phase), y − amplitude × reach × wave) and multiply the colour by 1 + 0.18 × reach × (cos(phase) + 0.8 cos(2.3 phase + 1.1)) so slopes catch light and shade, clamped to alpha. Drive time from TimelineView(.animation), pad the view vertically by 1.4 × amplitude (and take it back with negative padding) so the ripples have room, and apply through .visualEffect for the size. With Reduce Motion on, leave the view still.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// Waves the view like a flag in the wind, held at its leading edge: ripples
/// run along it, growing towards the free end, and the folds catch light
/// and shadow. Rendered with a Metal `layerEffect`
/// (`Shaders/FlagWave.metal`).
struct FlagWaveModifier: ViewModifier {
    var amplitude: Double
    var wavelength: Double
    var speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            content
        } else {
            TimelineView(.animation) { timeline in
                let time = Float(timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 3600) * speed)
                let amplitude = Float(amplitude), wavelength = Float(max(10, wavelength))
                let reach = CGSize(width: Double(amplitude), height: Double(amplitude) * 1.4)
                content
                    .padding(.vertical, Double(amplitude) * 1.4)
                    .visualEffect { effect, proxy in
                        effect.layerEffect(
                            motionShaders.motionFlagWave(.float2(proxy.size), .float(time), .float(amplitude), .float(wavelength)),
                            maxSampleOffset: reach
                        )
                    }
                    .padding(.vertical, -Double(amplitude) * 1.4)
            }
        }
    }
}

public extension View {
    /// Waves the view like a flag held at its leading edge.
    ///
    /// ```swift
    /// Image("banner")
    ///     .flagWave()
    /// ```
    ///
    /// Requires the `MotionShaders` product (Metal).
    ///
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - amplitude: Height of the ripples at the free end, in points.
    ///   - wavelength: Length of one ripple, in points.
    ///   - speed: How fast the ripples run.
    func flagWave(amplitude: Double = 9, wavelength: Double = 120, speed: Double = 1) -> some View {
        modifier(FlagWaveModifier(amplitude: amplitude, wavelength: wavelength, speed: speed))
    }
}

#Preview {
    VStack(spacing: 0) {
        Color.red
        Color.white
        Color.blue
    }
    .frame(width: 240, height: 150)
    .flagWave()
}

// MARK: - FlagWave.metal
// Save the shader below as FlagWave.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for FlagWave.swift (SwiftUI layer effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// Waves the layer like a flag on a pole at its leading edge: ripples run
/// along it, growing away from the pole, and the folds catch light and
/// shadow.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionFlagWave(float2 position, SwiftUI::Layer layer, float2 size, float time, float amplitude, float wavelength) {
    float reach = clamp(position.x / max(size.x, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0);
    float phase = position.x / wavelength * 2.0 * M_PI_F - time * 4.0;
    float wave = sin(phase) + 0.35 * sin(phase * 2.3 + 1.1);
    float dy = amplitude * reach * wave;
    float dx = amplitude * 0.25 * reach * cos(phase);
    half4 colour = layer.sample(float2(position.x + dx, position.y - dy));
    // Light on the slopes facing up, shade on the ones facing down.
    float slope = cos(phase) + 0.8 * cos(phase * 2.3 + 1.1);
    half shade = half(1.0 + 0.18 * reach * slope);
    return half4(clamp(colour.rgb * shade, 0.0h, colour.a), colour.a);
}
*/
```

---

## Voronoi Cells (`voronoi`)

Slowly drifting cells like stained glass, with soft seams between them.

- API: `VoronoiCells(colors:)`
- Component: Shader
- Trigger: Loop
- Requires: iOS 17+ · macOS 14+ · visionOS 1+
- Source: https://github.com/BigTsung/SwiftUI-Motion-Library/blob/main/Sources/MotionShaders/Voronoi.swift
- Files: Sources/MotionShaders/Voronoi.swift, Sources/MotionShaders/Shaders/Voronoi.metal

### Usage

```swift
import MotionShaders

VoronoiCells(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .pink, .orange, .teal])
    .ignoresSafeArea()
```

### How it works

Create a SwiftUI VoronoiCells(colors:cellSize:speed:) view (iOS 17+): a Rectangle with a Metal [[stitchable]] colour shader (position, colour, float time, float scale, device const half4 *palette, int count) driven by TimelineView(.animation). Work in cells of scale (60 pt); for the 3 × 3 neighbouring cells, the seed is cell + 0.5 + 0.4 × sin(time + 2π × hash2(cell)), so seeds drift. Track the nearest and second-nearest distances; colour the pixel with palette[hash(nearest cell) × count], darkened by smoothstep(0, 0.08, second − nearest) for soft seams and by 1 − 0.35 × nearest for a gentle glow at each seed. Pass the colours with .colorArray. With Reduce Motion on, pause the timeline. Hide it from accessibility.

### Source

```swift
import SwiftUI

/// A background of slowly drifting Voronoi cells, like stained glass or
/// living tissue: every point takes the colour of its nearest moving seed,
/// with soft dark seams between cells. Rendered with a Metal `colorEffect`
/// (`Shaders/Voronoi.metal`).
public struct VoronoiCells: View {
    private let colors: [Color]
    private let cellSize: Double
    private let speed: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - colors: Colours the cells are picked from.
    ///   - cellSize: Typical size of a cell, in points.
    ///   - speed: How fast the seeds drift.
    public init(colors: [Color] = [.indigo, .purple, .pink, .orange, .teal], cellSize: Double = 60, speed: Double = 0.6) {
        self.colors = colors.isEmpty ? [.gray] : colors
        self.cellSize = max(8, cellSize)
        self.speed = speed
    }

    public var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 3600) * speed
            Rectangle()
                .fill(.white)
                .colorEffect(motionShaders.motionVoronoi(.float(time), .float(cellSize), .colorArray(colors)))
        }
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }
}

#Preview {
    VoronoiCells()
        .frame(width: 320, height: 220)
}

// MARK: - Voronoi.metal
// Save the shader below as Voronoi.metal in your app target, and replace
// `motionShaders` with `ShaderLibrary.default`.
/*
// Stitchable shader for Voronoi.swift (SwiftUI colour effect).

#include <metal_stdlib>
#include <SwiftUI/SwiftUI_Metal.h>
using namespace metal;

/// A cheap, stable hash of a 2D point into 0...1, two values at once.
static float2 motionHash2(float2 p) {
    p = float2(dot(p, float2(127.1, 311.7)), dot(p, float2(269.5, 183.3)));
    return fract(sin(p) * 43758.5453);
}

/// Slowly drifting Voronoi cells: each pixel takes the colour of its nearest
/// moving seed (picked from `palette`), and the borders between cells are
/// drawn as soft dark seams.
[[ stitchable ]] half4 motionVoronoi(float2 position, half4 colour, float time, float scale, device const half4 *palette, int count) {
    float2 p = position / scale;
    float2 cell = floor(p);
    float nearest = 8.0, second = 8.0;
    float2 nearestCell = float2(0);
    for (int y = -1; y <= 1; y++) {
        for (int x = -1; x <= 1; x++) {
            float2 neighbour = cell + float2(x, y);
            float2 h = motionHash2(neighbour);
            float2 seed = neighbour + 0.5 + 0.4 * sin(time + 6.2831 * h);
            float d = length(p - seed);
            if (d < nearest) { second = nearest; nearest = d; nearestCell = neighbour; }
            else if (d < second) { second = d; }
        }
    }
    int index = int(motionHash2(nearestCell + 3.0).x * float(count)) % max(count, 1);
    half4 fill = palette[index];
    float seam = smoothstep(0.0, 0.08, second - nearest);
    float glow = 1.0 - nearest * 0.35;
    return half4(fill.rgb * half(seam * glow), 1.0h) * colour.a;
}
*/
```
